AI FRONT DESK : Upgrade Sales Playbook (AI Front Desk)

AI FRONT DESK
Upgrade Sales Playbook
For Upgrade SDRs & Account Executives
January 2026

What is AI Front Desk?

AI Front Desk is your practice’s smartest receptionist, one who never takes a day off, never puts anyone on hold, and never misses a call. It’s an add-on module that works around the clock to handle the routine stuff: scheduling, rescheduling, cancellations, and answering those same questions your team gets asked a hundred times a week.

When a caller has something more complex: billing questions, clinical details, insurance specifics. The AI doesn’t try to wing it. During business hours, it does a warm handoff to your staff with a quick summary of the conversation. After hours? It creates a prioritized task so nothing falls through the cracks.

It plugs right into what customers already have: Phones, Online Scheduling, and their EHR. That means it pulls real-time availability, knows which insurances they accept, understands their services, and can even share directions all without anyone having to re-enter a single piece of data.

Why Practices Love It

Here’s what you’ll hear from practices once they’ve been using it:

  • “We’re finally capturing those after-hours calls.” Every voicemail used to be a gamble, would they call back or just go somewhere else? Now those calls turn into booked appointments.
  • “No more hold music.” Callers hate waiting. The AI picks up instantly, so they’re never left listening to elevator music wondering if anyone’s coming back.
  • “It actually sounds like a person.” The voice is natural, not robotic. Patients often don’t even realize they’re talking to AI until we tell them.
  • “My staff can breathe again.” Scheduling calls are repetitive. Freeing the front desk from those means they can focus on patients who are actually standing in front of them.
  • “I can see exactly what’s happening.” Every call gets a transcript, a summary, and a sentiment score. The dashboard shows ROI in black and white, calls answered, appointments booked, new vs. existing patients.

Pricing (Keep This Simple)

$199-$299/month while they’re with Adit (normally $349), prorated into their billing. Each plan includes 200 minutes of agent talk time per month. If they go over, it’s just $1 per minute-transparent, no surprises.

Here’s the thing: 90% of practices never hit the overage limit. The 200 minutes is designed to cover typical usage generously. But if they do go over? That’s actually good news, it means the agent is handling a ton of calls and booking appointments. We’ve seen that on average, the agent books an appointment for every 20 minutes of talk time. So 200 extra minutes means roughly 10 extra appointments. At $200 per appointment, that’s $2,000 in revenue against a $200 overage. The math works in their favor every time.

1. Before the Call

A little homework goes a long way. Before you pick up the phone, take five minutes to understand their situation.

Who’s a Good Fit?

You’re looking for existing Adit customers who have missed calls. Prioritize practices with:

  • High call volume (check their Call Intelligence data)
  • Frequent missed calls10 to 20+ per week is a red flag they need help
  • Lots of after-hours voicemails piling up
  • Staffing crunches during peak hours

If you can pull a specific number “I noticed 36 missed calls across your locations in the last 15 days” you’ve got their attention.

Getting Them on the Line

Try their cell first, then the office line. If they don’t answer, leave a voicemail that’s friendly and to the point: “Hey, this is [Your Name] from Adit about our scheduled AI Front Desk review. Give me a call back or shoot me a text if you’re having trouble joining, I’ll send you a text reminder too.” Then actually text them.

You don’t need to hit every point. Read the room and focus on what matters to them:

Pain Point What They Get How Adit Delivers
Missed Calls 100% answer rate, zero calls going to voicemail Routes overflow and after-hours calls automatically
After-Hours Revenue Books appointments 24/7, even at 2 AM Dashboard shows exactly how many appointments were booked outside hours
Hold Time Frustration Instant pickup, no busy signals Warm transfers include conversation summaries
Staff Burnout Front desk focuses on patients in the office Handles scheduling, confirmations, common questions
Message Errors Full transcripts and summaries, no more “I thought she said Tuesday” Syncs to EHR and creates follow-up tasks
Impersonal Feel Natural voice, customizable name, warm handoffs Summarizes the call before transferring to staff
Staffing Gaps Always on, vacations, sick days, lunch breaks covered Scales during busy periods automatically

2. Discovery: The Most Important Part

Start with empathy. If there are multiple people on the call, acknowledge everyone: “Glad you could join us Sarah, always good to have more perspectives.”

Then dig in with questions that get them talking about their pain:

AI FRONT DESK : Upgrade Sales Playbook (continued, part 1)

  • “On a scale of 1 to 10, how happy are you with how after-hours calls are handled right now? What happens to those calls after 5 PM?”
  • “How many missed calls are you seeing in your VoIP logs each week? What do you think that’s costing you in new patients?”
  • “When your front desk says ‘please hold,’ how often do callers just hang up?”
  • “What repetitive tasks eat up your team’s time that could be spent on patient care?”
  • “Have you ever lost a patient because the phone was busy or nobody picked up?”
  • “If you could capture every call 24/7 without hiring another person, what would that mean for your practice?”
  • “What happens when your front desk is out sick or on vacation? How do you handle the call volume?”
  • “How often does your team get the same questions over and over-insurance acceptance, directions, parking? How much time does that eat up?”
  • “When a new patient calls and you’re already on another line, what’s your backup plan? Are you confident they’ll call back?”

Listen for the triggers: high missed call numbers, people hanging up on hold, voicemails that never get returned, staff feeling overwhelmed. When you hear it, connect the dots: “Based on what you’re telling me about those missed calls and voicemails, AI Front Desk would capture all of that. Let me show you exactly how.”

3. The Pitch: Tell a Story, Not a Feature List

Keep it tight 5 to 7 minutes max. Use the Problem, Solution, Proof framework:

“Here’s what we see all the time: practices losing potential patients because of missed calls, voicemails that pile up, or people who just hang up when they’re put on hold. Looking at your numbers, you had [X missed calls] recently, some with context, a lot without.

Our AI Front Desk fixes that. It answers every call instantly, 24/7, and handles scheduling, rescheduling, cancellations, and common questions using your EHR and Online Scheduling rules. No setup headaches, it pulls from what you already have.

You can customize everything: the voice, the name, scripts for how to handle insurance questions like ‘We don’t accept UnitedHealthcare, but here’s our cash pay option’ cancellation policies, text confirmations, all of it.

When something’s too complex, like a question about provider licensing or specialties, it either warm-transfers to your staff with a summary, or if it’s after hours, it creates a task so they can follow up first thing.

Every call gets transcribed with a summary and sentiment score. And the dashboard? It shows you exactly what’s happening: calls answered, appointments booked, new vs. existing patients, business hours vs. after hours.

Practices typically see 3-4x ROI monthly at $199/month.That includes 200 minutes of agent time, which covers most practices easily-and if you happen to go over, it’s just a dollar a minute. But honestly, if you’re going over, the agent is booking so many appointments that the extra cost pays for itself many times over.

Want to hear it in action? Let’s call the demo number right now.”

4. The Demo

The demo is everything. This isn’t like showing off other modules, you’re letting them experience something that feels almost human. The best approach: walk them through a structured flow, then hand them the number to try it themselves.

How the Agent Actually Works

Before you demo, understand the architecture so you can answer questions confidently. The agent operates entirely on Advanced Online Scheduling APIs. When a call comes in, it pulls real-time availability, insurance acceptance, services, provider info everything flows from what the practice already has configured. No duplicate data entry.

The call routing is flexible:

  • After-hours only: Call goes to agent outside business hours, staff handles everything during the day
  • Overflow: If the practice doesn’t answer within 20-30 seconds, call rolls to the agent, this catches those “almost missed” calls
  • Full-time: Agent handles everything, warm transfers when needed
  • Most practices start with after-hours + overflow. That means 90% of their after-hours calls, which are mostly new patients get handled automatically.

The Live Call Demo

Demo number: 832-590-3388 (confirm current number before your call)

Have the Client Call it and put it on speaker. Walk through this flow, it mirrors exactly what a new patient would experience:

AI FRONT DESK : Upgrade Sales Playbook (continued, part 2)

  1. Listen to the greeting. The agent introduces itself with a custom name (practices pick this) and the practice name. Notice how natural it sounds, we’ve tested dozens of voices and selected the four that perform best.
  2. Say you’re a new patient wanting to schedule. The agent will ask for your first and last name, then ask you to spell them (just like a real receptionist would). Then it asks for date of birth and confirms the phone number you’re calling from.
  3. Go through insurance. If you say you have BlueCross, the agent checks the practice’s accepted insurances. If you say Medicaid and they don’t accept it, the agent will politely explain that, and if they have in-house financing or cash pay options configured, it’ll mention those.
  4. Ask for an appointment. Give a preference like “Tuesday afternoon.” The agent pulls real-time availability from Online Scheduling and offers specific slots. If nothing works, it offers alternatives.
  5. Confirm the booking. The agent confirms the details and if the practice has it enabled, mentions they’ll receive a text confirmation. The appointment gets written directly to the EHR.
  6. Now throw a curveball. Ask something the agent won’t know: “What school did the doctor go to?” or “Is Dr. Smith board certified?” Watch what happens, the agent doesn’t make something up. It says it will have someone from the practice follow up, and creates a task. This is huge.

What to Show in the Module

After the call, share your screen and walk through what just happened on the backend. This is where you prove the value isn’t just a cool phone call, it’s actionable data.

Home Page (Interactions Feed):

Each call shows a one-line summary of what happened. Click into the call you just made. They’ll see the full transcript, a 3-6 line summary the AI generated, sentiment categorization, and the outcome (booked, created task, transferred, etc.). Point out how fast this processes, within 1-2 minutes of the call ending, everything is populated.

Tasks:

Show the task created from your curveball question. Each task includes the patient context, what they asked, and a link to the call recording. Tasks can be assigned round-robin across staff, to a specific person, or by task type (billing questions to one person, scheduling follow-ups to another). It’s like having an assistant who takes perfect notes.

Insights Dashboard:

Walk through the metrics: total calls handled, after-hours vs. business hours breakdown, scheduling calls booked vs. transferred vs. task-created, and reasons appointments weren’t booked. For practices worried about ROI, this page is gold. They can see exactly what the agent is doing for them.

Preferences (The Customization Page):

Show them how much control they have:

  • Agent name and voice: They pick a name (Amy, Sarah, whatever fits their brand) and choose from four tested voices
  • Custom greeting: They can script exactly how the agent introduces itself
  • AI disclosure toggle: Some practices want to disclose it’s AI, some don’t. We give them the option (and note we don’t recommend disclosure, people hang up more when they know)
  • Practice info: Parking, directions, anything patients commonly ask
  • Payment options: Medicare, Medicaid, CareCredit, FSA, in-house financing, whatever they accept gets added to the agent’s knowledge
  • Services: Which appointment types the agent can book (keep this focused, 3-5 services max for best performance)
  • Cancellation/reschedule windows: If they require 48 hours notice, the agent enforces that
  • Age restrictions: If they don’t see kids under 14, the agent will politely decline those bookings

What the Agent Won’t Do (And Why That’s Good)

Be ready to explain what’s intentionally limited:

  • It doesn’t guess. If someone asks a question outside its knowledge base, it creates a task instead of making something up. No hallucinations, no liability.
  • It filters sales calls. The agent recognizes solicitation calls and gatekeeps them, doesn’t transfer, just creates a “vendor” task if the practice wants to review later.
  • Services are kept focused. We recommend 3-5 service types max. More services = more context for the AI to process = slower, less accurate responses. Keep it tight.
  • Warm transfers respect business hours. If it’s after hours and someone asks for a human, the agent explains no one is available and offers to create a callback task.

Tie It Back to Their Practice

After the demo, connect what they just experienced to their specific pain points: “Remember those 36 missed calls we talked about? Every single one of those would have been answered, qualified, and either booked or turned into a follow-up task. How much revenue do you think that represents?”

5. Handling Objections

Objections are buying signals. Here’s how to handle the common ones:

AI FRONT DESK : Upgrade Sales Playbook (continued, part 3)

They Say… You Say…
“It sounds too robotic.” “You just heard it-what did you think? It’s best-in-class voice with almost no latency. And when it transfers, your staff gets a full summary so it feels personal.”
“Setup sounds like a headache.” “It’s a guided one-hour session with our team. Most of the prompts are pre-loaded-you’re just reviewing and tweaking. We do the heavy lifting.”
“What if someone asks something complicated?” “You saw it in the demo-it doesn’t guess. It either transfers with context or creates a task. Full transcripts for everything, so you’ve got an audit trail.”
“It’s another monthly cost.” “$199-$299 a month with 200 minutes included-that covers most practices. If it books just 3-4 appointments that would have gone to voicemail, it’s already paid for itself. And those practices that use more? They’re getting even more value.”
“My patients will hate talking to a robot.” “That’s what everyone thinks until they hear it. Most patients don’t even realize it’s AI. And the ones who do? They just appreciate not being on hold.”
“What if we go over the included minutes?” “Honestly? That’s a good problem to have. 90% of practices never hit the limit. But if you do, it means the agent is crushing it-booking appointments left and right. It’s just $1 per minute over, and for every 20 minutes of talk time, the agent typically books an appointment. So even if you go 200 minutes over, that’s roughly 10 extra appointments. At $200 per appointment, you’re looking at $2,000 in revenue for a $200 overage. The ROI is built in.”

6. Closing

Don’t overthink this. If the demo went well, the close is natural.

The Ask

“Should we get you started? I can send the agreement links right now, one for each location if you’ve got multiple.”

Walk Them Through Signing

Stay on the call while they sign. Talk them through it: “Click the plus button, then Next, then just sign with your name. The billing starts prorated to your renewal date.”

Book Onboarding Immediately

Don’t let them leave without a date on the calendar: “Great, let’s get your onboarding scheduled. It’s about an hour and we’ll set everything up together. Does Tuesday at 9 AM Eastern work?” Send the calendar invite before you hang up.

If They Need to Think About It

Send a follow-up email within the hour: quick recap of the switch factors that resonated, link to the demo recording if you have one, and a personalized ROI estimate based on their missed call numbers.

Remember: You’re Not Selling Software You’re solving a problem they deal with every single day. Missed calls mean missed revenue and stressed staff. AI Front Desk fixes both. Lead with that, show them it works, and getting to yes is the easy part.

AI training Document v2 (AI Front Desk)

AI Training Document: Adit Insurance Verification (RCM Module)

1. Product Overview (Core Facts)

  • Adit’s Insurance Verification is part of Adit’s Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) offering.
  • It automates and standardizes insurance eligibility checks to reduce claim denials, protect revenue, and streamline front-office operations.
  • Supported specialties: Dental, Orthodontic and Optometry practices. Scales from single-location clinics to large multi-specialty DSOs.
  • Combines automated EDI verification with optional manual verification by Adit’s RCM team (Advanced tiers).
  • Verification confirms in real time:
    • Status - whether the patient’s insurance is active
    • Financials - remaining deductibles, co-pays, out-of-pocket limits
    • Specialty limits - multi-phase treatment coverage (Ortho), vision-specific allowances (Optometry)
    • Benefit dates - plan effective dates and renewal cycles
  • Best practice to recommend: Verify eligibility 48-72 hours before every appointment because insurance details can change at any time.
  • The current module version is IV26, which allows upgrading individual appointments from Basic to Advanced (pay per upgraded appointment only).

2. Verification Tiers & Pricing

Tier Verification method CDT code coverage Pricing Failed verification handling
Basic (EDI Only) Fully automated EDI Up to 40 CDT codes $99/month, includes 300 free EDI verifications; $0.06 per additional verification No cost for failed verifications; no manual expert follow-up
Advanced - Standard EDI + manual expert validation by RCM team Up to 20 CDT codes $99/month + $1.00 per advanced verification If EDI fails, expert team manually verifies the appointment
Advanced - Extensive EDI + full manual expert validation (for complex/high-volume needs, e.g., Medicaid, HMOs) 20 to 40 CDT codes $99/month + $2.25 per advanced verification All failed verifications handled by the expert team at no additional cost
Add-on: Same-Day Verification Advanced verification with expedited turnaround Up to 40 CDT codes on the form Available on all plans (add-on) Results delivered within a 60-minute SLA

Shared benefits across all plans:

  • Verified PDFs and breakdown notes auto-posted into the EHR (if enabled)
  • No cost for failed verifications
  • Any individual appointment can be upgraded to Advanced verification at any time (One-Off Upgrade)

One-Off Upgrade (Basic → Advanced) options:

  • Standard: up to 20 codes
  • Extensive: ability to select additional codes, up to 40 codes
  • If no additional codes are selected, only the treatment codes defined in Preferences are verified.
  • Billing: customer pays only for the upgraded appointment.

Basic vs. Advanced Verification (definition)

  • Basic Eligibility Verification: Automated EDI-only check. Returns standard eligibility information from the payer’s EDI response, with limited benefit breakdowns or code-level analysis.
  • Advanced Eligibility Verification: Two layers - first EDI, then a second layer of verification by Adit’s RCM team. Includes detailed benefits: deductibles, out-of-pocket maximums, co-insurance, co-payments, coverage limitations, and plan-specific rules.

3. Setup / Onboarding Flow (RCM Module)

Order of setup steps the assistant should walk users through:

  1. Navigate to the RCM Module. If a welcome/demo screen appears, the account is not yet upgraded - direct the user to contact the Adit team (Upgrades) to enable access.
  2. Practice Information. Complete all mandatory fields (marked *). Incorrect/missing info can cause verifications to fail or return inaccurate results.
  3. NPI Settings.
    • One NPI: single default NPI for all verifications.
    • Multiple NPI: assign NPIs per provider. Click Add Provider and enter Provider Name, NPI, and Tax ID exactly as configured in the EHR.
    • Also configure each provider’s network participation and fee schedule so retrieved benefits reflect correct in-/out-of-network status.
  4. Verification Settings.
    • Trigger Selection: how many days before the appointment verification runs (e.g., 3 or 5 days before).
    • Frequency Selection: how often patients are re-verified between appointments (default: 6 months).
  5. EHR / PMS Settings.
    • PDF setting: Yes/No to attach the Eligibility Verification PDF to the patient file; if Yes, choose the destination folder. File name format: Verified Date - Patient Name.
    • Patient Note setting: Yes/No to add a note after verification.
    • Templates: define the PPO Template and HMO & Other Template note formats. Available fields include Insurance Carrier, Verification Date, Plan Maximum/Remaining, Ortho Maximum/Remaining, Deductible Met (Ind).
  6. Select Tx Codes. Choose which treatment codes are verified per tier. Each code carries 1-4 verification questions (coverage & percentage, age limits, frequency limits, patient eligibility/next eligible date).
  7. Notification Settings. Enable email alerts for failed verifications. If disabled, failures can go unnoticed → unverified patients at the front desk, billing issues.
  8. Automation Credentials. Provide insurance portal login credentials so Adit can auto-retrieve eligibility. Click Connect; status shows Authenticated when done. These credentials are for system automation only - not for manual login use.
  9. Portal Credentials. For insurances that don’t support full automation, provide portal username/password so Adit can perform manual verification or detailed eligibility audits.
  10. Insurance Mapping (final step). Map each insurance name from the EHR/PMS to Adit’s standardized master insurance list via dropdown (e.g., “BCBSTX” → “Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas”). Accurate mapping is critical for successful verification.

4. Dashboards & Statuses

After onboarding, users land on the Insurance Verification Dashboard in the RCM module. All packages see three dashboards:

  1. Basic Verification Dashboard (EDI-based checks)
  2. Advanced Verification Dashboard (EDI + manual review)
  3. Same-Day Verification Dashboard

4.1 Dashboard cards (Basic)

Card Meaning
Total Appointments All appointments in the selected date range
Scheduled Appointments Upcoming appointments eligible for verification
Skipped Appointments Excluded due to Cash patient or In-House insurance

Active Insurance Verified; patient’s insurance is active

Other Failure Reasons Failures due to payer responses, system issues, unsupported insurance logic

Cancelled by User Manually cancelled by practice or support
Basic Overage Cost Charges for Basic verifications beyond the included limit

Advanced dashboard adds: Cost to Customer card, plus columns for Insurance Type (Primary/Secondary), Eligible for Verification, and Cost for Verification. The Same-Day dashboard uses the same cards as Advanced.

4.2 Filters

Date Range, Trigger Date (when verification was initiated), Appointment Date (scheduled date in EHR), Verification Status.

4.3 Verification Status definitions

Status Meaning
In Queue Appointment synced from EHR, waiting for trigger
In Progress Verification triggered (typically 3 or 5 days before appointment)
Verified Eligibility check completed successfully
Failed Incorrect/missing data or payer response issues
Skipped Cash patient or In-House insurance

4.4 Insurance Status definitions

  • Active - insurance active at time of verification
  • Termed - insurance no longer active
  • Unknown - verification not completed / non-final status

4.5 Row-level data fields

Patient Name, Appointment Date, Trigger Date, Insurance Provider, Verification Status, Insurance Status, Verified On (completion date/time).

4.6 Available actions

Action What it does

Upgrade to Manual One-off upgrade (EDI followed by manual verification); only when enabled
Audit Logs Timestamped verification lifecycle events

Verify Same-Day Triggers Same-Day Advanced verification

5. Same-Day Verification (workflow detail)

How to initiate:

  1. Click Add on the Same-Day Verification dashboard
  2. Complete the Patient Verification Form
  3. Click Verify

Required form information:

  • Service Code Type (STC) - auto-populated by specialty (Dental / Orthodontics)
  • CDT Codes - maximum of 40
  • Provider Details - auto-populated
  • Subscriber Details - if subscriber = patient, enter subscriber details; if subscriber ≠ patient, enter both patient and subscriber details
  • Provider ID - select from dropdown
  • Insurance Card Upload - optional

SLA: The Advanced verification form is completed within 60 minutes of submission.

6. Failed Verifications (customer-action workflow)

  • Adit’s team handles most verifications. Customer action is required only when a verification fails due to missing/incomplete insurance or demographic information.
  • Workflow: Click Update on the Failed dashboard card → list of failed appointments opens → incorrect/missing data is highlighted → open the patient detail form → correct the data → resubmit. Each corrected submission re-triggers verification and updates the final status.
  • If enabled, reminder email notifications prompt the practice to fix missing info and re-initiate verification before the appointment.

7. Canonical Q&A Pairs (training examples)

Q: How do I sign up for Insurance Verification? A: It’s part of Adit’s RCM offering. Contact the Adit Upgrades team to enroll and get next steps. We also have an option for self onboarding.

Q: How do I change which treatment codes are verified? A: Email support at adit.com. The request is auto-logged as a ticket and routed to the right team. Note: because tiers (Basic, Advanced Standard, Advanced Extensive) are code-count based, changing codes may change your tier and pricing. Refer users to the “Guide to Insurance Verification Charges https://help.adit.com/portal/en/kb/articles/guide-to-insurance-verification-charges#1_Software-Only_Package” article.

Q: Will Adit update the patient file in my PMS/EHR? A: Yes - via a note, an attached PDF, or both, based on your preferences in the RCM module.

Q: How do I check the status of a verification? A: Open the RCM module; you land on the Verifications page. Check the color-coded Verification Status column and use the Actions column for the verification form or history.

Q: When do I need to take action? A: Only when a verification fails due to missing or incomplete insurance/demographic information. Update the details in the Adit App so verification can be re-triggered before the appointment.

Q: What’s the difference between Basic and Advanced verification? A: Basic is automated EDI-only with standard eligibility info. Advanced adds a second layer of manual review by Adit’s RCM team and returns detailed benefits (deductibles, OOP maximums, co-insurance, co-pays, limitations, plan-specific rules). Advanced comes in Standard (up to 20 codes) and Extensive (up to 40 codes).

Q: Can I stay on Basic but get detailed verification for one patient? A: Yes. With the IV26 module’s One-Off Upgrade, you can upgrade individual appointments to Advanced and pay only for that appointment.

Q: How am I billed? A: All plans are $99/month. Basic includes 300 free EDI verifications ($0.06 each after). Advanced Standard adds $1.00 per advanced verification; Advanced Extensive adds $2.25. Failed verifications are never charged. Direct users to the “Guide to Insurance Verification Charges” article for full details.

Q: How fast is Same-Day Verification? A: Results within a 60-minute SLA. It’s an Advanced add-on available on all plans, ideal for urgent or last-minute appointments.

Q: Why did my verification fail? A: Two failure categories: (1) Incorrect Data - missing or wrong patient/insurance information (fixable by the practice via the Failed card → Update flow); (2) Other Failure Reasons - payer responses, system issues, or unsupported insurance logic.

Q: Why was an appointment skipped? A: Appointments are skipped when the patient is marked as a Cash patient or has In-House insurance.

Q: What does “Expired” mean? A: The appointment date passed without a completed verification, or the verification was cancelled (Cancel Verification moves it to Expired).

Q: What are Automation Credentials vs. Portal Credentials? A: Automation Credentials are insurance portal logins Adit uses for automated retrieval (system use only). Portal Credentials cover insurances that don’t support full automation, enabling Adit’s team to do manual verification or detailed eligibility audits.

8. Escalation & Routing Rules for the AI Assistant

User intent Route
Enroll / purchase / upgrade plan Adit Upgrades team
Change verified treatment codes Email support at adit.com (auto-ticketed)
Billing disputes or charge questions beyond published pricing Adit Support Team
Setup walkthrough “How To: Set Up Insurance Verification” article
Status meaning questions “How To: Check the Status of an Insurance Verification” article
Pricing details “Guide to Insurance Verification Charges” (help.adit.com KB)
Plan selection help Adit Support Team

Assistant guardrails:

  • Never quote prices other than those in Section 2.
  • Never promise verification outcomes or guarantee payer coverage.
  • Do not ask for or store actual portal passwords in chat; direct users to enter credentials in the Automation/Portal Credentials setup screens.
  • If asked about specialties outside Dental, Ortho, Optometry, Chiropractic, state supported specialties and route to Sales/Upgrades.

9. Glossary

  • RCM - Revenue Cycle Management
  • EDI - Electronic Data Interchange; automated payer eligibility channel
  • CDT codes - Dental procedure/treatment codes verified per patient
  • STC - Service Code Type (auto-set by specialty on Same-Day forms)
  • NPI - National Provider Identifier
  • DSO - Dental Service Organization (multi-location group)
  • Termed - insurance policy no longer active
  • One-Off Upgrade - per-appointment Basic → Advanced upgrade (IV26)
  • SLA - Service Level Agreement (60 minutes for Same-Day)
  • PPO / HMO templates - note formats posted to the patient file by plan type
  • Basic client - EDI-only client service model (automated verification only)
  • Advanced client - EDI plus manual verification by the Adit RCM team
  • Frequency window - period defined by the client’s re-verification frequency setting, measured from the patient’s last full verification
  • Match / Non-match - all comparison values equal → match (reuse stored result); any divergence → non-match (escalate to fresh verification)

11.1 What IV26_v2 adds

Two connected capabilities:

  1. Configurable re-verification frequency at the client (practice) level.
  2. Intelligent routing that decides, per patient request, whether verification is served by enriched eligibility data, an EDI eligibility call, or a previously stored, still-valid automation result.

11.3 Frequency setting (Preferences page)

  • New dropdown with exactly three options: 1 Year, 6 Months (default), 3 Months.
  • Default is 6 Months for all clients; existing clients are migrated automatically at release with no action required.
  • Applies at the client (practice) level and governs all patients under that client.
  • A frequency change takes effect on the next verification request; it never retroactively re-processes past requests.
  • Visibility/editability follows the existing preferences-page permission model.

11.4 Connect Insurance pages

  • The existing Insurances Connected page is retained for manual portal logins.
  • Basic (soft) customers: one “Connect Insurance” page containing automation credentials.
  • Advanced (Soft + Manual) customers: two pages - one for RCM human agents (unchanged), one for automation credentials.
  • The automation list reflects the insurances supported through the client’s automation enablement; search/sort/status conventions follow existing page patterns.

11.5 Core concepts (canonical definitions)

  • First request: first verification request for a patient with no prior verified result on file for that client.
  • Frequency window: period defined by the client’s frequency setting, measured from the patient’s last full verification. Inside the window → candidate for comparison-and-reuse. Outside → full verification.
  • Comparison values: specific EDI-response fields compared against the stored automation result to detect material benefit changes (field set owned by Sofiyan; blocking dependency).
  • Match: all comparison values equal. Any divergence = non-match.

11.9 Charging rules

  • Basic clients: no charge impact - they already receive 300 free requests, and the new flow operates within that arrangement.
  • Advanced clients: matched, auto-resolved requests are charged $0; non-matched requests follow existing automated and manual-verification charging.

11.15 Internal Q&A pairs (post-release / internal training)

Q: What frequency options can a client choose? A: 1 Year, 6 Months, or 3 Months, set on the IV preferences page. Default is 6 Months for all clients, applied at the practice level.

Q: What happens when a patient is re-verified within the frequency window? A: The system runs a lightweight EDI check and compares defined values against the patient’s stored automated result. If everything matches, the stored result is reused and stamped with today’s date - for Advanced clients this is verified instantly at $0 with no manual queue entry. If anything differs, the system calls automation (if enabled) or saves the EDI result and routes to manual verification.

Q: Does changing the frequency reprocess old requests? A: No. It takes effect on the next verification request only.

Q: Are Basic (Soft) clients billed differently under IV26_v2? A: No - Basic (Soft) client charging is unchanged; they continue to receive 300 free requests.

Intro to AI Care Coordinator

AI Care Coordinator (also referred to as AI Recare or the AI Outreach Agent) is the outbound agent within the Adit AI Agent suite. While AI Front Desk handles all incoming communication to the practice and AI Web Chat engages website visitors, AI Care Coordinator plans and executes all relevant outgoing communication (calls and texts) to patients on behalf of the practice. Practices can fully customise for what, when, whom and how the agent reaches out.

Every outreach handled by the agent is fully documented, transcribed and analysed, and surfaces in the same Interactions framework used across the AI Agent suite. The agent is created per practice and per location, and updates instantly whenever preferences change.

Terminology

  • Outreach / Step - a single outbound call or outbound SMS sent by the agent to a patient. “Outreach” is the colloquial term; in the app it is a Step within a sequence.

  • Sequence - the full set of steps the agent performs for a particular patient for a particular use case (e.g., an appointment marked broken, a recall coming due).

  • Sequence Type - the kind of scenario for which the agent performs outreach. The conversations differ per type, so the agent only supports types it is fully trained on.

  • Enrolled Patient - every patient added to a sequence. The same patient can be enrolled in different sequence types.

  • Schedule - business-hours-like timings the agent must respect when reaching out. Multiple schedules can be created and assigned per sequence.

  • Flow - an organised collection of steps defining which step happens on which day and via which mode (Call or SMS). Multiple flows can be created and assigned per sequence.

  • Sequence Status - the ongoing status of an active sequence, or the final status of an ended one (full list under Other Info).

  • Step Outcome - the result of each individual step (full list under Other Info).

Supported Sequence Types

  • Unscheduled Broken Appointments - the agent reaches out to patients whose appointments are marked broken / no show (and optionally cancelled) with no future appointment, to get them rescheduled.

  • Recall Due - the agent reaches out to patients with a recall due and tries to schedule their appointment.

  • Unscheduled Treatment - the agent reaches out to patients who have not had an appointment in a long time (e.g., 9/12/15/18 months) and tries to schedule them.

  • Unconfirmed Appointments - the agent reaches out to patients with an upcoming appointment who have not confirmed via call or SMS, to get the appointment confirmed.

Note: Payment Due (agent reaches out to patients with outstanding payments to help clear dues) appeared in earlier scoping and is on the roadmap. It is not part of the current release and is excluded from the sections below.

How it Works - The Modular Model

A capable outreach agent must let the practice compose exactly what the agent should do for every scenario - e.g., “if a New Patient Exam goes broken with no future appointment, call in 48 hours, then SMS, then another call in 72 hours,” or “if a Hygiene recall is due and the patient had no completed appointment in the last 6 months, follow up 2 days before the due date, 3 attempts, twice by call and once by text.”

To support every permutation, the setup is modular. Four basic elements are abstracted and then composed into Outreach Sequences:

  • Services - the list of services the agent follows up on. Captured separately so the right patients are triggered (via treatment codes and appointment status) and so the agent has context about the service before calling. Treatment code mapping is mandatory to save a service.

  • Recall - the recall types the agent works with, including an explanation of each recall to give the agent context. Treatment code mapping is mandatory to save a recall type.

  • Schedule / Timings - when the agent is allowed to reach out. Different outreaches can run on different days/times (e.g., recall outreach Mon-Wed during business hours; confirmation outreach 6 days a week).

  • Flow - the mode of outreach for each step and the gap between steps. A recall flow may have 5 steps, a broken-appointment flow 3, a confirmation flow only 1.

Cloud vs On-Prem EHRs - the key structural split

Where recall data comes from depends on the EHR category. This split shapes field availability, editability and layout throughout the Preferences page.

EHR category Recall data behaviour
On-Prem EHRs Recall data is PULLED FROM the EHR - Recall Type, TX Code / Appointment Type, Last Completed Appt Date and Interval come from EHR records and are read-only in Adit. The only editable (and mandatory) field is the Select Service mapping. Sequence and Time are set in Adit.
Cloud EHRs Recall is SET UP entirely in Adit - the practice configures Recall Type, TX Code / Appointment Type, Due Date, Interval, Sequence and Time. Adit auto-creates recalls based on treatment codes and last completed appointment dates.

Within the 17 in-scope EHRs, two field groups exist: the TX Code group (OpenDental, Eaglesoft, Dentrix, Tracker, Cleardent, Abeldent, Crystal PM, PracticeWork, PracticeWeb) and the Appointment Type group (Officemate, Chirotouch, Eyefinity, Revolution, Jane, CT Cloud). Dentrix Ascend and Curve are the Cloud EHRs. Figma covers all four variants: Cloud with/without TX Code and On-Prem with/without TX Code.

Getting Started - 1. Settings Reused from AI Front Desk

AI Care Coordinator reuses most of the AI Agent setup that practices complete for AI Front Desk. If AI Front Desk is already configured, these carry over; if not, they must be completed as part of Recare onboarding. All settings are per-location.

  • Configure Agent - Agent Name, Practice Name and Agent Voice define the identity the agent uses on outbound calls. Capabilities (Scheduling / Rescheduling / Cancellation) govern what the agent may do when a patient wants to book, move or cancel during an outreach conversation.

  • Custom Messages - AI Disclosure applies to outbound conversations as well (default No; the agent confirms it is AI if asked directly).

  • Practice Details - address, time zone, business hours, website, parking, directions - the agent’s knowledge of the practice when talking to patients. Several fields are pulled from Online Scheduling.

  • Booking Settings - payment options, accepted insurances, services offered, availability settings, max booking window, cancellation/rescheduling windows and charges, price sheet, age limits, walk-ins. These govern the booking part of every outreach conversation.

  • Configure Tasks - how AI-generated tasks are assigned. “Recare” already exists as a task type, so follow-ups generated by outreach conversations route through the same assignment options (round robin / direct / by task type / unassigned).

Note: Inbound Call Settings and Inbound SMS Settings are NOT part of Recare - they are inbound-only AI Front Desk features.

Note: Eaglesoft does not support Rescheduling or Cancellation. For Eaglesoft practices both capabilities must remain off; the agent collects the request and creates a task instead.

Getting Started - 2. Service Mapping

This section captures the list of services the agent will follow up on. It exists separately in Outreach Settings for two reasons: (1) to trigger the correct patients for outreach based on treatment codes and appointment status, and (2) to provide the agent context on the type of service and its details before it contacts the patient.

Mapping treatment codes is mandatory to save a service. Ideally this page will auto-populate from the services set up in Online Scheduling; that is an upcoming enhancement and may not be available in the first iteration.

Outreach Mapping → Service Mapping - services for new and existing patients with TX codes

Getting Started - 3. Recall Set Up (Cloud vs On-Prem)

On-Prem EHRs

“Recall outreach will be done based on EHR data. Service mapping is required to activate each recall type.”

Each recall card shows Recall Type, TX Code / Appointment Type, Last Completed Appt Date and Interval as read-only fields pulled from the EHR. The only editable field is the Select Service dropdown, which is mandatory (validation: “Service Name cannot be blank”). There are no Sequence or Time fields on On-Prem cards. Go-live is blocked only when a service is not mapped; Sequence and Time can be completed in any order elsewhere.

Recall Set Up - On-Prem: read-only EHR fields; Select Service is the only editable field

Cloud EHRs

The practice sets up each recall type directly in Adit: Recall Type, TX Code / Appointment Type, Due Date, Interval, Sequence and Time (before / on / after the recall date). Based on the treatment codes and last completed appointment dates, Adit auto-creates recalls for the agent. Each recall set up in Adit also carries an explanation of the recall to give the agent context. Treatment code mapping is mandatory to save a recall type.

Recall Set Up - Cloud: recall types configured in Adit with TX codes and intervals

Note: CT Cloud and Jane calculate the recall due date from the appointment type plus the interval set in Adit; in Jane the recall type is fetched the same as the appointment type.

Getting Started - 4. Outreach Schedules

Schedules define when the agent is allowed to reach out, similar to business hours. The practice can create multiple named schedules (e.g., “New Patient Broken Appt Schedule”) and use the relevant one per sequence. For example, recall outreach can be restricted to Monday-Wednesday during business hours while appointment confirmation outreach runs six days a week. Schedule name is required.

Outreach Schedule - multiple named schedules with per-day timings

Getting Started - 5. Outreach Flows

Flows define the mode of outreach for each step and the gap between steps. Each flow has a required name (e.g., “Standard Sequence Flow”) and a set of steps, each with a Day (1 to 30 days) and a Mode (Call or Text). Multiple flows can be created and assigned per sequence - e.g., a 5-step recall flow, a 3-step broken appointment flow, a 1-step confirmation flow.

Outreach Flow - day-by-day steps with Call/SMS mode

Getting Started - 6. Outreach Sequences (per Sequence Type)

With the basic elements in place, the practice composes sequences. Creating a sequence starts with two fields - Sequence Name (custom) and Sequence Type (one of the four supported types) - and the remaining fields open up based on the type selected. Any number of sequences can be created per type, so the agent can take different steps for different services, recall types or patient brackets.

Common to all sequence types:

  • Sequence Schedule and Sequence Flow - select one of the schedules and one of the flows created earlier (required).

  • Skip if future appointment - option to skip patients who already have a future appointment booked.

  • Engage with - Active, Inactive, or Active and Inactive patients.

  • Additional Agent Knowledge - optional free text for sequence-specific context (promotions, pre-treatment care etc.). If provided, Knowledge Valid Till (a date) becomes applicable; when the date is reached the knowledge resets to blank for that sequence.

  • On / Off toggle - sequences can be temporarily turned off without deletion. Turning a sequence off deletes all future steps for all enrolled patients and updates their Sequence Status to Stopped.

Unscheduled Broken Appointments

The practice selects the applicable appointment statuses (at least one required - e.g., whether the outreach covers only Broken/No Show or Cancelled as well), then the applicable services (multi-select, from Service Mapping), schedule and flow. The trigger defines how many hours/days after the appointment the sequence is created.

Note: The statuses shown are EHR-specific. Some EHRs map cleanly to Cancelled + No Show/Missed; others expose their own status sets (e.g., Eaglesoft: Failed / Cancelled / Neither; Tracker: Cancelled / Office Cancel / Short Cancel / No Show / Pending / Waiting). The Preferences page displays the relevant statuses for the connected EHR.

Sequence - Unscheduled Broken Appointment (new patient example)

Sequence - Unscheduled Broken Appointment (existing patient example)

Recall Due

The practice selects the applicable recall types (multi-select, from Recall Set Up), then the minimum time that must have elapsed since the last completed appointment of ANY service for the patient to be considered - e.g., if a hygiene recall is due today but the patient had an emergency appointment 3 weeks ago, it may not make sense to reach out yet. The trigger defines when the sequence is created: before, on, or after the recall due date.

Sequence - Recall Due (applicable recall types + recall schedule and flow)

Unscheduled Treatment

A more generic outreach - the only check is the time since the last completed appointment, regardless of appointment type. The trigger defines how long it must have been (e.g., 9, 12, 15 or 18 months). Multiple sequences can serve different brackets.

Sequence - Unscheduled Treatment (months-since-last-appointment trigger)

Unconfirmed Appointments

The practice selects which services the agent should confirm, plus schedule and flow. The trigger defines how many hours/days before the appointment the sequence is created.

Sequence - Unconfirmed Appointments (hours-before-appointment trigger)

Getting Started - 7. Sequence Downtime

Sequence Downtime ensures the AI does not overwhelm patients by reaching out too frequently - it defines how many days must pass since the last sequence end date before a patient can be added to a new sequence (30 / 60 / 90 / 120 / 150 / 180 / 210 / 240 days).

Sequence Downtime - minimum days between sequences for the same patient

Getting Started - 8. Outreach Settings

The final Preferences screen collects cross-cutting outreach behaviour:

  • Confirm Insurance Details - whether the agent reconfirms insurance details and collects them if missing when scheduling an appointment (recommended: Yes).

  • Call Transfer Setting - whether the AI transfers the call to the practice if it comes across questions it can’t answer within practice business hours. Outside business hours, the agent takes a message and creates a task for the practice to follow up. An Extension Number can be provided.

  • Recare Agent Capabilities - what kinds of calls the agent handles end-to-end: Scheduling, Rescheduling, Cancellations (Yes/No each). For other call types the agent takes a message and creates a follow-up task or transfers, based on the settings.

  • Blocked Numbers & Patients - entry point to the blocked list (see next section).

Outreach Settings - insurance confirmation, call transfer, Recare agent capabilities, blocked list

Getting Started - 9. Blocked Numbers & Patients

The Manage modal lets the practice add a phone number or a patient to the blocked list (input + Add button), with type pills (Phone / Patient), the date added, a remove action per entry and a footer count. Blocked numbers and patients are permanently excluded from all outreach sequences.

Blocked Numbers & Patients - Manage modal

Agent Behaviour - Sequence Lifecycle & Flow

This section covers how the outbound flow works end to end - from patient enrollment through step execution to sequence completion.

Enrollment - how patients enter a sequence

  • Unscheduled Broken Appointments - when an appointment reaches one of the selected broken/cancelled statuses for a mapped service and the trigger time since the appointment elapses, the patient is enrolled (unless skipped for a future appointment).

  • Recall Due - when a patient’s recall due date approaches/passes per the before/on/after trigger for a selected recall type, and the minimum time since their last completed appointment (any service) has elapsed. Data is taken from the day the practice enrolls on AI Recare onward.

  • Unscheduled Treatment - when the configured number of months since the patient’s last completed appointment is reached.

  • Unconfirmed Appointments - when an upcoming appointment for a selected service remains unconfirmed at the configured hours/days before appointment time.

How the recall due date is determined

There is generally no directly stored recall due date usable across EHRs; the due date is identified per EHR. For recall-table EHRs, the system checks the nearest future recall due date for the patient, and if none exists, the nearest past due date, then verifies no future appointment is scheduled. For EHRs without usable recall records (e.g., OpenDental-style logic), the due date is derived in priority order: (1) the original recall appointment date, where a completed appointment has the Recall flag and Recall Type; (2) the patient recall interval applied to the last completed appointment; (3) a hygiene-procedure fallback - completed appointments with hygiene codes (D1110, D1120, D4341, D4910) plus a default 6-month interval. Only one final due date is selected per patient per recall type. If a step-1 result exists, later steps are skipped.

Recall status is then determined by matching the appointment against the recall (via TX code, or stored appointment id for certain configurations): Completed, Scheduled, Unscheduled, Overdue and Scheduled, or Overdue and Unscheduled.

Step execution

Once enrolled, the agent executes the assigned flow step by step - each step is a call or SMS on its configured day - within the time windows of the assigned schedule. Step outcomes are recorded per attempt (Answered, No Answer, Left Voicemail, Sent, Replied). During a conversation the agent behaves per the reused AI FD behaviour: it verifies the patient, works within Booking Settings, books/reschedules where capabilities allow, and creates tasks or transfers where they do not.

What ends or interrupts a sequence

  • Appointment scheduled (scheduling types) / appointment confirmed (confirmation type) - sequence ends successfully.

  • Patient not interested - sequence ends.

  • Call Back Later - the agent collects a callback time and the sequence restarts at that time.

  • Do Not Call - patient moved to the DNC list; excluded from all future sequences unless opted back in.

  • Out of Service - number unreachable; sequence ends.

  • Stopped - practice stops the sequence for a patient, or turns the sequence off entirely.

  • Sequence Ended - all steps completed without connecting with the patient.

Navigating AI Recare

The module’s left navigation comprises: Home, Interactions, Outreach (Enrolled Patients, Queued Steps, Completed Steps, Patients Overview), AI Tasks, Insights and Preferences.

Home

The Recare landing page with summary metrics and entry points into patients, steps and interactions.

Recare Home Page

Interactions

Every completed outreach conversation with summary, transcript and call analysis - consistent with the AI FD interaction detail experience: call summary, patient/sequence context, Call Analysis fields, tags, notes and associated tasks.

Interaction detail - summary, call analysis, sequence details and tasks

Enrolled Patients

All patients currently enrolled across sequences, with a Sequence Category chart by start date and a table of Patient, Category, Sequence Name, Service, Due Date, Start Date, Outcome, Sequence Status, Last/Next Step details, plus quick filters, saved views, CSV export and bulk actions (send message/email, update sequence result). Sequence status can only be manually updated to Stopped.

Enrolled Patients - chart, filters and sequence table

Queued Steps

Upcoming steps the agent is scheduled to perform: Next Step Date & Time, Patient, Sequence Type, Outcome so far, Mode (Call/Text) and Step Number, with bulk actions.

Queued Steps

Completed Steps

Steps already performed with their outcomes: a Step Outcome by Step Date chart plus a table showing Step Date and Time, Patient, Category, Sequence Name, Service, Due Date, Outcome, Sequence Result, Step Number, Attempted, Mode, Call Duration, Step Outcome and Remaining Steps.

Completed Steps - step outcomes and history

Patients Overview

One record per patient showing enrollment status across all four sequence types. Columns: Patient, Category, Sequence Name, Service, Due Date, Last Appointment, Last Completed Appt/Interval, Enrollment (Enrolled / Not Enrolled / Planned), Reason, Next Step, Next Step Mode, Sequence End Date and Next Eligible Date.

Patients Overview - one record per patient across sequence types

Preferences

All Getting Started sections above (service mapping, recall set up, schedules, flows, sequences, downtime, outreach settings, blocked numbers & patients).

Note: An Appointments Diagnostic page is planned: every appointment with the reason AI outreach did or did not occur, using a four-bucket status taxonomy (Reached Out, Queued, Not Reaching Out, Excluded), summary metrics, filter chips and a data table with reason and suggested fix.

Other Info - Sequence Status

If the sequence is ongoing this shows its current status; if it has ended, its final status.

  • Yet to Reach Out - sequence created, but no steps completed yet.

  • Reached Out - reached out via call or SMS, no response yet.

  • Call Back Later - patient asked to be called back later; a callback time is collected and the sequence restarts at that time.

  • Not Interested - for scheduling sequence types, the patient is not interested now. Sequence ends.

  • Scheduled - for scheduling sequence types, an appointment is scheduled. Sequence ends.

  • Confirmed - for the confirmation sequence type, the appointment is confirmed. Sequence ends.

  • Do Not Call - patient asked not to be contacted again. Moved to the DNC list and excluded from future sequences unless they opt back in or the practice moves them out.

  • Out of Service - outreach attempted, but the number is out of service. Sequence ends.

  • Stopped - practice manually stopped the sequence for a patient or turned the sequence off in Preferences.

  • Sequence Ended - all steps completed but the agent could not connect with the patient.

Note: Payment Collected exists as a status for the Payment Due sequence type and becomes relevant when that type ships.

Other Info - Step Outcome

  • Answered - an outreach call is answered.

  • No Answer - an outreach call is not answered and no voicemail is left.

  • Left Voicemail - an outreach call is not answered and the agent leaves a voicemail.

  • Sent - the agent sends an outbound SMS with no reply.

  • Replied - the agent sends an outbound SMS and the patient replies.

Other Info - Call Analysis Fields

Each completed outreach interaction carries six analysis data points, aligned with the AI FD taxonomy (no duplication with fields already shown on the interaction page):

Field Definition
Interaction Type The category of conversation. Outreach conversations are typed Recare (practice reaching out to book because of a missed appointment, due treatment, or a long gap since the last visit) or Confirmation, consistent with the AI FD Interaction Type list.
Outcome Booked / Not Booked for scheduling outreach; Resolved / Not Resolved for confirmation outreach; Cancelled where a rescheduling conversation ends in cancellation. (Expanded value set - renamed from Scheduling Status.)
Reason for Visit The service discussed, converted to the practice’s allowed service list (renamed from Service). Vertical-specific values per the AI FD master list (Dental/Ortho, Opto, Chiro).
Reason for Not Booking Captured when outcome is Not Booked or Cancelled. Includes Recare-specific values: Not Interested Right Now (declines without a specific callback time) and Call Back Later (explicitly names a time/day/period - vague statements do not qualify), alongside the standard values (price enquiry, slot not available, insurance not accepted, outstanding balance etc.).
Patient Type New or existing patient.
Revenue Potential $ / $$ / $$$ buckets mapped from Reason for Visit per vertical, per the AI FD master table.

Playbooks for AI Frontdesk (AI Front Desk)

AI FRONT DESK

Upgrade Sales Playbook

For Upgrade SDRs & Account Executives

January 2026

What is AI Front Desk?

AI Front Desk is your practice’s smartest receptionist, one who never takes a day off, never puts anyone on hold, and never misses a call. It’s an add-on module that works around the clock to handle the routine stuff: scheduling, rescheduling, cancellations, and answering those same questions your team gets asked a hundred times a week.

When a caller has something more complex: billing questions, clinical details, insurance specifics. The AI doesn’t try to wing it. During business hours, it does a warm handoff to your staff with a quick summary of the conversation. After hours? It creates a prioritized task so nothing falls through the cracks.

It plugs right into what customers already have: Phones, Online Scheduling, and their EHR. That means it pulls real-time availability, knows which insurances they accept, understands their services, and can even share directions all without anyone having to re-enter a single piece of data.

Why Practices Love It

Here’s what you’ll hear from practices once they’ve been using it:

● “We’re finally capturing those after-hours calls.” Every voicemail used to be a gamble, would they call back or just go somewhere else? Now those calls turn into booked appointments. ● “No more hold music.” Callers hate waiting. The AI picks up instantly, so they’re never left listening to elevator music wondering if anyone’s coming back.

● “It actually sounds like a person.” The voice is natural, not robotic. Patients often don’t even realize they’re talking to AI until we tell them.

● “My staff can breathe again.” Scheduling calls are repetitive. Freeing the front desk from those means they can focus on patients who are actually standing in front of them.

● “I can see exactly what’s happening.” Every call gets a transcript, a summary, and a sentiment score. The dashboard shows ROI in black and white, calls answered, appointments booked, new vs. existing patients.
Pricing (Keep This Simple)

$199 - $299/month while they’re with Adit (normally $349). prorated into their billing. It’s low-risk for them and easy to say yes to.

1. Before the Call

A little homework goes a long way. Before you pick up the phone, take five minutes to understand their situation.

Who’s a Good Fit?

You’re looking for existing Adit customers who have missed calls. Prioritize practices with:

● High call volume (check their Call Intelligence data)

● Frequent missed calls10 to 20+ per week is a red flag they need help

● Lots of after-hours voicemails piling up

● Staffing crunches during peak hours

If you can pull a specific number “I noticed 36 missed calls across your locations in the last 15 days” you’ve got their attention.

Getting Them on the Line

Try their cell first, then the office line. If they don’t answer, leave a voicemail that’s friendly and to the point: “Hey, this is [Your Name] from Adit about our scheduled AI Front Desk review. Give me a call back or shoot me a text if you’re having trouble joining, I’ll send you a text reminder too.” Then actually text them.

You don’t need to hit every point. Read the room and focus on what matters to them:

Pain Point What They Get How Adit Delivers
Missed Calls 100% answer rate, zero calls going to voicemail Routes overflow and after-hours calls automatically
After-Hours Revenue Books appointments 24/7, even at 2 AM Dashboard shows exactly how many appointments were booked outside hours
Hold Time Frustration Instant pickup, no busy signals Warm transfers include conversation summaries
Staff Burnout Front desk focuses on patients in the office Handles scheduling, confirmations, common questions
Message Errors Full transcripts and summaries, no more “I thought she said Tuesday” Syncs to EHR and creates follow-up tasks
Impersonal Feel Natural voice, customizable name, warm handoffs Summarizes the call before transferring to staff
Staffing Gaps Always on, vacations, sick days, lunch breaks covered Scales during busy periods automatically

2. Discovery: The Most Important Part

Start with empathy. If there are multiple people on the call, acknowledge everyone: “Glad you could join us Sarah, always good to have more perspectives.”

Then dig in with questions that get them talking about their pain:

● “On a scale of 1 to 10, how happy are you with how after-hours calls are handled right now? What happens to those calls after 5 PM?”

● “How many missed calls are you seeing in your VoIP logs each week? What do you think that’s costing you in new patients?”

● “When your front desk says ‘please hold,’ how often do callers just hang up?” ● “What repetitive tasks eat up your team’s time that could be spent on patient care?” ● “Have you ever lost a patient because the phone was busy or nobody picked up?” ● “If you could capture every call 24/7 without hiring another person, what would that mean for your practice?”

Playbooks for AI Frontdesk (continued, part 1)

● “What happens when your front desk is out sick or on vacation? How do you handle the call volume?”

● “How often does your team get the same questions over and over-insurance acceptance, directions, parking? How much time does that eat up?”

● “When a new patient calls and you’re already on another line, what’s your backup plan? Are you confident they’ll call back?”
Listen for the triggers: high missed call numbers, people hanging up on hold, voicemails that never get returned, staff feeling overwhelmed. When you hear it, connect the dots: “Based on what you’re telling me about those missed calls and voicemails, AI Front Desk would capture all of that. Let me show you exactly how.”

3. The Pitch: Tell a Story, Not a Feature List

Keep it tight 5 to 7 minutes max. Use the Problem, Solution, Proof framework:

“Here’s what we see all the time: practices losing potential patients because of missed calls, voicemails that pile up, or people who just hang up when they’re put on hold. Looking at your numbers, you had [X missed calls] recently, some with context, a lot without.

Our AI Front Desk fixes that. It answers every call instantly, 24/7, and handles scheduling, rescheduling, cancellations, and common questions using your EHR and Online Scheduling rules. No setup headaches, it pulls from what you already have.

You can customize everything: the voice, the name, scripts for how to handle insurance questions like ‘We don’t accept UnitedHealthcare, but here’s our cash pay option’ cancellation policies, text confirmations, all of it.

When something’s too complex, like a question about provider licensing or specialties, it either warm-transfers to your staf with a summary, or if it’s after hours, it creates a task so they can follow up first thing.

Every call gets transcribed with a summary and sentiment score. And the dashboard? It shows you exactly what’s happening: calls answered, appointments booked, new vs. existing patients, business hours vs. after hours.

Practices typically see 3-4x ROI monthly at $199/month.

Want to hear it in action? Let’s call the demo number right now.”

4. The Demo

The demo is everything. This isn’t like showing off other modules, you’re letting them experience something that feels almost human. The best approach: walk them through a structured flow, then hand them the number to try it themselves.

How the Agent Actually Works

Before you demo, understand the architecture so you can answer questions confidently. The agent operates entirely on Advanced Online Scheduling APIs. When a call comes in, it pulls real-time availability, insurance acceptance, services, provider info everything flows from what the practice already has configured. No duplicate data entry.
The call routing is flexible:

● After-hours only: Call goes to agent outside business hours, staff handles everything during the day

● Overflow: If the practice doesn’t answer within 20-30 seconds, call rolls to the agent, this catches those “almost missed” calls

● Full-time: Agent handles everything, warm transfers when needed

● Most practices start with after-hours + overflow. That means 90% of their after-hours calls, which are mostly new patients get handled automatically.

The Live Call Demo

Demo number: 832-590-3388 (confirm current number before your call)

Have the Client Call it and put it on speaker. Walk through this flow, it mirrors exactly what a new patient would experience:

1. Listen to the greeting. The agent introduces itself with a custom name (practices pick this) and the practice name. Notice how natural it sounds, we’ve tested dozens of voices and selected the four that perform best.

2. Say you’re a new patient wanting to schedule. The agent will ask for your first and last name, then ask you to spell them (just like a real receptionist would). Then it asks for the date of birth and confirms the phone number you’re calling from.

3. Go through insurance. If you say you have BlueCross, the agent checks the practice’s accepted insurances. If you say Medicaid and they don’t accept it, the agent will politely explain that, and if they have in-house financing or cash pay options configured, it’ll mention those.

4. Ask for an appointment. Give a preference like “Tuesday afternoon.” The agent pulls real-time availability from Online Scheduling and offers specific slots. If nothing works, it offers alternatives.

5. Confirm the booking. The agent confirms the details and if the practice has it enabled, mentions they’ll receive a text confirmation. The appointment gets written directly to the EHR. 6. Now throw a curveball. Ask something the agent won’t know: “What school did the doctor go to?” or “Is Dr. Smith board certified?” Watch what happens, the agent doesn’t make something up. It says it will have someone from the practice follow up, and creates a task. This is huge.

What to Show in the Module

Playbooks for AI Frontdesk (continued, part 2)

After the call, share your screen and walk through what just happened on the backend. This is where you prove the value isn’t just a cool phone call, it’s actionable data.

Home Page (Interactions Feed):

Each call shows a one-line summary of what happened. Click into the call you just made. They’ll see the full transcript, a 3-6 line summary the AI generated, sentiment categorization, and the
outcome (booked, created task, transferred, etc.). Point out how fast this processes, within 1-2 minutes of the call ending, everything is populated.

Tasks:

Show the task created from your curveball question. Each task includes the patient context, what they asked, and a link to the call recording. Tasks can be assigned round-robin across staff, to a specific person, or by task type (billing questions to one person, scheduling follow-ups to another). It’s like having an assistant who takes perfect notes.

Insights Dashboard:

Walk through the metrics: total calls handled, after-hours vs. business hours breakdown, scheduling calls booked vs. transferred vs. task-created, and reasons appointments weren’t booked. For practices worried about ROI, this page is gold. They can see exactly what the agent is doing for them.

Preferences (The Customization Page):

Show them how much control they have:

● Agent name and voice: They pick a name (Amy, Sarah, whatever fits their brand) and choose from four tested voices

● Custom greeting: They can script exactly how the agent introduces itself

● AI disclosure toggle: Some practices want to disclose it’s AI, some don’t. We give them the option (and note we don’t recommend disclosure, people hang up more when they know) ● Practice info: Parking, directions, anything patients commonly ask

● Payment options: Medicare, Medicaid, CareCredit, FSA, in-house financing, whatever they accept gets added to the agent’s knowledge

● Services: Which appointment types the agent can book (keep this focused, 3-5 services max for best performance)

● Cancellation/reschedule windows: If they require 48 hours notice, the agent enforces that ● Age restrictions: If they don’t see kids under 14, the agent will politely decline those bookings

What the Agent Won’t Do (And Why That’s Good)

Be ready to explain what’s intentionally limited:

● It doesn’t guess. If someone asks a question outside its knowledge base, it creates a task instead of making something up. No hallucinations, no liability.

● It filters sales calls. The agent recognizes solicitation calls and gatekeeps them, doesn’t transfer, just creates a “vendor” task if the practice wants to review later.

● Services are kept focused. We recommend 3-5 service types max. More services = more context for the AI to process = slower, less accurate responses. Keep it tight.

● Warm transfers respect business hours. If it’s after hours and someone asks for a human, the agent explains no one is available and offers to create a callback task.
Tie It Back to Their Practice

After the demo, connect what they just experienced to their specific pain points: “Remember those 36 missed calls we talked about? Every single one of those would have been answered, qualified, and either booked or turned into a follow-up task. How much revenue do you think that represents?”

5. Handling Objections

Objections are buying signals. Here’s how to handle the common ones:

They Say… You Say…
“It sounds too robotic.” “You just heard it, what did you think? It’s best-in-class voice with almost no latency. And when it transfers, your staff gets a full summary so it feels personal.”
“Setup sounds like a headache.” “It’s a guided one-hour session with our team. Most of the prompts are pre-loaded, you’re just reviewing and tweaking. We do the heavy lifting.”
“What if someone asks something complicated?” “You saw it in the demo, don’t guess. It either transfers with context or creates a task. Full transcripts for everything, so you’ve got an audit trail.”
“It’s another monthly cost.” “$199 a month. If it books just 3-4 appointments that would have gone to voicemail, it’s already paid for itself.”
“My patients will hate talking to a robot.” “That’s what everyone thinks until they hear it. Most patients don’t even realize it’s AI. And the ones who do? They just appreciate not being on hold.”

6. Closing

Don’t overthink this. If the demo went well, the close is natural.

The Ask

“Should we get you started? I can send the agreement links right now, one for each location if you’ve got multiple.”
Walk Them Through Signing

Stay on the call while they sign. Talk them through it: “Click the plus button, then Next, then just sign with your name. The billing starts prorated to your renewal date.”

Book Onboarding Immediately

Don’t let them leave without a date on the calendar: “Great, let’s get your onboarding scheduled. It’s about an hour and we’ll set everything up together. Does Tuesday at 9 AM Eastern work?” Send the calendar invite before you hang up.

If They Need to Think About It

Playbooks for AI Frontdesk (continued, part 3)

Send a follow-up email within the hour: quick recap of the switch factors that resonated, link to the demo recording if you have one, and a personalized ROI estimate based on their missed call numbers.

Remember: You’re Not Selling Software You’re solving a problem they deal with every single day. Missed calls mean missed revenue and stressed staff. AI Front Desk fixes both. Lead with that, show them it works, and getting to yes is the easy part.

Password OTP Troubleshooting (Account access)

Troubleshooting steps for users who say “I am not receiving my OTP”

1. Confirm with the user that the email inbox they are checking is the correct email associated with the User.
You can view their email by going to Settings -> Admin -> Users & Access -> Select User,

2. Have user search for “no-reply at adit.com“ in their email inbox to see if it shows anywhere.

3. Have user search for “OTP” in the inbox to see if it shows anywhere

4.Have user check “Spam”, “Junk”, and “All Mail” sections in their Email Inbox.

4. If they are still unable to find it, have the user click on “Forgot Password” and see if they get a reset pw link.

5. If they are still not getting anything, have the user reach out to the owner of their account and request them to change the email address on file. Here’s where the owner can do that
Go into Settings -> Admin -> Users & Access -> Select User -> Change Email

6. After changing the email, have user try signing in again, the OTP will trigger to the new email on file.

Troubleshooting steps for users who say “I don’t know my my email on file”

1. Go into Settings -> Admin -> Users & Access -> Select User,
Confirm what their username is, and check their email that’s associated with their username,

2. Make sure we verify their identity thoroughly before sharing their email information.
