How SMS Usage Is Calculated: A Mass Texting Reference Guide (Engage)

Mass texting is a communication tool that allows practices to reach a large number of patients instantly. However, SMS billing is not calculated solely based on the number of recipients. Charges are determined by SMS segments, which depend on message length, character type (GSM vs. Unicode), and formatting elements such as emojis or special symbols.

This training document explains how SMS units are calculated, why overages occur, and how to confidently interpret and communicate SMS charges to clients.

When a client sends a mass text (for example, to 3,538 recipients), they are not charged per person alone.

They are charged based on:

  • ✅ Number of recipients
  • ✅ Length of the message
  • ✅ Character encoding (GSM vs Unicode)
  • ✅ Special characters or emojis used

Each text sent may count as 1, 2, 3, or more SMS units per recipient.

Understanding SMS Character Limits

GSM Encoding (Standard Characters)

  • Limit: 160 characters per SMS
  • If message exceeds 160 characters:
    • It splits into multiple parts
    • Each part counts as 1 SMS unit

When split:

  • 161-306 characters = 2 units
  • 307-459 characters = 3 units
  • And so on

Unicode Encoding (Special Characters / Emojis)

If the message contains:

  • Emojis (🦷, 😊, etc.)
  • Curly quotes (“ ”)
  • Special symbols
  • Certain punctuation

Then it switches to Unicode encoding

  • Limit: 70 characters per SMS
  • Once over 70 characters, it splits faster
    • 71-134 characters = 2 units
    • 135-201 characters = 3 units

⚠️ Even a single emoji can reduce the character limit from 160 to 70.

Example: Lowell Dental Arts Case

Message Stats (from screenshot)

  • Total Characters: 290
  • GSM Characters: 287
  • Unicode Characters: 3 (due to emoji 🦷)
  • Total SMS per recipient: 5
  • Next part at: 45 characters

Why 5 Units?

Because:

  • Message length: 290 characters
  • Emoji present → Unicode encoding triggered
  • Unicode limit = 70 characters per SMS
  • 290 ÷ 70 ≈ 5 SMS units per recipient

So even though only 1 message was typed, it counted as 5 SMS segments per person.

Explaining the 7,131 Total SMS Units (5086 + 2045)

From invoices:

Billing Cycle SMS Units Charge
Dec 2025 2045 $20.45
Previous Period 5086 $50.86
Total 7131 $71.31

Now let’s connect this to the campaign: If:

  • 3,538 recipients received the message
  • Each message counted as multiple SMS segments

Example calculation:

If average SMS segments per recipient ≈ 2:

3,538 x 2 = 7,076 units

If ≈ 2.01 segments per recipient:

3,538 x 2.01 ≈ 7,113 units

The final billed amount (7,131 units) reflects:

  • Message segmentation
  • Possibly multiple campaigns
  • Replies or system messages
  • Different billing cycle splits (Nov 5-Dec 4, etc.)

This is why total SMS units are higher than total contacts.

Cost Breakdown

SMS overage is billed at:

$0.01 per SMS unit

So:

  • 2045 units = $20.45
  • 5086 units = $50.86
  • Matches invoice totals exactly.

Quick Formula for Estimating Cost

Step 1:

Check SMS segments per message

Step 2:

Multiply by number of recipients

SMS Units = Recipients × Segments Per Message

Step 3:

Multiply by $0.01

Total Cost = SMS Units × $0.01

Client-Facing FAQ Why Is My SMS Usage Higher Than My Contact List?

❓ I sent a message to 3,538 patients. Why was I charged for 7,131 SMS?

Great question!

SMS charges are based on message length, not just how many people receive it.

How It Works

  • Standard text allows 160 characters per message
  • If your message is longer, it splits into multiple parts
  • Each part counts as 1 SMS

If you use:

  • Emojis
  • Special symbols
  • Smart punctuation

The limit drops to 70 characters per message

That means your message may count as 2-5 SMS per person.

How Charges Are Calculated

Number of Recipients × SMS Segments = Total SMS Units

Each unit = $0.01

Example:

  • 7,131 units = $71.31

How to Reduce SMS Costs

  • Keep messages under 160 characters
  • Avoid emojis
  • Avoid special symbols
  • Use shorter reminders

SMS Status - Troubleshooting Guide (Engage)

SMS Status - Troubleshooting Guide

Overview

We have now launched the SMS Status feature in AditApp for Admin users.

With this update, Adit pulls the message status from the carrier and replicates the same status in Adit.

Status Mapping

  • Carrier → Delivered → Adit shows Delivered
  • Carrier → Failed → Adit shows Failed
  • Carrier → Sent → Adit shows Sent

Going forward, please follow the troubleshooting approach below when investigating SMS-related issues.

🔍 When Should a Ticket Be Raised to T3/Engineering?

Please only raise to T3/Engineering when there is a status mismatch between Adit and the carrier.

Examples

  • Carrier shows Delivered, but Adit shows Sent/Queued
  • Carrier shows Failed, but Adit shows Sent/Queued
  • Any other case where the status in Adit does not match the carrier

This approach will help Engineering focus on cases where there could potentially be an issue with our implementation or status synchronization.

📌 Carrier-Side Failures

If the Adit status matches the carrier status, please treat the issue as a carrier-side issue and reach out to the respective carrier for the failure reason.

Even if the error code displayed in Adit is unclear, please check with the carrier for the actual reason for the failure.

Adit Error Code Reference

Adit SMS Error Codes:
SMS Failure Code

Default Message for outside provided Error code : Comment by Kristy Do on Failed Reason from Telnyx & Plivo

Carrier References

  • Plivo Messaging Error Codes:
    https://www.plivo.com/docs/messaging/troubleshooting/error-codes
  • Telnyx Messaging Error Codes:
    https://support.telnyx.com/en/articles/6505121-telnyx-messaging-error-codes

⚠️ Adit Shows Failed, but There Is No Corresponding Carrier Log

There may be cases where the carrier does not show a corresponding message in its logs, while Adit shows the message as Failed.

In such cases, the carrier may have rejected the message at the time of sending, before it was fully processed or logged on their side.

When contacting the carrier, please provide the following information:

  • From number
  • To number
  • Approximate timeframe of the message
  • Relevant Adit message/error details

Providing these details will help the carrier investigate and identify the actual reason for the rejection.

🎯 Goal

By following this approach, we can clearly separate carrier-side issues from potential Adit-side issues, reduce unnecessary Engineering escalations, and ultimately reduce client turnaround time.

Quick Reference

Adit status = Carrier status
→ Investigate with the Carrier

Adit status ≠ Carrier status
→ Raise to T3/Engineering

Timezones

  • Adit app always shows the time of Location’s timezone
  • Telnyx Always shows the your local system’s timezone,
  • Telnyx webhook JSON shows timing in UTC format.
  • Plivo Console logs use the timezone configured for your Plivo dashboard/account. Which is US/Central.

Adit KB FAQ's 28 May 26 V1 (FAQ)

1. Adit Pay & Payment Terminals

1.1 Card Terminals - Supported Device

Adit currently provides one card reader model: the Stripe Reader S700. This is the only terminal available for purchase through Adit.

  • Terminal model: Stripe Reader S700

  • Dock station is available separately (sold as an optional add-on)

  • The S700 connects via Wi-Fi and processes in-person card payments through Adit Pay

Q: Which terminal model does Adit provide?

A: Adit provides the Stripe Reader S700. This is the only model currently available. If you need to purchase a terminal, contact your Adit account representative.

Q: My terminal is not turning on - what should I try?

A: First, confirm you are using the original power adapter. Unplug the power cable for 30 seconds, then reconnect. If the terminal still does not power on, contact Adit Support with your terminal model (S700) and a description of the issue.

1.2 Processing Fees - Adit Pay (Stripe)

Adit Pay uses Stripe’s blended pricing model. This means one rate applies to all card types - there are no separate tiers for different card types.

  • Card-present (terminal): 2.25% + $0.20 per transaction

  • Card-not-present (manual entry or Text-to-Pay): 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

Unlike some payment processors that divide transactions into qualified, mid-qualified, and non-qualified tiers, Adit Pay’s blended rate covers all card types under a single rate. There are no unexpected surcharges applied to specific card types.

1.3 How to Refund a Payment

The Refund button for a transaction is only available on the transaction’s details page. It is not visible from the main transactions list.

  1. Navigate to Adit Pay → Transactions.

  2. Search for the transaction by patient name, date, or amount.

  3. Click on the transaction row to open its details page. The Refund button is only available here.

  4. Click Refund, enter the refund amount (partial or full), and confirm.

  5. The transaction will update to show the refund has been processed.

2. Voice & Call Tracking

2.1 Accessing Voicemails

Voicemails in Adit can be accessed in two ways:

  • Through the Call Tracking / Call Intelligence module - navigate there from the Adit dashboard to view and listen to voicemails

  • Through the Call Pop - when an incoming call triggers a Call Pop notification, you can access a voicemail left by the caller directly from there

Q: Where do I find voicemails left by patients?

A: Go to Call Tracking / Call Intelligence from the Adit dashboard. From there you can view and listen to voicemail messages. You can also access voicemails through the Call Pop that appears when a call comes in.

2.2 Setting Up Voicemail Boxes

Voicemail boxes are configured in the Phone System section of Adit.

  1. Navigate to Phone System.

  2. Expand or select your Location.

  3. Click on Voicemail Boxes.

  4. From here you can add, edit, and configure voicemail boxes for that location.

Note: The Phone System section was previously named ‘Number List’ in older versions of Adit. If you see any documentation referring to ‘Number List’, this refers to the same area now called Phone System.

2.3 Call Override

Call Override allows you to temporarily redirect all incoming calls to a specified destination - for example, an after-hours number or a specific staff member’s phone.

How to enable Call Override:

  1. Go to Settings > Voice > Call Override.

  2. Select your Location from the top left of the page.

  3. Toggle Call Override to ON.

  4. Configure the destination where calls should be directed and how they are handled.

How to disable Call Override:

Return to Settings > Voice > Call Override → your Location and toggle Call Override to OFF.

Q: Can I set Call Override to turn off automatically at a specific time?

A: No - Call Override can only be turned on and off manually. There is no option to set an end time or schedule an automatic shutoff. Whoever enables Call Override must remember to return and toggle it off manually when it is no longer needed.

2.4 Missed Call Text

Missed Call Text is a feature that automatically sends a text message to a caller when their call to the practice goes unanswered. It is configured in the Engage module.

  1. Navigate to the Engage module from the Adit dashboard.

  2. Select sub-section “Auto-Reminders > Missed Call Text” within Engage.

  3. You can configure separate messages for missed calls during business hours and outside business hours.

  4. Save your settings and ensure that the reminder that was configured is enabled.

Q: Where is Missed Call Text configured?

A: Missed Call Text is configured within the Engage module.
Navigate to Engage > Auto-Reminders and look for the “Missed Call Text” section to set up your messages for within and outside business hours.

3. Engage - Messaging & Patient Communication

3.1 Canned Messages

Canned messages are pre-written text templates that staff can quickly insert when composing a message to a patient in Engage.

Q: Can canned messages be used for email?

A: No - canned messages are limited to be used in SMS (text messages) only within Engage. They cannot be used in email campaigns or email reminder templates.

3.2 Patient Segments

Segments in Adit are dynamic patient groups built from filter criteria. Adit uses segments to target specific groups of patients for mass texts and email campaigns.

How segments work:

Segments are created by setting one or more filters. When the segment is used, Adit automatically finds all patients who match the filter criteria at that time.
Filters include:

  • Last Appointment

  • Next Appointment

  • Patient status (Active, Inactive or Both)

  • Location

  • Age

  • Recall Due Date

  • Balance Amount

  • Remaining Benefits

  • Primary Provider

  • Secondary Provider

Q: Can I manually add specific patients to a segment?

A: No - segments in Adit are filter-based only. You cannot add individual patients to a segment by name, and you cannot import a list of patient names via CSV into a segment. Segments automatically populate based on the filters you set.

Q: Can I create a segment and add 60 specific patients by hand?

A: No - manual addition of specific patients to a segment is not supported. Segments work by applying filter criteria (such as last Appointment Date, Patient Status or Recall Due Date), and Adit automatically determines which patients qualify. To message a specific patient list, you would need to set filters that match those patients as a group.

3.3 Mass Texting - Shared Phone Numbers

Q: If three patients share the same phone number, will a mass text go to that number three times?

A: Yes - mass texts are sent per patient profile, not per phone number. If three patient profiles share the same phone number, three separate messages will be sent to that number. The platform does not automatically detect or consolidate duplicate phone numbers. If your practice has family accounts where multiple family members share one phone number, each person will receive their own message from the campaign.

3.4 Email Campaigns - CSV Import Requirements

When importing a “Mailing list” of patients for an email campaign using a CSV file, the file must follow strict formatting requirements.

CSV file requirements:

Your CSV file must contain exactly three columns with these exact header names:

  • First name

  • Last name

  • Email

Adding any other column - such as phone number, date of birth, location, or any other field - will cause the CSV import to fail. The file will be rejected entirely.

Q: Why is my CSV not importing for an email campaign?

A: Check that your CSV file contains only three columns: First name, Last name, and Email. Any additional columns or different header names will cause the import to fail. Remove all extra columns, save the file, and try importing again.

3.5 Messaging Attachment Limits

Adit Engage has two separate attachment limits depending on the type of message:

  • General Engage messages (SMS and in-app messages): 650 KB maximum file size and only .jpeg and .png formats are accepted.

  • Text-to-Pay payment request PDF attachments: 8 MB maximum file size

Q: What is the file size limit for attachments in Engage messages?

A: For general Engage messages, the attachment limit is 650 KB. For Text-to-Pay payment request PDFs, the limit is 8 MB. These are two separate limits - the 8 MB limit applies only to Text-to-Pay, not to regular messaging.

3.6 Creating a Follow-Up Task on a Message

You can create a follow-up task directly from a patient’s message thread in Engage. The option is accessed through the downward-facing arrow icon, not a labelled button.

  1. Open the patient’s Engage message thread.

  2. Find the specific message you want to follow up on.

  3. Click the downward-facing arrow icon at the top right of that message.

  4. This reveals the task and follow-up creation options.

  5. Fill in the follow-up task details and save.

3.7 Viewing Sent Email Reminders

Q: Can I view the exact email that was sent to a patient as their appointment reminder?

A: You can see a record that an email reminder was sent - the log shows the date, time, and type of communication (for example, appointment reminder or recall). However, you cannot view or preview the actual email content within Adit. The body of the email that was sent to the patient is not stored or displayed in the platform. To see the exact email, you would need to check from the patient’s own email inbox.

3.8 Schedule Confirmations for Same-Day Appointments

If a patient has two appointments on the same calendar day, the following rule applies for schedule confirmations (SC):

  • Both schedule confirmations are sent to the patient.

  • When the first appointment is booked, a schedule confirmation is generated for that appointment.

  • If a second appointment is booked on the same day at any other time than the first appointment, a new schedule confirmation is sent for the second appointment as well.

Example: An appointment was booked at 2:00 PM(schedule confirmation sent). The patient then books a 9:00 AM appointment on the same day. Scheduled confirmation for this will also be sent out as

Q: Will a patient with two appointments on the same day receive two schedule confirmations?

A: Yes - Schedule Confirmation is sent per appointment booked or rescheduled. If two appointments are booked on the same day, both Schedule Confirmations would go out as soon as the appointments are booked.

3.9 Spanish Language Support

Adit supports Spanish for appointment reminders (text messages and emails) when the patient’s Preferred Language is set to Spanish in the EHR.

Q: Can patients receive their intake forms or patient forms in Spanish?

A: No - Spanish-language patient forms are not currently available in Adit. Spanish is supported for appointment reminders only (text and email). Forms (intake forms, medical history, consents, etc.) are only available in English at this time.

Q: Can appointment reminders be sent in Spanish?

A: Yes - if a patient’s Preferred Language is set to Spanish in their profile, Adit will send their appointment reminders in Spanish.

4. EHR Integration

4.1 How EHR Sync Works - On-Premise vs. Cloud

Adit integrates with two types of EHR/PMS systems:

Cloud-based EHR (e.g., Dentrix Ascend, Revolution):

Cloud EHRs sync directly over the internet. Adit connects to Cloud systems using the Adit Chrome extension, which acts as a bridge between the Cloud EHR and the Adit platform.

On-premise EHR (e.g., Eaglesoft, Dolphin, Dentrix):

On-premise EHR systems are installed on a local server at your practice and are not hosted in the cloud. Adit connects to on-premise systems, which acts as a bridge between the EHR and the Adit platform. The Adit Pozative software must be running on the server that has access to the EHR for the sync to function.

4.2 On-Premise EHR Sync Frequency

Q: How often does Adit sync with an on-premise EHR?

A: For on-premise EHR integrations, appointments sync between the EHR and Adit every 5 minutes. This means a new appointment booked in your EHR will appear in Adit within 5 minutes of being entered.

Q: A new appointment was just booked. Why isn’t it showing in Adit yet?

A: For on-premise EHR systems, sync occurs every 5 minutes. If the appointment was just booked, it may take up to 5 minutes to appear in Adit. If it has not appeared after 10 minutes, confirm that the Adit-EHR connection is working by checking the “Last Sync On” section in Settings > EHR > Connection Status.

4.3 Dolphin EHR - Specific Notes

Dolphin is an on-premise dental practice management system used by many orthodontic practices. When using Dolphin with Adit, please note the following:

  • Dolphin is an on-premise EHR/PMS system.

  • For orthodontic practices using Dolphin: Adit can only pull one mobile phone number per patient from Dolphin. If a patient has multiple phone numbers on file in Dolphin, only one will sync to Adit. Ensure the correct mobile number is the primary number in Dolphin to make sure appointment reminders reach the right number.

4.4 AI Front Desk - What It Knows and Does Not Know

The Adit AI Front Desk handles incoming calls and texts on behalf of your practice. It answers questions, books appointments, and manages routine patient communication. It is important to understand the scope of what the AI Front Desk has access to.

What the AI Front Desk knows:

  • Scheduled future appointments that exist in your EHR and have synced to Adit

  • Your practice details configured during setup (name, address, business hours, accepted insurance, services offered, providers, booking rules)

  • Standard booking, rescheduling, and cancellation workflows

What the AI Front Desk does NOT know:

  • Treatment plans in progress (e.g., whether a patient is mid-way through a root canal or orthodontic treatment)

  • Clinical history, diagnoses, or clinical notes

  • Past appointment records or historical patient clinical data

  • Any information not tied to a scheduled future appointment in the EHR

Q: Will the AI know that my patient has an ongoing root canal and can answer their questions about it?

A: No - the AI Front Desk only knows about scheduled future appointments. It does not have access to treatment plans, clinical history, or any clinical data not associated with an upcoming appointment on the calendar. If a patient calls with questions about a treatment in progress, the AI will not be able to address those clinical specifics and the call will be handled according to your configured escalation settings.

5. Admin & Settings

5.1 Changing Your Practice Address

The practice address is managed under the General settings section, for each of the Locations section.

  1. Click the Settings (gear) icon and ensure the correct location is selected on the top left of the page.

  2. Navigate to General.

  3. Click on Logo & Address (this may also appear as Address & Logo).

  4. Update your address fields and save.

To update the address for the Organization, navigate to Settings > Organization > Edit Organization and update the address here. This is not for location level address information.

Q: Where do I go to update the practice’s physical address?

A: Go to Settings → General → Logo & Address. Update the address fields there and save. Note: the Admin Panel → Locations section is for managing location-level settings and is not where address changes are made.

5.2 Changing Your Practice Logo

Uploading a new logo requires one additional step that is easy to miss: you must click ‘Edit Organization’ before the upload option becomes visible.

  1. Click the Settings (gear) icon.

  2. Navigate to Admin → Organization.

  3. Click Edit Organization. (The upload option does not appear until this step is completed.)

  4. The Upload Logo / Choose File option will now be visible. Click on it to select and upload your new logo.

  5. Save changes.

Q: I went to Admin → Organization but I cannot see the option to upload a logo. Where is it?

A: You need to click ‘Edit Organization’ first. After clicking Edit Organization, the Upload Logo / Choose File option will appear. This step is required before the upload option becomes visible.

5.3 Managing User Access & Permissions

User roles and application access:

User roles and application (module) access are managed in Admin → Users & Access. From there you can add new users, assign roles, and control which applications each user can access.

Location-specific module access:

Q: Can I give a user access to a module on one location but not another?

A: No - application access in Adit applies across all locations. If a user is given access to a module, they will have access to that module on all locations they are assigned to. It is not currently possible to grant access to a module on one location while restricting it on another. This capability is planned for a future release.

5.4 Enabling and Disabling Applications (Modules)

To see which applications are enabled or disabled, and to turn them on or off:

  1. Go to Settings → Admin → Applications.

  2. You will see a list of all available modules with their current enabled/disabled status.

  3. Use the toggle next to each application to enable or disable it.

  4. To manage which users can access a specific application, navigate to Users & Access → Application Access.

5.5 Audit Logs

The Audit Log records actions taken in Adit - who made a change, what type of action was performed, and when it occurred. You can filter the log by date range and by user.

Q: Can I see what a setting was before and after a change was made?

A: No - the Audit Log shows that a change occurred (the user, the action type, and the timestamp) but does not display the specific before-and-after values for any change. Detailed before/after tracking is not currently available in the Audit Log.

5.6 Billing & Subscription

The Billing page in Adit shows payment method and transaction history information. To review your current subscription plan or renewal date, please contact your Adit account representative or the Adit billing team - this information is managed by Adit and is not displayed in the self-service billing page.

Q: Where can I see my current subscription plan and next renewal date?

A: Your subscription plan and renewal date are not displayed on the Adit billing page. To get this information, contact your Adit account representative or the billing team directly.

5.7 Logging Staff Out of the Mobile App

Q: Is there a way to log all staff out of the Adit mobile app remotely?

A: No - Adit does not support remote or bulk logout of staff from the mobile app. Individual users can end their own active sessions by going to My Profile → Password → Terminate all active sessions, but this is a self-service action that each user performs for their own account. An administrator cannot force-logout another user from the mobile app. To immediately remove a user’s access, the user’s account can be disabled in Admin → Users & Access.

5.8 Returning to the Previous Adit Layout

Q: Can we go back to the previous version of the Adit interface?

A: No - the current Adit interface is the only available version and cannot be reverted. Some modules include legacy reporting views within them (for example, Call Tracking includes Legacy Insights for older-style reports), but the overall platform layout and navigation cannot be changed back to a previous version.

6. Voice

The area in Adit where you manage phone numbers, call flows, voicemail boxes, and related voice settings is called Voice (Settings > Voice). In older versions of Adit, this section was called ‘Number List’. If you see any Adit documentation that still uses the term ‘Number List’, this refers to the same section now called Voice.

Q: Where is ‘Number List’ in Adit? I cannot find it.

A: ‘Number List’ is the old name for what is now called ‘Voice’. Navigate to Settings > Voice to find all phone number management, call flow, voicemail box, and eFax settings. The section was renamed and ‘Number List’ no longer exists as a separate area.

6.1 What Is in Phone System?

The Phone System is a sub section within Settings > Voice that contains:

  • Your Adit phone numbers by location

  • Call flows - how incoming calls are routed

  • Voicemail boxes

  • eFax numbers

Adit Knowledge Base · For customer use

Adit KB FAQ's PA - Engage 29 May 2026 V1 (FAQ)

Q: I want production goals to be calculated based on provider hours, but after updating hours the monthly goal didn’t change. Why is this happening?

A: Adit does not automatically recalculate production goals when provider hours are updated. Provider hours are used for reporting (like utilization and production per hour), but the actual monthly production goals are set separately in Preferences → Set Goals. Because of this separation, changing hours won’t update your goals automatically-you need to either update the goals manually or set them using a production-per-hour or similar target so they scale with scheduled hours going forward.

Q: In Practice Analytics, how do I create a patient list of patients with scheduled future appointments within a certain date range that only includes hygiene appointments and excludes doctor-side appointments?

A: Create a patient list in Practice Analytics → Patient Lists → New Patient List. Then add the following filters:

  • Date filter: Scheduled Appointment Date → set your future date range (start and end dates)
  • Appointment Type filter: Appointment Type = Hygiene (or select hygiene/prophy appointment types only)
  • Provider filter (to exclude doctors): Provider Role = Hygienist or Provider ≠ Dentist/Doctor

Run the list to confirm it only shows patients with future hygiene appointments, then save the Patient List for reuse or export if needed.

Q: Morning huddle shows unscheduled treatment. Where can I find the list of those patients?

A: Open Practice Analytics → Morning Huddle. The patient-level list (List View or Quick View on the Adit dashboard) shows today’s patients along with scheduled and unscheduled treatment amounts. You can sort or filter the Unscheduled Treatment column and click on a patient’s name to open their patient card.

For a quick snapshot, you can also use the Morning Huddle Quick View on the Adit landing page. For more follow-up tracking, use Analytics → Follow Ups, where you can view and manage unscheduled-treatment follow-ups.

Q: Need to add custom treatment codes in Practice Analytics. How do I add treatment codes?

A: Custom treatment codes cannot be created directly inside Practice Analytics. Adit pulls treatment/procedure codes from your connected EHR/PMS system. To add a new code, you must first create it in your EHR/PMS and allow it to sync into Adit. Once synced, the code will become available in Practice Analytics for reporting, filters, patient lists, and goal tracking. If the code does not appear after syncing, contact Adit Support for assistance with code mapping or synchronization.

Q: Why is scheduled production wrong?

A: Scheduled production may appear incorrect due to configuration, provider mapping, or EHR data issues. Common causes include:

  • Incorrect or missing Team Settings (provider roles or operatory assignments)
  • Provider Hours not configured correctly
  • Missing or outdated Provider Goals in Preferences → Set Goals
  • Incorrect appointment, procedure, or operatory data in the EHR
  • Appointments that were moved, cancelled, or left uncoded
  • Sync delays (Analytics updates approximately every 5 minutes)

It’s also important to note that Adit scheduled production is associated with the treatment plan and provider assignment in your EHR. If production is attached to the wrong provider in the EHR, it may display under the wrong provider in Adit as well.

Quick checklist:

  • Verify Team Settings and operatory assignments
  • Confirm Provider Hours templates and split blocks
  • Update Provider Goals in Preferences → Set Goals
  • Check appointment procedure codes, provider, and operatory assignments in the EHR
  • Wait for the next sync cycle and refresh the report/views

Q: Can I track hygiene reappointment?

A: Yes, Adit tracks hygiene reappointments through Practice Analytics → Reports → Reappointment. This report specifically tracks whether patients have a future appointment tied to a hygiene treatment code, making it the most direct way to monitor hygiene reappointment rates.

You can also use:

  • Patients → Recall or Patient Lists to filter patients by recall status, due date, or last hygiene visit
  • Morning Huddle to monitor upcoming hygiene appointments and unscheduled patients
  • Automated reminders and follow-up workflows to improve hygiene reappointment conversion rates

Q: Do users receive email notifications when a task is assigned or created, and is there a setting to enable this?

A: No, Adit does not currently send email notifications for task assignments or task creation. There is also no settings option to enable or disable email alerts for tasks.

Q: Can I highlight messages that I need to go back to?

A: Yes - you can use Tags in Engage to highlight and organize messages that need follow-up. Tags allow you to assign custom labels and colors to message threads so they are easier to find later.

To use Tags:

Adit KB FAQ's PA - Engage 29 May 2026 V1 (continued, part 1)

  • Go to Engage → Tags → Manage to create or edit tags
  • Open a message thread and use the Add Tag option to apply a tag
  • Tagged conversations can later be viewed and filtered from the Tags section

This helps track conversations that require follow-up, internal ownership, or special attention

Q: Can I find older messages that I need to address?

A: Yes. Use Engage → Messages to find and surface older conversations that still need attention:

  • Use the Search bar to find conversations by patient name, phone number, or keywords
  • Toggle the Unread filter or use Quick Filters to show only unread or specific message types
  • Use the Filter icon to refine views (for example, hide automated texts or show only internal messages)
  • Mark conversations as Unread or use Mentions (@) to flag messages you need to return to later

Q: Can I highlight messages that I need to go back to?

A: Yes - you can flag messages to return to later in Engage.

  • Mark a conversation as Unread from the conversation menu to keep it in your Unread list
  • Use Mentions (@) to surface messages where you’re tagged
  • Toggle the Unread filter or use Quick Filters on the Messages sidebar to show only items needing attention
  • Use the Filter icon to hide automated texts and narrow results to manual SMS or internal messages

Q: Can I listen to call recordings from the Adit mobile app?

A: No, call recordings are not currently available in the Adit mobile app. Call recordings can only be accessed through the Adit web app or desktop app.

Q: What should I know about accessing Phone System in Adit?

A: Phone System in the new admin panel, you can go to the Settings page → Phone System. If a location is already selected, you will be taken directly into the Phone System settings for that location without needing to reselect it.

The location selection screen will only appear when “All Locations” is selected, in which case you will be prompted to choose a specific location before proceeding.

Q: Can I upload a profile picture or logo to my Adit account?

A: Yes, you can now personalize your Adit account with a profile picture or office logo.

To update your profile picture:

  • Click your profile icon in the top-right corner
  • Select My Profile from the dropdown
  • Click Upload New Photo
  • Choose your image and click Save

Supported formats:

  • .jpg
  • .png

Recommended image size:

  • Larger than 300px by 300px for best quality

You can also remove or replace your profile photo anytime from the My Profile page.

Q58. What does “Official Integration” mean?

A: Official Integration means the EHR vendor formally supports or approves the ADIT integration.

Q59. What does “On Prem” mean?

A: On Prem means the EHR system is hosted locally on the client’s server.

Q60. What does “Cloud” mean?

A: Cloud means the EHR system is hosted online and accessed through the internet.

  • API availability

  • Cloud vs server deployment

  • Integration type (official vs legacy)

  • Cloud EHRs → full real-time feature support

  • Legacy server EHRs → partial dashboards and limited write-back

  • Older versions → reduced analytics and scheduling capabilities

Chiropractic PMS Compatibility - Adit Integration Overview

Q: Which Chiropractic PMS platforms does Adit support?

A: Adit supports the following Chiropractic PMS platforms:

  • ChiroTouch (On-Prem)
  • Jane (Cloud)
  • ChiroTouch (Cloud)

All platforms support core features like Engage, Online Scheduling, Patient Forms, and Payments, but Practice Analytics capabilities vary by system.

Q: Are all features available in every PMS system?

A: No. Feature availability depends on the PMS:

  • Some platforms support full scheduling and communication tools
  • Analytics and dashboards may be limited or not yet available in certain systems
  • Payment write-back and advanced reporting can also vary by PMS

Q: What Practice Analytics features are supported?

ChiroTouch (On-Prem)

A: Supports:

  • Morning Huddle
  • Schedule view
  • Practice Performance
  • Growth & Collections
  • Reports
  • Patient Lists & Patient Card
  • Automated Recall Report

Not fully supported:

  • Advanced dashboards (visual analytics)
  • Provider / Hygiene / Operatory performance breakdowns
  • Practice Health Score
  • Follow-ups analytics

Jane (Cloud) & ChiroTouch (Cloud)

A: Currently:

  • Practice Analytics dashboards are not available
  • Performance, growth, and recall analytics are not active yet

Q: Can Adit show Treatment Plans in Chiropractic PMS systems?

A: No. Treatment Plans and Treatment Plan PDF attachments are not supported in ChiroTouch (On-Prem), Jane, or ChiroTouch (Cloud).

Q: Does Adit support Online Scheduling with Chiropractic PMS systems?

A: Yes. All supported platforms include:

  • Real-time availability
  • Appointment creation inside PMS
  • Operatory hour syncing
  • Provider hour syncing

Online Scheduling is one of the strongest supported features across all Chiropractic systems.

Q: What Engage features are available?

A: All platforms support:

  • Appointment reminders
  • Auto-confirmations
  • Birthday messages
  • Recall reminders
  • ASAP lists
  • Schedule tracking inside Engage

Note:

  • Scheduled confirmations are only available in ChiroTouch (On-Prem)

Q: Does Adit support Patient Forms integration?

A: Yes, partially across all platforms.

Supported:

  • Import completed forms
  • PDF attachment to PMS
  • General patient fields
  • Insurance fields

Not supported:

  • Medical history fields
  • Allergies
  • Medical problems
  • Medications

Q: Can Adit read and write patient notes in Chiropractic PMS systems?

A: Yes. All platforms support:

  • Writing patient notes/logs into the PMS
  • Reading patient notes/logs back into Adit

Q: How does Adit Pay work with these systems?

ChiroTouch (On-Prem)

  • Payments written to communication logs: Yes
  • Ledger posting: Yes
  • Refunds: No
  • Discounts: No

Jane

  • Ledger posting: Yes
  • Refunds: Yes
  • Discounts: No
  • Communication logs: No

ChiroTouch (Cloud)

  • Ledger posting: Yes
  • Refunds: Yes
  • Discounts: Yes
  • Communication logs: No

Q: Does Adit support insurance verification (RCM) back into PMS?

A: No. Across all Chiropractic PMS systems:

  • Insurance verification PDFs cannot be pushed back into the PMS
  • RCM is used as an external workflow tool only

Q: What is the overall capability by system?

A:

  • ChiroTouch (On-Prem): Strong scheduling + partial analytics
  • Jane: Strong Engage & Payments, analytics still in roadmap
  • ChiroTouch (Cloud): Strong Engage & Payments, limited analytics today

Orthodontic PMS Compatibility - Adit Integration Overview (Q&A)

Q: Which Orthodontic PMS systems does Adit support?

A: Adit supports the following Orthodontic PMS platforms:

  • Orthotrac
  • Dolphin
  • Cloud 9

All three support core workflows like Engage, Patient Forms, Payments, and Insurance Verification, but advanced features like Practice Analytics and full Scheduling are limited.

Q: Do all Orthodontic PMS systems support full Adit features?

A: No. Feature availability varies significantly by PMS.

  • Core engagement and communication tools are supported across all systems
  • Practice Analytics dashboards are not supported
  • Online Scheduling is limited or partially supported depending on the system
  • Cloud 9 has the most functional limitations

Q: Are Practice Analytics available in Orthodontic PMS integrations?

A: No. Practice Analytics is not supported across Orthotrac, Dolphin, or Cloud 9.

This includes:

  • Morning Huddle
  • Schedule dashboards
  • Provider / hygiene / practice performance
  • Operatory utilization
  • Practice Health Score
  • Growth and collections dashboards
  • Reports and follow-ups
  • Treatment-code based analytics

Note:

  • Patient Lists are available in Orthotrac and Dolphin only
  • Cloud 9 does not support Patient Lists

Q: Can Adit attach treatment codes or use treatment plans in Orthodontic PMS systems?

A: No. The following are not supported across all three platforms:

  • Attaching treatment codes to appointments
  • Pulling treatment codes from appointments
  • Automated recall reports
  • Treatment plan PDFs

Q: Does Adit support auto-assigned forms in Orthodontic PMS systems?

A: Yes, partially.

Auto-assigned forms (without treatment codes) are supported in:

  • Orthotrac
  • Dolphin

Cloud 9 does not support this capability.

Q: Does Adit support Online Scheduling for Orthodontic PMS systems?

A: Limited support only.

Not supported:

  • Real-time availability
  • Writing appointments directly into the PMS

Supported:

  • Pulling operatory hours (all systems)
  • Pulling provider hours (Orthotrac only)

Online Scheduling should be positioned as limited sync, not full automation.

Q: What Engage features are supported?

A: All Orthodontic PMS systems support:

  • Appointment reminders (including family reminders)
  • Auto-confirmations
  • Birthday messages
  • ASAP lists
  • Schedule tracking inside Engage

Partial support:

  • Scheduled confirmations (available in Orthotrac and Dolphin only)
  • Recall reminders (not supported in Orthotrac, supported in Dolphin and Cloud 9)

Q: What Patient Profile features are supported?

A: Support varies by PMS.

Fully supported across most systems:

  • Active/inactive patient status
  • Preferred language

Partial support breakdown:

Feature Orthotrac Dolphin Cloud 9
New / Existing status Yes Yes No
Profile picture Yes Yes No
Patient notes Yes Yes No

Q: Does Adit support Patient Forms in Orthodontic PMS systems?

A: Yes. All systems support:

  • Importing completed forms
  • PDF attachment to PMS
  • General patient fields
  • Insurance fields

Partial support:

  • Medical history forms (Orthotrac & Dolphin only)

Not supported:

  • Allergies
  • Medical problems
  • Medications

Q: Where are patient form PDFs stored in each PMS?

A:

  • Orthotrac: OrthoTrac image folder → patient document/charting area
  • Cloud 9: Document Cabinet → Patient Document Listing
  • Dolphin: Patients → Documents

Q: Can Adit write or read patient notes in Orthodontic PMS systems?

A:

Capability Orthotrac Dolphin Cloud 9
Write notes to PMS Yes Yes No
Read notes from PMS Yes Yes No

Q: How does Adit Pay work with Orthodontic PMS systems?

A:

Orthotrac & Dolphin (Fully supported)

  • Payments written to ledger
  • Refunds supported
  • Discounts supported
  • CareCredit supported
  • Payment communication logs supported

Cloud 9 (Limited support)

  • Discounts not supported
  • CareCredit ledger write not supported
  • Other payment capabilities are limited compared to other systems

Q: Does Adit support insurance verification (RCM) in Orthodontic PMS systems?

A: Yes. All three systems support:

  • Insurance verification workflows
  • Attaching verification PDFs to patient files

Q: What is the overall capability of each Orthodontic PMS?

A:

  • Orthotrac: Strong Engage, Forms, Payments, and RCM support
  • Dolphin: Best-balanced orthodontic PMS with broadest support
  • Cloud 9: Core-only functionality with the most limitations

Q: What should be considered when selling Adit with Orthodontic PMS systems?

A:

  • Practice Analytics should not be sold or promised
  • Online Scheduling is limited (not full automation)
  • Engage + Payments + Forms are the core value drivers
  • Cloud 9 has the highest limitations and must be positioned carefully
  • PMS validation is required before onboarding

Optometry PMS Compatibility - Adit Integration Overview (Q&A)

Q: Which Optometry PMS systems does Adit support?

A: Adit supports the following Optometry PMS platforms:

  • OfficeMate (On-Prem)
  • Crystal PM (On-Prem)
  • RevEHR (Cloud)
  • EyeFinity (Cloud)
  • Revolution (Web)
  • Eyefinity

Each system has different levels of support for Engage, Scheduling, Forms, Analytics, and Payments.

Q: Do all Optometry PMS systems support the same features?

A: No. Feature support varies significantly by PMS type.

  • Engage, Scheduling, and Forms are widely supported
  • Practice Analytics is only available on select systems
  • Financial write-back (refunds/discounts) is generally not supported
  • Some cloud systems have limited or no analytics support

Q: Which Optometry PMS systems support Practice Analytics?

A: Practice Analytics is supported only in:

  • OfficeMate
  • Crystal PM
  • Revolution (Web) (partial support)

These systems support features like:

  • Morning Huddle
  • Schedule analytics
  • Dashboards
  • Practice Performance
  • Growth and Reports
  • Patient Lists and Recall Reports

Not supported across all Optometry PMS:

  • Provider performance analytics
  • Operatory utilization
  • Practice Health Score
  • Follow-ups analytics

Q: Which Optometry PMS systems do NOT support Practice Analytics?

A: The following systems do not support Practice Analytics:

  • RevEHR
  • EyeFinity (Cloud)
  • Eyefinity

These systems do not include dashboards, reporting analytics, or recall insights.

Q: Can Adit support Treatment Plans in Optometry PMS systems?

A: No. Across all Optometry PMS platforms:

  • Treatment Plans are not supported
  • Treatment Plan PDF attachments are not supported

Q: Does Adit support Online Scheduling for Optometry PMS systems?

A: Yes, partially.

Fully supported:

  • OfficeMate
  • Crystal PM
  • RevEHR
  • Revolution (Web)
  • Eyefinity

Not supported:

  • EyeFinity (Cloud)
  • Pulling operatory hours (not supported across all systems)

Online Scheduling includes:

  • Real-time availability (where supported)
  • Writing appointments into PMS
  • Provider hour syncing

Q: What Engage features are available?

A: Most Optometry PMS systems support core Engage features:

  • Appointment reminders
  • Auto-confirmations
  • Birthday messages
  • Recall reminders
  • ASAP lists

Not supported:

  • EyeFinity (Cloud)

Optometry-specific Engage features:

  • Eyeglass ready notifications
  • Eyeglass follow-ups

Supported in:

  • OfficeMate
  • Crystal PM
  • RevEHR
  • Revolution (Web)
  • Eyefinity

Q: Does Adit support Patient Forms in Optometry PMS systems?

A: Yes, across most systems.

Fully supported:

  • Import completed forms
  • PDF attachment to PMS
  • General patient fields
  • Insurance fields

Not supported:

  • Medical history fields (most platforms)
  • Allergies (limited support only in some systems)
  • Medications (limited support)

EyeFinity (Cloud) has the most limited support.

Q: Does Adit support Patient Profile features?

A: Yes, but support varies.

Example support breakdown:

Feature OfficeMate Crystal PM RevEHR EyeFinity Revolution Eyefinity
Patient status Yes Yes Yes No Yes Yes
New / Existing Yes Yes Yes No Yes Yes
Profile picture Yes No Yes No Yes No
Preferred language Yes Yes Yes No Yes Yes
Patient notes No Yes Yes No No No

Q: Does Adit support payments and financial write-back in Optometry PMS systems?

A: Yes, but limited.

Adit Pay ledger write support:

  • OfficeMate: Supported
  • Crystal PM: Supported
  • Others: Not supported

Refunds & discounts:

  • Not supported in any Optometry PMS system

Communication logs:

  • Supported only in Crystal PM

CareCredit:

  • Supported in OfficeMate and Crystal PM (region-dependent)
  • Not supported in other systems

Q: Does Adit support insurance verification (RCM)?

A: Yes, in most systems.

Supported in:

  • OfficeMate
  • Crystal PM
  • Revolution (Web)
  • Eyefinity

Capabilities include:

  • Insurance verification
  • PDF attachment to patient file

Not supported in:

  • RevEHR
  • EyeFinity (Cloud)

Q: What are the key sales rules for Optometry PMS systems?

A:

  • Practice Analytics should only be sold for OfficeMate, Crystal PM, and Revolution (Web)
  • Refunds and discounts write-back are not supported anywhere
  • EyeFinity (Cloud) should be positioned as Engage + Forms only
  • CareCredit availability depends on region
  • PMS validation is required before onboarding

Q: What is the overall capability of each Optometry PMS?

A:

  • OfficeMate: Best overall for Analytics + Scheduling
  • Crystal PM: Strong Analytics + Engage support
  • RevEHR: Engage + Scheduling only
  • EyeFinity (Cloud): Very limited integration
  • Revolution (Web): Partial Analytics + strong Engage
  • Eyefinity: Engage-focused with RCM support

Guide to Insurance Verification Charges (Insurance Verification)

Guide to Insurance Verification Packages

Adit offers three types of Insurance Verification services designed to meet different practice needs-from fully automated verification to expert-reviewed, high-accuracy verification.

1. Basic Verification (EDI Only)

Verification Type:
Fully automated EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) verification.

Pricing:
$99/month includes 300 free EDI verifications
Additional transactions are charged at $0.06 per verification

CDT Code Coverage:
Supports up to 40 CDT codes

Process:
Adit integration pulls eligibility information directly through EDI in real-time.

Failed Verifications:

  • No cost for failed verifications
  • Does not include manual expert follow-up

EHR Integration:
Verified PDFs and breakdown notes are automatically posted into your EHR

2. Advanced Verification (Standard)

Verification Type:
Combination of automated EDI verification and manual expert validation.

Pricing:
$99/month + $1.00 per advanced verification

CDT Code Coverage:
Supports up to 20 CDT codes

Process:
Adit pulls eligibility via EDI, which is then reviewed and finalized by our expert RCM team for improved accuracy.

Failed Appointments:

  • If EDI verification fails, the expert team manually verifies the appointment
  • Ensures higher success rates

Additional Flexibility:

  • Any individual patient appointment can be upgraded to Advanced verification

EHR Integration:
Verified PDFs and notes are automatically posted into your EHR

3. Advanced Verification (Extensive)

Verification Type:
EDI + Manual expert verification designed for complex or high-volume needs.

Pricing:
$99/month + $2.25 per advanced verification

CDT Code Coverage:
Supports 20 to 40 CDT codes

Process:
Eligibility is pulled via EDI and fully validated by the expert RCM team, making it ideal for complex plans such as Medicaid and HMOs.

Failed Appointments:

  • All failed verifications are handled by the expert team at no additional cost

Additional Flexibility:

  • Suitable for appointments requiring extended code coverage and deeper verification

EHR Integration:
Verified PDFs and notes are automatically posted into your EHR

Add-On: Same Day Verification

Verification Type:
EDI + Manual expert verification designed for complex or high-volume needs.

Pricing:
$6 per advanced verification

CDT Code Coverage:
Supports 40 CDT codes

Process:
Eligibility is pulled via EDI and fully validated by the expert RCM team, making it ideal for complex plans such as Medicaid and HMOs.

Failed Appointments:

  • All failed verifications are handled by the expert team at no additional cost

Additional Flexibility:

  • Suitable for appointments requiring extended code coverage and deeper verification

Summary of Key Benefits

  • Flexible verification options based on your practice needs
  • Automated + expert-backed workflows for higher accuracy
  • Seamless EHR integration with auto-posted PDFs
  • No cost for failed verifications across all plans
  • Ability to upgrade appointments to Advanced verification anytime

If you need help selecting the right plan or enabling features, please contact the Adit Support Team.

Tech OB Whitelisting Ticket Handling Process (Onboarding)

Tech OB Whitelisting Ticket Handling Process

Day 1 - The Tech OB is to send WL email to client / IT contact

  • Desk - use 6 Tech OB - 02 Whitelisting Info template
    • In table, add model #, line & MAC address
  • Tech OB record update the following fields
    • Whitelisting Ticket ID
    • Whitelisting Email
    • Acknowledged by IT / Practice Manager (when applicable)

Day 2 until Phone Install date

  • Continue to follow up with the client / IT contact via call / email / sms to verify that WL has been completed successfully.
  • Once complete, update ticket with private comment and close ticket
  • In Tech OB record, update Acknowledged by IT / Practice Manager
    *If not complete by PI date, continue below.

Phone Install Day

  • If WL is not completed by this date, OB is to explain the importance of completing WL to the client before completing the phone install call.
    • Note: while WL is not always required, it is highly recommended to ensure the voice traffic is optimized on the practice’s network.
    • Protects against Cyber attacks. VoIP phone systems are often targeted by fraud and denial-of-service attacks. Whitelisting helps prevent these attacks by only allowing approved IP addresses to communicate with protected resources.
    • Improves IT security by having control over what can run on or access systems.
    • Whitelisting rules or policies complement Network ACLs by explicitly defining which IP addresses are allowed to send and receive Voice traffic.
    • Even if a Firewall / Router has not blocked any IP traffic or kept it open for reaching the Internet earlier, it is highly recommended to create these policies to group our Adit Voice traffic to be assigned the Highest priority for flowing in and out of the practice network seamlessly, even during low internet bandwidth
    • Improved Performance: By limiting the number of allowed applications and devices, whitelisting can help improve network performance and reduce latency.
    • Prioritizes Voice packets through techniques like QOS and bandwidth management which helps in improved call quality.
  • The OB is to explain to the client that our VoIP team will observe the call quality up until 1 week after porting is complete to ensure the practice does not face any issues with the service.
  • The OB will explain to the client if issues arise with the phone system, they need to contact Adit as soon as possible.

After Install

  • If the client faces issues after the phone install, WL WILL BE mandatory.
  • In the event the client does not have an IT person or can not complete the WL themselves, Adit can assist. The client will need to give Adit access to the practice’s network / firewall in order to complete the necessary steps.
  • The Tech OB needs to update the subject line of the WL ticket to the following:
    • Whitelisting Needed - Client Name and then assign to VoIP - Whitelisting queue in Desk

1 week after Poring has been completed

  • At this point, if the client has not faced a single voip issue, then the WL ticket can be closed but first the following needs to be done:
    • The Tech OB must email the client from the WL ticket using the following template:
      • Incomplete Whitelisting
    • Once the client acknowledges WL has not been completed, WL ticket can be officially closed

OB Training: Communication, Expectation Setting, and Client Updates (Onboarding)

OB Training: Communication, Expectation Setting, and Client Updates

Effective communication is the foundation of successful client management and long-term retention. It is also the number one complaint we receive from clients-making it one of the most critical skills for an Onboarding Specialist to master.

The Role of an Onboarding Specialist

An Onboarding Specialist is responsible for:

  • Understanding the client’s needs and goals

  • Coordinating onboarding activities to meet those needs

  • Communicating clearly so the client feels both informed and understood

  • Advocating for the client within Adit

  • Representing Adit professionally in every client interaction

Understand Your Client

Our success-individually, as a team, and as a company-depends on how well we meet our clients’ needs.

The most important part of your role is truly understanding your client. This process begins during the kickoff call and should continue throughout every interaction. You should consistently seek to understand:

  • What are the client’s goals and expectations?

  • What motivated them to choose Adit?

  • What challenges or pain points are they experiencing?

  • How can Adit’s platform help address those needs?

Equally important is understanding how your client prefers to communicate. Adjust your communication style to match theirs-it is not the client’s responsibility to adapt to you. For example:

  • Do they prefer detailed phone calls or brief emails?

  • How strictly do they adhere to their schedule?

  • How responsive are they to follow-ups?

Once you understand your client’s needs, goals, and communication style, you can more effectively coordinate the many moving parts of their onboarding experience.

Communicate Effectively

Strong communication is a skill that requires constant practice. Always aim to:

  • Speak slowly and clearly

  • Actively listen and restate key points to confirm understanding

  • Ask open-ended questions that encourage clients to share more information

Clear communication builds trust and prevents misunderstandings before they arise.

Set and Manage Expectations

Set expectations with your client at every opportunity. Clients should always know:

  • When they will hear from you next

  • What the next communication will cover

  • When to expect updates from other teams, especially if an issue is in progress

Setting expectations is only effective if you follow through. If you commit to a call on Wednesday, you must call on Wednesday. If you promise an email the next morning, send it in the morning. Do not substitute one form of communication for another, and avoid reaching out at the end of the day when clients are typically busiest.

Reliability is a key driver of client confidence.

Share Frequent and Meaningful Updates

When another team (e.g., T2 Core Tech) is involved in resolving a client issue, it is your responsibility to:

  • Review ticket updates daily

  • Check notes and current status

  • Proactively relay relevant information to the client

Do not wait until an issue is fully resolved to provide an update, and do not rely on other teams to communicate directly with the client.

Even when there is no major change, letting the client know that work is ongoing reassures them that their issue is being actively addressed and that they remain a priority.

Advocate for Your Client

You are both:

  • The voice of Adit to the client, and

  • The voice of the client within Adit

While part of your role is to encourage adoption of Adit’s products and features, this must be done thoughtfully. Rather than pushing products, demonstrate their value by aligning recommendations with the client’s specific goals and business needs. Help clients understand both the benefits of using the platform and the potential cost of not doing so.

Above all, you are the client’s advocate. By fully understanding their needs, you can collaborate effectively with internal teams to resolve issues and deliver solutions that truly support their practice.

Own the Onboarding Process

You are responsible for tracking and managing all aspects of the client’s onboarding journey, including any offshoots such as technical issues or support tickets. This includes:

  • Coordinating issue resolution with internal teams

  • Asking questions to ensure tasks are completed correctly and on time

  • Reviewing relevant CRM records (e.g., Porting status, Adoption Score)

By proactively monitoring both the onboarding and support experience, you can often identify potential dissatisfaction before the client voices it. This allows you to address concerns earlier, communicate more effectively, and prevent escalation.

Final Takeaway

By mastering communication, expectation setting, and client advocacy, you build trust that extends beyond onboarding. These skills create confident, satisfied clients who not only succeed with Adit but become enthusiastic advocates for our platform within their communities.

4. Staff Training Process (Onboarding)

Staff Training Process

Purpose

The goal of this training is to teach the staff how to use the Adit platform in their day-to-day work. Remember that you are only training on the Core platform: Engage, Pozative, Patient Forms, and Adit Voice and eFax (if applicable).

If your client plans on using Online Scheduling and you have already met with them to fully configure it, you can include it as part of the Core Platform and train the staff on it at this stage. If they are not sure about using OS yet, it is better to save that conversation for the Adoption phase.

Before Training

Ensure that the Core platform has been fully configured and you know how the practice will use certain features, such as if they will send Review Requests manually instead of automatically. You will train the staff on the correct way to use the Adit platform; it is up to the POC, Office Manager, or practice admins who are implementing Adit for the practice to ensure the staff follows all of their internal processes.

Discuss with your POC at the practice ahead of time how their team prefers to ask questions:

  1. Interrupt as each question comes to mind?
  2. Wait until you pause for questions at the end of each section?
  3. Hold all questions until the end?
  4. Send all questions to the POC, who will forward them to you via email so you can answer in writing?

Each OB has their own preference, but in general we find that the options 2 or 4 are best for larger groups (6 or more people).

Staff Training Call

The Staff Training call should take around 60 minutes, though it can be longer if the staff has a lot of questions. Anyone who will be using the Adit platform or communicating with patients - including using Adit phones (if applicable) - should be included in this training session. If they cannot make it to the live training, that’s ok! We’ll send the recording after the call so they can share it with anyone who missed it, or use it to train new members of their team in the future.

You should not cover any settings or preferences in the staff training; 90% of staff will never change their settings and showing them how is just overloading them with more information than they need.

If applicable, pause after each section and check in with the staff to see if they have any questions.

Training Agenda

Be sure to cover the following:

  • Navigation
    • How to switch between modules
    • Notifications
    • How to access the help widget
    • How to search for a patient
    • Patient Card
    • Quick Text
  • Phones
    • Call pop and softphone
    • How to make an outbound call
    • How to check voicemails
    • How to view call history
    • Call Override
    • How to hold, park, and transfer on hardphones
  • eFax
    • How to send an eFax
    • How they will receive incoming faxes
    • How to see fax history
  • Engage
    • How to search for an existing conversation
    • How to start a new conversation
    • How to send a text message
    • How to tell when they have received a new text
    • How to send a Mass Text
  • Pozative
    • How to interpret the data the dashboard
    • How to manually send a review request
    • How to view and respond to reviews
  • Patient Forms
    • How to request a patient fill out a form
    • How to see requested and submitted forms, tabs in Forms page
    • How to re-send forms back to patients (i.e. to complete a skipped question)
    • How to view, approve, and archive forms
    • How to see if a form has been imported to the PMS

If you have configured OS for the practice, you should also include:

  • Online Scheduling
    • How to see an appointment request
    • How appointments write into their EHR (if applicable)
    • How to manually send an appointment request to a patient

If you have configured Treatment plan templates for the practice, you should also include:

  • Treatment Plans
    • How to interpret the data on the Tx Plans page
    • How to create a treatment plan for a patient
  • Email Campaigns
    • How to create an email campaign
    • How to duplicate or delete an existing campaign
    • How to interpret the data of the campaign report

After Training

Send Follow Up Email

Send a follow up email to the POC and thank them for their time. Provide the recording of the training session and link them to any resources that you think they may find particularly useful, such as a KB article for a feature their staff was excited about.

Update CRM

Update the Staff Training Complete field on the TO-record in CRM.

1. Tech Onboarding Process (Onboarding)

Tech Onboarding Process and Workflow

Adit’s tech onboarding consists of distinct phases that gently guide the client into using our full platform and integrating its functions into the daily work flow of their practice. These phases are:
Phase 0: Account Setup
Phase 1: Core Platform
Phase 2: Adoption
Phase 3: Go Live

How to Use This Document

This document outlines the entire tech onboarding process and the onboarding client lifecycle. It includes instructions on how to do every part of tech onboarding, including what fields to update in CRM and what parts of the process will require assistance from other teams.

Any steps of the onboarding process not covered directly in this document are calls or meetings that require their own separate process documentation; these are linked throughout the document where needed for easy reference as well as in the Appendix.

Use the Table of Contents (below) or the Outline (in the left navigation panel) to jump to a specific section.
