Phase 0: Account Setup

Account setup is almost entirely automated. It begins when a client signs their Agreement with Adit, which automatically creates the Tech OB record (also known as the TO-record) in CRM. This is still technically part of the Sales process; Onboarding does not begin until later.

Stage: Pending Server Install

The first stage for the TO-record is Pending Server Install. During this stage, the AE will guide the client through the account setup process, which includes installing the server sync app (Pozative.exe). This entire setup process occurs within the Adit platform’s “Get Started” checklist. The items set up during this stage can include:

  • Done by the client:
    • Add their business hours
    • Add their front desk / receptionist’s email address
    • Create users
    • Put a credit card on file for overage charges
    • Set up an outbound phone number (will be a temporary number if they are porting)
    • Provide porting information (if applicable)
    • Provide info about their IT provider (if they have one)
    • Install the server sync app (Pozative) on their server computer
    • Connect their Google Business page (optional)
    • Upload their practice’s logo (optional)
    • Download the Adit mobile and desktop apps (optional)
  • Done by Adit:
    • Order phones as selected by the client on their agreement (automatic)
    • Add tracking number and expected delivery date in CRM (automatic)

The specific items included in an individual client’s Get Started checklist will vary based on their package and their intent to use Adit Voice or not.

There are three requirements for a client move from the Account Setup phase into Onboarding:

  1. All required Get Started steps complete.
  2. Phones ordered and shipped (if applicable).
    1. Tracking Number / Expected Delivery Date for phones updated in CRM, or
    2. The client did not order phones.

Once all of these requirements have been met, the Deal stage will move to Onboarding and the Tech OB record stage will automatically update to Pending Phone Install. If the client will not be using Adit Voice, the stage will move to Pending Kickoff.

Phase 1: Core Platform

Stage: Pending Phone Install / Pending Kickoff {#stage:-pending-phone-install-/-pending-kickoff}

This is where Onboarding officially begins. The OB will see the client listed in their CRM dashboard, in the section for “Schedule/Reschedule Kickoff”, as well as receive an email notification. This is the OB’s signal to reach out to the client to introduce themselves, talk about the onboarding process and schedule their first three meetings.

Client Research

Before the OB calls the client for the first time, they will need to do a small amount of research in CRM:

  • Check the Deal to see what Package they have signed up for and if they will be using Adit Voice, Adit Pay, Analytics, RCM or Call Intelligence. This will tell the OB what modules are included in their package and will need to be set up during their onboarding.
  • Check the AE’s notes about the client’s current setup, their needs and goals, pain points, and other information.
  • Check the Account and Deal to see if the AE included any additional notes as to the client’s specific needs, who to contact, when to contact them, or anything else the OB may need to know about the client.
  • Check the TO-record and ensure the information in the following sections has pulled over correctly; if it has not, update it.
    • Deal Details (pulls over from Deal in CRM)
    • Module Opt In (depends on agreement and client preferences)
    • Account Set Up (pulls in from Adit App)
    • Server Install (is Server Install Complete checked)

*Note: If the client has opted out of Adit Voice, the stage of their TO-record will be Pending Kickoff. Please make sure to omit any parts of the onboarding process specific to phones and eFax. This includes (but is not limited to) whitelisting, phone installation, configuring call flow, and training on these features.

Intro Call

OB calls the client to introduce themselves and start building rapport. This call should only take about 15 minutes. Here are some things the OB must mention:

  • That you will be their main point of contact during their onboarding with Adit, and that you are excited to work with them!
  • Your direct contact info (direct phone number for calls and texts, support at adit.com for emails).
  • Confirm the main point of contact (POC) at the office for their onboarding.
    • Make sure you have that person’s correct name, phone number, and email.
    • Confirm and/or Update this info in CRM (on the Account, Deal, and TO-record) after the call.
  • Let them know you are calling today to schedule their three “big” onboarding calls.
  • Briefly explain the Kickoff Call / Phone Install:
    • Includes three parts:
      • Overview of the onboarding process,
      • Discussion about their practice needs and goals, and
      • Installing their new phones (if applicable).
    • If using Adit Voice:
      • Be prepared for this call to take at least two hours, possibly up to four depending on how many phones need to be installed. Make sure the client is aware of and agrees to this time commitment.
        • Kickoff portion: 30-60 minutes
        • Installing phones: about 30 minutes per phone for the first 3, plus about 10 minutes for each additional phone.
        • POC should be involved in the Kickoff portions of the call but does not need to handle the phone installation themselves; they can delegate the phone setup to their IT person or to another member of their team who can more easily commit to the required block of time.
      • Schedule the Kickoff w/ Phone Install:
        • Must be 5-6 days from today, should be the day before the Config Call.
        • Must be after the Phones Expected Delivery Date.
        • Must be able to meet for 2-3 consecutive days (for Kickoff, Config, and Staff Training).
      • Start preparing for a smooth phone installation. Refer to VoIP vs Traditional Phone Service for more information and questions to ask the client.
    • If no Voice:
      • Call will take around 30-45 minutes.
      • Schedule within the next 3 days.
  • Explain and schedule the Config Call:
    • About 60 minutes.
    • Allows the client to review and confirm the configuration of their platform.
    • Teaches the Office Manager and/or practice admins how to access and update settings if needed in the future.
    • Schedule the Config Call:
      • Should be the day after their Kickoff Call (no more than 2 days after).
      • Must be at least 7 days from today.
  • Explain and schedule the Staff Training:
    • About 1 hour, but can schedule for longer if they have a large team (more than 7).
    • Covers the core platform features that the staff will use on a daily or weekly basis.
    • Invite everyone on their team who will use any part of the Adit platform, including phones.
    • The training will be recorded. Anyone who cannot make the scheduled time can watch the recording at their earliest convenience.
    • Schedule the Staff Training:
      • Should be the day after the Config Call.
      • They will be turning on their Adit features during Config, so we want to make sure the staff is trained as soon as possible afterwards.

    1. Tech Onboarding Process (continued, part 1)

  • If the client has signed up for any of the following, a separate stand alone training session should be scheduled as well. Ex. Analytics, Pay, RCM or Call Intelligence

Update the Kickoff Call Sched Date, Config Call Sched Date, and Staff Training Sched Date fields in the TO-record in CRM with the agreed-upon date for each call. Update the contact info for your POC in the TO-record, Deal, and Account in CRM (if needed).

Email Phone Info

When the client’s phones are delivered, you will see an update in your CRM dashboard letting you know that you need to email the client. In Desk, use the Phone Info template to send an email to the client. Update any placeholder text with the appropriate client information. Also in Desk, use the Whitelisting template to send a second email to the client’s IT contact and cc your POC. Update the Whitelisting Email field to Sent in the TO-record when both emails are sent.

The first email will help the client prepare for a successful phone installation by showing them in advance how to plug in the physical phones. The Whitelisting email provides important information about required whitelisting. Whitelisting is only required for about 10% of clients, but it’s a good idea to have their IT check their network configuration before the Kickoff Call to ensure everything is in place for our phones to work as soon as they are plugged in.

The OB will continue to follow up daily with the client and/or their IT until they confirm that whitelisting is done. Once you have received that confirmation, update the Acknowledged by IT / Practice Manager field in the TO-record.

Confirm Kickoff Call & Phone Info {#confirm-kickoff-call-&-phone-info}

One business day before the Kickoff Call, call the client to confirm the date and time of their Kickoff Call.

If they are using Adit Voice, remind them that their phones will also be installed during this call, so their IT person (if they have one) needs to be available as well. Confirm they received the email regarding phone setup and whitelisting. If they did not receive the email, confirm the email address and resend it. Ask the client to forward that email to their IT, if they have one, and to cc us on it so that our team can reach their IT in case any issues arise.

Update the Kickoff Confirmed field in the TO-record once you have confirmed the Kickoff call will proceed as scheduled.

Kickoff Call

The Kickoff Call should occur within a few days of the client’s phones being delivered. For an in-depth look at the process and expectations before, during, and after this call, please see our Kickoff Call Process document.

The purpose of the Kickoff is to introduce the client to Adit and our Onboarding experience and set the client’s expectations for the rest of the onboarding process. You will also guide the client through installing their phones (if applicable) and give them a complete training on how to use them.

Once both the Kickoff Call and the Phone Install (if applicable) are completed successfully, click the Phone Installed, Pending Config transition on the TO-record

Phone Install Failed

If the phone installation was not successful, speak with the VoIP team, providing all relevant information to help get the issue resolved. The Onboarding cannot move forward until the phone install has been completed successfully.

Stage: Pending Config

During this stage, you will configure the Core platform for your client based on the information you have about them and the conversation you had during the Kickoff Call. This is only a preliminary configuration; you will update and confirm the settings once you have the client on the phone.

Remember that we are only concerned with the Core Platform at this phase of onboarding; you will only configure Engage, Pozative, Patient Forms, and eFax at this time. If your client plans on using Online Scheduling and knows how they want to set it up, you can include it as part of the Core Platform. If they are not sure about using OS yet, save that conversation for the Adoption phase so that you can spend as much time on it as needed.

Config Call

You will then have the Config Call with the client, during which you will:

  1. Show the client what you have set up for them.
  2. Walk them through what each of the settings do and why you chose the configuration you did for their specific needs.
  3. Encourage the client to discuss these decisions with you, and
  4. Make any necessary changes to ensure the final configuration is correct and will meet their needs and goals.
  5. Turn on all automated messages and reminders.

For an in-depth look at the process and expectations before, during, and after this call, please see our Configuration Call Processdocument.

Once the Config Call is complete and the client is happy with the configuration you’ve set up, click the Config Complete transition on the TO-record.

Stage: Pending Core Training

During this stage, you will train the staff at the practice - anyone who will be using the Adit platform or communicating with patients should be included in this training session, which should last around 60 minutes.

Since you turned on all of their automated messages and reminders in the Config Call, it is generally best to do the Staff Training as soon as possible after the Config.

Staff Training

The goal of this training is to teach the staff how to use the Adit platform in their day-to-day work. Remember that you are only training on the Core platform. For a detailed list of what to cover before, during, and after this call, please refer to Staff Training Process.

You should not cover any settings or preferences in the staff training; 90% of staff will never change their settings and showing them how is just overloading them with more information than they need.

In order for the Training Complete transition to be available, two requirements must be met:

  • The Staff Training Complete field must be updated to YES, and
  • The client’s Adoption Score must meet a threshold of 30 points (without Voice) or 60 points (with Voice). If they haven’t reached this threshold, they are not using the core features that you set up and enabled; follow up with the client to find out why and how you can help get them engaged with the platform.

Phase 2: Adoption

Stage: Pending Adoption

The Adoption stage is where we will handle the configuration, training, and adoption of the rest of the Adit App. This will likely be the longest phase of the onboarding process. Onboarding Specialists will continue to follow up with your clients, run interference for any issues or bugs, and encourage them to use various pieces of the platform.

Additional Training

If the client will be using Call Intelligence, this is when they will schedule their training, be sure to schedule the training session with the client for 60 minutes. If the client is not yet sure, schedule a demo call for the Upgrade team to pitch the platform to the client. Once their Call Intelligence training is completed, update the Call Intelligence Onboarding section of the TO-record. If the client will not be using Call Intelligence, make sure the feature is opted out in the TO-record.

If the client has Practice Analytics included in their package, this is when they will schedule their training with the PA team. To schedule this, have the client go into the Practice Analytics module and click the Schedule Training button near the top right of the page. Once this training session is scheduled, update the PA Training field to Scheduled. If the client decides they do not want to use Practice Analytics, you should involve their AE to ensure they were sold on the correct package. If necessary, they can be downgraded to a tech bundle.

If the client will be using Adit Pay, be sure to set them up for the Pay Configuration meeting with the Pay team. Note: when scheduling this call, be sure to check the availability on the Adit Pay Training calendar for proper availability, use this link for scheduling: Adit Pay & Terminal Set Up If the client is not yet sure, schedule a call for the Pay team to pitch their platform to the client. Once their Adit Pay Configuration is scheduled, update the Adit Pay Training field to Scheduled. If the client will not be using Adit Pay, make sure the feature is opted out in the TO-record.

If the client has signed up for RCM, this is when they will schedule their training with the RCM team. To schedule this, have the client go into the RCM module and click the Schedule Training button near the top right of the page. Be sure to walk the client through the Get Started steps in the module and ensure the set up is completed prior to their scheduled training with the RCM team. If the client is not yet sure, schedule a demo call for the Upgrade team to pitch the platform to the client. Once their RCM training is scheduled, update the RCM Set Up field to Onboarding. If the client will not be using RCM, make sure the feature is opted out in the TO-record.

Adoption Calls

The order of Adoption Calls is specifically designed to ensure that clients can pick up each additional piece and incorporate it easily into their existing knowledge about the Adit platform and their daily work flow. In each Adoption Call, you will configure that feature to meet the client’s needs as well as teach them how to use it. The client should pass any necessary information on to the rest of their staff as needed.

You should plan to make 1-2 Adoption Calls to each client per week; aim to have at least 3-4 days between each call. For example, if you have Adoption Call #2 on Monday, you can reach out on Thursday or Friday for call #3. As you complete each Adoption Call, check the corresponding box in the Pending Adoption section in the TO-record.

Adoption Call #1: Online Scheduling (can be skipped if OS was covered in Core phase)
Adoption Call #2: Call Intelligence (if using CI)
Adoption Call #3: Patient Segments / Patient Lists and Mass Texting
Adoption Call #4: Email Campaigns and Drip Campaigns
Adoption Call #5: Treatment Plans (if using Practice Analytics)
Adoption Call #6: Internal Chat
Adoption Call #7: Follow Ups (if using Practice Analytics)

For more information on what to discuss in each Adoption Call, please see Adoption Conversations.

Once all required Adoption calls have been made, the following criteria must be met:

  • PA Training = Scheduled or Completed, or PA opted out
  • Pay Training = Scheduled or Completed, or Pay opted out
  • The client’s adoption score has reached 100 (with Voice) or 70 (without).

For more information on adoption score metrics, please seeAdoption Metric Definitions.

At this point, the OB will need to evaluate the client’s status and if there are any ongoing issues. If the adoption score is met, the client is comfortable, and there are no issues with their platform or account, you will make your final check-in call and move the client to Pending Approval.

If the client is still not comfortable with the platform, is escalated or upset, or has repeated or ongoing technical issues, they are not ready to move to CSM. Click the Ongoing Issues transition to move them to the Pending Resolution stage.

Phase 3: Go Live

Stage: Pending Resolution

Resolution is a catch-all final stage for clients who have reached their adoption score but cannot move to CSM for some other reason. Common reasons include:

  • The client is escalated.
  • They have continuing issues, i.e. ongoing call quality problems.
  • They have recurring issues, i.e. server app stops syncing every few days.
  • They have requested additional training or frequently ask very basic questions, indicating that they are not comfortable using the platform.
  • They have requested porting of additional numbers or purchased additional equipment that will need to be set up.

While clients are in Pending Resolution, the OB’s job is to check in with the client as frequently as they need in order to resolve their issues and/or de-escalate their account. This may include following up with the client directly and with internal teams to ensure issues are resolved thoroughly.

When all outstanding issues are resolved, you will have a final check-in call with the client.

Final Check-In Call

Once all issues (if any) have been resolved and the client has met their required adoption score, you will make a final check-in call to the client. During this call, you must:

  • Inquire about how things are going with the platform.
  • Address any remaining questions, concerns, or issues.
  • Explain that you will be moving their account out of onboarding and over to our CSM team. Congrats on graduating!
  • Inform the client that a member of our CSM team would like to speak to them regarding their onboarding journey and to ensure we have met their needs. Inform the client this call will take no longer than 15 mins and you would like to schedule it within the next day or two.

Once the check-in call is complete, the client is ready for CSM. Update the Check In Call Date and Notes For CS fields in the TO-record. Make sure the correct contact person for the practice is updated on the TO-record, the Deal, and the Account in CRM, then click the Ready for CSM transition on the TO-record.

Stage: Pending Approval

The approval stage is the last step in the onboarding process. It allows us a small measure of accountability to ensure that clients are set up for success at the end of their onboarding.

Approval is handled entirely by the Tech CSM team. They use the following criteria to determine if a client is ready to leave onboarding:

  1. No open tickets.*
  2. Notes for CS field is filled out with any and all helpful information the Tech CSM will need in order to call the client and have a positive, productive conversation.
  3. All training completed and configuration questions resolved.
  4. PA check complete and training scheduled (if applicable).
  5. Contacts updated in Deal and Account.
  6. Adoption score reached.
  7. Client does not have any questions/issues/hesitation about successfully using the Adit platform.

*Note: Minor bugs/tickets that aren’t hindering the client from utilizing the platform may still be open if the client is not escalated because of those outstanding issues. These tickets must be new (not ongoing issues), unique (not recurring issues), and isolated (not affecting any other parts of the platform) in order for the move to CSM to be approved.

If a move to CSM is rejected, the TO-record will move back to Pending Resolution. The OB must work with the client to address any remaining tickets, questions, issues, escalations, etc. Once all issues are resolved, you can once again move the client to the approval stage by the Ready for CSM transition.

Appendices

Appendix A: CRM Fields

It is solely the OB’s responsibility to ensure that CRM is updated and maintained at all times throughout the onboarding process. Within this document, there are specific indications of when to update certain fields or sections in CRM, primarily on the Tech OB record. If a field is not specified in this document, it does not excuse the OB from ensuring it is updated.

The TO-record is organized into sections that roughly correspond to the Stage of the TO-record. You can use that to help ensure that you are filling fields out at the right time. Below is a list of the sections of the TO-record; any sections with a name in bold contain at least one field that the OB must update manually. Some fields in the TO-record will be updated by other teams; these are also indicated below.

  • Technology Onboarding Info
    • Updated by the OB.
    • Technology Onboarding Owner and Technology Onboarding Name should only be edited by Managers.
  • Sales Missteps
    • Updated by the OB if we discover something in onboarding that was either missed by the AE or misunderstood by the AE/Client.
  • Deal Details
    • Automatically updates from Deal fields, do not edit.
    • If any of these fields are incorrect, check and correct on the Deal.
  • Module Opt In
    • Will sometimes be auto-filled depending on the client’s package and other decisions made in the sales/signup process.
    • OB should update manually as well when needed.
  • Account Set Up
    • Filled in automatically when “Get Started” tasks are completed.
    • If any of these fields are not filled in automatically:
      • Let Manager know.
      • Check the Adit App to see if the info is updated there.
        • If so, update the fields manually.
        • If not, get the info from the client and update it in the Adit App, then update the CRM fields.
  • Server Install
    • Updated automatically if the app is self-installed by the client.
    • Updated manually by the Server Install team if support assistance is needed.
  • Porting Status
    • Updated manually by the Porting team
  • Phone Install
    • First six fields in the left column are about their phone hardware shipment. These are updated by Asset Management if phones were ordered.
    • Rest of the left column is updated by the OB.
    • Right column used only if the phone install fails or there are issues; fields can be updated by the OB or by the VoIP technician. Please coordinate with the VoIP tech on a case-by-case basis.
  • Pending Kickoff
    • All fields updated by the OB.
  • Pending Config
    • Left column updated by the OB.
    • Right column only used if the client is opting out of phones; updated by Manager.
  • Pending Training
    • All fields updated by the OB.
    • Left column is for Staff Training.
    • Right column is for training scheduled with other teams (Practice Analytics and Pay).
  • Pending Adoption
    • Left column All fields update automatically.
    • Right column All fields updated by the OB.
  • Pending Approval
    • Left column updated by the OB.
    • Right column updated by the Tech CSM team.
  • Porting Details
    • Filled in automatically when the client provides porting info in the Get Started process.
    • Can be updated manually by the OB if needed.
  • Whitelisting Details
    • Two fields the OB is required to update:
      • Whitelisting Email
      • Acknowledged by IT / Practice Manager
    • All other fields are updated by the VoIP team if/when needed.
  • RCM Set Up
    • Field updated by the OB.
  • Call Intelligence Onboarding
    • All fields updated by the OB.
  • Practice Analytics Set Up
    • Managed by the PA team.
  • Adit Pay Set Up
    • Managed by the Pay team.
  • Key Data Points
    • Updated automatically by fields and formulas.

2. Kickoff Call Process (Onboarding)

Kickoff Call Process

Purpose

The Kickoff Call serves as an introduction and helps set the client’s expectations for the rest of the onboarding process. This time must be utilized effectively to establish a trusting, collaborative relationship between the Onboarding Specialist and the client.

Before the Kickoff

Within one business day of the Kickoff Call, research your client. This is your first opportunity to get to know your client, their office, and their processes. Review the information available in CRM on the Account, Deal, and Tech Stack records, as well as what has already been updated in the Tech OB record.

Note any questions you have as you research and any points of clarification you’d like to discuss in more detail. Have recommendations ready for configuring the platform to meet the client’s stated needs and goals.

Talk to the AE as well. They should have provided notes in CRM for you, but they have also worked with the client throughout the signup process and may have some insights that will be helpful.

Here are some things you should take note of in your research:

  • Do they have 3rd party IT? Do we have contact info for this 3rd party?
  • Are they using Adit Voice? What about Practice Analytics? Pay? RCM? Call Intelligence?
  • What modules or features do they appear to be interested in?
  • What EHR/PMS software do they use?
  • Look through their website. Do they currently offer online booking, patient forms, or payments? Make a note if you think their website is outdated or difficult to navigate; they may be a good candidate for our marketing services later!

Confirm that the necessary account setup has been completed. These should have been done in the Get Started phase (before Onboarding), but if any are missing you may need to follow up:

  • CRM is accurate - POCs have been added as Contacts on the Account/Deal; Deal name is the practice name, etc.
  • Organization/Location is set up in the Adit App and named correctly.
  • Business Hours set up.
  • Receptionist Email added.
  • Logo uploaded.
  • Outbound number selected.
  • Server app installed and syncing.
  • GMB page connected.
  • Users created.

Confirm that all required items for VoIP are set up or in place:

  • In CRM:
    • Check phone tracking (in TO-record), make sure they have been delivered or will be before the call.
    • Check that phone info (Phones records) matches GDMS.
    • Confirm we know who their current phone provider is and if they are porting any numbers. Do we know how to do call forwarding for this provider?
    • Review the IT Details on the Deal level, confirm all numbers listed on the Invoice / CSR match what we will be porting over. If additional numbers are listed on the document but not added in the porting record, review with the client and get added if required.
  • In Adit App:
    • Check that phone info (in Lines) matches GDMS.
    • Make sure each line has an actual practice user associated with it, not the admin user with the @adit.com email.
    • Configure the basic Call Flow (simulring all lines for 45 seconds, then go to voicemail with an appropriate message) for any landline that is currently in service. This will be their temp number as indicated in CRM (if they are porting their landline) or their permanent phone number (if they are not porting a landline).

Send an email to the client reminding them of the meeting and include the Google Meet link. Make sure their IT is copied on that email if they will need to attend the meeting as well. If any of the account setup items in the list above are missing, remind the client to bring that information with them to the meeting. If necessary, include the Phone Info template as well.

Kickoff Call

The Kickoff Call is, first and foremost, a conversation. Use the time to get to know the client, their needs, and their goals for their practice; this information will be invaluable as you build a relationship with them over the next few weeks. The Adit platform is overwhelming; do not expose the client to all of it in this first call.

This time is also a key opportunity to get the client excited about using our platform. Match their enthusiasm. Avoid negative answers - for example, if they ask about a feature or function that we can’t do, approach the answer with positivity (“Yes, but we have to do it in a slightly roundabout way…”) instead of just telling them we can’t do it.

Below is a standard agenda that should work for nearly all Kickoff Calls. You don’t need to follow it precisely, but you can use it as a guideline to ensure you touch upon all of the important talking points the client needs to know. The sections highlighted in orange are examples of the types of questions you should be asking during this conversation; work them in naturally and allow the client to answer each one thoroughly. Getting to know your clients in this way is the primary goal of the Kickoff Call.

Kickoff Agenda

  • Introductions

    • If there is anyone in the call that you haven’t already met, ask them to introduce themselves! What is their role, how long have they been at the practice, etc.

  • Review Onboarding Process

    • Let the client know what to expect during the onboarding process:
      • Other teams/people they may hear from: tech support teams, PA team, VoIP team, etc.
      • Expected timeline: Full onboarding should take about a month. They will be up and running with our core platform in about 10 days; after that, it’s just about making sure they are comfortable and using the other parts of the platform before we shift them to our CSM team. The goal is to ensure they are all set up and using Adit thoroughly before their billing starts.
      • That there are three major planned meetings (including this one).
      • Total amount of time they will spend on calls/meetings with you is about 6-8 hours total over the course of the entire onboarding process.
    • Explain the structure/flow of their specific onboarding, which will vary based on their package.
      • Phase 1: Core Platform (weeks 1-2)
        • Today: Kickoff Call and phone install.
        • Tomorrow: OB will do their preliminary configuration (call flow, Pozative, eFax, auto-reminders, patient forms).
        • (Scheduled Date): Config Call, where you will review what you’ve set up for them, make any necessary changes to that configuration, and teach them how to update their settings when they need to in the future.
        • (Scheduled Date): Staff Training on core platform and day-to-day use.
          • Invite anyone in the office who will be using any part of the Adit platform, including the phones.
          • Training will be recorded and the recording provided to the client so team members who could not attend live can watch. They can also use it to train new members of their team.
      • Phase 2: Adoption (weeks 2 through 6)
        • Analytics training with PA team (if their package includes Analytics).
        • Adit Pay evaluation with Pay team.
        • Conversations about remaining modules, including configuration and training.
        • Additional Q&A for staff, if needed.
        • Regular check-in calls with OM.
        • Once they have been trained, the active part of onboarding is over and the rest of the process is simply making sure they are knowledgeable, comfortable, and using the platform.

  • Phone Install

    • Let the client know that you will now help them install their phones. If they need their IT person for this, make sure they are added to the call.
    • Make sure the client has watched the 1-minute “How to connect your Adit phones” video that you sent them previously.
    • Install the phones. For detailed instructions, see How to Install Adit Phones.
      1. Plug in one of each phone model.
      2. Wait for them to update.
      3. Test the installed phones.
      4. Set up call forwarding.
      5. Caller ID verification, see Caller ID Verification
      6. Have the client (or their IT) plug in the remaining phones.
        • Continue with Call Flow and training while you wait for the rest of the phones to update.
      7. Configure their Call Flow.
      8. Teach the client how to use the new hardphones.
        • Hold / unhold
        • Transfer (attended/warm and unattended/cold)
        • Intercom / call another office extension
        • Check voicemail
        • Park a call and pick up a parked call
        • Conference call / three-way call
        • Call override
      9. Test the remaining phones and the entire system.
    • If you run into any issues with the phone installation or testing, immediately message your VoIP tech in your Pod chat.

  • Get to Know the Client

    2. Kickoff Call Process (continued, part 1)

    • This is the most important part of the Kickoff Call.
    • Ask open-ended questions and let them talk.
      • What are their goals for the practice?
      • How large is the practice? How many operatories, doctors, hygienists, assistants, support staff?
      • Where in their community are they located? An office inside of a busy shopping mall will have different needs than one in a very rural community.
      • What kind of patients make up the majority of their patient base? Elderly patients may prefer to communicate differently than young families or college students.
      • Why did they choose Adit?
      • What parts of the Adit platform are they the most interested in or excited about?
      • What parts of the Adit platform are they not interested in using, and why? (i.e. Pozative because they don’t want negative reviews, OS because they don’t want patients to be able to schedule just anything.) You will be able to use their fears/concerns to provide customized configuration options that will allow them to use that feature without the downside that they anticipate.
      • What did they like or dislike most about their previous software, if any? Think of ways we can match the things they liked, and solve for the things they disliked.
      • What parts of their day do they find the most tedious or frustrating? Is there a feature within our platform that will solve that problem for them?
      • What else do they want us to know about their practice, their style, their personality, or their staff?
    • Be sure to ask any questions that you noted while you were researching.
    • Gather information about their current setup, if they have one, or what they would like to set up:
      • How do they communicate with their patients?
      • What timing/methods do they like to use for appointment reminders, recalls, unscheduled treatment?
      • Do they offer online appointment booking, patient forms, or payments?
      • What patient forms do they use regularly?
      • How many people are at the front desk? Who is involved with patient communication?
      • Do they have any unusual setup requirements, such as staff working remotely or additional locations?
      • Do they have any critical deadlines that we need to follow, such as end of service with another vendor?
    • The conversation you have had up until this point should have provided you with most of the information you need to do a preliminary configuration. If you need more info, you can ask them a limited number of direct questions about the Core features:
      • Auto Reminders
      • Patient Forms
      • Pozative
      • Online Scheduling
    • If the client is particularly interested in a feature that is not part of the Core platform (see previous bullet point), you can answer any questions they have about it and help maintain their enthusiasm while reassuring them that we will cover it in the second half of their onboarding. We want to get them comfortable with our Core operations before we introduce more advanced features.
    • If they say something in any of the above conversation that you think will lead to a specific use-case, ask them to go into more detail about that specific subject.

  • Confirm Next Meetings

    • Confirm the date and time of their Config Call (which should be the next day) and their Staff Training (which should be the day after that).

  • Final Thoughts

    • Recap anything that the client still needs to send you, and anything you will be working on for them.
    • Remind them that our goal is to get them set up as quickly and smoothly as possible to ensure minimal disruption to their patients.
    • Ask if they have any questions. Listen and answer thoughtfully.
    • Thank the client for their time!

After the Kickoff

All of the post-kickoff work is done by the OB Specialist.

Send Follow Up Email

Send the client a follow-up email promptly after the call concludes. Thank them again for their time, reiterate the importance of their participation and cooperation in the onboarding process, and remind them of the scheduled dates of their upcoming meetings. Send the phone guide again, if necessary.

You should also recap the conversation you had and give a quick bullet-point list of things that were important to them to show that you were paying attention to their needs and goals.

Update CRM

Make sure that the Account and Deal in CRM are updated with any additional points of contact they provided in the call, including their IT if necessary.

Make sure the Sched Config Call Date (for the config call) Sched Staff Training Date (for Staff training) are correct on the TO-record. Fill in any notes in the Notes for OB field and update the Next Touchpoint Date to the next date you will need to take action on this client. If the Kickoff portion of the call was completed, update the Kickoff Call Complete field to Yes. Update the Phone Install Result and Call Flow Configured fields based on the result of your call.

If the Kickoff Call was completed and the Phone Install was successful during this call, click the Phone Install Successful transition on the TO-record in CRM. This will update the TO-record stage to Pending Config.

If the Phone Install failed or was otherwise not completed on this call, but the Kickoff portion was completed, the VoIP team will be notified so they can step in and communicate directly with the client to resolve any underlying issues. They will update you when the phone install has been completed successfully.

If the client is not using Adit Voice and did not complete a phone install, the transition will be Kickoff Complete; in this case, the TO-record stage will move directly to Pending Config.

If neither the Kickoff Call nor the Phone Install was completed successfully, be sure to reschedule both parts. The TO-record stage will remain Pending Phone Install or Pending Kickoff until they are completed successfully.

Planning Next Steps

Shortly after the Kickoff Call, take some time to summarize your thoughts on the client and the information that they provided during your conversation. Think about how to incorporate our tools into their workflow and how we can demonstrate the value of our product and the cost to their business of not using it. You will need to do a lot of critical thinking here, but it will help you plan how to approach training and future adoption conversations with this client. Include this information in your notes in the TO-record.

3. Configuration Call Process (Onboarding)

`Configuration Call Process

Purpose

The Configuration (Config) Call allows you to walk the client through the Core platform’s settings while simultaneously showing them what you have set up for them and finalizing that configuration to meet their needs.

Remember that we are only concerned with the Core Platform at this phase of onboarding; you will only configure Engage, Pozative, Patient Forms, and eFax at this time.

If your client plans on using Online Scheduling and knows how they want to set it up, you can include it as part of the Core Platform and configure it at this stage. If they are not sure about using OS yet, it is better to save that conversation for the Adoption phase. Keep in mind that configuring OS is very involved and will require the client’s active participation; it may be better to cover it in a separate call than to make the Config Call even longer and risk overwhelming the client with too much information at once. See Adoption Conversations for more information of what OS settings need to be configured.

Before the Call

Offline Configuration

Before the scheduled Config Call, you will set up the Core platform for your client based on the information you have available (from Sales and the Kickoff Call). This is only a preliminary configuration; you will update and confirm the settings once you have the client on the phone.

Some features already have default settings configured. If you already know what changes your client will need, update them now; if not, you can wait until you confirm their preferences on the call.

Each of the Core platform features has some settings that can be configured in advance:

  • Engage
    • Set up Status Mapping in a logical way. Map all statuses to Confirmed or Unconfirmed in a way that makes sense.
    • Customize any auto-reminders that you know they want/need. Birthday Wishes, Scheduled Confirmations, Appointment Reminders, and Recall Reminders are already set up with default templates, but you should edit them based on the client’s needs, such as:
      • When to send each message.
      • To whom each message should be sent.
      • If they would like to use auto-confirmation on appt reminders.
    • Customize the text of each auto-reminder message.
      • Decide if the placeholder for Organization Name or Location Name makes the most sense for this client.
      • Update the default text if you feel it is appropriate.
    • Set Preferences for Appointment Date format and Quick Text.
  • Pozative
    • Make sure their logo has been added.
    • EHR Integration - keep on Manual for now, but know which Automatic option you will recommend based on their goals.
    • Goal - if you know what their goal is, update it now.
    • Make sure GMB is connected.
    • Choose the request flow and settings that will best meet their needs.
  • Patient Forms
    • Make sure their logo has been added.
    • Set the Reply-to and Receptionist emails.
    • Edit the default message text for form requests, resending forms, 2nd signature.
    • If they have a thank-you page, add it.
    • Specify which users are able to sign on behalf of the practice.
    • Customize any of the sample forms you know they need.
    • Set up any Auto-assign Forms that you know they will want to use.

Config Call

Call Expectations

The Config Call should be scheduled for 60 minutes. During this call, you will confirm the configuration and teach the Office Manager and/or practice admins how to find and update preferences for the Core platform features.

For each Core module, you will:

  1. Show the client what you have set up for them already.
  2. Walk them through what each of the settings do.
  3. Explain why you chose the configuration you did for their specific needs and goals.
  4. Encourage the client to discuss these decisions with you and suggest changes.
  5. Make any necessary changes to ensure the final configuration will both work and meet their needs.
  6. Turn on all automated messages and reminders.

Call Agenda

The following features and settings should be covered in this call:

  • Navigation
    • Module icons and how to switch between apps
    • Help menu
  • Voice
    • How to change recordings for greeting, menu, and voicemail
    • Where to upload custom hold music
    • Call recording for outbound calls
    • Call override setup
    • How to block callers
  • eFax
    • Settings > Numbers > fax number > edit
      • Add who should receive a copy of every incoming fax in the Incoming email field
  • Engage
    • Auto-Reminders
      • How to view and edit an auto-reminder
      • How to toggle an auto-reminder off or on
      • How to add a reminder
      • Text vs. Email vs. Voice reminders
        • Message priority (text/email/both)
        • Voice priority (cell/home/both)
      • Spanish reminders
        • How to set up Spanish reminders
        • How Spanish reminders are triggered instead of English ones
      • Customize text of each message (text, email, voice messages customized separately)
      • How to use placeholders in message text
      • Define each auto-reminder and what it is used for
      • Specific settings for each reminder:
        • Schedule Confirmation:
          • Add forms to a scheduled confirmation text
          • Send to new patients/existing patients/both
        • Appointment Reminders:
          • Auto-confirmation, confirmation response, mark C as read
          • Send reminder to (based on appointment status)
          • When to send before/after appt, hours/days/weeks, time of day
        • Recall Reminders:
          • Recall types
          • Send before/after due date
          • When to send and time of day
    • Preferences
      • Appointment Date format
      • Default messages for Quick Text - different from the auto-reminder text
    • Confirm reminders are configured how the client wants them
  • Pozative
    • Preferences
      • Logo
      • EHR Integration - recommend Automatic at 7pm, show various automatic options
      • Goal - set a goal for how many reviews they want to receive per month
      • Request Frequency
      • Connect business pages
      • Review Request flow
      • Text or Email or Both
      • Default review request text, how to use placeholders
      • Ability to filter (if using Flow A)
      • Widget - allows them to embed their reviews on their website (not required)
    • Insights
      • Explain that insights give them a summary of their review requests and activity
  • Patient Forms
    • Preferences > Forms
      • Logo
      • Reply-to email
      • Receptionist email
      • Default message text for form requests, resending forms, 2nd signature
      • Thank you page
      • Signers
    • Form Builder
      • Show the form library
      • How to edit/customize a form for their needs
        • Add/remove fields, edit fields
        • Add/remove sections, edit sections
        • Add/remove pages, edit pages
        • Reorder pages, sections, and fields
      • If they know what they need now, you can help them make those changes on the call, or do them after the call
      • Encourage the client to attempt these customizations on their own
    • Auto-assign Forms
      • Assign forms to new patients/existing patients/both
      • Advanced Filters based on appt type or treatment code
      • When to send before/after appt, hours/days/weeks, time of day
      • Add up to 5 forms to auto-assign to these patients based on the above criteria

Make sure you keep track of your allotted time during this call. If you reach the last 15 minutes or so and still have a lot to cover, schedule a second call (30-60 minutes) for later the same day or the next day.

Turn On Features

By the end of the Config Call, you have turned on all of the configured automations, including auto-reminders, form auto-assignments, automatic review requests, etc. We don’t want to duplicate reminders for that day, so be sure to confirm with your client first:

  1. Ask, “Did your current provider send out reminders already today?”
  2. If yes, make sure the auto-reminders are configured to go out at the right time, and will go out tomorrow instead of today.
  3. If not, update their auto-reminders to send out later today (the exact time will depend on what time it is now). After the reminders are sent, go back in and change the timing of each auto-reminder back to the correct time they should go out starting tomorrow.

Call Wrap Up

Wrap up the call by making sure the client is comfortable with what you showed them today and happy with the final settings that were agreed upon. Confirm the date and time of their Staff Training. Thank them for their time and congratulate them on using their Adit platform!

After the Call

Send Follow Up Email

Send a follow-up email to recap the most important parts of the conversation and provide links to any resources that you think the client will find particularly helpful, such as a KB article on building patient forms.

Update CRM

There are three fields in the TO-record that refer to configuration:

  • Basic Config Complete - update when you have finished your preliminary offline configuration
  • Config Call Complete - update when the call is complete and configuration is finished
  • Pref Train Complete - update when your POC has been trained on settings/preferences

If everything in the Config Call goes as planned, all three of these fields can be updated at the same time at the end of the call.

Once the Config Call is complete and the client is happy with the configuration you’ve set up, click the Config Complete transition on the TO-record.

Adit Patient Forms Configuration Guide (Patient Forms)

Adit Patient Forms Configuration Guide

Overview

Adit Patient Forms provide powerful tools for collecting patient information and integrating it directly with your EHR/PMS. This guide covers the key configuration options available within Patient Forms, including field mapping, clinical data integration, PDF settings, auto-import, EHR folder selection, and pre-fill functionality.

1. Mapping Fields in the Form to the EHR

What Is PMS Field Mapping?

PMS Field Mapping connects fields within your Patient Form to corresponding fields in your EHR. Once a patient completes a form and it is approved, the mapped information automatically updates the patient’s chart.

Benefits

  • Reduces manual data entry.
  • Improves data accuracy.
  • Keeps patient records updated automatically.

Available PMS Mapping Fields

Patient Demographics

  • Patient First Name
  • Patient Last Name
  • Date of Birth (DOB)
  • Preferred Name
  • Gender
  • Marital Status
  • Social Security Number (SSN)
  • Driver’s License Number

Contact Information

  • Address Line 1
  • Address Line 2
  • City
  • State
  • Zip Code
  • Email Address
  • Home Phone Number
  • Work Phone Number
  • Mobile Phone Number

Insurance Information

  • Primary Insurance Company Name
  • Secondary Insurance Company Name
  • Primary Insurance ID
  • Secondary Insurance ID

Clinical Custom Fields

  • Medications
  • Allergies
  • Problems

Important Notes

  • Available mapping fields may vary based on your EHR integration.
  • Clinical fields sync only when selected from the predefined dropdown lists.
  • Information writes back to the patient chart after form approval.
  • Proper mapping ensures accurate and automatic record updates.

2. Choosing the PDF Compression Layout

Adit Patient Forms provide multiple PDF layout options for downloaded forms.

Important

Changing the PDF layout affects only the downloaded PDF. The online patient experience remains unchanged.

How to Change the PDF Layout

Step 1: Access form manager

  1. Navigate to Patient Forms.

  2. Open form manager .

  3. Select the desired form.

Step 2: Choose a Layout

  1. Click the Download dropdown.
  2. Select your preferred PDF layout.

Available PDF Layouts

Compressed Layout

  • Minimizes file size.
  • Removes unnecessary whitespace.
  • Ideal for storage efficiency.

Table Layout

  • Place each field within its own table cell.
  • Provides a structured and organized appearance.
  • Useful for documentation and record review.

Large Print Layout

  • Closely matches the online form design.

  • Provides larger spacing and improved readability.

  • Ideal for reviewing detailed responses.

Important Notes

  • Layout changes only affect downloaded PDFs.
  • Patient-facing forms remain unchanged.
  • Layouts can be switched at any time before downloading.

3. Toggling Auto-Import ON or OFF

Auto-Import automatically transfers completed forms to the connected EHR/PMS, including uploading the PDF and updating mapped fields.

Benefits

  • Eliminates manual importing.
  • Reduces administrative workload.
  • Speeds up patient record updates.

When Auto-Import Works

Auto-Import is available only when forms are sent through:

  • Quick Text
  • Form Requests
  • Auto-Assign Rules

A specific patient must be selected.

When Auto-Import Does Not Work

Forms completed through a public URL cannot be auto-imported and must be manually matched and imported.

How to Enable or Disable Auto-Import

Option 1: From Form Manager

  1. Navigate to Patient Forms.
  2. Open Form Manager.
  3. Locate the form.
  4. Toggle Auto-Import ON or OFF.

Option 2: Within the Form

  1. Open the form for editing.
  2. Locate the Auto-Import setting.
  3. Enable or disable the feature.
  4. Save your changes.

Summary

When enabled, Adit automatically imports the completed PDF into the patient’s PMS record and updates mapped fields. Auto-Import is available only for forms sent through Form Requests, Quick Text, or Auto-Assign workflows.

4. Selecting the Folder in the EHR for Completed Form Uploads

Practices can specify which EHR folder receives completed form PDFs after import.

Why Use Folder Selection?

  • Keeps records organized.
  • Supports office-specific workflows.
  • Ensures forms are stored in the correct chart location.

Important Notes

  • Folders are created and managed within the EHR.
  • New folders must be created in the EHR before they become available in Adit.
  • Folder availability depends on EHR synchronization.

How to Select an EHR Folder

Option 1: From Form Manager

  1. Navigate to Patient Forms.
  2. Open Form Manager.
  3. Locate the form.
  4. Select the desired EHR Folder.

Option 2: Within the Form

  1. Edit the form.
  2. Locate the EHR Folder setting.
  3. Select the appropriate folder.
  4. Save your changes.

Result

After configuration, all completed and imported form PDFs will be uploaded automatically to the selected folder within the patient’s EHR chart.

5. Setting Fields as Pre-Fill Fields

Pre-Fill Fields allow staff to populate specific form fields before sending the form to a patient.

Benefits

  • Reduces patient data entry.

  • Ensures critical information is already included.

  • Supports internal workflow requirements.

    Supported Field Types

  • Single Line Text

  • Date Fields

  • Multi-choice
    checkboxes

Important Limitations

  • Pre-Fill fields cannot be marked as Required.
  • Patients cannot edit Pre-Fill fields.
  • Empty Pre-Fill fields remain blank after submission.

Part 1: Setting Up a Pre-Fill Field

Step 1: Open Form Manager

  1. Navigate to Patient Forms.
  2. Open Form Manager.
  3. Edit the desired form.

Step 2: Enable Pre-Fill

  1. Select an existing Single Line Text or Date field.
  2. Enable the Pre-Fill Field toggle.
  3. Save the form.

The field is now configured for pre-fill functionality.

Part 2: Entering Pre-Fill Information Before Sending

Pre-Fill fields can be completed when assigning forms through:

  • Quick Text
  • Patient Card → Assign Form

Pre-Fill Status Indicators

🟧 Orange Icon

  • One or more Pre-Fill fields are incomplete.

🟩 Green Icon

  • All Pre-Fill fields have been completed.

Two Ways to Complete Pre-Fill Fields

Option 1: Individual Entry

Best for a single form assignment.

  1. Click the Pre-Fill icon.
  2. Enter the required information.
  3. Save.
  4. Send the form.

Option 2: Bulk Entry

Recommended for multiple form assignments.

  1. Click Send or Assign.
  2. Complete all outstanding Pre-Fill fields from the review screen.
  3. Submit the forms.

Key Reminders

  • Only staff can edit Pre-Fill fields.
  • Patients cannot modify pre-filled information.
  • Empty Pre-Fill fields remain blank after submission.
  • Pre-Fill fields cannot be designated as required.

Common Use Cases

  • Appointment dates
  • Provider names
  • Internal reference numbers
  • Office-use-only information

Conclusion

By properly configuring field mapping, clinical data integration, PDF layouts, Auto-Import settings, EHR folder destinations, and Pre-Fill fields, practices can streamline patient intake, reduce manual work, improve data accuracy, and maintain well-organized patient records within their EHR.

6. Integrating Allergies, Medications, and Medical History into Your Forms Add Allergies to Patient Forms

Patient allergies can easily be pulled from your EHR and be placed into Adit’s Patient Forms. When patients select an allergy in their form, that data will then be imported back into their patient chart.
To add allergies to a patient form:

  1. Navigate to the Patient Forms module.

  2. In the top navigation menu, click Form Manager . If you don’t see this option in the menu, click the three dots to view the rest of the menu options.

  3. Click the Create Form button to create a new form, or click Form Name, or Edit icon on an existing form you want to update.

  4. On the Form building page, you will see a tool bar on the left side. This tool bar provides different types of fields that you can use in your form.

  5. Go to the custom fields section and drag the Allergies field into your form.

  6. You’ll see a pop-up appear, explaining that this field will automatically populate a list of Allergies based on the master list in your EHR. Select Yes to continue.

  7. Once the field is placed on your form, the right hand column will appear showing the field properties.

  9. Field Label - Use this field to write the question you want to ask the patient

    1. For Example: “Are you currently allergic to any of the following?”

  10. Hidden - you can hide this question on the patient form

  11. Required - you can make this field mandatory for patients

  12. Copy - this option is disabled for all custom fields because you can only have one in each form

  13. PMS Field - this field allows you to map where the data should write into your EHR. Since this is a custom field, it will be automatically mapped to the allergies in the patient’s chart.

  14. Allergy Name - these are automatically pulled based on the allergies available in your EHR.

    1. You can choose to select the Eye Iconto hide an allergy from the dropdown or select the X to remove it completely.
    2. Please note if you want to add any new allergies on this list, it will have to be added directly in your EHR first, and then once that information syncs over you have to remove and re-add this allergy field in your form.

  15. Reset - If you want to remove any updates you made to the medications field, you can select this buttonto start over.

  16. Once you are satisfied with your form and are ready to start using it, go to the top navigation and select either Save or Save & Exit

Add Problems to Patient Forms

Patient problems can easily be pulled from your EHR and be placed into Adit’s Patient Forms. When patients select a problem in their form, that data will then be imported back into their patient chart.
To add problems to a patient form:

  1. Navigate to the Patient Forms module.

  2. In the top navigation menu, click Form Manager . If you don’t see this option in the menu, click the three dots to view the rest of the menu options.

  3. Click the Create Form button to create a new form, or click Form Name, or Edit icon on an existing form you want to update.

  4. On the Form building page, you will see a tool bar on the left side. This tool bar provides different types of fields that you can use in your form.

  5. Go to the custom fields section and drag the Problems field into your form.

  6. You’ll see a pop-up appear, explaining that this field will automatically populate a list of Problems based on the master list in your EHR. Select Yes to continue.

  7. Once the field is placed on your form, the right hand column will appear showing the field properties.

  9. Field Label - Use this field to write the question you want to ask the patient

    1. For Example: “Do you currently have any of the following problems?”

  10. Hidden - you can hide this question on the patient form

  11. Required - you can make this field mandatory for patients

  12. Copy - this option is disabled for all custom fields because you can only have one in each form

  13. PMS Field - this field allows you to map where the data should write into your EHR. Since this is a custom field, it will be automatically mapped to the problems in the patient’s chart.

  14. Problem Name - these are automatically pulled based on the problems available in your EHR.

    1. You can choose to select the Eye Iconto hide an allergy from the dropdown or select the X to remove it completely.
    2. Please note if you want to add any new allergies on this list, it will have to be added directly in your EHR first, and then once that information syncs over you have to remove and re-add this allergy field in your form.

  15. Reset - If you want to remove any updates you made to the medications field, you can select this buttonto start over.

  16. Once you are satisfied with your form and are ready to start using it, go to the top navigation and select either Save or Save & Exit

Add Medications to Patient Forms

Patient medications can easily be pulled from your EHR and be placed into Adit’s Patient Forms. When patients select a medication in their form, that data will then be imported back into their patient chart.
To add medications to a patient form:

  1. Navigate to the Patient Forms module.

  2. In the top navigation menu, click Form Manager . If you don’t see this option in the menu, click the three dots to view the rest of the menu options.

  3. Click the Create Form button to create a new form, or click Form Name, or Edit icon on an existing form you want to update.

  4. On the Form manager page, you will see a tool bar on the left side. This tool bar provides different types of fields that you can use in your form.

  5. Go to the custom fields section and drag the medications field into your form.

  6. You’ll see a pop-up appear, explaining that this field will automatically populate a list of medications based on the master list in your EHR. Select Yes to continue

    .

  7. Once the field is placed on your form, the right hand column will appear showing the field properties.

    Field Label - Use this field to write the question you want to ask the patient

    1. For Example: “Are you currently taking any medications?”

  8. Hidden - you can hide this question on the patient form

  9. Required - you can make this field mandatory for patients to fill out

  10. Copy - this option is disabled for all custom fields because you can only have one in each form

  11. PMS Field - this field allows you to map where the data should write into your EHR. Since this is a custom field, it will be automatically mapped to the medications in the patient’s chart.

  12. Medication Name - these are automatically pulled based on the medications available in your EHR.

    1. You can choose to select the Eye Iconto hide a medication from the dropdown or select the X to remove it completely.
    2. Please note if you want to add any medications on this list, it will have to be added directly in your EHR first, and then once that information syncs over you have to remove and re-add this medication field in your form.

  13. Reset - If you want to remove any updates you made to the medications field, you can select this buttonto start over.

  14. Once you are satisfied with your form and are ready to start using it, go to the top navigation and select either Save or Save & Exit

  15. Now once you send a form request to a patient, this is how the medications field will look like from a patient’s perspective.

  16. Patients who have medications associated to their profile in the EHR will have the medications automatically pre-populated when they receive a form request.

    1. Patients will also be able to enter in new medications by using either of these methods:

      1. Clicking on the dropdown and selecting from a list of predefined medications
        1. Note: medications selected from the dropdown will be imported over to the patient’s profile once the form is approved
      2. Manually entering in their own medication
        1. Note: medications manually entered in will not be imported over.

    2. Patients can add more medications by clicking on + or remove a medication by clicking on X
