Important Information

CRM and Desk

In CRM, there are two “levels” that we work with - the Account level and the Deal level. Desk pulls most of its Account and Contact information from CRM but also pushes some data to CRM.

A Deal is approximately equal to an individual office or location, while an Account is usually more like an owner or company. An Account can have many Deals, but each Deal can only be associated with one Account.

For example, Dr. Smith owns two locations: Main Street Dental and Downtown Dental.
In CRM, the Account is listed as Dr. Smith Dental LLC. This account has two Deals associated with it, one for Main Street Dental and one for Downtown Dental.

It is important to note that both Tickets and Contacts are linked on the Account level, not the Deal level. This means all tickets for all Deals on an account will show the same account name in Desk. This can sometimes lead to confusion, so it is best to have a habit of always specifying the location in the Subject line or the body of the ticket.

In our example, any tickets for Main Street Dental will show the Account in Desk as Dr. Smith Dental LLC. Tickets for Downtown Dental will also show under the Dr. Smith Dental LLC account.

Accounts and Contacts

Every ticket must be associated with the correct Account. This allows both Adit users and clients to locate tickets quickly and easily, especially when investigating ongoing or repeat issues.

If the account is missing from a ticket, determine if the contact listed on the ticket is correct. If not, change the contact on the ticket.

If the contact is correct but not associated with the correct account, edit the contact to associate it with the correct account.

Change the Contact on a Ticket

The following are examples of situations when you would change the contact on a ticket:

  • An email is forwarded to the Support desk from an Adit employee, so the Adit employee or team is listed as the ticket contact.
  • Voicemail or missed call notification emails that show RingCentral as the ticket contact.
  • Notification from a vendor or business partner (Google, Dropbox, calendar apps, Plivo, etc.).
  • A request from a third party or competitor on behalf of a client (in this example, you would need to reach out to the client to get permission to work with the third party, then change the contact on the ticket to the person that you got permission from).

Once you have determined that the contact on a ticket needs to be changed, edit the ticket fields. If you know the email address of the correct contact, copy it now for a faster, easier contact search. To edit the contact:

  1. Click the three dots at the top right of the ticket detail screen.
  2. Select Edit from the menu.
  3. In the Contact Name field, click the x to clear the contact information from the ticket.
  4. Search for the correct contact using the Contact Name, Email, or Account field. Desk will suggest matches from our client database; select the correct suggestion to select it.
  5. Click the Save button at the bottom of the screen.

Edit a Contact

  1. In Desk, click on the Contact name to take you to the contact’s detail page.
  2. Click on any grey info field, as seen in the screenshot below.
    You can also click on the three dots at the top right corner of the contact detail page, then select Edit.
  3. In the Account Name field, type in the correct account name. Desk will suggest matches from our client database; click on the correct suggestion to select it.
  4. Update any other contact fields if needed.
  5. Click the Save button at the bottom of the screen.
  6. In the Update Account popup that appears next, select “Yes, update” and then click the Submit button.

Adit Teams and Ticket Routing

Tech Support

  • TS - Core T2 :: Assign any ticket regarding an issue with an Adit feature (other than Voice, Fax, and mobile app) to this team AFTER you have done standard troubleshooting steps, such as checking the setup and configuration and replicating the issue.
  • TS - Specialty :: Practice Analytics and Adit Pay.
  • TS - Server Installs : For Adit Server Application installs and reinstalls.
  • TS Routing :: A catch-all for tickets that need to go to a TS or VoIP team, but you don’t know which one. TS Managers will sort tickets assigned to this team to the right place.

VoIP Support

  • VoIP - CSM :: VoIP, fax, and mobile app issues for active clients in CSM.
  • VoIP - T2 :: Only VoIP team members will assign tickets to this team for further troubleshooting and dev support.
  • VoIP - OB :: Phone installs and VoIP issues for onboarding clients.
  • VoIP - BOPS :: Only VoIP team members will assign tickets to this team for bugs, outages, product issues, and service problems.

Tech OB

  • TechOB Leadership :: For manager use only.
  • TechOB Pod 1-12 :: Tech OBs work out of pods. If you know which OB a ticket should go to, assign it to the corresponding pod.
  • TechOB Routing :: A catch-all for tickets that need to go to a Tech OB pod, but you don’t know which one. TechOB Managers will sort tickets assigned to this team to the correct pod.

Implementation

  • Imp - Account Setup :: For new client account setup.
  • Imp - Phone Orders/Returns :: For ordering or returning phones.
  • Imp - Porting :: For phone and fax number porting.

Marketing CSM

  • MktgCSM Leadership :: For manager use only.
  • MktgCSM Pod A-J :: Marketing CSMs and their CSR partners work out of pods. You must assign tickets for a specific Marketing CSM to the correct pod.

Other

  • T1 Customer Support :: Handles all T1 issues for tech-only clients, including troubleshooting.
  • TechCSM :: For tech-only clients who are escalated or need additional adoption support.
  • Billing :: For issues with Adit invoicing / billing only.

Taking Great Notes

Every team member who works with tickets should know how to take great notes. Clear ticket notes make it easier to collaborate with other teams, ensure escalated issues are handled more quickly, and allow everyone to work more efficiently as they won’t have to repeat steps that have already been done. In addition, leaving great notes ensures that anyone who assists this client in the future will clearly understand what has already happened.

When documenting a phone call, make sure that you include:

  • The name of the person you spoke with
  • The best phone number to call them back at (in case of a call drop or to follow up)
  • The best email to reach them out, if they prefer follow-up by email
  • A summary of everything discussed on the call in as much detail as possible, including:
    • Any questions that were asked (and the provided answers)
    • Details about any configuration or settings that you changed
    • Any troubleshooting steps that you performed (and their results)
    • Any additional information that you found or that the client provided.

When taking notes about troubleshooting or an investigation, be sure to document:

  • The issue as the client described it
  • Your initial suspicions or ideas about the issue
  • What steps you took to replicate the issue
  • Any settings or configuration that you checked on or changed
  • The results of each step that you tried
  • The end result of your investigation, including if further troubleshooting is needed or if you resolved the issue.

Ticket Priority

Generally speaking, every team will prioritize their tickets following the same guidelines.

  1. New tickets (either in your team’s queue or assigned to you).
  2. Open tickets.
  3. Tickets that are waiting for the Adit team to take action.
  4. Tickets that are waiting for the client to take action.

Ticket Status

There are seven available ticket statuses. Most teams will not use all of them.

Open - An Open ticket needs immediate attention. All tickets have a status of Open when created. If a client responds to a ticket in any other status, the ticket will automatically reopen. Open should also be used when escalating or reassigning a ticket so the new owner knows the ticket needs immediate attention.

Pending Customer - A ticket is Pending Customer when it requires a response from the client in order to move forward. This status is not used when a response from the client is optional.

Pending Adit - Tickets that are Pending Adit require additional action from the Adit team. Use this status when you will manage communication with the client and coordinate any further work with other Adit teams. If you are handing the ticket off to another team to handle, change the status to Open instead.

Pending Meeting - This status is primarily for CSM and OB teams, but Tech Support can also use it. Use this status when a meeting is scheduled, and the ticket’s resolution is waiting for that meeting to occur. Ensure the date and time of the scheduled meeting are noted in the ticket.

Pending Development - Only T2 support teams use this status. Use this status when the Dev team is working on an issue or bug.

Under Observation - Only T2 support teams use this status. Use this status when the Dev team has resolved an issue and you are observing to ensure the ticket is fully resolved.

Closed - The ultimate goal for all tickets is to be Closed. If you have sent a response to a client that solves their problem or answers their question, Close the ticket.

Ticket Fields

In Desk, any fields that are labeled in red text are required fields. These fields may change based on what you select in another field. Required fields include:

  • Contact - Every ticket must be associated with a Contact and an Account. If the Contact or the Account is missing or incorrect, you must edit them. For more information, see Accounts and Contacts.
  • Status - Follow the requirements described in Ticket Status to select the appropriate status.
  • Subject - The Subject line for every ticket should be simple, professional, and descriptive. The Subject is used internally to help locate tickets and is shown to clients as the subject line of any emails we send them on the ticket. If the Subject line does not describe the ticket’s contents, you must edit it.
  • Classifications - Describe which department the ticket falls under. The Classification you select will also change what Category field you have to choose from. Note: The Admin and Ops classification is for manager use only.
  • Adit App Module - Required on all tickets. Select all of the modules that you worked on within this ticket. If the ticket did not involve the Adit App, select -None-.
  • Category - Provides additional detail about what kind of question or issue occurred in the ticket.

Check the Potential Escalation or Churn box if the issue being documented in this ticket has the potential to escalate or churn the client.

Ticket SOPs

Create a Ticket

We can create new tickets in four ways:

  • Automatically when a client sends an email to support at adit.com
  • Automatically when a client submits a ticket through the Help Widget on their Adit dashboard
  • Manually by clicking the + button in the top right corner of the Desk ticket screen
  • By splitting a message from an existing ticket

When creating a new ticket manually, there are several important things to remember:

  1. All ticket fields labeled in red text are required. You will not be able to create the ticket if any of these fields are left blank. For more information, see Ticket Fields.
  2. Contact is always required. You can look up an existing contact by typing the Contact Name, Email, or Account Name in the appropriate field; Desk will automatically suggest matches from our database. Click on the correct suggestion to select it.
  3. The Description should be left blank when creating a ticket manually. Any text entered in the Description field will appear on the ticket as if a client emailed us, which can confuse users. The Description is also emailed to the client automatically when a ticket is created.
  4. Status should always be set to Open when creating a new ticket.
  5. Ticket Owner will default to the user creating the ticket. Please edit this field to ensure you assign the ticket to the appropriate team and person. See “Assign a Ticket” below for guidelines on assigning a ticket.
  6. Channel will default to Phone, assuming the new ticket is being created in response to an inbound phone call from a client. If that is not the case, you can change the Channel to identify how the client contacted us with this issue.

Assign a Ticket

When assigning a ticket to another person or team, you must assign the ticket to the Team first, then the user.

When picking up a ticket, assign it to your team first, then to yourself.

  1. Click into the Ticket Owner field.
  2. Click TEAMS at the top of the list.
  3. Locate the team you need in the list.
  4. Click the team name to assign the ticket to that team’s queue.
  5. To assign the ticket to a specific person on that team, click the user icon to the right of the team name, then select the user’s name from the list.

To confirm a ticket is assigned correctly, ensure the team name is shown alongside the user’s name. This ticket is assigned to Parul via the Billing team in this example.

Pick Up a New Ticket

New tickets must be handled using the First In, First Out (FIFO) method. The FIFO method means that the earliest ticket received must be handled first. Cherry-picking to avoid complex or difficult tickets is not allowed on any client-facing team.

Check your Team Queue or custom View in Desk to see if there are new tickets for your team. Always take the oldest unassigned ticket in your team queue/view.

While most teams follow these general guidelines, some teams may have a slightly different process for picking up new tickets. Please talk to your manager if you require clarification on this process.

Handle a Ticket

Once a ticket is created and assigned to a team/agent, the agent will follow a fairly standard set of steps to handle that ticket.

  1. Review the Ticket. Read through the email or comment thread and ensure you understand the issue. Check the client’s account to see if they have recently contacted us about this issue. If another agent is already working on the same issue in a different open ticket, assign the new ticket to them; they must merge the tickets and continue working on the issue.
  2. Update Ticket Fields. Once you know what the ticket is about, update the ticket fields accordingly, including the Contact, Subject, Classifications, Category, Adit App Module, and the ticket’s Status. Document any additional information in a Private Comment on the ticket as needed.
  3. Investigate. Sometimes, this will be as simple as answering a quick question; in other cases, an agent may need to follow their team’s standard investigation process. Document any findings in a Private Comment (note) on the ticket.
  4. Respond. All tickets must receive their first response (an email from Adit to the client) within three business hours. If you are on the phone with the client, send a follow-up email summarizing your conversation once the call ends. If you call them and reach voicemail, send an email as well.
  5. Escalate if needed.
  6. Follow Up. If a ticket is not Closed after sending the first response, follow up on the ticket.

Follow Up

Not every ticket will be closed right away. Some will require additional information from the client, and others will require you to coordinate with other Adit teams to take care of the client’s request.
You must follow up regularly if a ticket is in any status other than Closed. Generally, we require every ticket to be checked at least once every few days and for clients to be updated at least once weekly.

For tickets that are pending action by Adit (including Pending Adit, Pending Development, and Under Observation):

  1. Check on whatever work is pending every 1-2 days and update the ticket accordingly.
  2. Send an email to the client to provide an update at least once per week; include what we are still working on and how much longer we expect it to take.
  3. You must update the ticket with a comment if you don’t email the client when you check on the ticket.

For tickets that are pending action by the client (Pending Customer status), reach out to the client every 1-2 days to remind them that we are waiting for something from them. Try a combination of calling and emailing on different days. If you call and leave a voicemail, send an email as well.

If you require a response from the client and they are unresponsive for a week (5 business days), your next follow-up steps will depend on what kind of ticket it is:

  • If the ticket was created by Adit and is required to continue doing business - such as for their onboarding, a billing issue, or a contract issue - continue to follow up once per week until the ticket is resolved.
  • If the ticket was created at the client’s request - they called or emailed and asked us to do something, then stopped responding - follow the Unresponsive Client Closeout Process detailed below.

Unresponsive Client Closeout Process

If a client is unresponsive to your requests for information, follow these steps to ensure that our obligations are covered while not negatively impacting your ability to do your job effectively.

  1. Attempt to follow up with the client every 1-2 days for the first week (5 business days). Set the ticket status to Pending Customer.
  2. On the 6th business day following the client’s last response, send the Unresponsive Client - 6th day email template in Desk. Set the ticket to Pending Customer.
  3. On the 8th business day following the client’s last response, send the Unresponsive client - 8th day email template in Desk. Set the ticket to Pending Customer.
  4. On the 10th business day following the client’s last response, call the client.
    If you speak to someone and get the necessary information, continue handling the ticket as normal.
    If you speak to someone, but they cannot provide the information you need, return to step 2 and continue to follow up as normal.
    If you cannot reach anyone, leave a voicemail and then send the Unresponsive Client - 10th day email template in Desk. Close the ticket.

Ticket Handling Flow Chart

Edit Ticket Fields

You are responsible for updating the ticket fields when you handle a ticket. Do not wait until you are ready to close the ticket to update relevant fields; get in the habit of updating them when you create the ticket or when you first handle the ticket to ensure they never get forgotten.

You can access most ticket fields in the left-hand info panel of the ticket. These include:

  • Assigned To
  • Status
  • Classifications (select the department this issue falls under)
  • Potential Escalation or Churn (check this box if the issue documented in this ticket has the potential to escalate or churn the client)
  • Category (the category field will depend on what Classification is selected)
  • Module (select which Adit App modules, if any, are covered in the ticket)
  • Any custom fields for your team

In addition, you should also review the Subject line and the Contact on the ticket to ensure they are accurate. To edit these, click the three dots in the top right corner of the ticket screen, then select Edit from the menu.

The Subject line for every ticket should be simple, professional, and descriptive. The Subject is used internally to help locate tickets and is shown to clients as the subject line of any emails we send them on the ticket. If the subject line provided by the client or another agent does not match what the ticket is about, change it.

For more information on why you would edit the contact, see Change the Contact on a Ticket.

Escalate a Ticket

Every team will have an escalation path that considers that team’s specific needs. Ticket Escalation is used when an issue needs to be handled by another team. Each agent is responsible for moving tickets to the right team when needed.

All agents in Onboarding, CSM, and Customer Support must perform basic troubleshooting before escalating a ticket, including checking settings/configurations, testing and replicating the issue, and any other requirements set by your specific team.

To Escalate a Ticket:

  1. Ensure you have taken thorough notes about what the client said, any investigation or troubleshooting you performed, and the results you found. Include screenshots when appropriate.
  2. Let the client know you are escalating their issue to another team, and tell them when they can expect to hear back from that team.
  3. Update any ticket fields and set the ticket status to Open.
  4. Reassign the ticket to the necessary team.

Merge a Ticket

Sometimes you may find that a client’s response to a ticket comes in as a new ticket rather than being added to your existing ticket. In a situation like this, you can merge those tickets to keep the conversation in one place.
You can merge up to 3 tickets at once. Merging cannot be undone.

When viewing tickets in a List view, check the box to the left of the tickets to be merged, then select the “Merge” option at the top of the list.

The next screen will have you select which ticket will become the “Master Record.” The Master Record is the ticket that will be kept, while the others will be merged into the Master Record. Select the radio button above the ticket you want to make the Master Record, then click the blue Merge button at the bottom of the screen.

The last step will ask you to confirm that you want to merge the tickets and warn you that this action cannot be undone. Click “Yes, Merge” to confirm.

You may occasionally need to merge tickets in other situations, such as when multiple people create tickets for the same inbound call or when a client sends multiple emails about the same issue outside our business hours.

Be careful not to merge tickets only because they appear to be about the same issue. You must confirm that they are the same instance of the same issue being reported at the same time to merge tickets.

Split a Ticket

If a client responds to an old or existing ticket with a new issue, you should split that new message into its own ticket and handle it separately. Splitting new issues allows us to keep conversations focused and on track and to ensure tickets do not remain open for longer than a single issue requires.

Open the ticket and locate the message to be split into a new ticket. Click the three dots at the top right corner of that message in the thread and select “Split Into New Ticket”.

In this example, you can see that the ticket was resolved on March 28, but the client responded to it regarding an entirely different issue on April 28. This is a case where you would split the client’s email into a new ticket.

Close a Ticket

All tickets will end up Closed at the end of their lifecycle. Our goal as a team is to close tickets as quickly as possible, as soon as the client’s question is answered or the issue is resolved.

Most tickets can be closed after the first response is sent, as most tickets are created to ask a specific question. Once the question is answered, close the ticket. If the client responds with additional questions, the ticket will reopen automatically.

All other tickets should be Closed after 72 hours, though tickets that are Pending Development (in T2 Tech Support) or Pending Meeting (in CSM) may be open longer.

All fields listed in red text in Desk are required to close a ticket. If you try to close a ticket without filling in all required fields, Desk will not give you an error message or popup to remind you - it just will not close the ticket. If you are trying to close a ticket and it keeps showing as Open in your ticket list or team view, check to ensure all required fields are filled in.

To close a ticket, click the Close Ticket button in the bottom right corner of the ticket screen. An email notification will be sent to the ticket contact to notify them that the ticket has been closed.

Appendices

Items in bold are required for every ticket. Missing any one of these is an automatic audit failure.

Items in italic may not apply to every ticket and will only count towards failure if they are applicable on the specific ticket being audited. If not applicable, you automatically pass the italicized requirement.

Missing up to 3 requirements will result in a passing score. Missing 4 or more requirements will result in a failing score.*

Appendix B: Anatomy of a Ticket

Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Ticket Handling Between T1 and T2 (Process)

Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Ticket Handling Between T1 and T2

1. Purpose

This SOP outlines the responsibilities and procedures for handling tickets between the Tier 1 (T1) and Tier 2 (T2) support teams to ensure efficient resolution, proper communication, and client satisfaction.

2. Scope

This SOP applies to all T1 and T2 support agents responsible for ticket resolution and customer interactions.

3. Responsibilities

  • T1 Team: Initial triage, investigation, and customer communication.

  • T2 Team: Advanced troubleshooting and resolution of tickets.

4. Process Guidelines (T1 to T2)

4.1 Ticket Closure Responsibility

  • Any ticket assigned to T2 from T1 will be the responsibility of T2 to investigate, resolve, and close.

  • T2 must ensure that all troubleshooting steps are documented before closing the ticket.

4.2 Client Satisfaction (CSAT) Collection

  • Upon resolving and closing a ticket, T2 is responsible for obtaining a Client Satisfaction (CSAT) rating from the client.

  • T2 should send a follow-up email to the client requesting feedback and addressing any additional concerns.

4.3 Handling Improperly Investigated Tickets

  • If T1 assigns a ticket to T2 without proper investigation, or having lack of basic understanding of the product, T2 will document the issue on the ticket and notify the following individuals by tagging them:

    • Karan

    • Ronnie

    • Sabariranjan

  • These individuals will review the matter and provide feedback to the concerned T1 agent to ensure proper handling in the future.

4.4 Client Education Cases

  • If T2 identifies that the issue is due to a lack of client understanding rather than a technical issue, they will return the ticket to T1.

  • T1 will be responsible for educating the client on the relevant topic and ensuring the client has the necessary knowledge to prevent recurring issues.

  • In this case, T1 will be responsible for closing the ticket after the client’s education is completed.

5. Process Guidelines (CSM to T2)

5.1 CSM to T2 Ticket Handling

  • Any tickets assigned to T2 from Customer Success Managers (CSMs) will be handled exclusively by T2.
  • T2 will communicate directly with the client regarding the resolution and provide all necessary updates.
  • Once the resolution is communicated, T2 will close the ticket and get CSAT from the client.
  • For CSM tickets, any client education required will be managed by the T2 agent.

6. Process Guidelines (OB/Mark to T2)

6.1 Ticket Closure Responsibility

  • Any OB/Mark Tickets where a client is escalated or needs urgent resolution will directly go to T2.

  • Any other tickets go to T1 first and If T1 will not be able to resolve the issue they will add the required details to the ticket and pass it to the T2.

  • After requiring details added in the ticket and ticket being assigned to T2 from T1 or OB/Mark, will be the responsibility of T2 to investigate, resolve, and close.

  • T2 must ensure that all troubleshooting steps are documented before closing the ticket.

  • Once the resolution is determined, T2 will communicate directly with the client regarding the resolution and provide all necessary updates..

6.2 Handling Improperly Investigated Tickets

  • Any tickets transferred from OB/Mark to T1 must include a basic preliminary investigation conducted by OB/Mark. This ensures that the issue is well-defined and that T1/T2 receives sufficient context to proceed with troubleshooting.

  • T1/T2 is responsible for working on the resolution of the issue but will not engage in direct communication with the client to gather additional details. OB/Mark should provide all necessary background information before transferring the ticket.

  • If Mark/OB assigns a ticket to T2 without proper investigation, or having a lack of basic understanding of the product, T2 will document the issue on the ticket and notify the team leads by tagging them in the ticket.

  • These individuals will review the matter and provide feedback to the concerned Mark/OB Agent to ensure proper handling in the future.

6.3 Client Education Cases

  • If any ticket comes to T1 and T2 finds that there is a client education part then T2 will return the ticket to T1 so T1 can educate the client.
  • In cases where client education is necessary, OB/Mark will handle the communication and explanation to the client. They must ensure that the client understands the resolution and any preventative measures necessary to avoid similar issues in the future.

6.4 Client Satisfaction (CSAT) Collection

  • Upon resolving and closing a ticket, T2 is responsible for obtaining a Client Satisfaction (CSAT) rating from the client.

  • T2 should send a follow-up email to the client requesting feedback and addressing any additional concerns.

5. Compliance & Accountability

  • All agents must adhere to this SOP to maintain efficiency and improve client experience.
  • Any repeated failure to follow these procedures will be escalated to the management team for review and corrective action.

6. Review & Updates

  • This SOP will be reviewed periodically to ensure alignment with best practices and operational requirements.
  • Any modifications will be communicated to all team members in advance.

Process Corrections and Updates (Process)

Process Corrections and Updates

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. Adit Task Visibility

Task visibility works similarly to Asana, where access is determined by task association and collaboration.

  • Patient-associated tasks: Visible to all applicable users (Collaborators) within the practice.

  • Project-associated tasks: Visible only to users who are members of the associated project.

  • Tasks not associated with a patient or project: Visible only to users who have been added as collaborators on the task and the Assignee.

Users who are not members of a project cannot view its tasks unless they are explicitly added as Collaborators to those individual tasks.

2. Online Scheduling - Deposit Payments

When navigating to Online Scheduling > Booking Link, enabling the Payment Method option currently applies only to New Patients.

  • New Patients: Can be required to pay a deposit during the online scheduling process.
  • Existing Patients: Will not be prompted to pay a deposit when booking an appointment.

Support for requesting deposits from Existing Patients is currently under development and is planned for a future release.

3. Pediatric Teeth Chart (Coming soon)

Support for a pediatric teeth chart in Treatment Plans is planned for a future update. This enhancement will include the standard primary (child) dentition chart, where teeth are identified using alphabetical notation, in addition to the existing adult tooth chart.

4. Adit Server requirements

Minimum requirements for Server Application:
Operating System: Windows Server 2008 R2 SP1 and higher
Memory: 8 GB RAM
CPU: 4 cores at 2.4 GHz
Local Drive Install Space: At least 10 GB on C: Drive (or where the practice management software is located)
Internet:
Download Speed: 10mbps
Upload Speed: 3mbps

Recommended requirements for Server Application:
Operating System: Windows Server 2008 R2 SP1 and higher
Memory: 8 GB RAM
CPU: 4 cores at 2.4 GHz
Local Drive Install Space: At least 50 GB on C: Drive (or where the practice management software is located)
Internet:
Download Speed: 10mbps
Upload Speed: 3mbps

5. Automate Tracking and Calculation of Additional Provider Services

In the event that a practice wants to calculate additional services per provider from the patient notes, it cannot be directly pulled from there.
Adit does not pull detailed information from patient notes beyond what is displayed in the patient card, so it cannot automatically calculate additional services documented in notes.

A recommended approach is to use custom procedure or service codes in the EHR/PMS to identify additional techniques (such as medical tape). These codes can then be reported on through Patient Lists in Adit or by using the reporting capabilities available within the EHR/PMS, making it much easier to track and calculate additional compensation.

6. Custom Hold Music

Settings > Voice > Hold Music

Adit supports custom hold music, allowing practices to upload their own audio that patients hear while they are placed on hold.

Supported file formats

  • MP3
  • WAV

Maximum file size

  • 4.5 MB

Approximate maximum duration

  • MP3 (128 kbps): Up to approximately 4.7 minutes
  • MP3 (96 kbps): Up to approximately 6.3 minutes
  • MP3 (64 kbps): Up to approximately 9.3 minutes
  • WAV (uncompressed): Approximately 20-30 seconds due to the larger file size.

Playback behavior

  • Hold music plays in a continuous loop while the caller remains on hold.
  • If a caller is taken off hold and then placed on hold again, playback resumes from the current loop rather than restarting from the beginning.

7. Guarantor Information (Child Appointment) in AI Front Desk Scheduling

Currently, AI Front Desk does not capture or create guarantor information when scheduling appointments for children. Although Dentrix supports guarantor records (such as when a parent schedules for a child), the guarantor field is not mandatory for appointment booking. Appointments can be successfully created in Dentrix (on-premises) without adding guarantor information.

8. QR Code for Direct Payments

Each location is assigned a dedicated Direct Payment Link (Adit Pay) unique to that location. This link can be converted into a QR code using any QR code generator (3rd Party), allowing patients to quickly access the payment portal by scanning the code. The Direct Payment Link can also be embedded as a widget on the client’s website.

The QR code serves as a convenient general payment method for each location and can be displayed on the practice’s website or printed for in-office use.

When patients scan the QR code (OR Click the Direct Payment Link), they are directed to the practice’s payment portal (Secure Adit Portal), where they can choose to:

> Log in using their phone number to make a payment as an existing patient.
> Continue as a guest to complete a payment.

9. E-Fax Limits

There is no monthly limit on the number of pages that can be sent using E-Fax. Offices can send an unlimited number of fax pages without any monthly page cap.

The maximum supported attachment size for an outgoing E-Fax is 10 MB, and the file must be in PDF, JPG and JPEG formats. If a PDF exceeds 10 MB, it must be compressed or split into multiple files before sending.

10. Surcharging Feature (Coming soon)

Once the surcharging feature is released, practices will have the option to pass the payment processing fee on to patients as a convenience fee, which will be added to the total transaction amount.

The processing fees themselves will remain unchanged:

  • Card Present: 2.25% + $0.30 per transaction
  • Card Not Present: 2.90% + $0.30 per transaction

There will be no reduced fee for debit card transactions; debit and credit cards will continue to be subject to the same applicable processing rates.

11. Accommodating Patients with Special Scheduling Needs

Practices can accommodate patients with disabilities, chronic illnesses, or other unique scheduling requirements by creating custom questions on their online booking page. This allows patients to provide relevant information or special requests when scheduling an appointment, helping the practice identify and address any accommodations needed before the visit.

12. Syncing Communication Preferences from EHR

At this time, communication preference settings (opt-in/opt-out) from the EHR are not synchronized with Adit.

If a patient has been marked in the EHR as not wanting communications from the practice, that preference will not automatically import into Adit.
Practices must manually update the patient’s communication preferences manually within Adit to ensure they are opted out of communications.

Patient card > Patient info > Opt Out Settings > Manage

13. Preferred Language Field Mapping for Eaglesoft

For Eaglesoft version 23 and later, Adit supports mapping the patient’s Preferred Language directly from the dedicated Preferred Language field instead of relying on the Notes/Memo field.

This issue has already been identified and resolved. To apply the fix for the affected client, the Adit Server App simply needs to be updated to the latest version or reinstalled. Once completed, Adit will correctly read the patient’s Preferred Language from Eaglesoft, ensuring that appointment reminders are sent in the appropriate language.

14. Tax Inclusion in Subscription Pricing

The subscription price quoted to an office is tax-inclusive. The final amount presented already includes applicable taxes, and no additional tax is added at checkout.

15. Intercom Support on Grandstream Phones

The intercom functionality is supported on Grandstream phones. If your office currently uses an intercom feature with the existing phone system, a similar intercom feature can be configured on the new Grandstream phones.

16. eFax module enhancements:

  • PDF type selection for better fax quality

    Customers were seeing image quality drop when faxing (especially X-rays and CT scans). When sending a fax, users now pick a PDF type first:

    • PDF with Images
    • PDF without Images (text-based)

    We apply a compression method tuned to each type, so faxes go out at the best possible quality. Big win for practices faxing imaging. 🦷

  • Resend button + new fax statuses

    No more re-uploading a failed fax to try again. Users can now retry the same fax with one click.
    • New Resend button in the Action column for failed faxes and call pop

    • New statuses show what happened on retry:
    - Failed → first try failed
    - Retrying → user clicked on retry -> since its multiple attempts try mechanism (this status will be shown for time being) 🔁
    - Resent - Delivered → retry went through ✅
    - Resent - Failed → retry also failed❌

    • Resend can be used once per fax to prevent overuse.
    🔍 How the retry logic actually works (FYI)
    What looks like “one send” is actually a provider-fallback sequence:

    • First send: Telnyx (primary) attempts 3× → if all fail, Documo attempts 1×. Only after all 4 fail does it show Failed.

    • Resend: runs that same 4-attempt sequence again silently - the user just sees the final Resent - Delivered or Resent - Failed.

    • So a single fax can go through up to 8 delivery attempts (4 + 4) before it’s truly done, even though the user only clicks Resend once.

17. Supported Languages for AI Front Desk and SMS Agent

The AI Front Desk and SMS Agent currently support the following languages:

  • English (US)
  • Spanish (Spain)
  • French (France)
  • French (Canada)
  • German
  • Portuguese (Portugal)
  • Portuguese (Brazil)
  • Italian
  • Dutch
  • Japanese
  • Korean
  • Vietnamese
  • Chinese (Simplified, China)
  • Russian
  • Turkish
  • Polish
  • Arabic (Saudi Arabia)

For conversations handled in languages other than English, the conversation transcript remains in the original language (e.g., Spanish or French), while the AI-generated summary and other insights are provided in English. At this time, Adit does not offer an option to translate the transcript into English.

18. Address Field Requirement in Online Scheduling

The Address field is currently mandatory in Online Scheduling and cannot be configured as optional. In general, fields that are required in Online Scheduling correspond to fields that the connected EHR/PMS requires when creating a new patient record.
Most EHR softwares require an Address field to create a patient.

19. California Compliance for Call Recording and AI Front Desk

  • Call Recording: California is an all-party consent state, so all participants must be informed before a call is recorded. This requirement can be met by playing a recorded announcement in the call flow before transferring the call to the practice or the AI Front Desk.

  • AI Disclosure: When the AI Front Desk is used only for administrative tasks (such as scheduling, reminders, patient intake, or billing inquiries), California law does not require disclosing that callers are interacting with AI. However, practices can enable the AI Disclosure setting in AI Front Desk Settings if they wish to notify callers.

20. Ophthalmology Practice Support

Ophthalmology is part of Optometry.
Adit supports ophthalmology practices and can provide services such as phone systems, appointment reminders, online scheduling, digital forms, and other practice management features, provided the practice’s EHR/PMS integrates with Adit. Supported EHRs include Eyefinity and Crystal.

Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) is not supported for ophthalmology practices, as most patients require medical insurance verification, which is outside the scope of Adit’s RCM services.

21. Manual vs. Automated Pozative Review Requests

  • Manual review requests (sent individually, through Create Request, or via Bulk Request from Patient Lists) always send, even if the patient has already received a review request within the configured restriction period (e.g., 90 or 365 days). The frequency restriction does not apply to manually initiated requests.
  • Automated review requests do honor the configured frequency setting. Before sending, the system checks when the last review request (quick text) was sent and will not send another automated request if it falls within the configured time window.
  • If a practice sends a bulk manual review request to all patients, everyone in the selected list will receive it, including patients who have already received an automated review request within the last 365 days.
  • There is no built-in option to automatically exclude patients who have already received a review request when sending a manual bulk request.
  • As a workaround, practices can create patient segments based on the Last Appointment Date (for example, selecting patients whose last appointment was before a specific date) to reduce the likelihood of sending duplicate review requests. If the practice uses Practice Analytics, additional filtering options may be available.

22. 90-Day Password Reset Policy

On April 22, a security update was released requiring users to reset their passwords every 90 days. As users approach the end of each 90-day period, they will receive prompts to reset their password in accordance with this policy.

If a user is unable to receive the password reset email, a Manager or Owner can update the email address associated with the user’s account. Once the email address has been updated, the email can be sent to the new address.

Alternatively, users can initiate the Forgot Password process directly from the login screen without signing in. However, this method also relies on a password reset email being sent to the email address associated with the account.

Enter the Username and click Reset Password.

Open the email and follow instructions to complete the password reset and login with the new password

23. Insurance Verification With and Without Portal Credentials

Insurance verification can be performed for some insurance providers without portal login credentials, although the available information may be limited.

When portal login credentials are provided, Adit can retrieve the maximum amount of eligibility and benefits information available from the insurance portal, resulting in more comprehensive verification results.

24. ACH Payment Support

Support for ACH bank connects and account payments is currently in development and might be available in a future release.

25. Show/Hide Services on Booking Links

Practices can now choose which services can be shown on their custom booking link.
You can do this by:

  • Log in to Adit and Select the Online Scheduling module
  • Open up “Booking Link”
  • Scroll down to the list of services.
  • Click on the checkboxes beside each service to customize until desired results are achieved.

This feature makes it easy to tailor the booking experience to fit each practice’s needs. For example, a dental practice running a summer special for new patients can create a booking link that only shows “New Patient Exam” and “New Patient Consult”

26. New Cloud EHR Sync Reporting (CRM section is internal classified information)

For Cloud EHR customers syncing via chrome extensions, Adit now shows three new data points that tracks the sync:

  • Last Extension Sync
  • Last Backup Sync
  • Backup Sync Location

Why we built this:
These data points make it easy to spot customers who aren’t syncing properly, whether due to improper extension usage or to identify issues in the backup sync.

How it works:

  • Last Extension Sync: the last time any chrome extension successfully synced on the customer’s end
  • Last Backup Sync: the last time a backup sync ran
  • Backup Sync Location: shows whether the backup sync runs on a VM (Adit-managed) or on a chrome extension (fully dependent on the customer’s machine)

This info is visible in the Adit App, Admin Panel, and Zoho CRM (Adoption module).

Please note:

  • The Adit App updates every 5 minutes, admin panel every 30 minutes, and Zoho CRM only refreshes once a day. Always check the Adit App if you need the most current status.
  • The timezone is CST.

27. Mobile App Enhancements (Coming soon)

The Adit mobile app is currently being enhanced to include additional features such as Call Tracking, AI capabilities, and support for more Adit modules, bringing it closer to the functionality available in the web application and competing platforms.

These improvements are in the early stages; hence, there is no estimated release timeline available at this time.

28. Collecting Card Information Without an Upfront Charge (Coming soon)

This is not currently supported. At this time, Adit cannot collect and store a patient’s credit card information during online scheduling.

A patient’s card can only be saved on file in one of the following ways:

  • The patient completes a payment through a Quick Text payment request and chooses to save their card during the checkout process.
  • The practice already has the patient’s card information and manually saves it on file.

Support for collecting and securely storing a patient’s card during online booking without an upfront charge is on the product roadmap for a future release.

29. Online Scheduling Service Type Shows “No Results” for Location

If the Location dropdown displays “No Results” while creating a Service in Online Scheduling, preventing the service from being activated:

  1. Navigate to Settings > Application.
  2. Disable Online Scheduling.
  3. Re-enable Online Scheduling.
  4. Refresh the page and try creating the service type again.
  5. Repeat multiple times and this could help resolve the issue.

Toggling the Online Scheduling setting off and back on typically resolves the issue.

30. Yealink T46S Phone Support

The Yealink T46S is not supported by Adit.

Additionally, the manufacturer has designated the Yealink T46S as an End-of-Life (EOL) device, meaning it no longer receives ongoing support, updates, or maintenance. For this reason, the phone model is not supported for deployment with Adit.

31. Accessing the Mobile Interface on a Computer

Yes. Practices can access a mobile view from the desktop application, allowing them to use an interface that closely resembles the mobile experience while working on a computer.

The Mobile Interface button is on the top-middle of the Desktop Application.

Click on the Desktop Interface button to return back to the original layout.

32. Porting Phone Numbers from GoTo to Adit

Estimated Porting Timeline

  • Voice services: Typically completed within 5-7 business days, provided there are no rejections or delays from the current phone provider.
  • SMS services: May require an additional 2-3 business days after the voice port is completed. This is because GoTo uses Bandwidth for SMS services, and Bandwidth does not release SMS functionality on the voice port’s Firm Order Commitment (FOC) date.

Information Required for Porting

To port phone numbers from GoTo to Adit, the following information and documentation are required:

  • Account Name
  • Authorized Person’s Name
  • Account Number
  • Port-Out PIN
  • Service Address
  • Landline Number(s)
  • Fax Number(s) (if applicable)
  • Tracking Number
  • GoTo Customer Service Record (CSR) document

33. Mass Texts Sent Outside the Texting Window

If a user attempts to send a mass text outside of the configured texting window, the message is automatically declined and will not be sent.

34. Blacklisted Patients and Appointment Requests

Patients added to the blacklist are typically identified as spammers or malicious callers. For this reason, the system does not notify them that their appointment request has been rejected or ignored.

This behavior is intentional. Informing blacklisted users that their appointment was not scheduled could alert spammers that they have been blocked, potentially encouraging them to find alternative methods to continue spamming the practice.

35. eFax Sender Name Fields No Longer Required

As part of a recent CRM update, the First Name and Last Name fields were initially made required when sending an eFax. This created a usability issue for some clients, particularly when sending faxes to frequently used recipients such as insurance companies, pharmacies, or referral offices.

Following client feedback, the requirement has been removed and the change has been deployed to production. The First Name and Last Name fields are now optional when sending an eFax, allowing users to send faxes without completing these fields.

For frequently used recipients, users can still save their information as Fax Contacts. This makes it easier to send future faxes without having to re-enter the recipient’s information each time.

36. Appointment colors on the Adit schedule : Desktop vs Mobile

Colors that are selected on the Adit schedule on the desktop do not reflect as of now on the mobile app.

We can select a color for each appointment status:

This feature is coming soon for the mobile Application to reflect the same colors.

37. Importing Historical Texting and Call History

Adit does not support importing historical texting or phone-call logs from other vendors into the Adit platform. Porting existing communication logs, including text and call history, from a previous platform into Adit is not supported.

  • Historical SMS or call-history records from a previous vendor cannot be imported directly into Adit.
  • There is no option to upload CSV, ZIP, or other file formats containing historical communication records.
  • Previous vendor records cannot be added to Adit’s Call Tracking or Engage message threads.
  • Customers should retain their previous vendor’s records separately if they need access to historical communication data.

Parent/Child Ticket Guide (Process)

Scribe Demo Link: Click here

📂 Parent / Child Ticket Guide Adit T1 Customer Support • Zoho Desk A step-by-step guide to linking, grouping, and managing related tickets using the Parent / Child feature.
📋 What this guide covers • What Parent and Child tickets are, and when to use them • Key terms you need to know • Part A - How to link a parent ticket from the child ticket • Part B - How to add child tickets from the parent ticket
SECTION 1 - What Are Parent / Child Tickets?

Parent / Child ticketing is a Zoho Desk feature that lets you group multiple related tickets under one umbrella. Use it when a single issue generates multiple inbound contacts, or when a ticket needs to be split into sub-tasks.

📂 Parent Ticket The main umbrella ticket. Groups and tracks all related child tickets in one place. Think of it as: “the case that owns all the sub-issues.” 🏷️ Child Ticket A ticket linked under a parent. Can still be worked independently, but is grouped within the bigger issue. Think of it as: “a related ticket that feeds into the bigger picture.”

When should I use this?

📢 Widespread issue - Multiple customers report the same problem (e.g., login outage, OTP not arriving). Create one parent ticket for the issue, then associate each inbound ticket as a child.
🔧 Sub-tasks needed - A single complex ticket needs to be split into smaller tasks handled by different agents. Create child tickets for each sub-task under the parent.
🔗 Duplicate reports - Two or more tickets turn out to be about the same thing. Associate them as children under one parent - nothing gets lost.

Key Terms

Term What It Means
Parent Ticket The main umbrella ticket. It owns and tracks all child tickets beneath it.
Child Ticket A ticket linked under a parent. Can work independently but is grouped with the parent.
Associate Parent Ticket Action done on a child ticket to link it under an existing parent.
Associate Child Tickets Action done on a parent ticket to pull existing tickets in as children.
Dissociate Parent Removes the parent-child link. The ticket goes back to standalone status.
Child badge Label shown in the ticket header once it has been linked to a parent.
Parent badge Label shown in the ticket header once it has child tickets attached.
⚠️ Important Restrictions A child ticket can only have ONE parent. The following CANNOT be used as parents: tickets that are already child tickets, parents with more than 200 children, archived tickets, spam tickets, or tickets in the recycle bin.
SECTION 2 - PART A | Linking a Parent Ticket (from the child ticket)
Use Part A when: You are already on a ticket and need to attach it under an existing parent.
STEP 1 Open the child ticket Open the ticket you want to set as a child. It should have no parent linked yet - the Parent-Child tab will show “No Parent/Child Tickets associated.”
📸 Ticket #350339 is open. No parent linked yet - Parent-Child tab shows empty state.
STEP 2 Click the PARENT - CHILD tab In the ticket’s top navigation bar, click the “PARENT - CHILD” tab (sits between Resolution and Time Entry).
📸 Parent-Child tab is now active. Showing “No Parent/Child Tickets associated” - expected at this point.
STEP 3 Open the dropdown Click “Associate Parent/Child Tickets” (top-right of the view). A dropdown appears with two options - use the bottom section: “Associate Parent Ticket.” Do NOT click the top option (“Associate Child Tickets”) - that one makes this ticket a parent instead.
📸 Dropdown expanded. Top section = Associate Child Tickets. Bottom section = Associate Parent Ticket. Use the bottom one.
STEP 4 Search for the parent Click “Associate existing ticket.” A search modal opens. Type the parent ticket number or keyword. The matching ticket appears in the results.
📸 Search modal open. Ticket #350329 found in results. Associate button is grayed out until a ticket is selected.
STEP 5 Select and confirm Click the ticket row - a blue checkmark appears. The “Associate” button turns active blue. Click it to complete the link.
📸 Ticket #350329 selected (blue checkmark). Associate button is now active. Click to confirm.
STEP 6 Verify The Parent-Child tab now shows the linked parent ticket. The ticket header displays a “Child” badge. Part A is complete.
📸 Ticket #350339 is now a child of #350329. Parent Ticket section is populated. Header reads “Child.”
⚠️ Restriction Reminder A child ticket can only have ONE parent at a time. If you need to switch parents, click “Dissociate Parent” first, then re-associate.
SECTION 2 - PART B | Adding Child Tickets (from the parent ticket)
Use Part B when: You are on the parent ticket and want to pull related tickets in as children.

Parent/Child Ticket Guide (continued, part 1)

STEP 7 Open the parent ticket Navigate to the parent ticket. Open the Parent-Child tab. Any child tickets already linked will be listed here.
📸 Parent ticket #350329 open on the Parent-Child tab. One child ticket already attached.
STEP 8 Open Associate Child Tickets Click “Associate Child Tickets” (top-right dropdown) → “Associate existing tickets.” The search modal opens.
📸 Search modal open. Ticket #350337 found. Checkbox is unchecked and Associate button is grayed out.
STEP 9 Search, select, and click Associate Type the ticket number or keyword. Check the checkbox - the modal title updates to show the count (e.g., “Associate Child Tickets - 1”). The Associate button turns active blue. Click it.
📸 Ticket #350337 checked. Modal shows count. Associate button is active blue. Click to confirm.
STEP 10 Verify all child tickets are listed The Parent-Child tab now lists all child tickets with their ticket number, account, SLA timer, and a “Child” badge. Part B is complete.
📸 Parent #350329 now shows two children: #350323 and #350339. Both display the Child badge.
⚠️ Restriction Reminder Tickets already in a parent-child relationship, archived tickets, spam tickets, and tickets in the recycle bin cannot be associated as children.
SECTION 3 - Quick Reference & Agent Tips

Which method do I use?

Situation What to Do
I’m on the ticket and want to attach it under a parent Part A - Associate existing ticket (under “Associate Parent Ticket”)
I’m on the parent and want to pull in related tickets Part B - Associate existing tickets (under “Associate Child Tickets”)
Multiple customers report the same issue Create one parent, then use Part B to group all related tickets as children
I want to create a brand new sub-task ticket Part B → click “Create new child ticket”
I want to remove a parent link Child ticket → Parent-Child tab → “Dissociate Parent”

Agent Tips

✅ Always check if a parent ticket already exists before creating a new one. Search by account name or issue keyword.
✅ When a widespread outage hits (e.g., login issues, OTP failures), designate one ticket as the parent and group all related inbound tickets under it.
✅ You can select multiple child tickets in one go in the modal - just check all the boxes you need before clicking Associate.
✅ Closing a parent does NOT automatically close child tickets. Close each child separately as they are resolved.
✅ Child tickets still count toward your own queue. Owning a child ticket means you’re responsible for resolving it.
Adit T1 CS • Internal SOP • For Agent Use Only •

Authorization Guide - Zoho Desk Client Bugs Tab (Process)

Zoho Desk: How to Authorize the Adit Client Bugs Tab

Follow the steps below to authorize the Adit Client Bugs Tab extension in Zoho Desk.
Once authorized, you will be able to view and manage client bug information directly from any Zoho Desk ticket.

Step 1: Open a Zoho Desk Ticket

  • Navigate to a Zoho Desk ticket.
  • Click the three lines button in the top-right area of the ticket.
  • From the dropdown, select CLIENT BUG INFO.

Step 2: Click Authorize in the Client Bug Info Tab

The Client Bug Info tab will open and display a message: “Your authorization is required to continue.” Click the red Authorize button to proceed.

Step 3: Authorize the Zoho Desk Connection

  • You will be taken to the Adit Client Bugs Tab extension page.
  • A popup will appear indicating that Authorization is Required.
  • Under the Connections tab, click the Authorize link next to Zoho Desk.

Step 4: Connect to Zoho Desk

  • A dialog box will appear for the Zoho Desk service connection.
  • Click the Connect button.
  • This will redirect you to the Zoho Desk login page to grant permission for the connection.

Step 5: Accept Permissions

  • A Zoho permissions page will appear listing the data that DRE IDC would like to access.
  • Check the checkbox next to “I allow DRE IDC to access the above data from my Zoho account,” then click the Accept button.

Step 6: Authorization Successful

You will see an “Authorized Successfully” confirmation message.

Step 7: Return to the Client Bug Info Tab

Navigate back to your Zoho Desk ticket and click on the CLIENT BUG INFO tab. If the client bug status hasn’t been entered yet, the tab will display “No client bug details yet”

Step 8: Client Bug Info Tab - With Data

If the client bug status has already been set, the tab will display the full section.

To learn more about the client bug tabs read here:
Understanding the Client Bug Tab in Zoho Desk

Adit Zoho Desk SOP v3 (Process)

ADIT Zoho Desk Standard Operating Procedure Enterprise Customer Support Operations - Global Reference Guide Document Version: 3.0 - 2025 Replaces: SOP v1.0 (2022) & SOP v2.0 (2025) Classification: Internal - Confidential Applicable Teams: T1 CS (Calls & Chat), T2 Tech Support, T3 Engineering, OB, CSM, Billing Authority: Adit Customer Operations Leadership
Document Purpose This SOP defines the complete, enterprise-grade process for operating Zoho Desk across all client-facing teams at Adit. It covers the full ticket lifecycle, automation frameworks (Workflows, Blueprints, Macros, Assignment Rules), SLA management, role-based permissions, integrations (CRM, RingCentral, SalesIQ), reporting and KPIs, knowledge base management, and quality audit standards. It supersedes all prior SOP versions and is the single source of operational truth for customer support at Adit.

Adit Technologies • Customer Operations • INTERNAL & CONFIDENTIAL

Table of Contents

Section 1: Introduction & Purpose

1.1 About This Document

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is Adit’s authoritative operational guide for all support activity conducted through Zoho Desk. It serves two audiences: trainees learning the platform, and experienced agents and managers who need a reliable daily reference. Every process has been cross-referenced against Zoho Desk’s official documentation and aligned with Adit’s internal workflows, team structures, and escalation practices as of 2025.

1.2 Why Zoho Desk?

  • Single source of truth - all client interactions tracked in one platform regardless of inbound channel

  • Native CRM integration - contact, account, and deal data flows from Zoho CRM into every ticket

  • Automation-first - SLAs, workflow rules, blueprints, macros, and assignment rules reduce manual effort

  • Tier-aware routing - teams and queues reflect Adit’s T1/T2/T3 support model

  • Reporting & accountability - built-in and advanced analytics provide real-time visibility into performance

1.3 Scope of This Document

Dimension In Scope Out of Scope
Teams Covered T1 CS (Calls & Chat), T2 Tech Support, T3 Engineering & QA, Onboarding, Marketing CSM, Billing External vendors, client-side users
Platform Zoho Desk (web & mobile), Zoho CRM, Zoho SalesIQ, RingCentral Personal email, WhatsApp, ad hoc tools
Processes Ticket lifecycle, escalation, automation, SLAs, reporting, integrations, quality audits HR, payroll, product roadmap decisions

1.4 How to Use This Document

  • New agents: Read Sections 1-6 in order - these form the complete onboarding training sequence

  • T2 agents: Sections 5, 7, 8, and 10 cover escalation and automation in depth

  • T3 Engineers & QA: Sections 7 and 9 cover your queue management and client bug process

  • Managers & Team Leads: Sections 8, 10, 12, and 14 cover automation, SLAs, reporting, and quality

  • Quick reference: Appendices A-E contain checklists, field guides, routing tables, and glossary

Section 2: Scope, Definitions & Key Terminology

2.1 Core Platform Terminology

Term Definition
Ticket The core unit of work. Every support request - by email, phone, chat, or web form - becomes a ticket with a unique ID, status, owner, and full conversation history.
Department A logical grouping within Zoho Desk organized by product line or function. Each department can have its own SLAs, workflows, and views.
Agent Any individual with a Zoho Desk login. Agents can view and act on tickets based on their assigned Role and Profile.
Team A group of agents organized around a function or queue. Tickets can be assigned to teams, enabling any team member to claim unassigned work.
Role Defines data visibility hierarchy - which tickets and records an agent can see (own, team, department, or all). Roles are hierarchical in Zoho Desk.
Profile Defines feature-level permissions - which modules, actions, and settings an agent can access. Profiles are independent from Roles and must be assigned separately.
Ticket Owner The agent currently responsible for a ticket. Must always be set alongside the team assignment.
Contact The individual person associated with a ticket. Must be the actual client - not RingCentral, an Adit employee, or a third party.
Account The company or practice owner in Zoho CRM. One account can have multiple Deals (locations). Tickets and contacts link at the Account level.
Deal A single office or location in Zoho CRM. One Account can have many Deals.
Private Comment Internal-only note. Clients never see these. Shown with yellow background. Used for all investigation notes, handoffs, and tier-to-tier communication.
Conversation (Reply) Public email sent to the client from within the ticket. Visible to the client. T3 engineering agents NEVER use this.
CSAT / Happiness Rating Customer satisfaction feedback collected via automated survey after ticket closure. Results: Good, Neutral, Bad.
SLA Service Level Agreement - defined targets for first response time and resolution time.
Blueprint Structured process automation enforcing mandatory actions before ticket stage transitions.
Macro A saved set of one-click actions an agent applies manually to a ticket.
Workflow Rule An automated trigger-action rule that fires when a ticket meets defined conditions.
Assignment Rule Automatically routes new tickets to teams or agents based on defined criteria.

2.2 Adit-Specific Terminology

Term Definition
T1 / Tier 1 First line of support - basic configuration, how-to questions, initial troubleshooting. Split into Calls and Chat teams at Adit.
T2 / Tier 2 Second line - investigates and troubleshoots bugs. Owns the client relationship throughout the bug lifecycle. Escalates to T3 when developer help is needed.
T3 / Tier 3 Engineering and QA - code-level investigation and bug fixes. Does NOT communicate with clients. Returns resolved tickets to T2.
Client Bug Section Custom Zoho Desk ticket fields for T3 escalations: EHR, Bug Summary, Client Bug Status, Priority, T2 Owner, T3 Team, Expected Live Date, Live Date, Root Cause Analysis.
FIFO First In, First Out - the mandatory ticket pickup method. Oldest unassigned ticket must always be picked up first.
EHR / PMS Electronic Health Record / Practice Management System. Third-party software Adit integrates with (e.g., Dentrix, Revolution, Ascend).
RCA Root Cause Analysis - explanation of what caused a bug and how the fix addresses it. Required from T3 before returning a ticket to T2.
Cherry-Picking Selecting easy tickets while skipping harder ones. Strictly prohibited at Adit.

Section 3: Roles, Permissions & Responsibilities

3.1 Zoho Desk Permission Model

Zoho Desk uses two parallel permission layers. Both must be assigned to every agent:

Permission Layer What It Controls How to Configure
Role Data visibility - which tickets and records the agent can see. Hierarchical: higher roles see data from roles below. A Manager role sees all team agent tickets. Setup → Agents & Permissions → Roles
Profile Feature access - which modules, actions, and settings the agent can use. Granular per module (view/create/edit/delete/manage). Setup → Agents & Permissions → Profiles

3.2 Role & Responsibility Matrix

Role / Title Zoho Desk Role Primary Responsibilities Key Zoho Desk Access
T1 CS Agent (Calls & Chat) Agent Answer calls/chats, create and handle tickets, FIFO queue pickup, basic troubleshooting, follow-up, escalate to T2 Tickets: View/Create/Edit. No Setup access.
T2 Tech Support Agent Agent (elevated) Advanced troubleshooting, bug investigation, fill Client Bug section, route to T3 queue, own client comms throughout bug lifecycle, weekly client updates Tickets: Full. Client Bug section: Edit. Reports: View.
T3 QA Agent Agent (T3 profile) QA investigation of escalated bugs, validate staging fixes, update Client Bug Status, private comments only Tickets: View/Edit (assigned). NO Conversations/Reply tab.
T3 Engineer Agent (T3 profile) Code-level investigation, implement fixes, set Expected Live Date, write RCA, reassign back to T2 Owner Tickets: View/Edit (assigned). Client Bug fields: Edit. NO client comms.
T3 Queue Manager Team Lead Daily T3 queue triage, assign tickets to QA/engineer, report on queue health and blockers Full T3 team ticket view. Reports: View.
Team Lead / Manager Manager Team performance monitoring, ticket audits, SLA compliance, approve process changes, review reports Full team ticket access. Reports: Full. Setup: Limited.
Admin / Ops Administrator Full platform config: workflows, SLAs, blueprints, macros, teams, roles, profiles, integrations Full Setup access. All modules. Billing management.

3.3 Adding a New Agent - Procedure

  1. Log in as Administrator → Setup (⚙) → Agents & Permissions → Agents

  2. Click Invite Agent - enter email, first name, last name

  3. Assign Department (required at invite time; additional departments added later)

  4. Assign Role (data visibility) and Profile (feature permissions)

  5. Click Send Invitation - agent receives email to activate account

  6. After activation, verify agent appears in the correct Team: Setup → Agents & Permissions → Teams

4.2 Anatomy of a Ticket - Full Field Reference

Field / Section What It Is Who Fills / Updates It
Ticket ID Unique auto-generated identifier. Referenced in Asana engineering tasks. Auto-generated
Subject One-line summary shown to client as email subject. Must be descriptive and professional. Agent - edit on pickup if unclear
Status Current lifecycle stage. See Section 5 for complete status reference. Agent - updated at every handoff
Priority Low / Medium / High. Set by T2 on escalation. Affects SLA countdown and queue ordering. T2 agent (on escalation)
Contact Individual client who submitted the ticket. Must be the actual client - not RC, an Adit employee, or a vendor. Auto (email) or agent (manual/corrected)
Account Company/practice owner. Linked via Contact. All tickets for a multi-location client share one account view. Synced from CRM via contact
Classification Department category for reporting and routing. Selection changes available Category options. T1 / T2 agent
Category Sub-category of the issue. Dependent on Classification selected. T1 / T2 agent
Adit App Module Which product feature(s) are involved. Select all that apply; use -None- if no module involved. T1 / T2 agent
Potential Escalation/Churn Checkbox flag. Check if the issue has risk of client escalation or cancellation. Any agent
Deal Info Panel (left) Deal stage, CSM/OB owner, number of locations, industry - synced live from Zoho CRM. Synced from Zoho CRM
Client Bug Section Custom fields for T3 escalations: EHR/PMS, Bug Summary, Client Bug Status, Priority, T2 Owner, T3 Team, Expected Live Date, Live Date, RCA. T2 fills before escalating; T3 updates during work
Conversations tab Public email thread with client. NEWEST FIRST - scroll to bottom to read original. T3 NEVER uses this. T1 / T2 - client-visible
Comments tab Internal-only private comments. Yellow background. Clients never see this. All tiers
Activity / Timeline tab Auto-logged system changes: status changes, reassignments, field edits with timestamps. System auto-logs
Attachments tab All files uploaded across all messages and comments on the ticket. Any agent or client
🚨 Critical Thread Order Rule: Zoho Desk displays the thread NEWEST FIRST - the most recent message is at the TOP.
When opening a ticket for the first time: scroll to the BOTTOM to read the original issue, then read UPWARD.
This is the OPPOSITE of Asana. Getting this wrong means acting on outdated context and is a common new-agent mistake.

4.3 Conversations vs. Private Comments

Dimension Conversations (Reply) Private Comments (Internal)
Client visibility YES - client receives an email immediately NO - internal only, never emailed to client
When to use Status updates to client, requesting info, communicating resolution Investigation notes, handoff summaries, call logs, escalation details
Who uses it T1 and T2 agents ONLY ALL tiers - T1, T2, T3, OB, CSM
T3 Engineering NEVER - T3 does not contact clients under any circumstance ALWAYS - T3’s only communication method in tickets
Reply All button DO NOT USE - emails all thread recipients. Never click this. N/A
Visual indicator White/standard background in thread Yellow background - easily distinguishable

4.4 Agent Queue vs. Team Queue

Queue Type Description Primary Use
Agent Queue (My Queue) Tickets assigned directly to you as ticket owner. Your personal workload. Check every login. These need YOUR action today.
Team Queue All tickets for your team, including unassigned. Any team member can see these. FIFO pickup. Monitor team-wide load. Pick up unassigned tickets here.
Assignment Rule (Always) TEAM first, then AGENT. Never assign only to an agent without a team. A ticket with no team is invisible to managers and teammates - a critical process failure.

Section 5: Ticket Lifecycle - End to End

5.1 Ticket Creation Channels

Channel How Ticket is Created Initial Status Required Agent Action
Email to support at adit.com Auto-created from sender email. Contact auto-populated. OPEN Verify Contact & Account. Fix Subject if vague. Update Classification and Category.
Inbound Call (RingCentral) T1 agent manually creates ticket after answering. Channel = Phone. OPEN Fill all fields. Set Channel = Phone. Handle immediately.
Voicemail / Missed Call RC notification email auto-creates ticket with RingCentral as contact. OPEN CHANGE CONTACT from RingCentral to actual client. Call back. Follow-up email.
Live Chat (Zoho SalesIQ) Chat converted to ticket via SalesIQ integration. OPEN Verify Contact & Account. If resolved in real time, close immediately with summary note.
Help Widget (Adit Dashboard) Client submits via embedded widget. Auto-created. OPEN Verify all fields. Treat same as email inbound.
Manual Creation by Agent Agent clicks + button. Used when no ticket was auto-created. OPEN Leave Description blank (it auto-emails client). Set Channel correctly. Assign team + self.
⚠️ Description Field Warning: NEVER put text in the Description field when manually creating a ticket. The Description auto-emails the client when the ticket is created. Use a Private Comment for all internal notes.

5.2 Ticket Status Reference

Status Meaning Who Sets It When to Use / Key Notes
Open Needs immediate attention Any agent; auto on creation Default at creation. Use when escalating or reassigning - signals new owner must act now.
Pending Customer Waiting on client response or action T1 / T2 Only use when you CANNOT proceed without the client’s response. Not for optional follow-ups.
Pending Adit Internal work in progress, agent managing client comms T1 / T2 Use when you own client comms AND are coordinating internally. Do NOT use if handing off entirely - use Open instead.
Pending Meeting Awaiting a scheduled meeting CSM / OB / T2 Requires meeting date/time documented in a Private Comment on the ticket.
Pending Dev Escalated to T3 engineering for code-level fix T2 (before T3 handoff) Set by T2 when all Client Bug fields are completed and ticket is being reassigned to T3 queue.
Under Observation Fix deployed; monitoring period before closing T2 / T3 Used after a bug fix goes live. Monitor before closing to confirm the resolution holds.
Closed Fully resolved Any agent ALL red-label required fields must be completed. Zoho Desk silently refuses to close if fields are missing.
⚠️ Silent Close Failure: If you click ‘Close Ticket’ and the ticket remains Open - a required red-label field is missing
Zoho Desk gives no error message
Check every red field before trying again

5.3 Ticket Status Flow Diagrams

T1 Direct Resolution (simple tickets):

STEP 1 OPEN Ticket created STEP 2 PENDING ADIT T1 investigating STEP 3 PENDING CUSTOMER Awaiting client info STEP 4 CLOSED Issue resolved

Full Bug Lifecycle - T1 → T2 → T3:

STEP 1 OPEN T1 creates / T2 picks up STEP 2 PENDING DEV T2 → T3 escalation STEP 3 T3 ACTIVE QA / Dev working STEP 4 UNDER OBS Fix live; monitoring STEP 5 CLOSED Confirmed resolved
