Section 6: Tier 1 Operations - Step-by-Step Procedures

6.1 Daily Login & Queue Routine

  1. Open Zoho Desk → navigate to Team Queue → [Your Team Name]

  2. Sort by Date Received: oldest first. Identify all unassigned tickets.

  3. Pick up the OLDEST unassigned ticket first - FIFO is mandatory

  4. Review Agent Queue: action all tickets assigned to you today

  5. Check Pending Customer tickets: follow up on any not responded to in 1-2 days

  6. Check Pending Adit tickets: confirm internal progress; email client if 7+ days since last update

🚫 FIFO is Mandatory: Cherry-picking tickets to avoid difficult ones is strictly prohibited at all times
Every client deserves support in the order they contacted us
Violations are subject to audit action

6.2 Handling a Ticket - Full Procedure

Step 1: Assign the Ticket Correctly

  1. Click Ticket Owner field → click TEAMS → select your team → click user icon → select yourself

  2. Confirm the owner field shows BOTH team name AND your name - both are required

[ SCREENSHOT PLACEHOLDER ] Zoho Desk - Ticket Owner field showing Team + Agent assignment dropdown

Step 2: Update All Required Fields First

Field What to Check / Do
Contact Is it the actual client? If it shows RingCentral, an Adit employee, or a vendor - change it (see Section 6.6).
Account Is an account linked? If the Account field is blank, edit the Contact to add the correct CRM account.
Subject Does it clearly describe the issue? Rewrite if vague (e.g., ‘Help’ or ‘Issue’ - not acceptable).
Classification Select the correct department category for this issue.
Category Select based on classification. Options change dynamically depending on classification chosen.
Adit App Module Select all product modules involved. Use -None- if no Adit app module is involved.
Status Should be OPEN when picked up. Change as the ticket progresses.
Potential Escalation/Churn Check this box if the issue could lead to client escalation or cancellation.

Step 3: Read the Ticket (Bottom-Up)

  • Scroll to the BOTTOM of the thread - the original client message is at the bottom

  • Read the thread upward (chronologically) to understand the full conversation context

  • Check the Deal Info panel on the left: deal stage, industry, number of locations, current CSM or OB

  • Check if another agent is working on this same issue in a different open ticket → if yes, assign the new ticket to them to merge

Step 4: Investigate & Document

  • Investigate the issue systematically - document EVERY step in a Private Comment, not the Description

  • Use the Investigation Log template (see Section 13.2)

  • Log into the client’s Adit account if needed to replicate the issue

Step 5: Respond to the Client

  • All tickets must receive their first response within 3 business hours of ticket creation (SLA requirement)

  • If on a call: send a follow-up email summarizing the call immediately after hanging up

  • If you leave voicemail: send a follow-up email at the same time - do not wait

  • Use the Conversations (Reply) tab only - never the Comments tab for client communication

Step 6: Resolve, Escalate, or Set Pending

  • If resolved: click Close Ticket. Client receives automatic closure notification.

  • If awaiting client: set status to Pending Customer. Follow up every 1-2 days.

  • If T2 expertise is needed: complete pre-escalation checklist (Section 6.5) first.

6.3 Follow-Up Standards

Ticket State Follow-Up Frequency Required Action
Pending Adit / Pending Dev / Under Observation Check every 1-2 days Verify internal progress. Email client update at least once per week. If no email, leave Private Comment confirming you checked.
Pending Customer Reach out every 1-2 days Alternate calls and emails. If voicemail → send email same time.
Pending Meeting Check before meeting date Confirm meeting is scheduled. Update ticket immediately after meeting.
No response for 5 business days Begin Closeout Process Follow Unresponsive Client Closeout Process (Section 6.4).

6.4 Unresponsive Client Closeout Process

📌 Exception: If the ticket was created by Adit (not the client) and is required for ongoing business (billing, onboarding, contract) - continue weekly follow-ups indefinitely
Do NOT close on Day 10
Business Day Action Template Status
Days 1-5 Follow up every 1-2 days, alternating calls and emails No template - personalized Pending Customer
Day 6 Send Day 6 unresponsive email template Unresponsive Client - 6th Day Pending Customer
Day 8 Send Day 8 unresponsive email template Unresponsive Client - 8th Day Pending Customer
Day 10 - Call Final call attempt. Leave voicemail if no answer. Voicemail message Pending Customer
Day 10 - Unreachable Leave voicemail + send Day 10 template + CLOSE Unresponsive Client - 10th Day → CLOSED
Day 10 - Info received Continue handling normally No template needed → Normal handling
Day 10 - No info Return to Day 6 and restart follow-up cycle Restart from Day 6 template Pending Customer

6.5 T1 → T2 Pre-Escalation Checklist

  • Settings and configuration checked on client’s account

  • Issue replicated or confirmed unreplicable (documented either way)

  • Private Comment written: client’s words, your hypothesis, every step taken, every result

  • Client informed of escalation and given expected response timeframe

  • All ticket fields updated: Contact, Account, Subject, Classification, Category, Module

  • Status set to OPEN before reassigning

  • Ticket reassigned to correct T2 team

6.6 Changing a Contact on a Ticket

  1. Click the three dots (⋯) at the top right of the ticket screen → select Edit

  2. In Contact Name field, click the X to clear the existing contact

  3. Search for the correct contact by name, email, or account name

  4. Click the correct suggestion from the dropdown to select them

  5. Click Save

6.7 Merging & Splitting Tickets

When to Merge

  • Client’s response creates a new ticket instead of replying to the original

  • Multiple agents create tickets for the same inbound call

  • ONLY merge if you are certain these are the SAME issue occurrence - not just similar issues

  • Maximum 3 tickets per merge. Merging CANNOT be undone.

Merge Steps

  1. In list view, check the box to the left of each ticket to merge

  2. Click Merge at the top of the list

  3. Select the Master Record (all others merge into this ticket)

  4. Click Merge → confirm with ‘Yes, Merge’

Splitting Tickets

Split when a client replies to an old resolved ticket with a completely new unrelated issue.

  1. Open the ticket → find the message to split

  2. Click three dots at the top right corner of THAT MESSAGE in the thread

  3. Select ‘Split Into New Ticket’ → handle the new ticket following standard procedure

Section 7: Tier 2 → Tier 3 Escalation - Client Bug Process

7.1 When T2 Escalates to T3

  • T2 has replicated and investigated the bug - it requires a code-level fix

  • The bug cannot be resolved through configuration changes or known workarounds

  • The issue involves an EHR/PMS integration failure, product module defect, or platform-level failure

7.2 Completing the Client Bug Section - T2 Responsibility

This is the Zoho Desk replacement for the old Asana client bug task. Everything lives here now.

Client Bug Field What to Enter
EHR / PMS Specific EHR or PMS system involved (e.g., Revolution EHR, Dentrix, Ascend)
Bug Summary One-line summary - equivalent to the old Asana task name
Client Bug Status Set to OPEN when creating the escalation
Priority Level Low / Medium / High - based on client impact and number of locations affected
T2 Owner Your name - T3 uses this to know who to reassign the resolved ticket back to
T3 Team Relevant T3 team based on issue type (see Section 7.3)
Bug Summary from T2 Perspective Full description: client complaint, investigation steps, what was replicated, what was ruled out
Expected Live Date Leave blank - T3 fills this once they have an engineering ETA
Live Date Leave blank - T3 fills this when the fix is deployed to production
Root Cause Analysis Leave blank - T3 writes this when the fix is deployed and confirmed

7.3 T3 Team Routing Reference

T3 Team Route Here For… Example EHRs / Modules
Cloud Integrations Cloud-based EHR/PMS sync failures Ascend, Curve, Denticon, Cloud9, Eyefinity, Revolution EHR, Jane, CT Cloud
OnPrem Integrations Server-installed EHR/PMS sync failures Dentrix, OpenDental, PracticeWeb, AbelDent, Dolphin, Eaglesoft, Cleardent, Crystal PM
Adit Pay / CRM / Tasks Payment processing, CRM data, task module bugs Adit Pay, Financing, Patients Module, CRM Build, Task Module
Practice Analytics Reporting, patient list, segment data issues Practice Analytics, Patient Lists, Segments
Online Scheduling Appointment booking, scheduler sync, API failures Online Scheduling, Scheduler, Sync APIs
Forms / Reminders Patient form submission, auto-assign, recall reminders Patient Forms, Auto-Assign, Form Reminders, Recall Report
Mobile / Engage / Settings Mobile app bugs, SMS, settings, onboarding features Mobile App, Engage SMS, Internal Chat, Pozative, Settings
VoIP Call quality, call handling, call log data VoIP Call Quality, Call Logs, Call Handling
RCM Revenue cycle management and verification issues Verifications

7.4 Reassigning to T3 Queue - T2 Steps

  1. Complete ALL Client Bug fields (Section 7.2)

  2. Write a final comprehensive Private Comment: what was investigated, what T3 needs to do, screenshots

  3. Set ticket Status to PENDING DEV

  4. Ticket Owner → TEAMS → locate the correct T3 queue → assign to team (leave individual blank)

  5. Inform the client: issue escalated to engineering team, updates will continue weekly

✅ T2 Retains Client Ownership: Even after reassigning the ticket to T3, T2 is still responsible for ALL client communication.
T2 must send the client a status update at least once per week while the bug is being worked on.
T3 NEVER contacts the client at any stage of their investigation or fix work.

7.5 T3 Investigation & Status Update Flow

T3 Stage Responsible Client Bug Status Key Actions Required
Initial Queue Triage T3 Queue Manager Open (unchanged) Read all T2 notes and Client Bug fields. Assign to appropriate QA or engineer.
QA Investigation QA Agent QA Investigation Replicate the bug. Check logs. Document all findings in Private Comment.
Dev Code Review Engineer Dev Investigation Code-level root cause analysis. Document findings.
Fix Development Engineer Under Development Set Expected Live Date immediately. Update as ETA changes.
Staging Validation QA Agent QA Review Stage Validate fix on staging/local. Document pass/fail and any edge cases.
Production Deployment Engineer Ready to Go Live → Solved and Deployed Deploy fix. Set Live Date. Write RCA. Reassign to T2 Owner. Status = Open.
Bug Recurrence T3 Queue Manager Reopened Re-investigate. Treat as new escalation.
Blocked T3 Queue Manager On Hold Document what is blocking progress. Notify T2 Owner.

7.6 Returning Resolved Ticket to T2 - T3 Steps

  1. Update Client Bug Status to ‘Solved and Deployed’

  2. Fill in Live Date field with today’s production deployment date

  3. Write Root Cause Analysis in the RCA field - plain language T2 can understand and summarize for the client

  4. Leave a Private Comment: what was fixed, the RCA, and instructions for T2

  5. Look up T2 Owner field - this is who you are returning the ticket to

  6. Reassign: Team = T2 Owner’s team, Agent = T2 Owner’s name

  7. Set Status = OPEN so T2 sees it in their queue immediately

Section 8: Automation - Workflows, Blueprints, Macros & Assignment Rules

8.1 The Four Automation Tools

Tool What It Does When to Use vs. Others
Workflow Rules Auto-trigger actions when tickets are created, edited, or fields updated: send alerts, update fields, assign tickets, fire webhooks. Use for background automation that should happen every time a condition is met - no agent action required. Example: auto-alert manager on SLA breach.
Macros One-click sets of saved actions applied manually by agents to individual tickets: field updates, status changes, email sends, private comment posts. Use for situation-specific actions that need agent judgment. Example: agent clicks ‘Voicemail Follow-Up’ macro - it sends the template email and sets status in one click.
Blueprints Structured process maps that enforce mandatory steps between ticket state transitions. A ticket CANNOT move to the next state without completing required actions. Use to enforce critical processes that must never be skipped. Example: T2 cannot set status to Pending Dev until all Client Bug fields are completed.
Assignment Rules Automatically route new tickets to specific teams or agents based on criteria (channel, keywords, contact, classification) at ticket creation. Use for initial routing only - when a new ticket arrives and needs to be directed to the correct queue immediately.

8.2 Workflow Rules - Configuration Guide

Navigate to: Setup (⚙) → Automation → Workflow Rules → New Rule

Component Configuration Options
Module Always select ‘Tickets’ for support workflow rules.
Trigger On Create (new ticket), On Edit (any field changed), On Field Update (specific field only - more precise), Date-Based (fires at interval after a date field, e.g., 2 days after Due Date)
Criteria Conditions ticket must meet for rule to fire. AND/OR logic. Up to 25 criteria per rule.
Actions Send Email Alert, Create Task, Update Field, Assign Agent/Team, Fire Webhook.

Recommended Workflow Rules for Adit

Rule Name Trigger + Criteria → Action
Auto-flag RC voicemail tickets On Create | Contact contains ‘RingCentral’ → Tag: ‘contact-change-needed’, Assign to T1 Calls team
Alert on Potential Churn On Field Update | Potential Escalation/Churn = Checked → Email alert to Team Lead with ticket link
Notify T2 when T3 returns ticket On Edit | Status = Open AND Client Bug Status = Solved and Deployed → Email alert to T2 Owner field value
Weekly Pending Customer reminder Date-Based | Status = Pending Customer, trigger 5 days after last modified → Create Task for ticket owner: ‘Follow up or close’
High Priority bug alert On Field Update | Priority = High AND Client Bug Status = Open → Email T3 Queue Manager
SLA pre-breach warning SLA Escalation Rule | 30 min before First Response SLA breach → Notify assigned agent
[ SCREENSHOT PLACEHOLDER ] Zoho Desk - Workflow Rule configuration screen (Setup → Automation → Workflow Rules → New Rule)

8.3 Macros - Creating & Using

Navigate to: Setup (⚙) → Automation → Macros → New Macro

  1. Enter a descriptive name (e.g., ‘Voicemail Follow-Up Email Sent’)

  2. Add actions in sequence - each runs in order when the macro is applied

  3. Set visibility: Only Me (personal) or All Agents (team-shared)

  4. Save. The macro appears in the Macros dropdown inside any ticket.

Macro Name Actions Configured
Voicemail Follow-Up Sent 1. Send template ‘Voicemail Follow-Up Email’ 2. Add Tag ‘voicemail-left’ 3. Set Status = Pending Customer
Unresponsive Day 6 1. Send template ‘Unresponsive Client - 6th Day’ 2. Set Status = Pending Customer 3. Private Comment: ‘Day 6 template sent [date]’
Close - Resolved 1. Send template ‘Resolution Confirmation’ 2. Set Status = Closed
T3 Ticket Returned - Action Needed 1. Private Comment: ‘Bug resolved by T3. Fix is live. Review RCA and update client.’ 2. Set Status = Open

8.4 Blueprints - Enforcing the T2 → T3 Process

Navigate to: Setup (⚙) → Process Automation → Blueprints → New Blueprint

💡 Recommended Blueprint - T2 to T3 Escalation: State 1 (Open): T2 investigating. Transition to ‘Pending Dev’ requires: EHR/PMS not empty, Bug Summary not empty, T2 Owner not empty, T3 Team not empty, Bug Summary from T2 Perspective not empty.
State 2 (Pending Dev): T3 working. Each sub-stage transition updates Client Bug Status and can require a Private Comment before proceeding.
State 3 (Returned to T2): Auto-notify T2 Owner when T3 completes and reassigns ticket.
This Blueprint prevents tickets from being sent to T3 with incomplete information - the most common failure mode in the escalation process.

8.5 Assignment Rules - Initial Ticket Routing

Navigate to: Setup (⚙) → Automation → Assignment Rules

New Ticket Condition Criteria → Assignment Action
Email inbound to support at adit.com Channel = Email AND no Classification set → Assign to Team: T1 Customer Support (round-robin)
RingCentral auto-ticket Contact Name contains ‘RingCentral’ → Assign to Team: T1 Calls + Tag: ‘contact-correction-needed’
Adit Pay keyword in subject Subject OR Description contains ‘Adit Pay’ OR ‘payment’ → Assign to Team: TS - Specialty
SalesIQ chat origin Channel = Chat → Assign to Team: T1 Chat
Onboarding client deal stage Deal Stage = Onboarding → Assign to Team: TechOB Routing

Section 9: Views, Queues & Custom Filter Management

9.1 Creating a Custom View - Step by Step

  1. Tickets module → left panel → Views → click the + (plus) icon

  2. Enter a descriptive View Name (e.g., ‘T3 Cloud Integrations - Open Bugs’ or ‘My Pending Customer Tickets’)

  3. Add Filter Criteria using AND/OR logic. Examples by role:

    • T1 agent: Assignee = Me AND Status = Open

    • T2 agent: T2 Owner = Me AND Client Bug Status is not Solved and Deployed

    • T3 queue manager: Team = [T3 Team] AND Status = Open AND Assignee is empty

  4. Click Manage Columns - select which fields appear in the list

  5. Recommended columns: Ticket ID, Subject, Contact/Account, Status, Priority, Client Bug Status, EHR/PMS, T2 Owner, Expected Live Date, Ticket Owner

  6. Set Visibility: Only Me, All Agents, or Specific Agents

  7. Click Create - view appears in your sidebar under Views

Section 10: SLA Policies & Escalation Matrix

10.1 SLA Concepts in Zoho Desk

SLA Concept Detail
First Response Time (FRT) Clock starts at ticket creation. Stops when first outbound reply sent to client. Adit target: 3 business hours for T1.
Resolution Time Total time allowed from creation to closure. Varies by tier and priority.
Business Hours SLA clocks count business hours only (configured in Setup → Business Hours). After-hours ticket creation does not penalize agents.
SLA Breach Ticket passes its SLA target without the required action. Zoho Desk marks it overdue and triggers escalation rules.
Pause on Pending Customer SLA clock pauses when status = Pending Customer. Resumes when client responds.
Happiness Rating (CSAT) Auto-survey sent to client after ticket closure. Client clicks Good / Neutral / Bad. Visible in ticket history and Customer Happiness report.

10.2 Adit SLA Policy Targets

Tier / Priority First Response Target Resolution Target Notes
T1 - All inbound 3 business hours Same business day (standard issues) Primary SLA. Audited in weekly reports.
T2 - High Priority 1 business hour (from T2 assignment) 5 business days (target) Based on client impact and affected locations.
T2 - Medium Priority 4 business hours (from T2 assignment) 10 business days (target) Most common T2 bug category.
T2 - Low Priority 1 business day (from T2 assignment) 20 business days (target) Non-urgent cosmetic or minor bugs.
T3 - Engineering Internal SLA (not client-facing) Tracked via Expected Live Date field Set by engineer once investigation is complete.

10.3 Configuring SLA Policies (Admin)

Navigate to: Setup (⚙) → Automation → SLAs → New SLA Policy

  1. Enter Policy Name (e.g., ‘T1 Standard - 3hr First Response’)

  2. Select Department and Working Hours schedule

  3. Define criteria that triggers this SLA (e.g., Priority = Standard, Team = T1 Customer Support)

  4. Set First Response Time target and Resolution Time target

  5. Save and activate the policy

[ SCREENSHOT PLACEHOLDER ] Zoho Desk - SLA Policy configuration screen (Setup → Automation → SLAs → New SLA Policy)

10.4 Escalation Rules within SLAs

Escalation Level Trigger Recommended Action
Level 1 - Warning 30 minutes before First Response SLA breach Email notification to assigned agent: ‘Ticket [ID] about to breach first response SLA.’
Level 2 - At Breach At the moment of First Response SLA breach Email to agent AND Team Lead. Add tag ‘sla-breached’.
Level 3 - Post Breach 2 hours after First Response SLA breach (unresponded) Notify Manager. Consider reassigning to senior agent.
Resolution Warning 24 hours before Resolution Time breach Email to agent and T2 owner if applicable.
Resolution Breach At Resolution Time breach Email to Manager. Flag in reports. Add tag ‘resolution-sla-breached’.

Section 13: Note-Taking & Documentation Standards

13.1 The Standard - What Makes a Good Private Comment?

Quality Standard What It Means in Practice
Complete Contains everything the next agent needs to act. No need to re-read the thread or contact the previous agent.
Chronological Structured in the order events happened - issue, investigation steps in sequence, result of each step.
Specific Includes exact field names checked, setting values, error messages, reproduction steps, and results.
Actionable Ends with a clear statement of what comes next.
Screenshot-Supported Attach screenshots when they provide evidence of the issue or the fix.

13.2 Note Templates

Phone Call Log Template

📞 CALL LOG Date/Time: [Date & time of call] Spoke with: [Full name of person] Callback number: [Phone number] Follow-up preference: [Phone / Email] - [Email if email preferred] Summary: [Everything discussed - questions asked, answers given, configs changed, troubleshooting done, outcomes reached] Next steps: [What happens next - waiting on client / escalating / closing / etc.]

Investigation / Troubleshooting Log Template

🔍 INVESTIGATION LOG Issue as reported by client: [Client’s exact words / complaint] My understanding of the issue: [Your interpretation / hypothesis] Steps taken to investigate: Step 1: [What you did] → Result: [What happened] Step 2: [What you did] → Result: [What happened] Step 3: [What you did] → Result: [What happened] Conclusion: [Resolved / Unable to replicate / Needs T2 escalation / Root cause identified] Next steps: [Close / Escalate to T2 with reason / Await client / etc.]

T3 Resolution Summary Template (Before Returning to T2)

✅ T3 RESOLUTION SUMMARY Fix deployed to production: [Live Date] What was fixed: [Plain-language description of the fix - what changed and why] Root Cause Analysis: [What caused the bug - specific technical root cause in plain language] T2 Owner - please verify the fix with the client and close the ticket once confirmed.

Section 14: Quality Standards, Audit Checklist & Best Practices

14.1 Ticket Audit Checklist

Managers use this checklist during random ticket audits. BOLD items are automatic failures if missing. Italic items are conditional - only apply if that situation arose in the ticket. Pass threshold: missing 3 or fewer applicable items.

ASSIGNMENT & ROUTING

  • Ticket picked up in FIFO order (oldest unassigned first)

  • Assigned to Team first, then Agent - not directly to agent alone

  • [If escalating] T1 pre-escalation checklist fully completed before reassigning to T2

  • [If reassigned] Routed to the correct team per routing reference

TICKET FIELDS

  • Correct contact - not RingCentral, Adit employee, or vendor

  • Account is linked to the contact and visible on the ticket

  • Subject line is descriptive, professional, and accurate

  • Classification appropriate for ticket content

  • Category appropriate given classification selected

  • All relevant Adit App Modules selected (or -None-)

  • Status accurately reflects current ticket state

  • [If T3 escalation] All Client Bug fields completed before status = Pending Dev

COMMUNICATION

  • First response sent within 3 business hours of ticket creation

  • Client received email update at least once per week on any pending ticket

  • [If voicemail] Follow-up email sent at the same time as voicemail

  • [If Pending Customer 5+ days] Unresponsive Client Closeout Process followed

  • All outbound emails are professional, clear, and grammatically correct

HANDLING & PROCESS

  • [If applicable] Merge or Split performed when appropriate

  • Ticket closed promptly when resolved - not left in pending unnecessarily

  • Private comments left every 2-3 days on any pending ticket

  • [If T3 return] T2 notified, client updated, ticket closed or set to Under Observation

NOTES QUALITY

  • Notes are clear, complete - next agent can act without additional context

  • Required templates and team-specific note formats followed

  • [If phone call] Log includes: name, callback number, email preference, full summary

  • [If troubleshooting] Log includes: client issue, steps, results, resolution or next step

  • [If T3] RCA written in plain language before ticket returned to T2

14.2 Audit Scoring

Score Criteria
PASS Missing 3 or fewer applicable checklist items. Coaching may be recommended for recurring gaps.
FAIL Missing 4 or more applicable checklist items. Formal coaching session required.
AUTO-FAIL ANY single BOLD item missing - automatic failure regardless of all other items.

14.3 Best Practices

For All Agents

  • Log into Zoho Desk before taking any calls or chats at the start of every shift

  • Update ticket fields as you work - not at end of day. Stale fields confuse teammates and managers.

  • Never use personal email to communicate with clients about support issues

  • If unsure which team to route to - use the catch-all routing team (TS Routing / TechOB Routing)

For Team Leads & Managers

  • Review SLA compliance reports weekly. Address breach patterns before they become trends.

  • Conduct random ticket audits at least twice per month per agent

  • Review bad Happiness Ratings within 24 hours and conduct call review with the agent

  • Keep workflows, macros, and SLA policies reviewed quarterly - automation must keep pace with evolving processes

For T3 Engineers & QA

  • Never communicate directly with a client - all client comms go through T2, always

  • Update Client Bug Status every time the ticket changes hands or stage

  • Set Expected Live Date as soon as you have an engineering estimate

  • Write RCA in plain language - T2 agents who are not engineers must be able to understand and summarize it for the client

Appendix C: Client Bug Status Quick Reference

Client Bug Status Meaning / When to Set It
Open T2 escalated; T3 queue has the ticket but no individual has claimed it yet
QA Investigation QA agent actively investigating - replicating the issue, checking logs
Dev Investigation Engineer reviewing code and investigating the technical root cause
Under Development Fix actively being coded. Set Expected Live Date as soon as ETA is known.
QA Review Stage Fix deployed to staging/local. QA validating the fix works correctly.
Ready to Go Live QA approved. Pending production deployment.

Term Definition

Role Permission layer defining data visibility hierarchy.

Ticket Core unit of work. Every support request becomes a ticket with a unique ID and full history.
Ticket Owner Agent currently responsible for a ticket. Must always be set alongside the team.

CSR Automation - Process Document (Product)

CSR Automation - Process Document (Zoho CRM → Asana)

1) Introduction & Purpose

This document defines the end‑to‑end automation to generate and deliver a CSR (Customer Service Record) PDF for a Deal in Zoho CRM, coordinate fulfillment via Asana, and write back delivery outcomes to the Deal. The automation is initiated by a single checkbox in the Deal: Request for CSR.

Scope: Deals module in Zoho CRM; Asana for task management; Export CSR data and produce a PDF.

2) Goals & Objectives

  • Single‑click request: Trigger CSR creation from a checkbox on the Deal.
  • Zero‑touch fulfillment: Auto‑create an Asana task (assigned to Summit) with all Deal context and a checklist.
  • Reliable CSR generation: Export CSR data and produce a standardized PDF file.
  • Closed‑loop updates: On task completion, CSR PDF attached to the Deal, Update CSR Delivery Date, and tag CSM/Manager for visibility.
  • Auditability: Keep a clear activity trail in both Zoho and Asana.

3) Roles & Responsibilities

  • Deal Owner (Sales/SDR/AE/CSM): Checks Request for CSR on the Deal; reviews attachment and date after delivery.
  • Summit (Assignee in Asana): Owns fulfillment, validates generated CSR, marks task complete when ready.
  • CSM/Manager: Tagged at delivery; reviews and takes any follow‑up action with the customer.
  • Sales Ops / Admin: Maintains automation rules, Asana template, field mappings; monitors error queue and retries.

4) Process Steps

Trigger (Zoho Deals)

  1. User ticks Request for CSR (checkbox) on a Deal.
  2. Fire flow Create_AsanaTask_For_CSR with Deal ID.

Task Creation (Asana → Assigned to Summit)

  1. Create task in Asana using a standard template:
    • Task Name: CSR: <Account Name> - <Deal Name> (#<Deal ID>)
    • Assignee: Summit
    • Project/Section: Customer Docs / CSR Requests
    • Due Date (SLA): Today
    • Description (auto‑filled):
      • Deal URL
      • Deal Name

Fulfillment (CSR Export & PDF)

  1. Summit calls CSR Export Service with Deal ID → returns PDF (and log/metadata).
  2. If generation succeeds → attach PDF to Asana task (for QA).
  3. Update Deal with CSR Delivery Date

5) Important Notes & Considerations

  • Field Mappings (minimum):
    • Deal: Deal Name, Deal ID
    • Request for CSR (Checkbox), CSR Delivery Date (Date/Time),
  • Security: Limit CSR PDF visibility to relevant roles. Avoid embedding sensitive tokens in task descriptions.
  • SLA: Default 1 business days; configurable in an Admin Settings record or function parameter.

6) Important Notes & Considerations

  • Report Links
    • https://crm.zoho.com/crm/org56875003/tab/Reports/1607362001524340554

KB Article RCM Guide (RCM)

Guide to Adit’s Multi-Specialty Revenue Cycle Management (RCM)

Adit’s Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) - Insurance Verification solution enables healthcare practices to automate and standardize insurance eligibility checks, significantly reducing claim denials, safeguarding revenue, and streamlining front-office operations. Unlike manual workflows or basic EDI-only tools, Adit’s RCM combines automated verification with optional manual verification, delivered through clearly defined tiers aligned to clinical complexity and cost transparency.

Designed as a cross-specialty solution for Dental, Orthodontic, Optometry, and Chiropractic practices, Adit’s Insurance Verification eliminates the operational burden of manual carrier calls while improving accuracy and consistency across eligibility checks.

By integrating real-time automated verification with professionally managed manual verification, Adit delivers a scalable, enterprise-ready solution that supports practices of all sizes-from single-location clinics to large, multi-specialty DSOs.

Insurance Verification Overview

Adit’s service confirms patient coverage details in real-time, tailored to your specialty’s unique needs:

  • Status: Is the patient’s insurance active?
  • Financials: Remaining deductibles, co-pays, and out-of-pocket limits.
  • Specialty Limits: Multi-phase treatment coverage (Ortho), or vision-specific allowances (Opto).
  • Benefit Dates: Plan effective dates and renewal cycles.

We support both Basic and Advanced eligibility checks, and can even retrieve procedure-level benefit details for enhanced accuracy.

💡 Best Practice: Verify eligibility 48-72 hours before every appointment. Insurance details can change at any time-doing so reduces claim denials and billing surprises.

FAQs

How do I sign up for Adit’s Insurance Verification service?

Adit’s Insurance Verification is part of our Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) offerings. To get started, please contact our Upgrades team, who will assist you with enrollment and next steps.

How do I set up Adit’s Insurance Verification module?

A member of our team will guide you through the setup process. As part of the configuration, you will define the following settings:

  • The lead time before an appointment at which insurance verification should be triggered
  • Whether verification results should be attached to the patient’s record as a PDF or note
  • The treatment codes to be validated for Basic and Advanced verifications
  • our team may contact your practice to request additional insurance information, if required

For a step-by-step walkthrough of the configuration process, please refer to our article: How To: Set Up Insurance Verification.

What is the difference between Basic Eligibility Verification and Advanced Eligibility Verification?

Basic Eligibility Verification

Basic Verification is an automated eligibility check performed via EDI. It returns the standard eligibility information available through the payer’s EDI response, with limited benefit breakdowns or detailed code-level analysis.

  • Eligibility and benefits validation for up to 40 preset CDT codes

Advanced Eligibility Verification
Advanced Verification provides a comprehensive eligibility and benefits checks. First layer goes through EDI and and second layer of verification is done by Adit’s RCM team. It includes detailed benefit information such as deductibles, out-of-pocket maximums, co-insurance, co-payments, coverage limitations, and plan-specific rules.

Advanced Verification is further categorized as:

  • Standard Advanced Verification: Eligibility and benefits validation for up to 20 CDT codes
  • Extensive Advanced Verification: Eligibility and benefits validation for up to 40 CDT codes

Adit’s new Insurance verification - IV26 module gives you the flexibility to upgrade individual appointments to Advanced. In an ideal scenario, you can be a subscriber to our Basic plan and get your appointments verified 72 hours before the appointment date - while upgrading one-off appointments to the paid Advanced tier for detailed verification. You just pay for that appointment.

When do I need to take action on an Insurance Verification?

Adit’s team will manage the majority of insurance verifications on your behalf. Action is required from your side only when a verification fails due to missing or incomplete insurance or demographic information.
In such cases, you will need to update the required details in the Adit App so the verification can be retriggered prior to the patient’s appointment.
If enabled, we can also send reminder notifications to your registered email address prompting you to update the missing information and reinitiate the verification in a timely manner.

How do I change which treatment codes are being verified?

To update the treatment codes used for insurance verification, please contact our support team by emailing support at adit.com. Your request will be automatically logged as a ticket in our ticketing system and routed to the appropriate team for review and action.

Since insurance verification is offered across multiple tiers-Basic, Advanced (Standard), and Advanced (Extensive)-the treatment codes selected may impact your verification tier and pricing.

For more information on how treatment codes align with each tier and how pricing may change based on your selections, please refer to our article on https://help.adit.com/portal/en/kb/articles/guide-to-insurance-verification-charges#1_Software-Only_Package.

Will you update the patient file in my PMS/EHR software?

Yes, the patient file can be updated in two ways: by adding a note and by attaching a PDF.
You may choose to enable either option, or both, through your preferences in the RCM module.

How do I check the status of an insurance verification?

You can easily monitor the status of all insurance verifications from a single, centralized view. When you navigate to the RCM module within the Adit platform, you will be directed automatically to the Verifications page.
Review the Verification Status column to view color-coded status indicators, and refer to the Actions column for Verification forms or History of Verification.
For a detailed explanation of each verification status, please refer to our article: How To: Check the Status of an Insurance Verification.

How am I billed for Insurance Verifications?

Read our Guide to Insurance Verification Charges to learn more! https://help.adit.com/portal/en/kb/articles/guide-to-insurance-verification-charges#1_Software-Only_Package

2.2 Basic Verification
Basic Verification is a fully automated eligibility check performed via EDI (Electronic Data
Interchange). It returns standard eligibility information from the payer's EDI response.
•​ Supports up to 40 CDT codes
•​ No manual intervention - entirely EDI-driven
•​ Includes 300 free transactions per month
•​ Overage charge: $0.06 per transaction beyond 300
•​ Cancelled verifications do not count toward the transaction limit

2.3 Advanced Verification
Advanced Verification provides a comprehensive eligibility and benefits check, including detailed
benefit information: deductibles, out-of-pocket maximums, co-insurance, co-payments, coverage
limitations, and plan-specific rules.
•​ Standard Advanced: up to 20 CDT codes - EDI + Manual verification
•​ Extensive Advanced: 20-40 CDT codes - EDI + Manual verification
•​ Includes 'Next Eligible Date' information
•​ Monthly fee: $149; tiered per-verification fees apply

2.4 One-Off Upgrade (Basic → Advanced)
Basic plan clients can upgrade individual appointments to Advanced verification without switching
their entire plan. They pay only for that specific appointment.
•​ Upgrade option available from the dashboard for In Queue or Verified appointments
•​ If Upgraded after EDI completes, cost = EDI cost + Advanced cost
•​ Standard upgrade: up to 20 codes
•​ Extensive upgrade: up to 40 codes

2.5 Same-Day Verification (Paid Add-On)
Available across all tiers for walk-ins or urgent eligibility needs.
•​ Supports up to 40 CDT codes
•​ Instant Active/Termed notification within a 60-minute SLA
•​ Detailed benefit breakdown continues processing in the background
•​ Cost: $6 per verification (displayed via tooltip in the dashboard)
•​ PDF sync is included

2.6 Medicaid & HMO Handling
For Medicaid and HMO insurance plans, the system bypasses standard EDI calls because CDT
codes and plan information are typically unavailable via EDI.
•​ Uses scraper APIs to download eligibility and history PDFs
•​ Pricing follows the same structure as the selected verification tier (Basic or Advanced)
3. Setting Up Insurance Verification

3.1 Getting Started
To access Adit's Insurance Verification, your account must be upgraded to include RCM. If the RCM
module shows a welcome/demo screen, the account has not yet been upgraded.
•​ Contact the Adit Upgrades team to enroll
•​ Schedule a consultation via the platform - the Adit team will guide the entire configuration

3.2 Setup Steps
Step 1 - Practice Information
Enter basic practice details used exclusively by the Adit verification team for accurate insurance
coverage checks. Complete all required fields, then click Next.

Adit RCM AI Training Knowledge Base.pdf (continued, part 1)

Step 2 - Verification Settings
Trigger Settings: Configure how far in advance of an appointment verification should be initiated -
either 3 days or 5 days before the appointment date.
EHR/PMS Write-Back Settings: Choose how verification results are returned to the patient record:
•​ Attach a PDF of verification results to the patient record
•​ Add a note to the patient's chart (synced to Communication Logs in the EHR)
•​ Both options can be enabled simultaneously
•​ If PDF is enabled, select the EHR folder where PDFs should be stored

Step 3 - Select Treatment Codes (Tx Codes)
Select the CDT codes that should be verified for Basic and/or Advanced verifications. Each code
includes 1-4 verification questions covering:
•​ Whether the treatment is covered and at what percentage
•​ Age limitations for coverage
•​ Frequency limitations
•​ Patient eligibility and next eligible date (if applicable)

Basic package: up to 40 codes. Advanced Standard: up to 20 codes. Advanced Extensive: up to 40
codes.

Step 4 - Insurance Mapping
Map insurance names from your EHR/PMS to Adit's master insurance list. This standardization
ensures consistent handling across the RCM module.
Example: Your EHR may list 'BCBSTX'; Adit's master list uses 'Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas'.
Select the correct standardized option from the dropdown.
•​ Adit supports 350+ insurers in its master list
•​ Medicaid/HMO plans are handled via scraper - not EDI
4. Verification Status Lifecycle

4.1 How Status Flows
When appointments are synced from your EHR, they enter the RCM module and progress through
a defined lifecycle until verification is complete or the appointment date passes.

In Queue → In Progress → Verified / Failed / Skipped / Expired

4.2 Verification Status Definitions
Status Meaning
In Queue Appointment synced from EHR and waiting for the verification
trigger date.
In Progress Verification has been triggered (3 or 5 days before appointment).
EDI attempts are ongoing. Remains In Progress until a final
resolution is reached.
Verified (Active) Eligibility check completed successfully - patient's insurance is
currently active.
Verified (Termed) Eligibility check completed - patient's insurance is no longer
active. Charge: $0.75 only for advanced package
Failed Verification failed due to incorrect/missing patient or insurance data,
or payer response issues. Does NOT automatically expire - can
be retried after correction.
Skipped Appointment excluded from verification - applies to Cash patients
or In-House insurance plans.
Expired Appointment date has passed and verification was not completed.
Applies to cancelled appointments, no-shows, past dates, and
non-patients.

4.3 Insurance Status Definitions
Status Meaning
Active Insurance is active at the time of verification.
Termed Insurance is no longer active at the time of verification.
Unknown Verification is not yet complete or falls under a non-final status (e.g.,
In Progress).
4.4 Retry & Expiration Logic
•​ System makes up to 3 automated retry attempts for payer-side EDI failures
•​ After 3 retries, practice can correct the data and re-trigger - up to 2 additional manual
reattempts
•​ Failed verifications do NOT move to Expired automatically - they persist until the
appointment date passes
•​ Appointments only expire when the appointment date has passed and verification is still
incomplete

4.5 Advanced Verification Logic (Soft + Hard)
•​ EDI Success (Termed) → No manual verification needed
•​ EDI Success (Active) → Triggers manual (hard) verification. View icon enabled immediately
while hard verification continues
•​ EDI Failed + Manual Verified → Final status: Verified
•​ EDI Failed + Manual Failed → Final status: Failed
•​ Manual verification status shows amber while pending; turns green when complete

6. Same-Day Verification
Same-Day Verification is a paid add-on available across all tiers. It delivers active/termed
notifications within a 60-minute SLA while the full benefit breakdown loads in the background.

6.1 How to Initiate a Same-Day Verification
•​ Click Add from the Same-Day Verification dashboard
•​ Complete the Patient Verification Form
•​ Click Verify

6.2 Required Information
•​ Service Code Type (STC) - Auto-populated based on specialty (Dental, Optometry,
Orthodontics)
•​ CDT Codes - Up to 40 codes
•​ Provider Details - Auto-populated
•​ Subscriber Details - If subscriber = patient, enter subscriber details; if different, enter both
patient and subscriber details
•​ Provider ID - Select from dropdown
•​ Insurance Card Upload - Optional

6.3 Same-Day Status Definitions
Status Meaning
Pending (In Queue) Form submitted, verification in progress
Active Successfully verified - insurance is active
Termed Successfully verified - insurance is no longer active
Failed Verification failed - update missing or incorrect information

7. Managing Failed Verifications

7.1 When Does a Practice Need to Take Action?
Adit's team handles the vast majority of verifications. Practice action is only required when a
verification fails due to missing or incorrect data.

Practice Action Required When:
•​ Verification fails due to missing or incorrect patient demographic information
•​ Verification fails due to missing or incorrect insurance information
•​ The practice receives an email reminder from Adit prompting a data update

7.2 How to Fix a Failed Verification
•​ From the dashboard, click Update on the Failed card to see all failed appointments
•​ Incorrect or missing fields are highlighted
•​ Select the appointment to open the patient detail form
•​ Correct the data and resubmit - this re-triggers the verification
•​ Up to 2 correction reattempts are allowed per verification

7.3 Failure Reasons
•​ Incorrect/missing patient demographic data
•​ Incorrect/missing insurance information
•​ Payer rejection or on-hold response
•​ System issues or unsupported insurance logic
•​ Could not identify patient
•​ Termed insurance (insurance lapsed)
•​ Other payer-specific reasons
8. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
These Q&A pairs are designed for direct use in AI assistant training.

Q: How do I sign up for Adit's Insurance Verification?

A: Insurance Verification is part of Adit's RCM offerings. Contact Adit's Upgrades team to get
started. They will assist with enrollment and next steps.
•​ Visit: https://calendly.com/d/ckb6-4w6-qff/rcm-walkthrough
•​ An Adit representative will guide you through onboarding

Q: How do I set up the Insurance Verification module?

Adit RCM AI Training Knowledge Base.pdf (continued, part 3)

A: An Adit team member will guide you through setup. During configuration you will define:
•​ How far in advance verification should trigger (3 or 5 days before appointment)
•​ Whether results are attached as a PDF, note, or both in your EHR/PMS
•​ Which treatment codes (CDT codes) are included for Basic and Advanced
verifications
•​ Insurance mappings from your EHR to Adit's master insurance list

Q: What is the difference between Basic and Advanced Eligibility Verification?

A: Basic Verification is automated EDI-only, covering up to 40 CDT codes with no manual
intervention. Advanced Verification adds professional manual verification on top of EDI and
includes detailed benefit breakdowns (deductibles, co-pays, OOP maximums, coverage
limitations). Advanced Standard covers up to 20 codes; Advanced Extensive covers 20-40
codes.

Q: Can I upgrade a single appointment from Basic to Advanced without changing my
plan?

A: Yes. Adit's IV26 module supports one-off upgrades. You stay on the Basic plan for routine
verifications, and pay only for the individual appointment you upgrade to Advanced.

Q: When does my practice need to take action on a verification?

A: Adit manages verifications on your behalf. You only need to act when a verification fails
due to missing or incorrect patient or insurance information. In that case, update the details in
the Adit app so the verification can be retriggered before the appointment.
•​ Email reminders can be configured to notify you when action is needed
Q: How do I change which treatment codes are being verified?

A: Email support at adit.com. Your request will be logged automatically and routed to the
appropriate team. Note that changing codes may affect your verification tier and pricing.

Q: Will Adit update the patient file in my PMS/EHR?

A: Yes. Adit can update the patient file in two ways: by attaching a PDF of the verification
results, and/or by adding a note to the patient's chart. You can enable either or both options
in RCM preferences.

Q: How do I check the status of an insurance verification?

A: Navigate to the RCM module in the Adit platform. You'll land on the Verifications page. The
Verification Status column shows color-coded status indicators. The Actions column provides
access to verification forms, PDFs, and history.

Q: What is the 60-minute SLA for Same-Day Verification?

A: Same-Day Verification provides an instant Active/Termed notification while the detailed
benefit breakdown continues loading in the background. The full advanced verification form is
completed within 60 minutes.

Q: Does a failed verification automatically expire?

A: No. Failed verifications do not automatically expire. They remain in Failed status and can
be corrected and re-triggered (up to 2 reattempts). Appointments only move to Expired once
the appointment date has passed.

Q: How does Adit handle Medicaid or HMO insurance plans?

A: Medicaid and HMO plans are processed differently from standard insurance. Because
CDT codes and plan information are typically unavailable via EDI, Adit bypasses EDI and
uses scraper APIs to download eligibility and history PDFs. Pricing follows the same structure
as your selected verification tier.

Q: How many times can a failed verification be retried?

A: The system makes up to 3 automated EDI retry attempts. After that, the practice can
correct the data and manually re-trigger - up to 2 additional reattempts are allowed, as long
as the appointment date has not yet passed.
Q: What does 'Skipped' mean in the verification dashboard?

A: A Skipped status means the appointment was intentionally excluded from insurance
verification. This happens for Cash patients and appointments using In-House insurance -
neither requires an insurance eligibility check.

Q: Can I verify a walk-in patient?

A: Yes. Use Same-Day Verification, available across all tiers. Complete the Patient
Verification Form with the patient's subscriber and insurance details, and Adit will return an
Active/Termed notification within 60 minutes.

Q: What specialties does Adit's Insurance Verification support?

A: Adit's Insurance Verification is designed for Dental, Orthodontic and Optometry practices.
Specialty-specific benefit checks include multi-phase treatment coverage for Ortho and
vision-specific allowances for Optometry.

Q: What is the audit log?

Adit RCM AI Training Knowledge Base.pdf (continued, part 4)

A: The Audit Log (accessible via the History icon in the Actions column) captures the full
lifecycle of a verification with timestamps: when it entered In Queue, In Progress, was
Verified or Failed, any EDI reattempts, and any demographic updates made by the practice
or the Adit RCM team.

https://app.supademo.com/demo/cmjsqrffw8dnq3zz23j324tod?utm_source=link

If your customer is using ONLINE SCHEDULING, it is especially important that you check their account and help your customer go through the getting started steps to unlock the OS module.

1. When the getting started steps are not complete, pages in OS will not be fully accessible.
If you want to view the customer’s appointments you can still access it by navigating to “all locations” and going to their appointment page.
This will tell you if they have been using online scheduling and receiving appointments.

2. You should check all of their existing booking links, especially the ones used on their website.

  • Open up their website and click on the “book now” buttons. Make sure the booking links look normal.
  • All existing booking links before migrating to the new platform should still work properly and not face any disruptions.
    • The microsite link from the old OS will automatically be converted to the “Default booking link” that you see on the new booking link page
    • If getting started is not complete, then you can still access this page by going to “All Locations” and seeing the list from there
      ****
  • If the booking link isn’t showing any availability, that is a red flag. This means you should urgently reach out to the customer and help them reconfigure their OS. If you see this then make sure to check their operatory/service/provider mapping matrix

3. Make sure that if the customer is using Advanced Online Scheduling, then we should be showing real time available slots in the booking link.

4. Otherwise if they are on basic online scheduling it should show “Morning, Afternoon, Evening” like this.

5. Also make sure that their available times on their booking link make sense.

  • For example if there are any odd times like 2AM or 3AM slots available then that is a red flag.

  • You can look at the Practice’s schedule on the home page to cross reference available time slots

Other Things to Look Out For:

  1. Does their booking link show services properly for both NEW and Existing Patients? It shouldn’t look empty.
  2. Do all services show available time slots?

3. Check their google maps on the booking link, does it look accurate?
****

If it doesn’t show properly, that means the address needs to be updated in the Adit settings page
****

4. Do they have a logo showing properly in their booking link? If they don’t, either upload a logo or hide it from the custom booking link
****

Phone Order Process - Internal and Client-Facing Guidelines (Voice)

FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY

Overview

This article outlines the process for handling client requests to order additional VoIP phones. Since there is no self-service option within Adit for ordering phones, all requests must be manually processed through a support ticket and routed to the appropriate queue.

Step-by-Step Process

  1. Confirm the Order Request
    • Verify the client’s request.
    • Confirm the device model(s) they would like to order.
    • Confirm quantity and any additional relevant details.
  2. Create a Support Ticket
    • Open a new ticket in the ticketing system.
      • Clearly document all relevant details in the ticket comments, including:
        • Client name and location
        • Device model requested
        • Quantity
        • Any special instructions provided by the client
        • Tag @Jay Adesara
  3. Route the Ticket

    • Assign and forward the ticket to the VoIP Assets Management queue.

    • Ensure all required information is included before routing to avoid delays.

  4. Notify the Client (if needed)
    • Confirm with the client that their request has been submitted to the appropriate team.
    • Provide any expected next steps if applicable.

CLIENT-FACING INSTRUCTIONS

How Clients Can Order Additional Phones

At this time, clients cannot order phones directly through the Adit app. To request additional phones, they may use one of the following methods:

  • Email: Send the request to support at adit.com

  • Submit a Ticket: Create a request through our Adit ticketing system

  • Call Adit Support Team: Contact us at 281-468-1445
    ****

Once the request is received, our team will review the details and coordinate the order.

PBX User Manual (Voice)

PBX Portal

Login

To access the portal, sign in using your account credentials.

  • Username: [staff email]
  • Password: 123xxxx789

Enter your username and password in the respective fields, then click Login to access your account.

Welcome to the dashboard:

Organization
Select the organization for which you want to view and manage the available PBX features and settings.

Location
An organization may have multiple locations. Select the required location to display the corresponding data and settings throughout the portal.

Note: After selecting the organization and location, click Save Selection to apply your choices. The portal will then display the data and settings associated with the selected organization and location.

Dashboard

Dashboard Overview

The Dashboard provides a quick overview of the selected organization’s location and easy access to commonly used features.

The dashboard includes:

  • Feature Summary: Displays the total number of PBX features configured for the selected location, including Extensions, Ring Groups, DID Numbers, and Voicemails.
  • Recent Call Logs: Provides a list of the most recent call activities for quick reference.
  • Quick Actions: Offers shortcuts to frequently used tasks to view Extension, Ring Group, DID Numbers, and Call Flows.

Extensions ****

The Extensions page displays all extensions configured for the selected location, along with their associated details.

The following information is available for each extension:

  • Extension Number
  • Line Type
  • Assigned Device
  • Device Model
  • Status

Extension Number Format

  • Hardline Extensions: Three-digit numbers ranging from 101 to 750.
  • Softline Extensions: Three-digit numbers ranging from 001 to 100.

Extension Parking

The Extension Parking section displays the parking details configured for extensions at the selected location.

This page provides information about parked calls and their associated parking extensions, allowing users to view and manage call parking assignments efficiently.

Voicemail Box

Group Mailbox and Extension Mailbox

This section displays the configured Group Mailbox and Extension Mailbox. Users can view the assigned mailbox information from this section.

Ring Groups

Ring group listing will be displayed in this section

Add a Ring Group

Use this section to create and configure a Ring Group for incoming calls.

Ring Strategy

Select the ringing strategy that determines how calls are distributed among the destinations. Available strategies include:

  • Simultaneous - Rings all destinations at the same time.
  • Random - Rings a randomly selected destination.
  • Other available strategies, depending on your system configuration.

Ring Timeout

Specify the Ring Timeout in seconds. This defines how long the system will attempt to ring the configured destinations before executing the failover action.

Destinations

Add one or more destinations that will receive incoming calls. You can configure:

  • Extensions - Select one or more available extensions.
  • External Numbers - Add external phone numbers as call destinations.

Multiple destinations can be added to the same Ring Group.

Failover Destination

Configure the action to be performed if the call is not answered within the specified ring timeout. Available options include:

  • Hang Up - Disconnect the call.
  • Transfer to Extension - Forward the call to a selected extension.
  • Send to Voicemail Box - Route the call to a selected voicemail box that has already been created.

Caller ID

Optionally, configure the Caller ID Name and Caller ID Number that will be presented when the Ring Group places outbound calls.

Call Forwarding

If Call Forwarding is enabled, specify the Forward Destination where calls should be redirected.

IVR Menu

The Create IVR Menu feature allows administrators to create an Interactive Voice Response (IVR) menu that routes incoming callers based on their DTMF (keypad) input.

Field Required Description
IVR Name Yes Enter a unique name for the IVR menu (e.g., Main Menu, Support IVR).
Description No Provide a brief description of the IVR menu for administrative reference.
Timeout (sec) Yes Specifies the number of seconds the system waits for caller input before triggering a timeout action. Default: 10 seconds.
Max Failures Yes Maximum number of invalid key presses allowed before executing the failure action. Default: 3.
Max Timeouts Yes Maximum number of consecutive timeouts allowed before executing the timeout action. Default: 3.
Allow Direct Dial No When enabled, callers can directly dial an extension without navigating the IVR menu.
Enabled Yes Determines whether the IVR menu is active and available for incoming calls.
DTMF Options No Configure keypad options (0-9, *, #) and define the action performed when callers press a specific key.

DTMF Options

The DTMF Options section defines the actions performed when a caller presses a specific key during the IVR call flow. Click + Add Option to create one or more DTMF mappings.

Available Actions

1. Execute Application

Routes the caller to a specific application or destination.

Parameter: Enter the application or destination identifier (for example, transfer 101, queue Sales, or another configured application).

Example

Digit Action Parameter Description
1 Execute Application transfer 101 Sales Department

2. Sub Menu

Transfers the caller to another IVR menu.

Parameter: Select or enter the target IVR submenu.

Example

Digit Action Parameter Description
2 Sub Menu Support Menu Technical Support

3. Return to Top

Returns the caller to the main (top-level) IVR menu.

Parameter: Not required.

Example

Digit Action Description
9 Return to Top Return to Main Menu

4. Go Back

Returns the caller to the previous IVR menu.

Parameter: Not required.

Example

Digit Action Description
* Go Back Return to Previous Menu

5. Exit

Ends the IVR interaction or exits the current menu according to the configured call flow.

Parameter: Not required.

Example

Digit Action Description
# Exit End Call

Validation Rules

  • Digit is mandatory.
  • Only one entry is allowed per DTMF digit within the same IVR menu.
  • Supported digits are 0-9, *, and #.
  • Action is mandatory.
  • Parameter is required only for actions that require a destination, such as Execute Application and Sub Menu.
  • Description is optional but recommended for easier administration.

Notes

  • Configure each DTMF option according to your organization’s call-routing requirements.
  • Ensure all referenced applications, extensions, queues, or submenus exist before saving the IVR.
  • Multiple DTMF options can be added using the + Add Option button.
  • Use clear descriptions to simplify future maintenance and troubleshooting of the IVR configuration.

Business Hours The Create Business Hours feature allows administrators to define operating schedules that determine when the system is considered open or closed. Business hours can be configured using a weekly schedule, holidays, and special hours.

Tab Description
Weekly Schedule Configure the regular operating hours for each day of the week.
Holidays Define holidays when normal business hours should not apply.
Special Hours Configure temporary schedules for specific dates, such as company events or seasonal hours.

Quick Presets

Quick Presets provide commonly used schedules that can be applied automatically.

Preset Description
Mon-Fri 9-5 Sets Monday through Friday to 09:00-17:00. Weekends remain closed.
Mon-Fri 8-6 Sets Monday through Friday to 08:00-18:00. Weekends remain closed.
24/7 Enables all seven days with continuous 24-hour availability.
All Closed Disables business hours for every day of the week.

Additional Field Descriptions

Field Required Description
Description No Enter an optional description for the business hours configuration. This can be used to provide additional information, such as the purpose or intended use of the schedule (e.g., Main office operating hours for customer support).
Active No Enables or disables the business hours configuration. When Active is enabled, the schedule can be used by the system. When disabled, the configuration is saved but will not be applied until it is activated.

STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE

VoIP Asset Management

Actioning Pending Phone Equipment Orders

Document Information

Item Details
SOP Title Actioning Pending Phone Equipment Orders
Department VoIP - Asset Management
Process Owner VoIP Asset Management Team
Applicable Teams VoIP Asset Management, Onboarding, CSM, Billing, Finance
Systems Used Phones-Asset Management Dashboard, Adit App, CRM, GDMS, Asana, Zoho Desk, Teledynamics Portal

  1. Objective

This SOP provides the VoIP Asset Management Team with a standardized process for reviewing, validating, ordering, tracking documenting, and completing pending phone and equipment orders.
The process applies to:

  • Clients in Onboarding (OB)
  • Additional phone and equipment orders
  • CSM-related additional equipment orders Orders communicated by Billing
  • Orders assigned through Asana by the Tech OBs or Tech CSMs

  1. Scope

This SOP covers the process from the initial notification of a pending phone or equipment requirement through:

  1. Order identification

  2. Order verification

  3. Equipment selection

  4. Order placement through Teledynamics & NTS Direct

  5. Finance notification

  6. Customer communication

  7. Shipment tracking

  8. Final documentation and record updates

  9. Systems and Tools Used

The following systems and tools are used during this process:

  1. Phones-Asset Management Team Dashboard

Used to identify pending phone orders for Onboarding clients through the “Phones yet to Be Ordered” “Pending Phone Order - By Date section.

  1. CRM

  • Access the relevant Deal

  • Review order-related attachments and agreements

  • Update applicable account and equipment information.

    1. Adit App

  • Add applicable phone lines

  • Update phone and equipment records

  • Maintain Voice module information

    1. GDMS

  • Used to add and maintain applicable phone information, including device details when available.

    1. Asana

  • Receiving tasks from Tech OB or Tech CSM

  • Creating order-related tasks

  • Organizing daily orders under the relevant parent task Notifying Finance

  • Marking related tasks complete after all required actions are documented.

    1. Zoho Desk

  • Used for handling tickets related to additional phone and equipment orders assigned to the Imp-VoIP Assets Team.

    1. Teledynamics & NTS Direct Portal

Used to:

  • Search for requested equipment
  • Add equipment to the cart
  • Enter shipping details
  • Select shipping method
  • Verify billing
  • Obtain tracking information once generated

  1. Inventory Covered

The following equipment is included in the current inventory covered by this SOP:

  • GRP 2616
  • GRP 2613
  • Wall Mount (Big) for GRP 2616 Wall Mount (Small) for GRP 2613
  • Plantronics Wireless Headset CS540 for GRP 2616 and GRP 2613
  • DP 720 Cordless Phone
  • DP 750 Cordless Base Station

  1. How the Asset Management Team is Notified

Pending orders may be identified or communicated through the following channels:

  1. Onboarding Clients

Review the “Phones yet to Be Ordered” section in the Phones-Asset Management Team Dashboard.

  1. Additional Phone and Equipment Orders

Zohoform notification received in the email notifies the VoIP Asset Management Team regarding additional equipment requirements for:

  • CSM Clients

  • OB Clients

    1. Direct Task Assignment

  • The Tech OB or Tech CSM may directly assign or communicate the requirement through an Asana task.

  1. Process A - Onboarding Client Phone Orders {#process-a---onboarding-client-phone-orders}

Step 1: Identify the Pending Order

Access the Phones-Asset Management Team Dashboard. Navigate to:

Phones yet to Be Ordered

Step 2: Access the Deal

Open the applicable Deal associated with the client.
Step 3: Review Supporting Documentation
Navigate to the attachments available under Agreements. Review the relevant attachment to identify and verify:

  • Phone model
  • Quantity
  • Equipment requirements

Equipment to be ordered must match the information documented in the applicable attachment

Step 4: Access the Teledynamics/NTS Direct Portal {#step-4:-access-the-teledynamics/nts-direct-portal}

Log in to the Teledynamics/NTS Direct Portal using the credentials provided by the Manager.

Step 5: Search and Add Equipment

  • Search for the requested phone or equipment model.
  • Add the required equipment to the cart.

Before proceeding to checkout, verify that:

  • The correct model has been selected
  • The correct quantity has been added
  • All requested accessories have been included where applicable.

Step 6: Proceed to Checkout

  • Click the Checkout button.

Step 7: Configure Shipping Information

Under Ship To, select:

“Drop Ship Order to my Customer”

  • Select the option to enter the customer’s shipping address manually.
  • Enter the shipping address as required for the applicable customer order.
  • The shipping information should be carefully reviewed before placing the order.

Step 9: Select Shipping Method

  • Under Ship Method, select:

“UPS Ground Only” “FedEx Ground Only”

Step 10: Verify Billing

  • Under Billing, ensure that the designated billing card/ Use Card on file ending in
    8515 is selected.

Step 11: Capture Order Evidence

Before placing the order:
Review the complete Order Summary Capture a screenshot of the Order Summary

Step 12: Place the Order

Place the order after verifying:
Equipment model, Quantity, Customer shipping information, Return address, Shipping method & Billing selection.

Step 13: Create Finance Task

  • Create an Asana task for the orders and send or assign it to the Finance Team (Oshin) as established by workflow.

Step 14: Update the Tech OB Record

In the Tech OB record, under the Phone Install section:

  • Mark the phones as Ordered
  • Update the Phone Ordered Date

  1. Process B - Additional Phone and Equipment Orders {#process-b---additional-phone-and-equipment-orders}

Step 1: Receive the Notification

  • Receive the equipment requirement from the email notification & inform Billing Team on

https://chat.google.com/room/AAQAYaqxYFI?cls=7

  • Open the applicable client Deal.

Step 3: Review the Order Form

  • Same as Ordering phone from Teledynamics/NTS Direct
