T1 - Voice Module & Phone System Training (Voice)

Voice Module & Phone System Training

Training Session Recap & Reference Guide

Training Session: Friday (11th Sept’26)
Topic: Voice Module & Phone System
Purpose: Training recap and reference guide for the team

1. Training Overview

This document summarizes the key topics covered during the Voice Module & Phone System training session held last Friday.

The session focused on understanding the Voice Module, managing phone configurations, handling common phone-system requests, performing basic troubleshooting, and resolving eligible requests through First Call Resolution (FCR).

The objective is to ensure trainees are comfortable navigating the system, identifying the correct feature or configuration, making basic changes, and guiding customers through any required actions.

2. Lines & Line Management

What are Lines?

Lines represent the actual phones or extensions used by the practice.

Line Management allows us to:

  • Associate a user with an extension.
  • Change the label/name displayed on the physical phone.
  • Identify whose phone it is during call transfers.

Steps to Configure

  1. Navigate to Lines / Line Management.
  2. Locate the required extension.
  3. Click the Pencil/Edit icon next to the extension.
  4. Update the Label Name and User Association.
  5. Save the changes.

Important - Phone Reboot

After changing a label name, the physical phone must be rebooted for the new label to appear.

Manual Phone Reboot

  1. Press Menu on the phone.
  2. Scroll to the bottom.
  3. Locate the Reboot option/icon.
  4. Select Reboot.
  5. Allow the phone to restart.

Training Tip: If the label has been updated in the system but is not appearing on the physical phone, ask the user to reboot the phone.

3. Blocked Callers

Blocked Callers allows practices to prevent specific phone numbers from calling them.

Navigation

Voice Module → Blocked Callers

Steps

  1. Open the Voice Module.
  2. Select Blocked Callers.
  3. Add the required phone number.
  4. Save the changes.

4. Call Hold

Call Hold allows staff to temporarily place a patient/caller on hold. While on hold, the caller will hear hold music.

Hold / Unhold a Call

  1. Press the Pause/Hold button to place the caller on hold.
  2. Press the appropriate button again to resume the call.

Change Hold Music

Navigation:
Voice Module → Hold Music

The practice can change the standard hold music to another available recording.

5. Call Override

Call Override temporarily changes the normal routing of incoming calls.

It can be used when the practice is:

  • Closed for a holiday.
  • Unexpectedly closed.
  • Temporarily unavailable.

When enabled, calls can be routed to voicemail or an external number.

Steps

  1. Go to Voice Module → Call Override.
  2. Enable Call Override.
  3. Select or verify the required destination.
  4. Save the configuration.

Important

When the practice resumes normal operations, Call Override must be turned OFF.

If it remains enabled, incoming calls may continue to bypass the normal call flow.

6. Audio Library

The Audio Library stores recordings used throughout the phone system, including:

  • Greetings
  • Voicemail recordings
  • Hold music
  • Menu prompts

Navigation

Voice Module → Audio Library

Option 1 - Record Your Own

  1. Select Record Your Own.
  2. Connect the required headphones/microphone.
  3. Record the message.
  4. Save the recording.

Option 2 - Upload

  1. Select Upload.
  2. Choose the required audio file from the computer.
  3. Upload the file.
  4. Save/confirm the recording.

7. Call Recording

Call Recording allows practice calls with patients to be recorded for:

  • Training
  • Quality checks
  • Reviewing conversations
  • Resolving disputes

Incoming Call Recording

For incoming calls, check the Call Flow to determine whether recording is enabled or disabled.

Outgoing Call Recording

Navigation:
Voice Module → Call Recording

Check the configuration for outgoing call recording.

Key Troubleshooting Approach

First identify whether the issue concerns an incoming or outgoing call, then check the appropriate recording configuration.

8. Multiple Voicemail Boxes

Multiple voicemail boxes allow practices to have separate voicemail boxes for different staff members or departments.

Version-Based Requirement

  • V4: Additional voicemail boxes can be created without approval.
  • V2/V3: Approval is required before creating an additional voicemail box.

Important

Always confirm the Voice version before proceeding with a voicemail-box request.

9. eFax

eFax allows practices to send and receive faxes digitally without using a physical fax machine.

Steps to Send an eFax

  1. Go to the ADIT Home Screen.
  2. Click the Blue + icon.
  3. Select the Fax Machine icon.
  4. Enter the required details.
  5. Enter the recipient’s fax number.
  6. Attach the required document.
  7. Verify the details.
  8. Send the fax.

Important

The attached document should be in PDF format.

Always verify the fax number and attachment before sending.

10. Call Tracking

Call Tracking allows you to review the practice’s call history, including:

  • Incoming calls
  • Outgoing calls
  • Missed calls
  • Voicemails
  • Call recordings

Steps

  1. Open Call Tracking.
  2. Select the required date range.
  3. Use the available filters.
  4. Select the required call type.
  5. Review the results.
  6. Open the relevant call when additional details or recording playback is required.

Training Tip

When looking for a specific call:

First narrow down the date range → Then apply the appropriate call-type filter.

11. Call Flow

Call Flow determines the path an incoming call takes through the phone system.

It can contain:

  • Greeting
  • Menu
  • Schedule
  • Ring
  • Simulring
  • Voicemail

Navigation

Voice Module → Phone System → Call Flow

Adding an Element

  1. Open Call Flow.
  2. Click the + icon.
  3. Select the required element.
  4. Configure the element.
  5. Arrange the elements in the required order.
  6. Save the changes.

Important Call Flow Rules

Element Purpose
Greeting Should always be placed first when a greeting is required.
Voicemail Should always be at the end of the relevant call path.
Schedule Used for business hours.
Ring Used when one specific line or external number needs to ring.
Simulring Used when multiple lines/numbers should ring simultaneously.

Example Call Flow

Incoming Call → Greeting → Schedule → Business Hours → Simulring → Multiple Staff Phones → No Answer → Voicemail

12. First Call Resolution

Common FCR Requests

Examples include:

  • Changing a greeting
  • Updating voicemail
  • Enabling/disabling Call Override
  • Enabling DND
  • Basic line/user association
  • Basic phone troubleshooting
  • Checking call recordings
  • Reviewing Call Flow

FCR Approach

Use the following sequence when handling eligible requests:

Understand the Issue → Identify the Correct Feature → Make the Change → Verify the Change → Explain Any Required Customer Action → Confirm Resolution

The goal is to complete the request correctly while ensuring the customer understands any action they need to take.

13. Grandstream & Yealink Phones

Grandstream and Yealink phones have similar basic call-management functions.

New trainees should be comfortable with:

  • Answering calls
  • Holding/unholding calls
  • Blind transfers
  • Attended transfers
  • Playing voicemail
  • Muting/unmuting
  • Enabling/disabling DND
  • Rebooting the phone

13.1 Call Hold

  1. Answer the call.
  2. Press the Hold/Pause button.
  3. The caller is placed on hold.
  4. Press the appropriate button again to resume the call.

13.2 Blind Transfer

A Blind Transfer sends the caller directly to another extension/number without speaking to the receiving person first.

Steps

  1. Press Transfer.
  2. Enter the destination extension number.
  3. Press Transfer again to complete the transfer.

Example:
Patient → Reception → Directly transferred to Billing

13.3 Attended Transfer

An Attended Transfer allows the user to speak with the receiving person before transferring the caller.

Steps

  1. Press Transfer.
  2. Enter the destination extension number.
  3. Speak with the receiving staff member.
  4. Once the recipient is ready, press Transfer again.

Example:
Patient → Reception → Reception speaks with Billing → Patient transferred to Billing

Transfer Comparison

Blind Transfer Attended Transfer
Transfer → Destination extension → Transfer again Transfer → Destination extension → Speak with recipient → Transfer again
No conversation with recipient first Speak with recipient first

13.4 Playing Voicemail

  1. Locate the Voicemail button/option.
  2. Press it.
  3. Follow the phone prompts.
  4. Enter the PIN/credentials if requested.
  5. Select the voicemail message.
  6. Play the message.
  7. Use the available options to manage the message.

Note: The exact button may vary depending on the Grandstream or Yealink model.

13.5 Mute

Mute stops the other person from hearing the user’s microphone while keeping the call connected.

Steps

  1. Press the Mute button.
  2. Verify that mute is active.
  3. Press Mute again to unmute.

Troubleshooting Tip: If the caller says, “I can’t hear you,” check whether the phone is accidentally on Mute.

13.6 Do Not Disturb (DND)

DND prevents the phone from ringing for incoming calls according to the phone/system configuration.

Enable DND

  1. Locate the DND option/button.
  2. Press it.
  3. Verify that DND is displayed as active.

Disable DND

Press the DND option/button again.

Troubleshooting Tip

If a user’s phone is not ringing, always check DND first before making system-level changes.

13.7 Phone Reboot

A phone reboot may be required after certain configuration changes, such as updating the phone’s label name.

Steps

  1. Press Menu.
  2. Scroll to the bottom.
  3. Select Reboot.
  4. Confirm if prompted.
  5. Wait for the phone to restart.

14. Phone Troubleshooting Quick Guide

Issue What to Check
Phone is not ringing DND enabled; correct user associated with extension; extension active; Call Flow routing; Call Override enabled
Updated label is not showing Label saved; correct extension updated; physical phone rebooted
Caller cannot hear the user Mute enabled; handset/headset connected correctly; unmute and test again
Need to transfer a call Use Blind or Attended Transfer based on the requirement
Calls are routing somewhere unexpected Call Flow, Schedule, Call Override, Ring, Simulring, and Voicemail destination

DND Quick Action

The training also covered the phone shortcut:

  • Long press Mute → Enable DND
  • Long press Mute again → Disable DND

15. Quick Navigation Reference

Requirement Navigation / Action
Change extension label Lines → Edit/Pencil
Change user association Lines → Edit/Pencil
Reboot phone Phone → Menu → Reboot
Block a number Voice Module → Blocked Callers
Change hold music Voice Module → Hold Music
Enable/disable Call Override Voice Module → Call Override
Add audio recording Voice Module → Audio Library
Record audio Audio Library → Record Your Own
Upload audio Audio Library → Upload
Check outgoing recording Voice Module → Call Recording
Check incoming recording Call Flow
Create additional VM box Voicemail / VM section
Send eFax ADIT Home → Blue + → Fax
Review calls Call Tracking
Configure call routing Voice Module → Phone System → Call Flow
Hold a call Phone → Hold/Pause
Transfer without speaking Transfer → Destination extension → Transfer
Transfer after speaking Transfer → Destination extension → Speak → Transfer
Mute/unmute Phone → Mute
Enable/disable DND Phone → DND
DND shortcut Long press Mute

16. Key Training Takeaways

Trainees should be able to:

  1. Navigate the Voice Module and identify the correct feature.
  2. Manage Lines and User Associations.
  3. Understand when a phone reboot is required.
  4. Configure basic Blocked Caller settings.
  5. Handle Call Hold, Call Override, Audio Library, and Call Recording requests.
  6. Understand the requirements for additional voicemail boxes based on the practice version.
  7. Send an eFax correctly.
  8. Use Call Tracking to locate and review calls.
  9. Understand and troubleshoot basic Call Flow configurations.
  10. Apply the FCR approach to eligible customer requests.
  11. Perform basic Grandstream and Yealink phone functions.
  12. Troubleshoot common issues such as phone not ringing, no audio, incorrect routing, DND, and label updates.
  13. Distinguish between Blind Transfer and Attended Transfer.
  14. Use the Quick Navigation Reference when handling live tickets.

17. Final Reference

The expectation following this training is that trainees use this document as a quick reference when handling basic Voice Module and phone-system requests.

For any request that falls outside the covered functionality or requires additional authorization, the appropriate support/escalation process should be followed rather than making an unsupported configuration change.

Introduction to Adit voice

Adit Voice is an All-In-One VOIP Phone System designed specifically for dental offices to centralize patient communication. It is user-friendly and easy to install, operating using your internet connection. This system is intended to help dental practices move beyond traditional landlines, offering more tools for the front desk for a fraction of the cost, and saying goodbye to missed calls.

Key Features and Functionality

Centralized Communication Management:

  • Adit Voice allows practices to manage all calls, text messages, and faxes in one place.
  • It functions using the existing internet connection and does not require changing the current phone number.
  • Through the Engage Integration, practices can use one phone number for texting, reminders, and voice.

Integration with Practice Management Software:

  • Adit Voice integrates with dental practice management software to centralize all patient data.
  • When a patient calls, a pop-up window appears on the receptionist’s computer screen immediately.
  • This pop-up shows relevant patient information, including the Patient’s Name, Phone Number, Last & Next Appointment Date, and Balance Due.
  • Integrating with Adit’s Notify Desktop App allows staff to immediately see the Caller ID of the inbound caller.

Advanced Call Handling and Routing:

  • The system allows practices to build call flows that automatically route calls.
  • Calls can be routed based on criteria such as the time of day, call source, or other unique criteria that work for the practice.
  • This functionality provides enhanced control over how, when, and where calls are routed, moving beyond the capabilities of regular dental office phones, which often only offer caller ID and tone-based routing.

Data and Operational Insights

Adit Voice integrates with Adit’s existing Call Tracking feature to collect valuable data and operational insights. This integration records and stores all phone calls, faxes, and voicemails in one place.

Key Insights Provided:

  • Identification of at what times of the day the practice is missing calls.
  • Tracking the number of rings it takes before a staff member picks up the call.
  • A comparison of staff members who are picking up and making outbound calls.
  • Data on how often staff members are answering or following up on missed calls.
  • Insights into why leads are not converting.
  • Identification of which team member brings in more new patients.

AI Technology and Value Optimization

Adit Voice goes beyond a typical dental VoIP phone system by incorporating AI technology.

  • AI technology is used to qualify all inbound and outbound calls.
  • It provides a dashboard that shows which calls carry the highest potential value based on the type of procedure needed.
  • This AI feature ensures that team members know how to prioritize calls and maximize revenue.
  • The system helps practices tap into the potential patient pool represented by the 78% of all inbound inquiries to dental offices that typically do not book an appointment.

Platform Context

Adit Voice is one component of the larger Adit platform. It is categorized under the “Centralize Communications” module, which also includes Phones & TeleMed, Emails & eFax, Texting & Reminders, and Call Tracking. The overall Adit platform is described as the All in One AI-Powered Platform. Promotions are frequently offered, such as Free phones & VoIP for life when signing up with Adit.

What is Adit Voice?

Adit Voice is a cloud-based VoIP communication platform designed specifically for healthcare practices.
It unifies phone calls, texts, emails, voicemails, and faxes into one centralized system, giving staff a streamlined and efficient way to manage all patient communications. Integrated directly with your practice management and EHR system, Adit Voice helps teams deliver faster service, reduce missed opportunities, and create a smoother patient experience.
From AI-powered call scoring to voicemail-to-text transcription and advanced analytics, Adit Voice equips healthcare teams with tools that improve efficiency, boost conversions, and enhance overall operational performance.

How Does Adit Voice Work?

Adit Voice works by combining cloud-based VoIP technology, real-time system integrations, and automation tools to simplify communication across your entire practice:

1. Cloud-Based Phone System:
All calls are made and received over the internet, eliminating the need for traditional phone lines or on-site hardware.
Staff can use desktop softphones, mobile apps, or desk phones-anywhere, anytime.

2. Unified Communication Hub
Calls, texts, voicemails, and faxes all appear in one centralized dashboard, allowing front desk teams to manage every patient interaction from a single place.

3. Real-Time EHR & PMS Integration
When a patient calls, Adit Voice instantly displays key information from your systems, such as:
-Name
-Upcoming appointments
-Account balance
-Past communication history
This helps staff personalize each interaction and work more efficiently.

4. Automated Reminders & Messaging
Adit Voice automatically sends appointment reminders, confirmations, and follow-ups reducing no-shows and saving staff time.

5. Smart Call Routing
Custom call flows ensure every call reaches the right person or department based on:
-Time of day
-Caller type
-Custom rules set by the practice

This helps keep wait times low and patient satisfaction high.

6. Advanced Analytics & AI Insights
Adit Voice tracks call volumes, missed calls, wait times, staffing performance, and more.
AI evaluates calls, identifies high-value leads, and highlights missed opportunities-helping practices grow and convert more patients.

7. Always-On Reliability
Even during internet issues or outages, calls can automatically forward to mobile devices, ensuring communication never stops.

Port your number(s) to Adit

Before we get started, please keep in mind that only the Owner-level and Manager-level users are able to port in numbers.
Port in your existing Number.

Typically, when you sign up for Adit there is a section in your first Welcome Questionnaire that asks you for information about any numbers you would like to port. If for some reason your practice still needs to port in a number, please follow the below instructions. These instructions apply to landline numbers, fax numbers and tracking numbers.

To Port in your existing number:

  1. Click on the Settings gear icon at the top right corner of your Adit platform.

  2. Select Phone System Under the Voice menu..

  3. Select the Location

  4. Click the “Port-In” button

  5. Select the location you are wanting to port the number for and click Continue

  6. Fill out the form and click submit. Our team will follow up with you on further instructions and updates on the status of your port. This can typically take 1 to 2 weeks depending on your existing provider.

How to setup Multiple voicemail boxes

This guide outlines the step-by-step process for setting up and managing multiple voicemail boxes in the Adit App.

Step 1: Log into the Adit App

  • Go to the Adit App and log in using your credentials.

Step 2: Access Settings
From the dashboard, click on the gear icon to open the Settings menu.

Step 3: Navigate to Number List

  • Under Voice, click on Voicemail Boxes.

Step 4: Enable Multiple Voicemail Boxes

  • Important: The toggle to enable multiple voicemail boxes can only be activated by the Adit Support Team. The Default Voicemail Box is already present in the VM box.
  • Once enabled :You will see Add Voicemail box option

(Note: default voicemail settings are limited and shared across all users by default).

Step 5: Create New Voicemail Boxes
Once multiple voicemail boxes are enabled:

  1. Click “Create New Voicemail Box”.
  2. Enter a name for the voicemail box (e.g., Front Desk).
  3. From the drop-down, assign users who should access this voicemail.
  4. Optionally, enable email and/or text alerts for message notifications.
  5. Click Save.

You can repeat this process to create voicemail boxes for different teams, roles, or departments.

Step 6: Assign Voicemail Boxes in the Call Flow
After creating a voicemail box:

  1. Go back to Settings > Voice > Voicemail Boxes> Click on your location name.
  2. Hover over the landline number and click the pencil icon to edit the call flow.
  3. In the call flow editor, navigate to the part where the voicemail should occur.
  4. Select the appropriate Voicemail Box from the options available under the select voicemail box and through the drop down option you assign the voicemail.
  5. Save the changes.

Step 8: Assign Voicemail Boxes Under the Line Section
To complete the voicemail setup, it is important to assign the voicemail box to the appropriate extension/line:

  1. Once location is selected, go to the Lines/ Prefixes under Voice section.
  2. Locate the line that is assigned to the user who should receive the voicemail.
  3. You will see a Voicemail Box option for each extension.
  4. From the drop-down list, select the voicemail box you previously created (e.g., Front Desk).
  5. Save the changes.

This will automatically link the voicemail box to that specific extension.

Note:

  • Default Voicemail Box: This is automatically used unless a custom voicemail box is assigned. It cannot be customized.
  • User Access: Only assigned users will have access to messages left in the voicemail box they are assigned to.
  • Alerts: Ensure alerts are enabled if you want to be notified of new voicemails via email or SMS.
  • Make sure the same voicemail box is assigned both in: The Call Flow, and the Line settings of the assigned user/extension.

This ensures that messages are properly routed to the intended user or group.

For assistance enabling multiple voicemail boxes or if you don’t see the option, please contact the Adit Support Team.

A Guide to Managing Users and Their Access

The Adit platform makes it easy for you to invite users, manage their permissions, and control access points across multiple applications and locations.

You will need to understand the 4 key roles a user can be added as in the Adit platform.

  1. Owner: Generally the owner of the practice. Has the ability to edit all settings, edit banking information, export data, etc.
  2. Manager: Generally the office manager. Has the ability to edit most settings.
  3. Staff: Generally the front-desk, associates, and those who would engage with patients.
  4. Read-Only: Generally a consultant. Has the ability to view all information but not edit or engage

Please go to this link to understand all of the adit role permissions: Understanding Adit’s User Role Permissions

If a user is added to the adit app with just access to internal chat, then by default they will be given a read-only user role.

Where to manage user permissions

  1. Click on the Settings gear icon in the top right corner

  2. Select Users

  3. Clicking on “Location Access” will allow you to see all the users and which locations they have access to.

  4. Clicking on “Application Access” will let you see which users have access to which modules.

  5. Please note that all users will have the same level role and same app-level permissions across all locations that they will have access to.

How to add a new user

  1. Click the Add User button

  2. Fill in the user’s information

  3. Select the applications/modules you would like to provide access to this user

  4. Select locations you would like to provide access to this user

  5. You can choose to create a password or send the user an email where they can create their own password.

How to edit an existing user

  1. Click on the User you want to edit

  2. Use the dropdown menu to edit the role

  3. Click on the necessary toggles to change location and module access

Call Tracking - Feature Overview Document

1. Introduction

Call Tracking is an essential feature within the AddIt VoIP system that helps users monitor, analyze, and manage all call-related activities. It provides complete visibility into incoming and outgoing calls, voicemails, faxes, and reporting tools.

This section is accessible from the Call Tracking icon located on the left blue panel at the bottom of the AddIt app.

2. Components of Call Tracking

Call Tracking consists of the following sections:

  • Call Logs
  • Unique Callers
  • Voicemails
  • Insights
  • Faxes
  • Leads
  • Export Call CSV
  • Call Intelligence

Each section provides specific details and tools to help users manage communication efficiently.

3. Call Logs

The Call Logs section gives a detailed breakdown of each call received or made by your organization. It includes caller information, call duration, timestamps, and actionable tools to review or filter call data.

1. Call Volume Graph (Call Volume Breakdown)

At the top of the Call Logs page, you will see a Call Volume Breakdown graph. This graph visually represents:

•   The total number of calls

•   Call frequency over selected dates

•   Trends in call activity

This helps users quickly understand call traffic for the time range selected.

2. Call Information Displayed in Call Logs

Each call entry in the log will show the following details:

a. Caller Information

Displays the caller’s name and phone number.

If the caller is saved in the system, their name will appear. Otherwise, the number only will be shown.

b. Location

Shows the location/office where the call was received.

This is useful for multi-location practices or businesses.

c. Date & Time

Displays the exact date and time when the call occurred.

d. Patient Type

Shows the classification of the caller based on their relationship to the business.

(This is visible for practices using patient categorization.)

e. Call Duration

The total time the call lasted-useful for tracking call handling length and agent performance.

f. Actions Tab

Each call log has an Actions button that includes:

•   **Play Recording** - Listen to the recorded call, if call recording is enabled.

•   **Profile Card** - Displays detailed caller information such as past interactions, notes, and call history.

•   **Timeline** - Shows a chronological sequence of all interactions with that caller, including calls, messages, voicemails, etc.

These tools help in understanding customer communication history.

3. Filters Available in Call Logs

Filtering allows you to narrow down call data based on specific criteria.

A. Quick Filters

You can quickly filter calls by:

•   **New Patients**

•   **Existing Patients**

•   **Scheduling Calls**

•   **Booked Calls**

•   **Not Booked Calls**

•   **Not Resolved Calls**

•   **Missed Calls**

These filters help you categorize calls and analyze specific call types.

B. Date & Time Filters

You can filter call logs based on the date range. Common preset filters include:

  • Today
  • Last 7 Days
  • Last 30 Days
  • Last Month
  • Last Year

You can also select a custom date range to search for calls during a specific period.

C. Add Filter (Advanced Filters)

Under the Add Filter option, you can filter based on:

•   **Number** (Search using a specific phone number)

•   **Source**

•   **Tags**

•   **Extension**

•   **Duration** (Search long or short calls)

•   **Answer Status** (Answered, Missed, Busy, No Answer)

•   **First-Time Calls**

•   **Tracking Number**

•   **Location**

These filters help refine call logs for deeper analysis.

4. Table Settings

The Table Settings option allows users to customize which columns they want to display in the Call Logs table. You can toggle visibility for:

•   **Location**

•   **Time**

•   **Source**

•   **Patient Type**

•   **Duration**

•   **Tracking Number**

•   **Extension Number**

This helps personalize the view based on user preference.

5. Export Options (CSV & PDF)

The Call Logs section also provides export options for reporting or documentation.

A. Export CSV

You have two CSV export choices:

1\. **Export CSV - Current View**

•   Exports only the columns visible in your current table settings.

2\. **Export CSV - All Columns**

•   Exports all available call log data regardless of your on-screen view.

B. Download PDF

You can export the complete call log data into a PDF format for easier sharing or offline reference.

C. Save View

Allows you to save custom table settings + filters so you can quickly access the same configuration later without re-selecting filters.

4. Voicemails

The Voicemail section helps users manage all voicemail messages received on the account.

Voicemails Table will have the following columns. Table can be customized to show based on practice preference

Adit Voice : Master Document (continued, part 1)

  • Caller - User id of the caller
  • Tracking Number - The original number that received the voicemail
  • Time - Time stamp of the voicemail
  • Location - Location of the organization which received the voicemail
  • Source - Based on the source from the tracking number that received the voicemail
  • Duration - Total duration of the voicemail
  • Voicemail Box - The voicemail box which received the voicemail
  • Voicemails will also have an archive functionality when archived will push the voicemail to the Archived tab. To unarchive click on the unarchive option and it will push the voicemail back to the inbox

Voicemail Transcription

  • The system automatically converts voicemail audio into text format.
  • Benefits include:
  • Quickly reviewing message content without listening to the recording.
  • Improving documentation and faster response times.
  • Accessibility for users who cannot play audio in certain environments.

Call Summary is a short, automatically generated overview of the voicemail message.

When the system transcribes a voicemail, it also creates a quick summary so that you can understand the main purpose of the caller’s message without listening to the entire voicemail or reading the full transcription.

What it means:

  • It highlights the key points from the voicemail.
  • Gives you a brief idea of why the caller contacted you.
  • Helps you quickly decide if the voicemail is urgent or what action is needed.
  • Saves time by summarizing the most important details.

5. Faxes

The Fax section stores and manages all incoming and outgoing fax communications.

Details available in Fax Section:

  • Location / Fax Number: Which fax number received or sent the fax.
  • Date & Time: When the fax was received or delivered.
  • Sender Information: Shows the number from which the fax was sent.
  • Pages: Number of pages in the fax.
  • Status: Indicates whether the fax was received, delivered, failed, etc.
  • Open Fax File: You can open and view the fax document directly.
  • Archive / Unarchive: Helps in organizing fax records.

6. Insights

The Insights section in the Call Tracking module provides a complete analytical overview of your organization’s call performance. It visually displays call trends, call volume, caller behavior, patient types, and call outcomes. This data helps businesses evaluate communication efficiency, identify patterns, and optimize call handling processes.

1. Overall Call Summary

The top section of Insights displays a summarized breakdown of all call activities for the selected time period. These metrics help you quickly understand total call volume and caller behavior.

A. Total Number of Calls

This represents the overall count of all calls received and made by your practice or business during the selected date range.

It includes:

•   Incoming calls

•   Outgoing calls

•   Answered, missed, and busy calls

This number gives you an overall picture of call traffic.

B. Incoming Calls

This metric shows the total number of calls your business received from customers or patients.

Incoming calls include:

•   Answered calls

•   Missed calls

•   Calls missed during business hours

Monitoring incoming calls helps evaluate how well your team handles customer inquiries.

C. Outgoing Calls

This displays the total number of calls made by your team to customers, patients, or leads.

Outgoing calls may include:

•   Follow-ups

•   Appointment confirmations

•   Reminders

•   Call backs

Tracking outgoing calls helps measure outreach and follow-up productivity.

D. Unique Callers

Unique callers represent the total number of individual people who contacted your business during the selected timeframe.

Even if a person calls multiple times, they are counted once in this section.

This helps identify:

•   How many different customers reached out

•   First-time caller trends

•   Repeat engagement levels

E. Unique Recipients

This shows the number of unique people your team dialed out to.

It includes:

•   New outbound contacts

•   Follow-ups to different individuals

•   Callbacks to patients or leads

This metric helps understand outbound communication reach.

2. Incoming Calls Breakdown

The Insights section includes a dedicated breakdown of incoming calls to show call outcomes.

A. Total Incoming Calls

This is the total number of inbound calls received from all customers during the selected date period.

B. Incoming Calls Answered

Shows how many inbound calls were successfully answered by your team.

This helps measure staff responsiveness and call handling efficiency.

C. Incoming Calls Missed

This displays the total number of calls that rang but were not answered.

Tracking missed calls helps identify staffing gaps, peak call times, and areas requiring improvement.

D. Incoming Calls Missed During Business Hours

This is a critical metric.

It shows how many calls were missed during your official working hours.

These missed calls often indicate:

Adit Voice : Master Document (continued, part 2)

•   Missed opportunities

•   Understaffing during peak hours

•   Customer dissatisfaction risks

This helps businesses take corrective action in real time.

3. Graphs and Visual Analytics in Insights

The Insights section provides multiple visual graphs to help you interpret call trends more clearly.

A. Total Calls by Call Direction (Graph)

This graph visually represents calls based on direction:

•   Total inbound calls

•   Total outbound calls

It helps you compare call flow patterns and understand communication workload distribution.

B. Call Volume by Hours (Graph)

This graph breaks down call volume hour-by-hour.

It helps identify:

•   Peak call hours

•   Hours with low call activity

•   Best staffing times

•   Patterns in customer calling behavior

This is especially helpful for scheduling and workforce planning.

C. Unique New Callers by Call Direction (Graph)

This graph displays:

•   How many first-time callers contacted your business

•   Whether they were inbound or outbound

•   Trends in new customer engagement

It helps track new patient acquisition, first-time inquiries, and outreach effectiveness.

4. Calls Breakdown by Patient Type

This section categorizes all calls based on patient type (useful for healthcare/medical practices).The breakdown includes:

A. All Calls

Shows the total number of calls, regardless of caller type.

B. New Patient Calls

Displays how many first-time patients or customers contacted your practice.

C. Existing Patient Calls

Shows calls from individuals who are already registered with your practice.

D. Unknown & Answered Calls

Represents calls from unknown callers that were answered.

E. Unknown & Missed Calls

Shows calls from unknown callers that were missed. This is crucial because unknown callers may include new potential patients.

5. Total New Patient Calls by Call Source

This section displays where new patient calls originated from, such as:

•   Google Ads

•   Organic search

•   Website

•   Direct calls

•   Social media numbers

•   Tracking numbers

This breakdown helps identify which marketing channels are bringing in new patients, enabling better budget allocation and stronger marketing decisions.

6. Filters in the Insights Section

You can refine your insights using multiple filters for better analysis.

A. Quick Filters

These allow you to instantly filter data based on predefined criteria such as:

•   New patients

•   Existing patients

•   Scheduling calls

•   Missed calls

•   Business-hour calls

•   First-time callers

These make it easy to analyze specific categories quickly.

B. Date & Time Filters

You can filter insight data by selecting:

•   Today

•   Yesterday

•   Last 7 Days

•   Last 30 Days

•   Last Month

•   Custom Date Range

These help review call trends for specific periods.

Summary

The Insights section gives you a complete analytical overview of your call activities, including:

•   Total calls

•   Incoming & outgoing calls

•   Unique callers & recipients

•   Missed vs. answered calls

•   New vs. existing caller breakdown

•   Call behavior trends

•   Hourly call volume

•   Patient-type analytics

•   Marketing source contribution

•   Beautiful, detailed graphs for data interpretation

•   Full filtering options for deeper reporting

This section is designed to help businesses track performance, optimize staffing, boost patient/customer engagement, and make informed operational decisions.

8. Export Call CSV Report

The Export Call CSV feature allows you to generate a detailed CSV report of all call logs.

Uses:

  • Helps in creating performance reports.
  • Useful for call volume analysis, team tracking, and business reporting.
  • Can be exported for sharing with management or for record-keeping.

7. Call Intelligence

Call Intelligence provides advanced reporting and analytical tools to understand caller behavior and agent performance.

Features Include:

  • Detailed caller analytics.
  • Call patterns and time-of-day trends.
  • Insights into frequently calling customers.
  • Performance metrics across different numbers or teams.

This section helps organizations make data-driven decisions, optimize their call routing, and improve the overall customer experience.

Call Tracking in Adit VoIP provides a centralized place to view and manage all forms of communication calls, voicemails, faxes, and caller insights. It supports better customer service, accurate reporting, and smooth day-to-day operations for any business.

This helps personalize the view based on user preference.

5. Export Options (CSV & PDF)

The Call Logs section also provides export options for reporting or documentation.

A. Export CSV

You have two CSV export choices:

1\. **Export CSV - Current View**

•   Exports only the columns visible in your current table settings.

2\. **Export CSV - All Columns**

•   Exports all available call log data regardless of your on-screen view.

B. Download PDF

You can export the complete call log data into a PDF format for easier sharing or offline reference.

C. Save View

Allows you to save custom table settings + filters so you can quickly access the same configuration later without re-selecting filters.

Voicemails

The Voicemail section helps users manage all voicemail messages received on the account.

Voicemails Table will have the following columns. Table can be customized to show based on practice preference

  • Caller - User id of the caller
  • Tracking Number - The original number that received the voicemail
  • Time - Time stamp of the voicemail
  • Location - Location of the organization which received the voicemail
  • Source - Based on the source from the tracking number that received the voicemail
  • Duration - Total duration of the voicemail
  • Voicemail Box - The voicemail box which received the voicemail
  • Voicemails will also have an archive functionality when archived will push the voicemail to the Archived tab. To unarchive click on the unarchive option and it will push the voicemail back to the inbox

Voicemail Transcription

  • The system automatically converts voicemail audio into text format.
  • Benefits include:
  • Quickly reviewing message content without listening to the recording.
  • Improving documentation and faster response times.
  • Accessibility for users who cannot play audio in certain environments.

Call Summary is a short, automatically generated overview of the voicemail message.

When the system transcribes a voicemail, it also creates a quick summary so that you can understand the main purpose of the caller’s message without listening to the entire voicemail or reading the full transcription.

What it means:

  • It highlights the key points from the voicemail.
  • Gives you a brief idea of why the caller contacted you.
  • Helps you quickly decide if the voicemail is urgent or what action is needed.
  • Saves time by summarizing the most important details.

Faxes

The Fax section stores and manages all incoming and outgoing fax communications.

Details available in Fax Section:

  • Location / Fax Number: Which fax number received or sent the fax.
  • Date & Time: When the fax was received or delivered.
  • Sender Information: Shows the number from which the fax was sent.
  • Pages: Number of pages in the fax.
  • Status: Indicates whether the fax was received, delivered, failed, etc.
  • Open Fax File: You can open and view the fax document directly.
  • Archive / Unarchive: Helps in organizing fax records.

Leads

Leads in Call tracking refers to all the scheduling opportunities that practice had for unique new patients that reached out to them. Leads will be housed in 3 sections in Call Intelligence -

  • Follow Up List - Leads that have not booked yet and needs to be followed up on
  • Won Leads - Leads which have booked
  • Lost Leads - Leads which have not booked even after follow up or can’t be booked for other reasons (Insurance not accepted, procedure not offered, doesn’t meet min age requirement etc)

The following actions are available against a lead -

  • Call Detail - This will show the call which resulted in the creation of the Lead
  • Lead Card - This will be the profile card of Lead
  • Create Task - This will create a follow up task against the Lead

Insights

Call Tracking - Insights Section

The Insights section in the Call Tracking module provides a complete analytical overview of your organization’s call performance. It visually displays call trends, call volume, caller behavior, patient types, and call outcomes. This data helps businesses evaluate communication efficiency, identify patterns, and optimize call handling processes.

1. Overall Call Summary

The top section of Insights displays a summarized breakdown of all call activities for the selected time period. These metrics help you quickly understand total call volume and caller behavior.

A. Total Number of Calls

This represents the overall count of all calls received and made by your practice or business during the selected date range.

It includes:

•   Incoming calls

•   Outgoing calls

•   Answered, missed, and busy calls

This number gives you an overall picture of call traffic.

B. Incoming Calls

This metric shows the total number of calls your business received from customers or patients.

Incoming calls include:

•   Answered calls

•   Missed calls

•   Calls missed during business hours

Monitoring incoming calls helps evaluate how well your team handles customer inquiries.

C. Outgoing Calls

This displays the total number of calls made by your team to customers, patients, or leads.

Outgoing calls may include:

•   Follow-ups

•   Appointment confirmations

•   Reminders

•   Call backs

Tracking outgoing calls helps measure outreach and follow-up productivity.

D. Unique Callers

Unique callers represent the total number of individual people who contacted your business during the selected timeframe.

Even if a person calls multiple times, they are counted once in this section.

This helps identify:

•   How many different customers reached out

•   First-time caller trends

•   Repeat engagement levels

E. Unique Recipients

This shows the number of unique people your team dialed out to.

It includes:

•   New outbound contacts

•   Follow-ups to different individuals

•   Callbacks to patients or leads

This metric helps understand outbound communication reach.

2. Incoming Calls Breakdown

The Insights section includes a dedicated breakdown of incoming calls to show call outcomes.

A. Total Incoming Calls

This is the total number of inbound calls received from all customers during the selected date period.

B. Incoming Calls Answered

Shows how many inbound calls were successfully answered by your team.

This helps measure staff responsiveness and call handling efficiency.

C. Incoming Calls Missed

This displays the total number of calls that rang but were not answered.

Tracking missed calls helps identify staffing gaps, peak call times, and areas requiring improvement.

D. Incoming Calls Missed During Business Hours

This is a critical metric.

It shows how many calls were missed during your official working hours.

These missed calls often indicate:

•   Missed opportunities

•   Understaffing during peak hours

•   Customer dissatisfaction risks

This helps businesses take corrective action in real time.

3. Graphs and Visual Analytics in Insights

The Insights section provides multiple visual graphs to help you interpret call trends more clearly.

A. Total Calls by Call Direction (Graph)

This graph visually represents calls based on direction:

•   Total inbound calls

•   Total outbound calls

It helps you compare call flow patterns and understand communication workload distribution.

B. Call Volume by Hours (Graph)

This graph breaks down call volume hour-by-hour.

It helps identify:

Adit Voice : Master Document (continued, part 4)

•   Peak call hours

•   Hours with low call activity

•   Best staffing times

•   Patterns in customer calling behavior

This is especially helpful for scheduling and workforce planning.

C. Unique New Callers by Call Direction (Graph)

This graph displays:

•   How many first-time callers contacted your business

•   Whether they were inbound or outbound

•   Trends in new customer engagement

It helps track new patient acquisition, first-time inquiries, and outreach effectiveness.

4. Calls Breakdown by Patient Type

This section categorizes all calls based on patient type (useful for healthcare/medical practices).The breakdown includes:

A. All Calls

Shows the total number of calls, regardless of caller type.

B. New Patient Calls

Displays how many first-time patients or customers contacted your practice.

C. Existing Patient Calls

Shows calls from individuals who are already registered with your practice.

D. Unknown & Answered Calls

Represents calls from unknown callers that were answered.

E. Unknown & Missed Calls

Shows calls from unknown callers that were missed. This is crucial because unknown callers may include new potential patients.

5. Total New Patient Calls by Call Source

This section displays where new patient calls originated from, such as:

•   Google Ads

•   Organic search

•   Website

•   Direct calls

•   Social media numbers

•   Tracking numbers

This breakdown helps identify which marketing channels are bringing in new patients, enabling better budget allocation and stronger marketing decisions.

6. Filters in the Insights Section

You can refine your insights using multiple filters for better analysis.

A. Quick Filters

These allow you to instantly filter data based on predefined criteria such as:

•   New patients

•   Existing patients

•   Scheduling calls

•   Missed calls

•   Business-hour calls

•   First-time callers

These make it easy to analyze specific categories quickly.

B. Date & Time Filters

You can filter insight data by selecting:

•   Today

•   Yesterday

•   Last 7 Days

•   Last 30 Days

•   Last Month

•   Custom Date Range

These help review call trends for specific periods.

Summary

The Insights section gives you a complete analytical overview of your call activities, including:

•   Total calls

•   Incoming & outgoing calls

•   Unique callers & recipients

•   Missed vs. answered calls

•   New vs. existing caller breakdown

•   Call behavior trends

•   Hourly call volume

•   Beautiful, detailed graphs for data interpretation

This section is designed to help businesses track performance, optimize staffing, boost patient/customer engagement, and make informed operational decisions.

Call Intelligence provides advanced reporting and analytical tools to understand caller behavior and agent performance.

Features Include:

This section helps organizations make data-driven decisions, optimize their call routing, and improve the overall customer experience.

How to Set Up Your Call Flow (Call Tree)

The call flow allows you to do the following:

  • Select which phones in your office should ring and when
  • Establish your office schedule for inbound calls
  • Play a greeting when patients call you
  • Play a voicemail greeting for when you are not available
  • Route calls intelligently based on the options your patients select in the call tree
  • And so much more!

Numbers Overview:

Our system provides two types of phone numbers under each account:

  • Landline Number - Used for regular inbound and outbound voice calls.
  • Fax Number - Dedicated for sending and receiving faxes.

  8. Schedule: branch out your call flow based on the time of the day and day of the week

How to Update a Voicemail in a Simple Call Flow:

Purpose

This article explains how users can update or change the voicemail in a simple call flow within the Adit platform.

Prerequisites

  • Users must have access to the Adit account.
  • User must have permission to modify Call Flows.
  • The voicemail audio file (if using a custom recording) should be available in the Audio library

Steps to Update Voicemail in a Simple Call Flow

1. Log in to Your Adit Account

  • Navigate to the Adit login page.
  • Enter your credentials and access the dashboard.

2. Go to the Settings

Click the Gear Icon (Settings).

3. Select Phone System Under the Voice menu.

4. Select the Location

  • Click on the Location Name under the blue left panel.
  • The section expands and displays related settings.

5. Access the Call Flow

  • On the Top, you will see two numbers:
  • One assigned to Fax
  • One assigned to Landline
  • Click on the landline number to open the call flow editor.

6. Scroll to the Bottom to Find the Voicemail option

In a simple call flow, the Voicemail section is located toward the bottom of the call flow page.

7. Update the Voicemail

There are two options for updating voicemail:

Option A: Read Message

  • Select Read Message.
  • Enter the text you want the caller to hear.
  • The system will read the text using a robotic text-to-speech voice.

Option B: Play Recording

  • Select Play Recording.
  • Choose a pre-recorded audio file from your Audio Library.
  • If the file is not yet uploaded:
  • Upload it to the Audio Library first.
  • Then select it for the voicemail.

8. Save the Voicemail Settings

  • After updating the voicemail section, click Save inside the voicemail section.

9. Update the Call Flow

  • Scroll to the bottom of the call flow page.
  • Click the Update icon/button to finalize the call flow changes.

Result:

The voicemail for the selected call flow is successfully updated. All incoming calls to that number will now receive the newly configured voicemail message.

How to Create and Use a Duplicate Call Flow in Adit

Overview

A duplicate call flow is useful when:

  • A client wants to create a backup of their existing call flow
  • The main call flow was accidentally deleted
  • The client wants to create a test version before applying changes to the main number

This article explains how to create, copy, and apply a duplicate call flow to a landline number or tracking number.

1. How to Access the Call Flow Section

To view and manage call flows:

  • Log in to your Adit app.

  • Click on the Settings (gear) icon.

  • Go to Call Flow Templates under the Voice section.

  • Select the Location Name from the Drop menu on the top Left Corner

  • Once selected, it will expand all available sections.

  • Click on Call Flow.

  • This is where duplicate call flows, backup flows, or test flows can be created and managed.

2. How to Create a Duplicate Call Flow

If a client wants to prepare a backup or a test version:

  • In the Call Flow section, click on Create Call Flow.
  • Enter a name for the new call flow for example:
  • Test Call Flow
  • Main Flow Copy
  • Backup Flow
  • Build or replicate the call flow as needed.
  • Save the call flow once all changes are completed.

This duplicate call flow can be used to restore the main flow if the original is ever deleted.

3. How to Copy an Existing Call Flow to the Main Line Number

Adit Voice : Master Document (continued, part 6)

  • If the main call flow was deleted, you can restore it using the duplicate call flow:
  • Open the duplicate call flow from the Call Flow section.
  • Scroll to the bottom of the pageant click the Copy Flow button.
  • A list of numbers will appear.
  • Select the main landline number to which you want the call flow applied.
  • Confirm and save the changes.
  • This will copy the entire call flow setup to the main number.

4. How to Apply the Duplicate Call Flow to a Tracking Number

If a client wants a tracking number to use the newly created duplicate call flow:

  • Go to Settings.
  • Under Voice , Click on Tracking numbers
  • In the Action column, click the Pencil (edit) icon.
  • Under Route To, select Call Flow.
  • A dropdown will appear choose the call flow you created.
  • Scroll down and click Save at the bottom.

This updates the tracking number so it now uses the selected duplicate call flow.

5. When Should You Use a Duplicate Call Flow?

A duplicate or backup call flow is recommended when:

  • Clients frequently change their call flow and want a safe version to revert to the original call flow was deleted and needs to be restored
  • Testing is required without affecting live calls
  • Separate call patterns for tracking numbers need to match the main line’s structure

KB Article: Call Flow Update - Questions & Answers

1. How can I update the schedule in my call flow?

Answer:
To update the business hours or schedule in your call flow, follow these steps:

  1. Log in to your Adit app.
  2. Click on the Settings (gear) icon.
  3. Go to Phone system under the Voice section.
  4. Click on the Location Name.
  5. Click on the Landline Numbers, to open the call flow.
  6. Click on the Schedule option.
  7. Update the days and hours as per your requirement.
  8. Once all the changes are done, click the Update button to save.

2. How can I add or update Menu Options (IVR) in the call flow?

Answer:
If a client wants multiple menu options such as:

  • Press 1 for Front Desk
  • Press 2 for Appointments
  • Press 3 for Voicemail

Follow these steps:

  1. Log in to the Adit app and open the Call Flow by following the same steps mentioned above.
  2. Click on the Menu option.
  3. Add a Greeting and mention the available options (e.g., “Press 1 for Front Desk, Press 2 for Appointments, Press 3 for Voicemail”).
  4. Under Option 1, enter the Extension Number for the Front Desk.
  5. Under Option 2, enter the Extension Number for Appointments.
  6. Under Option 3, select Voicemail.
  7. After configuring all options, click the Update icon to save the changes.

3. How can I update the voicemail greeting in the call flow?

Answer:
To update the voicemail greeting, follow these steps:

  1. Open the Call Flow and scroll to the bottom where the voicemail option appears.
  2. You will have two options to update voicemail: Text Format: Type the message and it will be read using the AI voice. Play Recording: Use your own recorded audio as the voicemail greeting.
  3. If choosing Play Recording, make sure the recording is already uploaded in the Audio Library. Otherwise, it will not appear in the list.
  4. Select your recording from the Play Recording dropdown.
  5. Click Save, and then hit the Update icon to apply changes.

4. How can I add an external number to the call flow?

Answer:
If a client wants to forward calls to an external number (for example, forwarding to an AI answering service), follow these steps:

  1. Open the Call Flow.
  2. Add a Ring option at the desired position in the flow.
  3. Enter the External Phone Number you want to forward calls to.
  4. Select the Ring Duration e.g., 10-20 seconds, depending on the client’s preference.
  5. Save and click Update to finalize.

5. How can I update the After Hours call handling?

Answer:
To make changes to After Hours behavior:

  1. Open the Call Flow.
  2. Click on the Any Other Time option (this represents After Hours).
  3. Depending on the client’s requirement, you can:
  • Send calls directly to Voicemail: Scroll to the voicemail section and update the greeting if needed.
  • Add a Menu (IVR) during After Hours: Add menu options following the same steps mentioned in the Menu section.
  • Forward calls to an External Number: Click on the Ring option and enter the external number, then save.
  • Once done, click Update to apply all changes.

How to Enable Inbound & Outbound Call Recording

Follow the steps below to confirm call recording is enabled for both Outbound and Inbound calls.

1. Enable Outbound Call Recording

Outbound recording is enabled at the organization level and applies to each location individually. Depending on your setup, you may see one location or multiple locations.

  1. Go to the Settings page by clicking the Settings icon in the top-right corner.

  2. Under the Voice section, click Call Recording.

  3. Select the Location Name from the Drop menu on the top Left Corner

  4. You’ll now see the Call Recording page showing all the selected locations. Toggle Outbound Recording to ON for each location.

    Outbound recording is now enabled.

2. Enable Inbound Call Recording

Inbound recording is configured at the number level. You’ll need to enable recording on each main line or landline number.

  1. Go to Settings → Voice→ Phone System

  2. Select the location

  3. Click on the Landline Number.

  4. Toggle Record Inbound Calls to ON.

  5. Inbound recording is now enabled for the selected location.

If You Have Multiple Locations

Repeat the inbound recording steps for each location’s main line number. Outbound toggles will already appear per-location under the Call Recording section.

Final Check

  • Outbound recording toggles are ON for all locations
  • Inbound recording is enabled for each main line number

How to setup Multiple voicemail boxes

This guide outlines the step-by-step process for setting up and managing multiple voicemail boxes in the Adit App.

Step 1: Log into the Adit App

  • Go to the Adit App and log in using your credentials.

Step 2: Access Settings
From the dashboard, click on the gear icon to open the Settings menu.

Step 3: Navigate to Voicemail Boxes

  • Under Settings, click on Voicemail Boxes under the Voice Section.

Step 4: Enable Multiple Voicemail Boxes

  • Important: The toggle to enable multiple voicemail boxes can only be activated by the Adit Support Team. The Default Voicemail Box is already present in the VM box.
  • Once enabled :You will see Add Voicemail box option

(Note: default voicemail settings are limited and shared across all users by default).

Step 5: Create New Voicemail Boxes
Once multiple voicemail boxes are enabled:

  1. Click “Create New Voicemail Box”.
  2. Enter a name for the voicemail box (e.g., Front Desk).
  3. From the drop-down, assign users who should access this voicemail.
  4. Optionally, enable email and/or text alerts for message notifications.
  5. Click Save.

You can repeat this process to create voicemail boxes for different teams, roles, or departments.

Step 6: Assign Voicemail Boxes in the Call Flow
After creating a voicemail box:

  1. Go back to Settings > Voice > Voicemail Boxes> Click on your location name.
  2. Hover over the landline number and click the pencil icon to edit the call flow.
  3. In the call flow editor, navigate to the part where the voicemail should occur.
  4. Select the appropriate Voicemail Box from the options available under the select voicemail box and through the drop down option you assign the voicemail.
  5. Save the changes.

Step 8: Assign Voicemail Boxes Under the Line Section
To complete the voicemail setup, it is important to assign the voicemail box to the appropriate extension/line:

  1. Once location is selected, go to the Lines/ Prefixes under Voice section.
  2. Locate the line that is assigned to the user who should receive the voicemail.
  3. You will see a Voicemail Box option for each extension.
  4. From the drop-down list, select the voicemail box you previously created (e.g., Front Desk).
  5. Save the changes.

This will automatically link the voicemail box to that specific extension.

Note:

  • Default Voicemail Box: This is automatically used unless a custom voicemail box is assigned. It cannot be customized.
  • User Access: Only assigned users will have access to messages left in the voicemail box they are assigned to.
  • Alerts: Ensure alerts are enabled if you want to be notified of new voicemails via email or SMS.
  • Make sure the same voicemail box is assigned both in: The Call Flow, and the Line settings of the assigned user/extension.

This ensures that messages are properly routed to the intended user or group.

For assistance enabling multiple voicemail boxes or if you don’t see the option, please contact the Adit Support Team.

This behavior is intentional to ensure the correct location configuration is accessed. Guide to Adit’s eFax

Go paperless with Adit’s eFax! To get started on Adit’s eFax please follow these instructions. If you do not have a fax number in the Adit platform already, please refer to the last section of this article: “Adding a Fax Number

Configuring Your Fax Number

  1. Go to Settings

  2. Select Phone System Under the Voice menu.

  3. Click on the Location name

  4. Locate and click on your Fax number

  5. In the “Send incoming faxes to” field, enter the email address where you would like to receive a copy of every fax.
    ****

  6. Click the Add button.

Set Up and Verify Your Outgoing Email

Next, you have to configure and verify the outgoing email.

  1. Navigate to Communications under General (Location-Level).
  2. Type the email address you want to use in the Sender Address field.
    ****
  3. Click the Send Verification Email button.
    ****
  4. You will receive a verification email at the address you entered. Click the link in that email to verify the email address.

Sending a Fax

  1. Navigate and click on the Create Request button at the top
    ****

  2. A pop up will appear
    ****

  3. Click on the Send Fax icon in the pop up.
    ****

  4. Select the Location.

  5. Type in the fax number of the recipient.

  6. If you would like to include a cover sheet, you can toggle the button ON and then type in the subject line and message.
    ****

  7. Upload the document(s) you would like to send. Please only use PDF files.

  8. Click on Send
    ****

Viewing Your Faxes

There are 2 ways to view your faxes.

  1. In the Call Pop

    1. Click on the Call Pop.
    2. Click on the Faxes tab.
      ****

  2. In the Call Tracking module:

    1. Click on the Call Tracking module
      ****

    2. Navigate and then click Fax.

    3. Here you can view your faxes in tabular format. Be sure to update the date range according to your preferences.

Adding a Fax Number

If you do not have a Fax number in your Adit account, you can add a fax number in two ways:

  1. Port-in your existing Fax Number:

  2. Click on the Settings gear icon at the top right corner of your Adit platform.

  3. Select Phone System Under the Voice menu..

  4. Select the Location

  5. Click the “Port-In” button

  6. Select the location you are wanting to port the number for and click Continue

  7. Fill out the form and click submit. Our team will follow up with you on further instructions and updates on the status of your port. This can typically take 1 to 2 weeks depending on your existing provider.

  8. Purchase a new Fax Number:.

  9. Go to Settings

  10. Select Phone System Under the Voice menu.

  11. Click “Order New”

  12. Select the location and country

  13. Select Fax Numbers

  14. Search available Fax Numbers by searching an area code. Please note, some number availability may be limited based on your area. If there is no availability for your desired area code, we recommend trying other area codes within the same vicinity.

  15. Click Place Order.

To open the notification settings, you click on the bell icon located on the top right side of the application interface. This action opens the Desktop Notifications configuration screen.

If you turn off the top element, Desktop Notifications, it acts as a global switch and will turn off all subsequent notifications listed below it.

Here are the elements displayed in the settings screen, explained in one line:

General

  • Desktop Notifications: This global switch enables or disables all alerts for the desktop application.
  • Always on top: This controls whether the application window remains visible above other open applications.
  • Location (Select Location(s)): This allows the user to specify which location(s) they wish to receive notifications for.

Snooze Delay

  • Time to Delay: This sets the duration (e.g., 10 Minutes) before a notification is alerted again.

Communications

  • Incoming Calls: Settings for managing notifications and sound related to calls being received.
  • Parked Calls: Settings for managing notifications and sound related to calls temporarily held.
  • Voicemail: Settings for managing notifications and sound related to new voicemail messages.
  • Missed Calls: Settings for managing notifications and sound related to calls that were not answered.
  • Pages: Settings for managing notifications and sound related to received pages.
  • Call Coaching: Settings for managing notifications and sound related to call coaching events.
  • Missed Opportunity: Settings for managing notifications and sound related to business opportunities that were missed.
  • SMS Receive: Settings for managing notifications and sound related to incoming text messages.
  • Internal Chat Messages: Settings for managing notifications and sound related to internal messages.

Operations

  • Appointment Request: Settings to control notifications for new appointment requests.
  • Appt Double Booking: Settings to control notifications when appointments conflict.
  • Contact Request: Settings to control notifications for requests related to contacts.
  • Patient Forms: Settings to control notifications regarding patient forms.
  • Document Plans: Settings to control notifications for updates concerning document plans.
  • Insurance Verification Passed: Settings to control notifications when insurance verification is successful.
  • Review Received: Settings to control notifications upon the submission of a new review.
  • Follow Up Due: Settings to control notifications alerting that a follow-up action is pending.

Adit Pay

  • Payment Received: Settings to control notifications when a successful payment is recorded.
  • Refund Initiated: Settings to control notifications when the refund process begins.
  • Payment Disputed: Settings to control notifications when a payment is challenged.
  • Payment Plans: Settings to control notifications concerning established payment plans.
  • Subscriptions: Settings to control notifications regarding recurring subscription services.

Mobile Notifications:

To manage notifications:

  1. After opening the application (which shows a Home screen with an Inbox), you navigate to the Settings screen.
  2. On the Settings screen, under the ‘Notifications’ heading, you have access to the Notifications menu, and you can also toggle Do Not Disturb.Tapping into the main Notifications menu reveals multiple categories for which you can independently turn notifications on or off using toggles.

The specific notification options you can manage within the app fall into these categories:

  • Calls: Options include Missed Calls, Voicemails, Faxes, Call Coaching, and Missed Opportunity.

  • Appointments: You can control notifications for Appointment Request, Appointment Double Booking, and Contact Request.

  • Forms: Alerts are available for Patient Form Received and Treatment Plan Accepted.

  • Reviews: Notifications can be managed for Review Received and Feedback Received.

  • SMS Receive: This category includes options for SMS Receive and Internal Chats.

Notification Settings and Call Tracking Management

1. How to Access the Notifications Section

To access the notification configuration within the system:

  1. Navigate to the main application interface (implied by the interface view showing the notification inbox).
  2. Click the Settings icon (typically located in the upper right corner of the application interface).
  3. In the Settings menu, locate the “My Profile” section and select Notifications.
  4. Selecting Notifications may present further options, such as Alerts and Summary. The subsequent settings discussed below are found under the Alerts/Notifications configuration area.

2. Notification Sections Overview

Once in the notification settings, there are four primary categories for setting alerts:

  1. Call Tracking
  2. Online Scheduling
  3. Pozative
  4. Engage
  5. Practice Analytics
    ****

3. Managing Existing Call Tracking Notifications

The Call Tracking section is used to add or edit notifications related to calls and texts to your tracking numbers.

  • Existing Entries: The list displays configured notifications, showing the User, Location, Number, Interaction types (e.g., “All Calls, Voicemail, eFax Delivery Failure…”), and Alert Type (e.g., Email).
  • Editing and Deleting: Each entry has symbols for modification: a pencil symbol is available to edit the parameters, and a delete/trash symbol is available to remove the entry.

4. How to Add New Call Tracking Notifications

To add a new notification to Call Tracking:

  1. Click the “+ Add Call Tracking Notifications” link located below the list of existing entries.
  2. A window labeled “Add Notifications” will appear.

Within this window, you must specify the following parameters:

  • Select Location: Choose the location for the notification (e.g., “North Miami Beach”).
  • Select User: Choose the recipient user from a dropdown list. Options may include specific individuals or organizations (e.g., “Andrea Prieto Poleo,” “Hodson & Meister Orthodontics”).
  • Numbers: Specify the numbers associated with the notification.
  • Interaction (Service Selection): Select the specific events for which the user should be notified using checkboxes. These interactions can include:
    • Calls
    • Missed Opportunities
    • Coaching Opportunities
    • Voicemails
    • eFax Delivery Failure
    • eFax Delivery Success
    • eFax Failed to Receive
  • Alert Type: Select the method of notification (e.g., Email Notification).
  • Click create to activate your new alert
  1. After configuring the settings, click “Create” to save the new notification.

Here are the key fields for the other sections:

  • Online Scheduling: Used to receive alerts for appointments booked. You configure the alert using the Interaction field.
  • Pozative: Used for review alerts, which are configured by selecting the Review Type (e.g., to filter for specific types of reviews).
  • Engage: Used for engagement alerts, which, like Call Tracking, require configuration via the Interaction field.
  • Practice analytics : used for Daily , weekly and monthly reports

To access the browser notifications, you typically click on the bell icon located in the upper right section of the interface.

Notification Panel Structure and Controls

  • Toggle Switch: At the top of the notification panel, there is a toggle labeled “Browser Notification” which allows you to toggle the notifications on or off.
  • Sections: The notifications are organized into two main sections: Inbox and Archive.
  • Filters: A dedicated “Filters” section, shown on the top right (e.g., “Filters: 27”), allows users to segregate and choose notifications according to their requirements.

Notification Content and Details

The list of notifications displays essential details, such as those shown for “Missed Call” entries, including:

  • Sender/Receiver Details: A phone number (e.g., 502-365-4593).
  • Time Stamp: The specific start date and time (e.g., Start Time: Dec 05 at 10:06 AM).
  • Relative Time: The time elapsed since the event (e.g., 1 hour ago).
  • Actions: Each item provides options to “View” or “Mark Read”.

Types of Notifications Available for Segregation (Filtering)

The available filters categorize notifications into three main groups: Communications, Scheduling, and Billing.

Communications This category includes notifications related to calls, texts, and faxes:

  • Missed Call

  • New Message and Voicemail

  • Fax Notifications: Incoming fax and delivered fax message Billing : payment related notifications etc.

    Filters :The filters are used to segregate and manage the list of notifications according to specific requirements,. By selecting the filters, users can refine the notification display to show only the types of events they need to focus on,.

  • The notification panel indicates the total number of filters currently selected (e.g., “Filters: 27”),. Once filters are chosen from the selection menu, the user must click “Apply” to update the list,.

Adit Phone - Quick Start Guide

Overview

Adit Phone systems provide professional communication solutions with multiple models designed for different business needs. This comprehensive guide covers setup, features, and operation for the GRP2613, GRP2616, DP720, and DP750 models.

GRP2613 - Quick Start Guide

Phone Features and Keys

The Adit Phone GRP2613 is equipped with the following key features and buttons:

Adit Voice : Master Document (continued, part 8)

  • Call Park Key - Press to park incoming calls in designated slots (901 or 902). A red light will appear across all phones to indicate a parked call.
  • Hold/Resume Key - Places calls on hold or resumes held calls with the Hold/II button.
  • Voicemail Key - Direct access to voicemail messages.
  • New Message Indicator - LED display showing incoming messages at the top of the device.
  • Conference Key - Initiates conference calls with multiple participants.
  • Headset Key - Enables headset mode once a headset is connected.
  • Mute Key - Mutes microphone during calls and activates Do Not Disturb (DND) mode.
  • Transfer Key - Transfers calls to other extensions or departments (blind or attended transfer).
  • Navigation Key - Scrolls through menus and options on the display.
  • Speaker Key - Enables/disables speakerphone functionality.
  • Phone Key - Initiates phone calls.

The device features a large backlit display showing call information, dual-line indicators, and a numeric keypad (0-9, *, #) with intuitive button layout for easy operation.

Connecting Your Adit Phone GRP2613

Follow these four simple steps to set up your Adit Phone:

Step 1: Find the Ethernet Cable
Locate the ethernet cable connecting your computer to your wall socket or router.

Step 2: Unplug and Reconnect
Unplug the end connected to your computer and plug it into the LAN port on the back of the phone.

Step 3: Connect Additional Ethernet Cable
Connect an additional ethernet cable from your computer into the PC port on the back of the phone.

Step 4: Power Connection
Connect the 12V DC plug to the power jack on the phone, and plug the other end into an outlet.

Using Your Adit Phone GRP2613

  • Call Park Operation:
    1. Press the park soft key and the call will park in that designated slot (901 or 902)
    2. A red light will appear across all your phones to indicate that a call has been parked
    3. Press the park soft key again to pick up that call

  • Call Hold/Resume:
    Press the Hold⏸️ button to place a call on hold and to resume the call.

  • DND Mode (Do Not Disturb):
    Press the mute button to turn Do Not Disturb mode ON/OFF.

  • Headset Mode:
    Press the headset button to use the headset once it’s connected.

  • Intercom:
    Press the intercom soft key or dial 999.

  • Call Transfer:
    There are two different ways to transfer a call:

  1. · Blind Transfer - Transfer directly without speaking to the recipient
  2. · Attended Transfer - Wait for the call to connect first, then press transfer
    1. Press transfer during an active call
    2. Enter in the number and press either blind transfer or attended transfer
    3. If using attended transfer, wait for the call to connect first, then press transfer
  • 3-Way Conference:
    1. Press the conference call key while on an active call
    2. Enter in the number and press dial
    3. Once the call connects, press conference call again
    4. Both calls are now in a conference
