    How to Connect Grandstream GRP2616 to Wi-Fi

Purpose: Configure the GRP 2616 IP phone to connect to a wireless network.

To connect a Grandstream GRP2616 IP phone to a Wi-Fi network, navigate to the phone’s settings, enable Wi-Fi, scan for available networks, select your desired network, and enter the password if required.

Here’s a more detailed breakdown:

1. Access the Wi-Fi settings:

  • Press the “Menu” button on the phone.
  • Navigate to “System” then “Wi-Fi settings”.

2. Enable Wi-Fi:

  • Set Wi-Fi to “Enabled” and save the changes.

3. Scan for networks:

  • Select “Scan”. The phone will automatically search for available Wi-Fi access points.

4. Select a network:

  • A list of available Wi-Fi networks will appear. Use the arrow keys to select your desired network.

5. Enter the password (if needed):

  • If your network requires a password, enter it using the keypad and press “OK”.

6. Connect:

  • Once the password is entered (if applicable), the phone will connect to the Wi-Fi network.

7. Verify connection:

  • You should see a Wi-Fi icon in the upper right corner of the display, indicating a successful connection.

DP720 & DP750 - Quick Start Guide

Adit Phone - DP720 (Wireless Phone)

Phone Features and Keys

The DP720 is a wireless handset designed to work with the DP750 base station:

  • Left Soft Key - Accesses menu options and soft key functions.
  • Dial Key - Initiates calls.
  • Speaker Key - Enables speakerphone functionality.
  • Mute Key - Mutes microphone and activates DND mode.
  • Right Soft Key - Accesses additional menu options.
  • Navigation Key - Scrolls through menus and contacts.
  • End Key - Ends calls and turns off the phone (press and hold).
  • 3.5mm Headset Jack - Connects compatible headsets.
  • Numeric Keypad - Standard 0-9, *, #, and letter keys (ABC, DEF, GHI, JKL, MNO, PQRS, TUV, WXYZ).
  • Menu & Contacts Buttons - Quick access to menu and contact list.

The DP720 is a wireless device that requires batteries and pairs with the DP750 base station for network connectivity.

DP750 Base Station

The DP750 is the base station that provides network connectivity for the DP720 wireless phone:

Radio Button - Located on back of base station; controls subscription and pairing mode.

Micro-USB Power Port - Connects to power outlet via included adapter.

Internet Port - Connects to router via ethernet cable.

Connecting Your Adit Phone DP720 & DP750

For DP720 (Wireless Phone):

Step 1: Install Batteries and Turn On
Put the batteries into the handset and plug the charging base into an outlet. Press and hold the end key to turn on the phone.

For DP750 (Base Station):

Step 2: Connect Power
Connect the micro-USB connector into the power port of the base station, and connect the other end into an outlet.

Step 3: Connect to Network
Connect one end of the ethernet cable into the internet port and the other end into a router.

Step 4: Activate Radio/Begin Subscription
Once the DP750 is on, the radio icon should start blinking. If it isn’t, press and hold the radio button on the back of the base station for 7 seconds until it does. This will begin the subscription process.

Step 5: Pair the Devices
On the DP720, press the subscribe button and the devices will start pairing.

Using Your Adit Phone DP720

  • Call Park:
    You have 2 designated park slots - 901 and 902.
    1. Press the left soft key and select “Blind Transfer”
    2. Dial either 901 or 902
    3. Hit transfer to park the call

  • Call Hold/Resume:
    While on an active call, press the right soft key to place a call on hold and to resume the call.

  • DND Mode (Do Not Disturb):
    Press the mute button to turn Do Not Disturb mode ON/OFF.

  • Intercom:
    Dial 999.

  • Call Transfer:
    There are two different ways to transfer a call:

Blind Transfer:

1. Press options while on an active call

2. Select “Blind Transfer”

3. Enter a number and press transfer

Attended Transfer:

1. Press options while on an active call

2. Select “Attended Transfer”

3. Enter a number and press call

4. Wait for the call to connect first

5. Press options and select transfer

3 Way Conference:

1. While on call, select options

2. Select either “Conference” to cold conference or “New Call” to warm conference

3. If you selected “New Call”, wait for the call to connect first, then press options and select “Conference”

4. If you selected “Conference”, it will merge the calls immediately

Yealink T54W -

The Yealink T54W is a feature-rich desktop IP phone that combines professional design with advanced communication capabilities. It supports up to 16 SIP accounts and includes both wired and wireless connectivity options.

Physical Features

  • 4.3-inch Color Display - High-resolution pixel display (480x272) showing call information and menus

  • Adjustable Screen - Display can be tilted for optimal viewing angle

  • 10 Line Keys - Primary line access with LED indicators

  • 27 Memory Keys - Up to 27 virtual feature keys with 3-page navigation view

  • Ergonomic Design - Professional desktop phone with optimized layout

  • Bluetooth 2.0 - Wireless connectivity for compatible devices

  • Integrated WiFi - Wireless network connectivity option

  • USB 2.0 Port - Connect compatible USB devices

  • Handset Port - RJ9 (4P4C) connection for handset

    Phone Features and Keys

  • Line Keys - Enable you to select a phone line, view calls on a line, or quickly call a favorite contact. LED indicators show line status.

  • Soft Keys - Context-sensitive keys that display along the bottom of the screen. Functions change based on current activity (idle, on call, in menu, etc.).

  • Navigation Keys - Allow you to scroll through options and lists on the display. Press left, right, up, or down to navigate. Press OK key to confirm selections.

  • Message Key - Provides direct access to voicemail messages. Press to retrieve voicemail and manage voice messages.

  • Headset Key - Toggles headset mode on/off. LED indicator glows green when headset is active. Enables hands-free calling with compatible headsets.

  • Hold Key - Places a call on exclusive hold. Press again to resume a held call.

  • Mute Key - Mutes audio during calls and conferences. LED indicator shows mute status.

  • Redial Key - Displays a list of recently called numbers and allows you to redial from the list.

  • Transfer Key - When phone is idle, forwards calls to another number. When on an active call, transfers the call to another number (internal or external).

  • Speaker Key - Toggles speakerphone on/off. LED indicator glows green when speaker is active.

  • Volume Control Keys - Adjust the volume of the handset, headset, and speaker during calls.

  • Cancel/Exit Key (X) - Cancels actions, exits menus, or rejects incoming calls.

  • Numeric Keypad - Standard 0-9 keys with letter assignments (2=ABC, 3=DEF, 4=GHI, 5=JKL, 6=MNO, 7=PQRS, 8=TUV, 9=WXYZ) for dialing and menu selection.

Connecting Your Yealink T54W

Follow these steps to set up your Yealink T54W:

Adit Voice : Master Document (continued, part 10)

Step 1: Unpack and Assemble
Step 2: Attach the Stand
Locate the stand attachment points on the back of the phone. Insert the stand into the designated slots and secure it as desired for optimal viewing angle.
Step 3: Connect the Handset

  • Locate the handset port on the left-hand side of the device
  • Take the handset coil cord and connect the short end to the bottom of the handset
  • Connect the long end of the coil cord to the handset port on the phone
  • Route the cable neatly along the cable management path on the back of the phone

Step 4: Connect Network Cable
Plug one end of the ethernet cable into the Internet port on the back of the phone. Connect the other end to Your network switch or router (standard connection), OR A PoE (Power over Ethernet) compliant port if using PoE

Step 5: Connect Power
There are two network and power connection options:

Option A: Separate Power (Non-PoE)

1. Connect the power adapter to the DC 5V port on the back of the phone

2. Plug the adapter into an electrical outlet

3. The phone will boot and begin provisioning

Option B: Power over Ethernet (PoE)

1. If using a PoE-compliant switch or router, the phone receives power through the ethernet cable

2. No separate power adapter is required

3. The phone will boot and begin provisioning

Step 6: Optional - Connect USB Devices

· Connect USB headsets, storage devices, or other USB peripherals to the USB 2.0 port on the top of the phone

· The phone will recognize and configure the device automatically

Step 7: Optional - Connect Bluetooth Devices

· Enable Bluetooth on your compatible device (wireless headset, smartphone, etc.)

· On the phone, navigate to Menu > Settings > Bluetooth

· Select “Scan” to discover nearby devices

· Select your device and confirm pairing

Using Your Yealink T54W

Making Calls

Using the Handset:

1. Pick up the handset from the cradle

2. Enter the phone number or extension

3. Press the Send key or wait for dial tone and listen for ring

4. Press the handset down to end the call, or hang up the handset

Using the Speakerphone:

1. Enter the number

2. Press the Speakerphone key, Answer soft key, or the blinking line key

3. Speak clearly toward the phone’s microphone

4. Press the Speakerphone key or End Call soft key to end

Using the Headset:

1. With a headset connected, press the Headset key to activate headset mode

2. The LED indicator glows green when active

3. Enter the number and press the Send key

4. Press the End Call soft key to end the call

Answering Calls

Using the Handset:

1. When a call comes in, pick up the handset from the cradle

2. You are now connected

Using the Speakerphone:

1. Press the Answer soft key or the blinking line key

2. Speak toward the phone’s microphone

Using the Headset:

1. Press the Answer soft key or the blinking line key

2. Speak through the headset

Call Hold and Resume

Place a Call on Hold:

1. While on an active call, press the Hold key

2. The call will be placed on hold

3. You can now make another call or perform other functions

Resume a Held Call:

1. Press the Hold key again

2. The held call will resume

Call Transfer

Blind Transfer (Transfer without speaking to recipient):

1. Press the Transfer soft key during an active call

2. The current call will be placed on hold

3. Enter the extension or phone number

4. Press the Transfer soft key again to complete the transfer

Attended Transfer (Speak to recipient before transferring):

1. Press the Transfer soft key during an active call

2. Dial the extension or phone number (using *+ extension format)

3. Speak with the recipient to introduce the caller

4. Press the Transfer soft key again to complete the transfer

Call Park

Park a Call:

1. Press one of the Call Park buttons (1-3) that are green (available)

2. The button light will turn red, indicating the call is parked

3. Alternatively, dial *7 and the system will announce the park extension

Retrieve a Parked Call:

1. Go to any phone in the office

2. Press the same Call Park button to retrieve the call

3. Alternatively, dial the park extension announced by the system

Call Conferencing

Initiate a Conference Call:

1. While on an active call, press the Conference soft key

2. Enter the phone number or extension of the person you want to add

3. Press the Call or Dial soft key to connect them

4. Once connected, press the Conference soft key again to merge all calls into the conference

Add Multiple Participants:

1. Repeat the above steps to add additional participants

2. Each person will be merged into the existing conference

3. All participants can hear each other

Do Not Disturb (DND) Mode

Activate DND:

1. Press the Mute key

2. The mute/DND LED indicator will illuminate

3. Incoming calls will not ring through

Deactivate DND:

1. Press the Mute key again

2. The LED indicator will turn off

3. Incoming calls will ring normally

Call Redial

Redial the Last Called Number:

1. Press the Redial key

2. The phone will display a list of recently called numbers

3. Select the desired number from the list

Adit Voice : Master Document (continued, part 11)

4. Press the Call or Send key to dial

Voicemail Access

Access Voicemail:

1. Press the Message key

2. Enter your voicemail password (default is your extension)

3. Follow the voicemail menu options:

o Press 0 to access main voicemail menu

o Press 1 to record your “Unavailable” message

o Press 2 to record your “Busy” message

o Press 3 to record your name

o Press 4 to record your “Temporary” greeting (vacation message)

Muting the Microphone

Mute During an Active Call:

1. Press the Mute key during a call

Yealink T53W

Phone Overview

The Yealink T53W is a feature-rich desktop IP phone that combines professional design with advanced wireless connectivity. It supports up to 12 SIP accounts and includes both wired and wireless networking options for maximum flexibility.

Physical Features

  • 3.7-inch Adjustable Graphical Display - 360x160 pixel LCD with backlight showing call information and menus
  • Adjustable Screen - Display can be tilted for optimal viewing angle
  • 8 Line Keys - Primary line access with dual-color (red/green) LED indicators
  • 21 Memory Keys - Programmable feature keys up to 21 various features with 3-page navigation view
  • Ergonomic Design - Professional desktop phone with optimized keyboard layout
  • Bluetooth 4.2 - Advanced wireless connectivity for compatible devices
  • Dual-Band WiFi - 2.4G/5G wireless network connectivity (802.11a/b/g/n, up to 433Mbps)
  • USB 2.0 Port - Connect compatible USB devices, headsets, or expansion modules
  • Dual-Port Gigabit Ethernet - Network connectivity with PC pass-through capability
  • Handset Port - RJ9 (4P4C) connection for handset with coiled cord

Phone Features and Keys

  • Line Keys - Enable you to select a phone line, view calls on a line, or quickly call a favorite contact. Dual-color LED indicators show line status (red for active, green for available).
  • Soft Keys - Context-sensitive keys that display along the bottom of the screen. Functions change based on current activity (idle, on call, in menu, etc.).
  • Navigation Keys - Allow you to scroll through options and lists on the display. Press left, right, up, or down to navigate. Press OK key to confirm selections.
  • Message Key - Provides direct access to voicemail messages. Press to retrieve voicemail and manage voice messages.
  • Headset Key - Toggles headset mode on/off. LED indicator glows green when headset is active. Enables hands-free calling with compatible headsets.
  • Hold Key - Places a call on exclusive hold. Press again to resume a held call.
  • Mute Key - Mutes audio during calls and conferences. LED indicator shows mute status.
  • Redial Key - Displays a list of recently called numbers and allows you to redial from the list.
  • Transfer Key - When phone is idle, forwards calls to another number. When on an active call, transfers the call to another number (internal or external).
  • Speakerphone Key - Toggles speakerphone on/off. LED indicator glows green when speaker is active.
  • Volume Control Keys - Adjust the volume of the handset, headset, and speaker during calls.
  • Cancel/Exit Key (X) - Cancels actions, exits menus, or rejects incoming calls.
  • Numeric Keypad - Standard 0-9 keys with letter assignments (2=ABC, 3=DEF, 4=GHI, 5=JKL, 6=MNO, 7=PQRS, 8=TUV, 9=WXYZ) for dialing and menu selection.

Connecting Your Yealink T53W

Step 1: Unpack and Assemble

Step 2: Attach the Stand
Locate the stand attachment points on the back of the phone. Slide the stand into the designated slots until you hear a click to secure it for optimal viewing angle.

Step 3: Connect the Handset

· Connect the long end of the coil cord to the handset port on the phone

· Route the cable neatly along the cable management path on the back of the phone

Plug one end of the ethernet cable into the Internet port on the back of the phone. Connect the other end to:

· Your network switch or router (standard connection), OR

Step 5: Connect Power
There are two network and power connection options:

Option A: Separate Power (Non-PoE)

1. Connect the power adapter to the DC 5V port on the back of the phone

2. Plug the adapter into an electrical outlet

3. The phone will boot and begin provisioning

Option B: Power over Ethernet (PoE)

1. If using a PoE-compliant switch or router, the phone receives power through the ethernet cable

2. No separate power adapter is required

Using Your Yealink T53W

Making Calls

Using the Handset:

1. Pick up the handset from the cradle

2. Enter the phone number or extension

3. Press the Send key (# key) or wait for dial tone and listen for ring

4. Hang up the handset to end the call

Using the Speakerphone:

1. Enter the number

2. Press the Speakerphone key, Answer soft key, or the blinking line key

3. Speak clearly toward the phone’s microphone

4. Press the Speakerphone key or End Call soft key to end

Using the Headset:

1. With a headset connected, press the Headset key to activate headset mode

2. The LED indicator glows green when active

3. Enter the number and press the Send key

4. Press the End Call soft key to end the call

Answering Calls

Using the Handset:

1. When a call comes in, pick up the handset from the cradle

2. You are now connected

Using the Speakerphone:

1. Press the Answer soft key or the blinking line key

2. Speak toward the phone’s microphone

Using the Headset:

1. Press the Answer soft key or the blinking line key

2. Speak through the headset

Call Hold and Resume

Place a Call on Hold:

1. While on an active call, press the Hold key

2. The call will be placed on hold

3. You can now make another call or perform other functions

Resume a Held Call:

1. Press the Hold key again

2. The held call will resume

Call Transfer

Blind Transfer (Transfer without speaking to recipient):

1. Press the Transfer soft key during an active call

2. The current call will be placed on hold

3. Enter the extension or phone number

4. Press the Transfer soft key again to complete the transfer

Attended Transfer (Speak to recipient before transferring):

1. Press the Transfer soft key during an active call

2. Dial the extension (using *+extension format)

3. Speak with the recipient to introduce the caller

4. Press the Transfer soft key again to complete the transfer

Call Park

Park a Call:

1. Press one of the Call Park buttons (1-3) that are green (available)

2. The button light will turn red, indicating the call is parked

3. Alternatively, press the park soft key to park the call

Retrieve a Parked Call:

1. Go to any phone in the office

2. Press the same Call Park button to retrieve the call

3. Alternatively, use the soft key to pick up the parked call

Call Conferencing

Initiate a Conference Call:

1. While on an active call, press the Conference soft key

2. Enter the phone number or extension of the person you want to add

3. Press the Call or Send key (# key) to connect them

4. Once connected, press the Conference soft key again to merge all calls into the conference

Add Multiple Participants:

1. Repeat the above steps to add additional participants (up to 5-way conferencing)

2. Each person will be merged into the existing conference

3. All participants can hear each other

Split Conference Calls:

1. Press the Split soft key to separate the conference back into two calls

2. Both calls will be placed on hold

3. You can resume one call and transfer or conference again as needed

Do Not Disturb (DND) Mode

Activate DND:

1. Press the Mute key

2. The mute/DND LED indicator will illuminate

3. Incoming calls will not ring through

Deactivate DND:

1. Press the Mute key again

2. The LED indicator will turn off

3. Incoming calls will ring normally

Call Redial

Redial the Last Called Number:

1. Press the Redial key

2. The phone will display a list of recently called numbers

3. Select the desired number from the list

4. Press the Call or Send key to dial

Voicemail Access

Access Voicemail:

1. Press the Message key

2. Enter your voicemail password (default is your extension)

3. Follow the voicemail menu options to listen to messages and manage greetings

Muting the Microphone

Mute During an Active Call:

1. Press the Mute key during a call

2. The mute LED indicator illuminates

3. The other party cannot hear you

Factory Reset

Troubleshooting Quick Reference

Phone won’t power on:

· Check power adapter connection to phone and outlet

· If using PoE, verify the switch/router is PoE-compliant and powered

· Try a different electrical outlet

No network connection:

· Check ethernet cable is fully inserted into Internet port

Adit Voice : Master Document (continued, part 13)

· Verify cable is connected to a powered switch or router

· If using WiFi, check WiFi is enabled and network is visible

· Verify DHCP server is active on your network

WiFi won’t connect:

· Verify WiFi is enabled in Menu > Settings > Basic Settings > WiFi

· Check network name and password are correct

· Move closer to WiFi router if signal is weak

· Try forgetting the network and reconnecting

Poor call quality:

· Move closer to WiFi router if using wireless

· Switch to wired Ethernet connection if experiencing issues

· Check for background noise and use mute when not speaking

· Ensure adequate bandwidth on network

· Enable quality of service (QoS) settings on your router

Bluetooth device won’t pair:

· Ensure device is in pairing mode

· Bring device closer to the phone

· Clear previous pairing attempts and try again

· Check device is compatible with Bluetooth 4.2

Calls won’t transfer:

· Verify target extension is valid and in service

· Try attended transfer instead of blind transfer

· Check Call Forward settings aren’t interfering

Voicemail not working:

· Confirm voicemail service is provisioned on your account

· Verify Message key is functional

· Check password is correct (default is extension number)

USB recording not working:

· Verify USB drive is properly inserted

· Check recording feature is enabled in settings

· Ensure USB drive has sufficient space

· Try a different USB device to rule out device compatibility

GRP2613 - Quick Start Guide

Phone Features and Keys

Connecting Your Adit Phone GRP2613

Step 1: Find the Ethernet Cable
Locate the ethernet cable connecting your computer to your wall socket or router.

Unplug the end connected to your computer and plug it into the LAN port on the back of the phone.

Step 3: Connect Additional Ethernet Cable
Connect an additional ethernet cable from your computer into the PC port on the back of the phone.

Connect the 12V DC plug to the power jack on the phone, and plug the other end into an outlet.

    How to Connect Grandstream GRP2616 to Wi-Fi

Purpose: Configure the GRP 2616 IP phone to connect to a wireless network.

To connect a Grandstream GRP2616 IP phone to a Wi-Fi network, navigate to the phone’s settings, enable Wi-Fi, scan for available networks, select your desired network, and enter the password if required.

Here’s a more detailed breakdown:

1. Access the Wi-Fi settings:

  • Press the “Menu” button on the phone.
  • Navigate to “System” then “Wi-Fi settings”.

2. Enable Wi-Fi:

  • Set Wi-Fi to “Enabled” and save the changes.

3. Scan for networks:

  • Select “Scan”. The phone will automatically search for available Wi-Fi access points.

4. Select a network:

  • A list of available Wi-Fi networks will appear. Use the arrow keys to select your desired network.

5. Enter the password (if needed):

  • If your network requires a password, enter it using the keypad and press “OK”.

6. Connect:

  • Once the password is entered (if applicable), the phone will connect to the Wi-Fi network.

7. Verify connection:

  • You should see a Wi-Fi icon in the upper right corner of the display, indicating a successful connection.

Connecting Your Adit Phone DP720 & DP750

For DP720 (Wireless Phone):

Step 1: Install Batteries and Turn On
Put the batteries into the handset and plug the charging base into an outlet. Press and hold the end key to turn on the phone.

For DP750 (Base Station):

Step 2: Connect Power
Connect the micro-USB connector into the power port of the base station, and connect the other end into an outlet.

Step 3: Connect to Network
Connect one end of the ethernet cable into the internet port and the other end into a router.

Once the DP750 is on, the radio icon should start blinking. If it isn’t, press and hold the radio button on the back of the base station for 7 seconds until it does. This will begin the subscription process.

Blind Transfer:

1. Press options while on an active call

2. Select “Blind Transfer”

3. Enter a number and press transfer

Attended Transfer:

1. Press options while on an active call

2. Select “Attended Transfer”

3. Enter a number and press call

4. Wait for the call to connect first

5. Press options and select transfer

3 Way Conference:

1. While on call, select options

2. Select either “Conference” to cold conference or “New Call” to warm conference

3. If you selected “New Call”, wait for the call to connect first, then press options and select “Conference”

4. If you selected “Conference”, it will merge the calls immediately

Yealink T53W - Quick Start Guide

Phone Overview

The Yealink T53W is a feature-rich desktop IP phone that combines professional design with advanced wireless connectivity. It supports up to 12 SIP accounts and includes both wired and wireless networking options for maximum flexibility.

Physical Features

  • 3.7-inch Adjustable Graphical Display - 360x160 pixel LCD with backlight showing call information and menus
  • Adjustable Screen - Display can be tilted for optimal viewing angle
  • 8 Line Keys - Primary line access with dual-color (red/green) LED indicators
  • 21 Memory Keys - Programmable feature keys up to 21 various features with 3-page navigation view
  • Ergonomic Design - Professional desktop phone with optimized keyboard layout
  • Bluetooth 4.2 - Advanced wireless connectivity for compatible devices
  • Dual-Band WiFi - 2.4G/5G wireless network connectivity (802.11a/b/g/n, up to 433Mbps)
  • USB 2.0 Port - Connect compatible USB devices, headsets, or expansion modules
  • Dual-Port Gigabit Ethernet - Network connectivity with PC pass-through capability
  • Handset Port - RJ9 (4P4C) connection for handset with coiled cord

Phone Features and Keys

  • Line Keys - Enable you to select a phone line, view calls on a line, or quickly call a favorite contact. Dual-color LED indicators show line status (red for active, green for available).
  • Soft Keys - Context-sensitive keys that display along the bottom of the screen. Functions change based on current activity (idle, on call, in menu, etc.).
  • Navigation Keys - Allow you to scroll through options and lists on the display. Press left, right, up, or down to navigate. Press OK key to confirm selections.
  • Message Key - Provides direct access to voicemail messages. Press to retrieve voicemail and manage voice messages.
  • Headset Key - Toggles headset mode on/off. LED indicator glows green when headset is active. Enables hands-free calling with compatible headsets.
  • Hold Key - Places a call on exclusive hold. Press again to resume a held call.
  • Mute Key - Mutes audio during calls and conferences. LED indicator shows mute status.
  • Redial Key - Displays a list of recently called numbers and allows you to redial from the list.
  • Transfer Key - When phone is idle, forwards calls to another number. When on an active call, transfers the call to another number (internal or external).
  • Speakerphone Key - Toggles speakerphone on/off. LED indicator glows green when speaker is active.
  • Volume Control Keys - Adjust the volume of the handset, headset, and speaker during calls.
  • Cancel/Exit Key (X) - Cancels actions, exits menus, or rejects incoming calls.
  • Numeric Keypad - Standard 0-9 keys with letter assignments (2=ABC, 3=DEF, 4=GHI, 5=JKL, 6=MNO, 7=PQRS, 8=TUV, 9=WXYZ) for dialing and menu selection.

Connecting Your Yealink T53W

Step 1: Unpack and Assemble

Step 2: Attach the Stand
Locate the stand attachment points on the back of the phone. Slide the stand into the designated slots until you hear a click to secure it for optimal viewing angle.

Step 3: Connect the Handset

· Locate the handset port on the left-hand side of the device

· Take the handset coil cord and connect the short end to the bottom of the handset

· Connect the long end of the coil cord to the handset port on the phone

· Route the cable neatly along the cable management path on the back of the phone

Step 4: Connect Network Cable
Plug one end of the ethernet cable into the Internet port on the back of the phone. Connect the other end to:

· Your network switch or router (standard connection), OR

· A PoE (Power over Ethernet) compliant port if using PoE

Step 5: Connect Power
There are two network and power connection options:

Option A: Separate Power (Non-PoE)

1. Connect the power adapter to the DC 5V port on the back of the phone

2. Plug the adapter into an electrical outlet

3. The phone will boot and begin provisioning

Option B: Power over Ethernet (PoE)

1. If using a PoE-compliant switch or router, the phone receives power through the ethernet cable

2. No separate power adapter is required

3. The phone will boot and begin provisioning

Step 8: Optional - Connect via WiFi

· Navigate to Menu > Settings > Basic Settings > WiFi

· Enter the WiFi password if required

Using Your Yealink T53W

Making Calls

Using the Handset:

1. Pick up the handset from the cradle

2. Enter the phone number or extension

3. Press the Send key (# key) or wait for dial tone and listen for ring

4. Hang up the handset to end the call

Using the Speakerphone:

1. Enter the number

2. Press the Speakerphone key, Answer soft key, or the blinking line key

3. Speak clearly toward the phone’s microphone

4. Press the Speakerphone key or End Call soft key to end

Using the Headset:

1. With a headset connected, press the Headset key to activate headset mode

2. The LED indicator glows green when active

3. Enter the number and press the Send key

4. Press the End Call soft key to end the call

Answering Calls

Using the Handset:

1. When a call comes in, pick up the handset from the cradle

2. You are now connected

Using the Speakerphone:

1. Press the Answer soft key or the blinking line key

2. Speak toward the phone’s microphone

Using the Headset:

1. Press the Answer soft key or the blinking line key

2. Speak through the headset

Call Hold and Resume

Place a Call on Hold:

1. While on an active call, press the Hold key

2. The call will be placed on hold

3. You can now make another call or perform other functions

Resume a Held Call:

1. Press the Hold key again

2. The held call will resume

Call Transfer

Blind Transfer (Transfer without speaking to recipient):

1. Press the Transfer soft key during an active call

2. The current call will be placed on hold

3. Enter the extension or phone number

4. Press the Transfer soft key again to complete the transfer

Attended Transfer (Speak to recipient before transferring):

1. Press the Transfer soft key during an active call

2. Dial the extension

3. Speak with the recipient to introduce the caller

4. Press the Transfer soft key again to complete the transfer

Call Park

Park a Call:

1. Press one of the Call Park buttons (1-3) that are green (available)

2. The button light will turn red, indicating the call is parked

3. Alternatively, press the park soft key to park the call

Retrieve a Parked Call:

1. Go to any phone in the office

2. Press the same Call Park button to retrieve the call

3. Alternatively, use the soft key to pick up the parked call

Call Conferencing

Initiate a Conference Call:

1. While on an active call, press the Conference soft key

2. Enter the phone number or extension of the person you want to add

3. Press the Call or Send key (# key) to connect them

4. Once connected, press the Conference soft key again to merge all calls into the conference

Add Multiple Participants:

1. Repeat the above steps to add additional participants (up to 5-way conferencing)

2. Each person will be merged into the existing conference

3. All participants can hear each other

Split Conference Calls:

1. Press the Split soft key to separate the conference back into two calls

2. Both calls will be placed on hold

3. You can resume one call and transfer or conference again as needed

Do Not Disturb (DND) Mode

Activate DND:

1. Press the Mute key

2. The mute/DND LED indicator will illuminate

3. Incoming calls will not ring through

Deactivate DND:

1. Press the Mute key again

2. The LED indicator will turn off

3. Incoming calls will ring normally

Call Redial

Redial the Last Called Number:

1. Press the Redial key

2. The phone will display a list of recently called numbers

3. Select the desired number from the list

4. Press the Call or Send key to dial

Voicemail Access

Access Voicemail:

1. Press the Message key

2. Enter your voicemail password (default is your extension)

3. Follow the voicemail menu options to listen to messages and manage greetings

Muting the Microphone

Mute During an Active Call:

1. Press the Mute key during a call

2. The mute LED indicator illuminates

3. The other party cannot hear you

4. Press Mute again to unmute

To connect via WiFi:

1. Navigate to Menu > Settings > Basic Settings > WiFi

2. Press the right navigation arrow to Enable WiFi

3. Select Available Networks to scan for available WiFi networks

4. Select your network from the list

5. Enter the WiFi password if required

6. The phone will connect and display WiFi signal strength and connection status

Factory Reset

To restore the phone to factory default settings:

1. Navigate to Menu > Settings > Advanced Settings > Reset

2. Confirm the reset action

3. The phone will reboot and restore all settings to factory defaults

Troubleshooting Quick Reference

Phone won’t power on:

· Check power adapter connection to phone and outlet

· If using PoE, verify the switch/router is PoE-compliant and powered

· Try a different electrical outlet

No network connection:

· Check ethernet cable is fully inserted into Internet port

· Verify cable is connected to a powered switch or router

· If using WiFi, check WiFi is enabled and network is visible

Adit Voice : Master Document (continued, part 18)

· Verify DHCP server is active on your network

WiFi won’t connect:

· Verify WiFi is enabled in Menu > Settings > Basic Settings > WiFi

· Check network name and password are correct

· Move closer to WiFi router if signal is weak

· Try forgetting the network and reconnecting

Poor call quality:

· Move closer to WiFi router if using wireless

· Switch to wired Ethernet connection if experiencing issues

· Check for background noise and use mute when not speaking

· Ensure adequate bandwidth on network

· Enable quality of service (QoS) settings on your router

Bluetooth device won’t pair:

· Ensure device is in pairing mode

· Bring device closer to the phone

· Clear previous pairing attempts and try again

· Check device is compatible with Bluetooth 4.2

Calls won’t transfer:

· Verify target extension is valid and in service

· Try attended transfer instead of blind transfer

· Check Call Forward settings aren’t interfering

Voicemail not working:

· Confirm voicemail service is provisioned on your account

· Verify Message key is functional

· Check password is correct (default is extension number)

USB recording not working:

· Verify USB drive is properly inserted

· Check recording feature is enabled in settings

· Ensure USB drive has sufficient space

· Try a different USB device to rule out device compatibility

5. How to make and receive calls on Adit’s mobile app

With Adit’s mobile app, you will be able to take and make calls for your practice. Can be useful for unexpected closures, or when you are away from the actual phone.

Notes: This feature is only available if you have Adit Voice enabled on your account.

To make a call:

  1. When you are logged in the app, on the home page there are 2 places to go to make a call: the Dialpad or the Patients tab ****

Call Flow Update - Questions & Answers

1. How can I update the schedule in my call flow?

Answer:
To update the business hours or schedule in your call flow, follow these steps:

  1. Log in to your Adit app.
  2. Click on the Settings (gear) icon.
  3. Go to the Phone system under the Voice section.
  4. Click on the Location Name.
  5. Click on Landline Number.
  6. Click on the Schedule option.
  7. Update the days and hours as per your requirement.
  8. Once all the changes are done, click the Update button to save.

2. How can I add or update Menu Options (IVR) in the call flow?

Answer:
If a client wants multiple menu options such as:

  • Press 1 for Front Desk
  • Press 2 for Appointments
  • Press 3 for Voicemail

Follow these steps:

  1. Log in to the Adit app and open the Call Flow by following the same steps mentioned above.
  2. Click on the Menu option.
  3. Add a Greeting and mention the available options (e.g., “Press 1 for Front Desk, Press 2 for Appointments, Press 3 for Voicemail”).
  4. Under Option 1, enter the Extension Number for the Front Desk.
  5. Under Option 2, enter the Extension Number for Appointments.
  6. Under Option 3, select Voicemail.
  7. After configuring all options, click the Update icon to save the changes.

3. How can I update the voicemail greeting in the call flow?

Answer:
To update the voicemail greeting, follow these steps:

  1. Open the Call Flow and scroll to the bottom where the voicemail option appears.
  2. You will have two options to update voicemail: Text Format: Type the message and it will be read using the AI voice. Play Recording: Use your own recorded audio as the voicemail greeting.
  3. If choosing Play Recording, make sure the recording is already uploaded in the Audio Library. Otherwise, it will not appear in the list.
  4. Select your recording from the Play Recording dropdown.
  5. Click Save, and then hit the Update icon to apply changes.

4. How can I add an external number to the call flow?

Answer:
If a client wants to forward calls to an external number (for example, forwarding to an AI answering service), follow these steps:

  1. Open the Call Flow.
  2. Add a Ring option at the desired position in the flow.
  3. Enter the External Phone Number you want to forward calls to.
  4. Select the Ring Duration e.g., 10-20 seconds, depending on the client’s preference.
  5. Save and click Update to finalize.

5. How can I update the After Hours call handling?

Answer:
To make changes to After Hours behavior:

  1. Open the Call Flow.
  2. Click on the Any Other Time option (this represents After Hours).
  3. Depending on the client’s requirement, you can:

Adit Voice : Master Document (continued, part 19)

  • Send calls directly to Voicemail: Scroll to the voicemail section and update the greeting if needed.
  • Add a Menu (IVR) during After Hours: Add menu options following the same steps mentioned in the Menu section.
  • Forward calls to an External Number: Click on the Ring option and enter the external number, then save.
  • Once done, click Update to apply all changes.

Updated Schedule Call Flow

Category: Call Routing / Schedule Configuration Applies To: Offices with lunch closures

Overview

This article explains the updated call schedule structure for offices that close during lunch. The new three-branch setup replaces the previous two-branch method, making schedules easier to build, read, and troubleshoot.

What Changed

Previous Setup (2 Branches) New Setup (3 Branches)
Branch A - Morning + Afternoon hours Branch B - Lunch hours (voicemail) Each weekday is entered twice in Branch A Branch A - Before lunch Branch B - Lunch hours (voicemail) Branch C - After lunch One entry per weekday per branch

Why it changed:

The reason for this update:

With the previous setup, the schedule had opening and closing hours configured within the same branch. This meant that in Branch A, we had to create duplicate schedules for each day (for example, two Mondays and two Tuesdays).

For example:

  • The office opened at 7:00 AM and closed at 12:00 PM for lunch in Branch A.
  • Branch B was then used only for the lunch hours from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM.
  • After lunch, the office reopened from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM in Branch A again.

With this setup, calls were routed back to Branch A after lunch hours, which created a second leg in the call flow. This caused issues with call routing, and at times, the phones did not ring properly, leading to the issues reported by the client.

With the new setup, we have eliminated the need to route calls back into the same branch after lunch hours. Instead, the new Branch C is being used for the reopening schedule, which provides a cleaner call flow and helps maintain proper ringing functionality.

How to Connect Grandstream GRP2616 to Wi-Fi

Purpose: Configure the GRP 2616 IP phone to connect to a wireless network.

To connect a Grandstream GRP2616 IP phone to a Wi-Fi network, navigate to the phone’s settings, enable Wi-Fi, scan for available networks, select your desired network, and enter the password if required.

Here’s a more detailed breakdown:

1. Access the Wi-Fi settings:

  • Press the “Menu” button on the phone.
  • Navigate to “System” then “Wi-Fi settings”.

2. Enable Wi-Fi:

  • Set Wi-Fi to “Enabled” and save the changes.

3. Scan for networks:

  • Select “Scan”. The phone will automatically search for available Wi-Fi access points.

4. Select a network:

  • A list of available Wi-Fi networks will appear. Use the arrow keys to select your desired network.

5. Enter the password (if needed):

  • If your network requires a password, enter it using the keypad and press “OK”.

6. Connect:

  • Once the password is entered (if applicable), the phone will connect to the Wi-Fi network.

7. Verify connection:

  • You should see a Wi-Fi icon in the upper right corner of the display, indicating a successful connection.

How to Change Your Phone’s Ringtone

This article will guide you through the process of changing the ringtone that plays when a patient calls into your practice. There are a variety of options available to you that you can choose from. Below are the steps you’ll need to take in order to set your new ringtone.

To change your ringtone:
Navigate to and press the button in the middle of the directional buttons on the right side of the phone

  1. Navigate to the Preferences option using the directional keys and press the center button

  2. Navigate to Sounds in the menu using the directional keys and press the center button

  3. Navigate through the available ringtones by pressing the left and right directional keys and stop on the ringtone you would like to use

  4. (Optional) Adjust the ring volume by navigating to the Ring Volume setting using the down directional button and then adjusting the volume using the left and right directional buttons

  5. Press the Save button located in the top portion of the phone just under the display screen.

3CX Call Forwarding:

To forward all calls from your business number to an external number using the 3CX VoIP platform, follow these steps:

1. Log in to the 3CX Management Console

  • Open your web browser and navigate to the 3CX Management Console URL.
  • Enter your admin credentials to log in.

2. Select the Extension to Forward

  • In the left-hand menu, click on “Extensions.”
  • Find and select the extension you want to forward calls from.

3. Configure Call Forwarding Rules

  • Once you’ve selected the extension, click on the “Forwarding Rules” tab.
  • You will see several sections such as “Available,” “Away,” “Do Not Disturb,” etc. Configure the forwarding rule for the desired status. Usually, you might want to set this for the “Available” status if you want calls forwarded at all times.

4. Set the Forwarding Number

  • In the chosen status section (e.g., “Available”), look for the option to forward calls.
  • Check the option “Forward to External Number.”
  • Enter the external phone number to which you want to forward the calls. Make sure to enter the number in the correct format required by your VoIP provider (e.g., including the country code).

5. Apply and Save Changes

  • After entering the forwarding number, make sure to click “OK” or “Apply” to save your changes.
  • Double-check that the settings have been applied correctly.

6. Test the Call Forwarding

  • To ensure the forwarding is working correctly, call the business number from another phone.
  • Verify that the call is being forwarded to the external number you specified.

Example of Forwarding Rule Setup

If your business number is +1 555-555-1234 and you want to forward all calls to an external number +1 555-555-5678, here is an example of how the setup might look:

  • In the “Available” status section, check “Forward to External Number.”
  • Enter +15555555678 as the external number.

HTC Call Forwarding:

If you are switching from HTC to Mango Voice, we currently do not recommend forwarding calls from HTC to Mango Voice during the number porting process. Mango Voice’s system allows simultaneous inbound calls, but HTC’s system only seems to allow one active call at a time. This means that while forwarding from HTC; if your office is on an inbound call and another comes in, the second (and any subsequent calls) will receive a busy tone. Once your numbers have ported, your Mango Voice phones will ring for inbound calls.

VoIP Audio Quality Issues: Common Causes, Investigations and Fixes

The key for solving all audio quality issues is to try to identify a pattern

  • Time of call, carrier, phone instrument, provider, call duration, geographic location etc.
  • Same issue is affecting one client (at a particular time/different times)
  • Same client facing multiple issues
  • Multiple clients facing same issue
    .

  1. Call Drop

    Investigation: (Try to identify a pattern)

  • Does the call drop soon after the call connects - like within the first 30 seconds or so?

  • Do the calls drop after the call is placed on mute/hold by either or both sides?

  • Calls drop at random time on the call while speaking - but mostly during peak hours of the day

    Calls drop after 30 seconds:

  • Most likely ACK message is not received to complete the SIP Invite

  • This may happen from time-to-time because UDP is “best-effort” protocol and not a guaranteed delivery protocol

  • Solution: We can change the SIP protocol to TCP (for this client) if this happens frequently for a particular client

  • If it still doesn’t solve the problem then we should look at the NAT and Firewall

    Calls drop after being placed on mute/hold

  • This is mainly due to RTP timeout(setting on our PBX) or UDP timeout - basically it is assumed that either party is not available because they left the call but BYE packet was lost and hence the call is cancelled by PBX or UDP connection is closed by client’s router because there was no UDP traffic

  • Please reach out to the development team with this observation

  • Solution (Developers): Try changing Silence Suppression and VAD settings on Phones. This will send periodic RTP packets to keep connection open

    Calls drop during peak time (Try to gather more information around source numbers, carriers, providers (plivo/telnyx), VHTelephony Servers

  • Could be Adit PBX Load, Telnyx, Plivo or upstream carrier

  • If PBX load related then it would affect different clients on that server during peak times but not the same client

  • If it is affecting the same client then could be Telnyx/Plivo issue

  1. Audio Quality (Audio In/Out, Robotic Voice, Static, Crackling Sound, Inaudible Audio, Delayed Audio)

  • Mostly due to Jitter/Delta on client network
  • Sometimes can be due to PBX server load/Telnyx/Plivo/Upstream Carrier
  • Solution 1: Change the codec to PCMU/PCMA. It requires lower bandwidth compared to OPUS 48000
  • Solution 2: Change the Jitter Buffer on the phone to “Fixed Buffer” with 100ms jitter. Don’t increase this more than 100ms otherwise the client will experience voice lag
  • Solution 3: Check if this happens during peak hours and which PBX server is affected. Further investigation to be done by Developers
  • Solution 4: Check client’s available bandwidth (download and upload). Do an actual file upload/download instead of doing standard “speed test”. If that is not possible then do it with multiple sites. Preferably during the time when they are facing problems

  1. One-way Audio/Audio cuts out completely from one/both sides but call is still connected

  • Need to be extra-careful in differentiating one-way audio from delayed audio. True one-way audio issues are rare. The user could just say “hello, hello” 3-4 times and then hang up where they could have received audio if they had stayed on call. These are not one-way audio issues but delayed voice
  • Investigation: Ask the users to stay on the line for a few more seconds (10+ seconds) to check if they are still not receiving any audio
  • Mainly due to NAT/Firewall issues
  • UDP packets are blocked by NAT/Firewall on the client (clinic) side
  • Solution: Recheck all NAT/Whitelisting/Firewall settings
  • Solution: Enable STUN based NAT on the phones. Both Grandstream and Yealink phones have this option
  • Solution: Increase UDP Port Range - allowing more UDP connections
  • Solution: Implement QoS to prioritise RTP traffic
  • Solution (for large practices): Implement VLAN with QoS to prioritise Voice Traffic
  • Solution: If it affects multiple clients at the same time, then it could be due to the PBX load but it’s unlikely. Please gather as much information as possible (time of call, provider, carrier etc) to form a pattern and reach out to the developer

Adit Call Tracking Update - What’s New & How to Navigate the Enhanced UI

A concise, practical guide to the major UI changes and where to find familiar functions in the updated Call Tracking experience.

Purpose

This article explains the most important changes introduced in the new Call Tracking UI and provides quick direction for common tasks. It is focused on the high-impact changes and practical navigation steps so teams can adapt quickly.

Key improvements

  • Dedicated Call Detail page: playback, structured call fields, tasks, tags and notes are consolidated in a single detail screen.
  • Voicemail transcripts and AI summaries: faster triage without full audio playback.
  • New Insights dashboard: richer analytics for operations and marketing (hourly volume, call-source attribution, patient-type breakdowns).
  • Tasks from calls & voicemails: create and assign follow-ups from the call context.
  • Export and saved views: export CSV/PDF from table settings and save custom table views for repeat reporting.
  • Legacy Insights preserved: older reports remain available under Legacy Insights for continuity.

Core differences - Old UI vs New UI

Area Old UI New UI
Playback Bottom popup panel (playback + quick actions) Dedicated Call Detail page with waveform, transcript, summary and structured fields
Tags & Notes Available inline in popup Moved to Call Detail → Tags / Notes (editing happens there)
Inline action items Play, Notes, Appointment, Timeline, Tags Call Detail, Patient Card, Task, Timeline (Archive for voicemails)
Unique Callers & Export CSV Visible as sidebar items Removed from sidebar; export options now in Table Settings; Save View available
Numbers Numbers section in the left menu Numbers removed from left menu - manage under Settings → Numbers
Insights Legacy charts within old Insights New Insights dashboard (advanced analytics); old charts accessible under Legacy Insights
Voicemail Playback in popup; no transcript or summary Detail page with AI-generated summary and transcript tab; tasks and archive available
Automation / mapping No structured mapping; manual tagging only Manual entry in editor maps to structured fields on save via backend mapping

Where to find common items

  • Open call playback: Click the call row → Call Detail page.
  • Add or edit tags & notes: Call Detail → Tags / Notes.
  • Create tasks: Use the Task action or the Tasks area at the bottom of Call Detail.
  • Export & Save View: Use Table Settings → Export CSV / Download PDF / Save View.
  • Manage phone numbers: Settings → Numbers (admin area).
  • Access older reports: Call Tracking → Legacy Insights.
  • Access new analytics: Call Tracking → Insights.

Admin checklist - recommended actions

  1. Inform staff that playback and editing now occur on the Call Detail page and provide a short demonstration.
  2. Create a single-page quick guide: Open Call Detail → Add Tags/Notes → Create Task.
  3. Confirm DIDs and number settings under Settings → Numbers.
  4. Decide which reports to Save View and set up recurring exports where needed.
  5. Grant Insights access to staff responsible for operations and marketing.

Voicemail & Insights - highlights

Voicemail

Voicemail entries now include an AI-generated summary and a transcript tab in Call Detail. This reduces the need to listen to entire messages and enables faster triage and follow-up.

Insights

The new Insights module offers operational and marketing views such as hourly call distributions, call-source attribution, patient-type breakdowns and saved, filterable views. Legacy Insights retain the older charts for continuity.

Data handling & migration notes

  • All historical recordings and logs remain accessible.
  • Structured call fields introduced in the new UI are populated from manual edits and mapped via the backend where applicable.
  • No action should be required to retain existing data. If you require a full export for audit or archival purposes, contact Support.

FAQ

Q: Has any customer data been deleted?

A: No. Existing recordings, notes and tags remain accessible. Some items have moved to different sections of the UI.

Q: Where do I export call data now?

A: Open the table and use Table Settings → Export CSV / Download PDF. Save View stores filters and columns for repeat use.

Q: Who should I contact for help or training?

A: Contact Support at support at adit.com or call us @281-468-1445

Q: Where are the older Insights?

A: Older charts are available under Call Tracking → Legacy Insights.

Instructions for Bringing Your Existing Yealink Phone to Adit

This document outlines the steps and requirements for onboarding your existing Yealink IP phone to the Adit platform. Following these instructions carefully will help ensure a smooth and error-free setup.

1. Release the Phone from the Previous Service Provider

Before a Yealink phone can be added to Adit, it must be fully released (unlocked) from the previous service provider.

  • Phones that are still locked to another provider cannot be provisioned on Adit.
  • Please contact your previous provider and confirm that the device has been released for third-party use.

2. Provide Clear Phone Label Photos (Mandatory)

To avoid any human or manual entry errors, we require clear photos of the phone’s label.

Please ensure the photo clearly shows:

  • MAC Address
  • Serial Number

📸 Photo Guidelines:

  • The image should be well-lit and in focus
  • All characters must be clearly readable
  • Do not crop out any part of the label

These details are required to correctly add the device to the Adit system.

3. Device Addition on Adit

Once the phone is:

  • Released from the previous provider, and
  • The MAC address and serial number have been verified

The device will be added to the Adit platform by our team.

4. Factory Reset the Phone

After the phone has been successfully added to Adit, a quick factory reset is required to complete the provisioning process.

Factory Reset Steps (Yealink Phones):

  1. Press and hold the OK button on the phone.
  2. Continue holding it until you see a prompt asking to initiate a factory reset.
  3. Confirm the prompt to proceed.
  • The factory reset will allow the phone to fetch the new Adit configuration
  • Once reset, the phone should automatically provision and become operational

5. Final Notes

  • Do not perform a factory reset before the phone is added to Adit
  • Ensure the phone is connected to a stable internet connection during provisioning

Adit Phones Guide v2 (Voice)

Guide to Adit Phones

Adit Voice · v.2

Everything you need to know about Adit phones in one place - connection setup, call handling, voicemail, hold, transfer, and call parking across all three supported hardware models.

📥 Quick Start Guide (PDF): Download - 300 DPI GRP & DP Phones v.2

SECTION 1 - Connecting Your Adit Phone

Adit supports three hardware phone models. Follow the steps below for your specific model to complete the initial setup.

📱 Model GRP2613 - Corded Desktop Phone

Connecting your GRP2613 is a simple 4-step process.

🎬 Tutorial Video: Watch on YouTube - GRP2613 Connection Guide

  1. Find the ethernet cable currently connecting your computer to the wall socket or router.

  2. Unplug the end connected to your computer and plug it into the LAN port on the back of the phone.

  3. Connect an additional ethernet cable from your computer into the PC port on the back of the phone.

  4. Connect the 12V DC plug to the power jack on the phone, and plug the other end into a wall outlet.

📱 Model GRP2616 - Corded Desktop Phone (Expanded)

Connecting your GRP2616 follows the same 4-step process as the GRP2613.

🎬 Tutorial Video: Watch on YouTube - GRP2616 Connection Guide

  1. Find the ethernet cable currently connecting your computer to the wall socket or router.

  2. Unplug the end connected to your computer and plug it into the LAN port on the back of the phone.

  3. Connect an additional ethernet cable from your computer into the PC port on the back of the phone.

  4. Connect the 12V DC plug to the power jack on the phone, and plug the other end into a wall outlet.

📱 Model DP720 - Cordless Handset (with DP750 Base Station)

Setting up the DP720 cordless phone requires pairing with the DP750 base station. This is a 5-step process.

🎬 Tutorial Video: Watch on YouTube - DP720 Connection Guide

  1. Insert batteries into the DP720 handset and place it in the charging base. Plug the base into an outlet. Press and hold the End key to power on the handset.

  2. Connect the micro-USB connector into the power port of the DP750 base station and plug the other end into a wall outlet.

  3. Connect one end of an ethernet cable into the internet port on the DP750, and the other end into your router.

  4. Once the DP750 is powered on, the radio icon should start blinking. If it does not blink, press and hold the radio button on the back of the base station for 7 seconds until it begins. This starts the subscription pairing process.

  5. On the DP720 handset, press the Subscribe button. The two devices will begin pairing automatically.

SECTION 2 - Using Your Adit Phone

The following reference covers day-to-day call actions for each phone model. Where steps differ between models, they are documented separately.

📱 Model GRP2613 - Call Action Reference

Hold - Placing & Picking Up

  • Press the Hold button to place an active call on hold.

  • Press the Hold button again to resume the call.

  • A call on hold can only be picked up from the same phone that placed it.

📌 Note: When managing multiple calls simultaneously, use the flashing line buttons on the phone screen to switch between them.

Hold Music

Hold music is managed through the Adit platform, not the phone hardware.

  • Navigate to: Settings → Numbers → Hold Music

Transferring a Call

  • Press the Transfer button on the phone.

  • Dial the 3-digit extension or full 10-digit phone number for the transfer destination.

Calling Another Phone in the Office

Simply dial the extension number of the phone you would like to reach.

Checking Voicemail

✅ PREFERRED: Use the Adit platform’s Visual Voicemail feature instead of checking directly on the phone.

In the Adit platform, voicemail can be accessed from:

  • The “What’s Happening” section on the Home page

  • The Call Pop icon in the top Menu Bar

Visual Voicemail lets you:

  • Quickly identify which voicemail you need without listening through all messages sequentially.

  • Access archived voicemails and eFaxes in the same location.

To check voicemail directly on the GRP2613 (not preferred):

  • Press the Message (envelope) button.

  • Press the round Select button in the centre of the direction pad.

  • Voicemail messages will begin playing automatically.

Parking a Call

  • Press the Park soft key. The call will park into the designated slot.

  • A red light will appear across all phones in the location to indicate a parked call.

Picking Up a Parked Call

A parked call can be picked up from any desktop phone at the same location.

  • Press the steady red light on any phone to answer the parked call.

Making an Outbound Call While a Call Is Parked

  • Press an available extension button first (e.g., Ext 1).

  • Then pick up the handset.

📌 Note: If the handset is picked up without first pressing an empty extension, the phone will pick up the parked call by default.

Receiving an Inbound Call While a Call Is Parked

  • Press the inbound call extension FIRST, then pick up the handset.

  • If the handset is picked up without first pressing the inbound extension, the phone will default to picking up the parked call.

📌 Note: Do not leave a patient parked for more than 60 seconds. If a call remains parked beyond 60 seconds, it will return as an inbound call to the phone that originally parked it. While a call is parked, none of the phones will ring for new inbound calls - the first available extension will blink instead.

📱 Model GRP2616 - Call Action Reference

The GRP2616 operates identically to the GRP2613 for all call actions. Refer to the GRP2613 section above for full steps. Key actions are summarised below for quick reference.

Hold - Placing & Picking Up

  • Press the Hold button to place a call on hold; press again to resume.

  • A held call can only be resumed from the same phone.

📌 Note: Use the flashing line buttons to switch between multiple active/held calls.

Hold Music

  • Settings → Numbers → Hold Music (managed in Adit platform).

Transferring a Call

  • Press the Transfer button, then dial the 3-digit extension or 10-digit number.

Calling Another Phone in the Office

Dial the extension of the phone you wish to reach.

Checking Voicemail

✅ PREFERRED: Use Visual Voicemail in the Adit platform (Home page or Call Pop).

To check directly on the GRP2616:

  • Press the Message button → Press the round Select button → Messages play automatically.

Parking a Call

  • Press the Park soft key to park the call. Red light appears across all phones.

Picking Up a Parked Call

  • Press the steady red light on any phone at the same location.

Outbound / Inbound Calls While a Call Is Parked

  • Outbound: Press an available extension first, then pick up handset.

  • Inbound: Press the inbound extension first, then pick up handset - otherwise the parked call is picked up by default.

📌 Note: 60-second park limit applies. Parked call returns to originating phone after 60 seconds. Inbound calls show as blinking extensions, not rings, while a call is parked.

📱 Model DP720 - Cordless Handset Call Action Reference

Hold - Placing & Picking Up

  • While on an active call, press the right soft key to place the call on hold.

  • Press the right soft key again to resume the call.

Hold Music

  • Managed via the Adit platform: Settings → Numbers → Hold Music.

Transferring a Call

  • Press Options on the handset.

  • Select Transfer.

  • Dial the 3-digit extension or full 10-digit phone number for the transfer destination.

Calling Another Phone in the Office

Dial the extension number of the phone you wish to reach.

Checking Voicemail

✅ PREFERRED: Use Visual Voicemail in the Adit platform (Home page or Call Pop).

To check directly on the DP720 (not preferred):

  • Press the Message button → Press the round Select button → Messages play automatically.

Parking a Call

  • Press the left soft key and select Blind Transfer.

  • Enter 901 or 902 and press Transfer.

  • The call is now parked.

Picking Up a Parked Call

Once parked, the call can be picked up from any phone in the same location.

  • On a cordless handset, dial 901 or 902 and press Dial to pick up the parked call.

Update regarding porting process Getting Started to Onboarding (Voice)

Update regarding porting process Getting Started to Onboarding

1. The sales team is helping the porting team to get the porting details and documents from the client.

2. After all the GT steps are done and the IT details record is marked as Valid by porting, the deal gets moved from Getting Started to Onboarding.

3.Deals are marked as invalid if the porting details or documents are incomplete or incorrect.

4. An automation task is sent to Ruchi after the deal is marked as invalid.

5. For invalid deals Ruchi helps the porting team to get the correct details and documents from clients.

6.We have maintained a porting rule book which has the contact details and other details of Adit competitor companies. Porting details and document required sheet

7. If there are any additional numbers apart from landline and fax numbers in client current phone provider company CSR or invoice which is not updated in IT details record that is supposed to be confirmed by the OB of the deal before the config call date is updated in tech OB record.

Note: We have observed multiple issues while obtaining porting details and required documents from the current phone provider. These issues often include delays in sharing information or providing incomplete details in the CSR or invoice. Similar problems sometimes continue even after the porting process has started, where porting requests may be rejected by the current phone provider despite submitting correct details and documentation.

Therefore, we request you to kindly set the right expectation with the client that until the number is successfully ported, any delays or issues encountered during the process may occur due to the current phone provider or their carrier.

Below are the main reasons for porting getting rejected.
· The current phone provider company or carrier company didn’t get approval from client (owner of the number) to release the number when they received the port out request which we have raised.

· The current phone provider company does this intentionally so that they can make the process complicated and convince the client to stay with them.
